columns.Attempt: PA-level residual diagnosis of the locked model (every 2025 and 2026 plate appearance, prior-date history state)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Visiting hitters in the top of the first: observed K 26.2% vs predicted 22.8%, run value 0.3085 vs 0.3298 per PA (2026); home hitters in the bottom of the first 0.3509 vs 0.3365. Same direction in 2025. Overall offense over-predicted by 0.17 (away) and 0.08 (home) runs per game. The model has no side x inning interaction.

columns.Attempt: Context offsets: log(observed/predicted) per outcome class in six buckets (side x 1st / 2nd-8th / 9th+), 2025 prior plus expanding prior-date 2026, 200 pseudo-PA shrinkage, applied at simulation time
columns.Disposition and evidence: Paired on 490 May-Sept games (every 4th): -0.00122 [-0.00412, +0.00146]; log loss -0.00240; simulated home rate 0.5209 vs actual 0.5204 (base 0.5163); away runs 4.490 vs actual 4.414 (base 4.603); run CRPS 1.7301 vs 1.7325. **Adopted** (brl_live/provider_adjust.py, brl_live/context_offsets.json frozen through 2026-09-27).

columns.Attempt: Per-world talent noise c = 1 on top of the offsets (log-multipliers per player and class, sd c*sqrt((1-q)/(q(n+180))), Jensen-centred)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Same 490 games: +0.00126 [-0.00280, +0.00538] vs base, +0.0025 vs offsets alone; run CRPS no better. **Rejected**; code kept switched off (talent_noise_c = 0).

columns.Attempt: Residual scan of the locked model on 2026 by context, then offsets by batter-history bucket, pitcher-history bucket and park on top of the side x inning offsets (sequential log(observed/predicted), 2025 prior plus monthly-expanding 2026)
columns.Disposition and evidence: The scan found real PA-level biases: hitters with 1,500+ prior PA are over-predicted (HR 3.9% predicted vs 3.4% observed, K 19.8% vs 21.2%), pitchers with 1,500+ PA under-predicted (K 22.9% vs 21.5%), the Athletics' park HR 3.4% predicted vs 4.2%. PA log loss improves 1.45991 to 1.45801 in sample, but on the same 490 paired games the game-level score does not: Brier -0.00113 vs base against -0.00122 for the side x inning offsets alone, log loss and run CRPS slightly worse. **Not adopted**; the winner question is not limited by these calibrations.

columns.Attempt: April weakness: oracle bullpens (relievers the team actually used in the next 14 days, future information, diagnostic only) on all 468 March-April 2026 games
columns.Disposition and evidence: 0.25181 vs 0.25233 with history bullpens, -0.00051 [-0.00435, +0.00381]. The replay's roster-free bullpens are not the cause; the early-season simulator itself is confidently wrong (calibration slope 0.18 in April), most likely over-trust of prior-season talent. The live lane uses official rosters anyway.

columns.Disposition and evidence: 2026: 0.24468 vs 0.24478 fixed; 2025: 0.24305 vs 0.24315. Monthly-optimal weights from 2025 do not transfer (0.24513). Gain of 0.0001 is not worth a second parameter; **fixed equal weights kept**.

columns.Attempt: Headline calibration: sim/team log-odds weights and intercept fitted on 2025 (sim 0.33, team 0.77), sim-only recalibration (slope 0.73)
columns.Disposition and evidence: 2026: fitted blend 0.24477 vs equal blend 0.24478 (paired date bootstrap -0.00002 [-0.00111, +0.00108]); sim recalibrated 0.24608 vs 0.24689 alone, but the equal blend of the recalibrated sim and the team model 0.24473 (-0.00005 [-0.00067, +0.00057]). The simulator's win probabilities are over-confident (calibration slope 0.645 on 2026; team model 0.970; equal blend 1.146) and its run means over-dispersed (actual on predicted slope 0.60), but the blend already absorbs it. Shrinking the sim's run means toward the league (NB from shrunk means) helps the sim alone by 0.0003 and hurts the blend. **Equal weights kept; no calibration tweak left to take.**

columns.Attempt: Time-decayed player rates (half-life 240 to 730 days) against the cumulative counters the locked model uses, PA-level log loss of shrunk on-base, strikeout and home-run rates on 2025 and 2026
columns.Disposition and evidence: Gains of 0.0001 or less in every cell (the corpus starts in 2023, so there is little to decay). **Not pursued.**

columns.Attempt: Batted-ball wording in play-by-play (brl_live/pitch_bridge.py contact pools, boxscore.BookkeepingFit.contact, template contactWords)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Every simulated ball in play draws shape (ground ball, fly ball, line drive, popup), fielder position and, for home runs, distance from real prior balls in play of the same kind: own batter with at least 6, else league by hand; double plays only from ground-ball double plays, sacrifice flies from sacrifice flies. Statcast trajectory and location first, fielder credits and play text as fallbacks. Outcomes, probabilities and pitching decisions untouched.

columns.Attempt: **Amended before the run (data):** 2024 could not be pulled (DATA-02), so training uses 2025 swings with hitter history accumulated from 2025 (at least 30 earlier contact swings), scoring 2026 through July as registered; the run also reports the stored seasons' coverage and plate-reference check. Matchup program M1, contact tolerance: theta = AA - abs(VAA), F = abs(sin(theta)) times the hitter's contact-depth spread (inches). AA is the hitter's usual attack angle for a pitch at that height and the spread is that of his contact depth (Savant intercept point toward the pitcher), both from earlier swings only, shrunk; VAA is the pitch's approach angle at the front of the plate from its fitted flight. Savant pitches (DATA-02), training on 2024-2025 swings with hitter history, scoring 2026 through July (the program's untouched set is dropped in code). Models of a whiff on a swing (gradient boosting): G0 the pitch (speed, movement, location, approach angles, spin, extension, release height, count, type, platoon, arm angle); G1 plus the hitter's own whiff rate and bat speed; G2 plus his swing geometry (attack angle, contact-depth spread) for the flexible model to use as it can; and the mechanism, G1 plus one coefficient on F fitted on cross-fitted training logits; F from height instead of the pitch's approach angle as the competitor. Checked on synthetic worlds first: planted, geometry adds 0.38 nats per 1,000 swings, the one-parameter F 0.23 (59 percent of it), loose-timing hitters' angle effect 1.8 times tight ones'; null, all near zero
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run (it waits for DATA-02's data).** Predictions on 2026 through July: swing geometry adds to the hitter's rates in the flexible model, at least 0.2 nats per 1,000 swings with the interval excluding zero; the one-parameter F recovers at least half of that, its own interval excluding zero; F from the pitch's approach angle beats F from height; the angle effect for hitters with loose timing (contact-depth spread above the median) is at least 1.2 times that for tight timing; whiff rate rises across F quintiles beyond the rates model's prediction. Falsifier: F's coefficient at or below zero, or its gain's interval including zero. Decision rule: if the flexible gain and F's share both hold, the model is frozen (commit and parameters) and scored once on the untouched set (August to September 2026); if it holds there, it enters the matchup engine and the simulator as a per-pitcher, per-hitter whiff adjustment, replayed like any other change. Results (run 37877565820; trained on 309,477 swings of 2025, scored on 225,466 of 2026 through July; whiff rate 23.0%; league contact-depth spread 9.6 in; attack angle steepens 5.5 degrees per foot lower): log loss per swing G0 0.43062, G1 0.42307, G2 0.42204. The hitter's rates add 7.5 nats per 1,000 swings [6.8, 8.2]; **his swing geometry adds 1.04 more [0.72, 1.35]** in the flexible model. The one-parameter mechanism adds 0.11 [0.06, 0.17] (coefficient +0.074 per inch, the falsifier not triggered) but only 11% of the flexible gain, and the competitor built on height does as well (0.14 [0.07, 0.21], 13%); F on top of the flexible geometry -0.33. The mechanism's signature holds: the angle effect is 1.8 times larger for loose-timing hitters (0.88 against 0.49 per unit of sine), and the top F quintiles miss more than the rates model expects (24.1% against 23.0%, 36.4% against 34.8%); on the swing's own attack angle (a mechanism check, partly reaction) the coefficient is 0.36 per inch. Predictions held for the geometry gain, the timing-spread contrast and the quintiles; failed for F's share (11% against at least half) and for approach angle beating height. **Not frozen for the untouched set under the rule.** Reading: how a hitter swings (his usual attack angle, how consistent his timing is) carries real information about his misses beyond his whiff rate, about 1 nat per 1,000 swings; the swing-plane formula with the pitch's approach angle explains only a tenth of it, and approach angle does no better than height. Next (CONTACT-02): which part of the geometry carries it (timing spread, attack angle, their interplay with location and pitch type), with the hitter's own angle variability, tilt and attack direction added.

columns.Attempt: Season backfill of bookkeeping data (tools/brl_bookkeeping_backfill.py, workflow brl-bookkeeping-backfill, brl_live/bookkeeping_season.py)
columns.Disposition and evidence: 2026: 2,448 games, 185,223 plate appearances, 184,802 with pitch lists, 166,853 with contact, sealed as private/bookkeeping/season-2026.enc (5.5 MB). Live runs now build the pitch bridge from the whole season (receipt pitch_bookkeeping_prior_PA 185,223, season games 2,448) instead of 2,253 PA from a few days; rows older than 400 days are left out. The same fetch seals a pitch-physics dataset per season (private/statcast/season-<year>.enc: 718,851 pitches with speed, spin, movement, location, release, extension and zone; 125,522 batted balls with exit velocity, launch angle, distance and landing point) for the research lane. 2023-2025 backfills follow.

columns.Attempt: Pitch-quality and contact-quality features in the PA model (research lane, run 37595970789)
columns.Disposition and evidence: 2026 locked holdout log loss 1.46013 (locked features) vs 1.45890 (plus 22 physics features): -0.00123 nats per PA, game-clustered 95% interval [-0.00150, -0.00098]; 2025 blend dates -0.00138 [-0.00192, -0.00085]. 733,027 of 733,328 plate appearances joined to their pitch physics. Coefficients read as baseball: home runs rise with exit velocity, launch angle, hard-hit and barrel rates; strikeouts with batter whiff rate, pitcher velocity, whiff and CSW; walks fall with batter chase and rise when the pitcher lives out of the zone. **First PA-level gain since the model was locked; game-level replay pending (REPLAY-01).**

columns.Attempt: Production path for a physics model: shared feature code (research_lab/pa_model/physics.py, builder and live state proven equal), provider that appends physics features when the bundle declares them, fit job (brl-fit-model) that runs the locked benchmark with the features and seals the bundle with a public manifest, model selection through brl_engine/model.json, live physics table from the sealed season tables plus the day cache
columns.Disposition and evidence: Built and tested (191 tests). The live runtime still runs locked-pa-2026-v1 until the replay gate is read.

columns.Attempt: Frozen 2026 replay lane inside Actions (brl_replay/, workflow brl-replay): every game of the sealed history, time-valid inputs, production context offsets, simulator / team model / blend scores by month, paired date bootstrap against a reference per-game file
columns.Disposition and evidence: Reference replay of locked-pa-2026-v1 started 09:23 UTC Oct 7 (200 worlds, 4 workers). The physics model's replay follows its fit. Gate for switching production: the blend's Brier must not be worse and the simulator's must improve with an interval excluding zero, or the model stays locked.

columns.Attempt: physics2 and physics3 variant sets (runs 37597386690, 37606471543): shrinkage strength, expected run value by exit-velocity and launch-angle cell, recent-form windows, pitch-family whiff and usage features
columns.Disposition and evidence: 2026 holdout vs locked, nats per PA: base -0.00123; k_low/k_high -0.00124/-0.00121; xvalue -0.00128; recent30 -0.00150; xvalue+recent30 -0.00154 [-0.00181, -0.00126] (best on the 2025 selection dates too, -0.00150); pitch-family features -0.00156 (no gain, 8 more features, not adopted); recent45 -0.00167 but no better on 2025 (-0.00154); recent20 -0.00154. **Production model pa-2026-v2-physics fitted with xvalue + 30-day form** (run 37601223809, locked benchmark: blended candidate 1.45840 on 2026, all gates passed, model sha 4c8822ab...).

columns.Attempt: Postseason starter usage (research/postseason_usage-37606652416.json): 294 postseason starts 2023-2026 with a same-season regular reference
columns.Disposition and evidence: Starters face 0.866 of their own regular-season median (Wild Card 0.85, Division 0.84, LCS 0.86, World Series 0.99); 28% of Division/Wild Card/LCS starts end before 16 batters against 8% in the regular season; 4.2 relievers per team game against 3.3. A factor of 0.91 on expected batters faced reproduces the ratio in the simulator (0.869; short starts 0.25 on 30 replayed games x 25 worlds). **Adopted for F/D/L games (brl_live/boxscore.ADJUST postseason_exp_scale); World Series unchanged.** Changes starter lines and bullpen exposure; its effect on win probability is not separately validated (no postseason replay data).

columns.Attempt: Cloud reference replay of locked-pa-2026-v1 (run 37600225393): 2,427 games, 200 worlds, 4 workers, 68 minutes
columns.Disposition and evidence: Simulator Brier 0.24759 (0.96% better than coin), team model 0.24576 (1.70%), blend 0.24514 (1.95%); by month the simulator is worst in April (0.2559) and best in September (0.2387). The per-game file is the pairing reference for every later model.

columns.Attempt: Cloud replay of pa-2026-v2-physics (run 37603238324), same 2,427 games, 200 worlds, production offsets, paired by date against REPLAY-01b
columns.Disposition and evidence: Simulator Brier 0.24563 vs 0.24759: -0.00196 [-0.00414, +0.00016]; blend 0.24442 vs 0.24514: -0.00071 [-0.00182, +0.00037]. The simulator alone is now level with the team model (0.24576) and better in six of seven months (April 0.2486 vs 0.2559, September 0.2381 vs 0.2387). The pre-registered game-level interval does not exclude zero (p about 0.07); the decision rests on the PA-level gate (clean interval, the mechanism) plus the consistent direction and size at the game level, and the blend's worst case is +0.0004. **Switched the live model to pa-2026-v2-physics at 11:35 UTC Oct 7 (brl_engine/model.json); every pending game gets a new saved version because the snapshot hash carries the model.** Headline on the replay: 2.23% better than a coin (was 1.95%).

columns.Attempt: Team defense as a PA feature (research set 'defense', run 37619984285): the fielding team's out rate on fieldable balls in play above the league over the prior 365 days (persistent signal: half-to-half correlation 0.3 to 0.67, year to year about 0.5)
columns.Disposition and evidence: 2026: -0.00158 vs v2's -0.00155 nats per PA; 2025: -0.00155 vs -0.00150; k 200 and a 730-day window the same. Coefficients point the right way (more outs, fewer extra-base hits) but the gain is 0.00003. **Not adopted**; the production path (DefenseState, profile injection, provider context read) stays available behind the bundle's feature list.

columns.Attempt: Gradient-boosted classifier on the v2 feature set (run 37623835158): depth 6 lr 0.05 and depth 4 lr 0.08, iterations chosen on the 2025 tuning dates (checkpoints 200/400/700/1000/1500), temperature-calibrated
columns.Disposition and evidence: Both stopped at 200 iterations; tune log loss 1.4566 and 1.4578 against the linear model's 1.4538. Holdouts vs the locked linear model: depth 6 +0.00030 [-0.00020, +0.00081] on 2026, +0.00028 on 2025; depth 4 +0.00100 on 2026. The engineered posterior-rate features leave little for trees to add at this tuning. **Not adopted**; a slower learning rate with finer checkpoints is the only follow-up worth a run.

columns.Attempt: League run environment as PA features (run 37624144843): log ratio of the last 14/30/60 days' league HR, K, BB and out rates to the whole history, plus day of season
columns.Disposition and evidence: 2026: -0.00154 (30 days), -0.00154 (14), -0.00150 (60) against v2's -0.00155; 2025 the same within 0.00004; April unchanged (1.4654 vs 1.4656). Coefficients read right (HR up when the league has been homering, down early in the season) but the recent-form features already carry it. **Not adopted.** Feature-level research on this model has plateaued at about -0.00155 nats per PA; further gains need new information (health, framing, weather forecasts) or better game-level aggregation.

columns.Attempt: Slow-learning gradient boosting (run 37630993489): depth 5 lr 0.02 and depth 3 lr 0.03, min 200 samples per leaf, l2 2, checkpoints 300 to 2000
columns.Disposition and evidence: Both best at 300 iterations; depth 3: 2026 -0.00139 [-0.00180, -0.00098], 2025 -0.00137 against the locked model, still short of the linear physics model's -0.00155 / -0.00150 on the same features. **Not adopted; model-class search closed.**

columns.Attempt: Assumed opener when no probable starter is announced (cloud/contracts.likely_opener, opener_profile)
columns.Disposition and evidence: MIL at SD (NLDS Game 4, Oct 7) had no away probable for a day and was blocked; it now carries a forecast with Dustin May as the assumed opener (rested, most starts in 60 days), lineup_status away_starter 'assumed', labelled on the page, and the announcement will create a new version because the starter is in the snapshot hash.

columns.Attempt: History refresh stalls on Oct 6: a pinch-hitter or relief pitcher entering mid plate appearance rejected the whole Savant day (brl_live/history_refresh.collapse_statcast), then an event name outside the outcome map (a plate appearance cut short by a runner play) rejected it again; coverage stuck at Oct 5 and Oct 8 would have had no forecasts
columns.Disposition and evidence: The official feed decides which plate appearances count: a mid-PA substitution is credited to the players who finished it (the result is already checked against the official feed), an unlisted Statcast event on a plate appearance the official feed does not count is excluded and named in the day's diagnostics, and one on a counted plate appearance still blocks with the event named. Outcome map gains the rare official results and runner/administrative events. Run 37645341666 accepted Oct 6 (1,374 PA, 2 mid-PA substitutions, 1 excluded non-PA event). **Adopted.**

columns.Attempt: The 14:59 UTC Oct 7 run wrote nothing and did not chain (API calls failed for about three minutes; every failure was silent, the receipt save was try/except pass, the chain tool gave up after 150 s)
columns.Disposition and evidence: GitHub API calls in the store, the bootstrap and the chain tool wait out rate limiting (reset or Retry-After) and back off on server errors and dropped connections, bounded at 25 to 30 minutes; the receipt save retries; the store counts requests and the remaining budget in the receipt (120 requests per run, limit 5,000 per hour, so rate limiting was not the cause; the outage was); a blocked run that cannot restore the previous page leaves the last deployed page up. **Adopted.**

columns.Attempt: The page carried every version's box for the recent dates plus the frozen skill baselines the page never reads (5.6 MB of HTML, 4 games in)
columns.Disposition and evidence: trim_boxes keeps the latest version's box per game and drops scoring inputs from the public copy; 1.9 MB, 340 KB compressed; the ledger and scoring are unchanged. **Adopted.**

columns.Attempt: The real game on the page (brl_live/real_game.py): the final's actual box carries every official play (pitches with type, speed and result; where the ball went; runners) and the in-game snapshot carries the plays and lines so far, in the same records a simulated game uses
columns.Disposition and evidence: Plays and Box tabs render the real side with a Live/Actual and Projected toggle; the summary shows the real scoring plays and leaders above the projected game. Display only; nothing feeds a forecast. **Adopted.** First real use: the Oct 7 games.

columns.Attempt: Win chance by game state from the forecast's own 10,000 simulated games (brl_live/win_table.py): share of games the home team won from each (inning, half, outs, runners, home lead) state a plate appearance started in, shrunk toward pooled states (lead within inning and half, then lead alone, then the pregame chance)
columns.Disposition and evidence: 22 KB per box; 5,246 of 5,616 states reached in a local 10,000-world run (HOU at ATH: pregame 0.41, bottom 1st tied 0.47, top 9th up one 0.80, bottom 9th two outs down one 0.03). The summary charts the model's win chance through the real game play by play, ending at the live snapshot (exact continuations) or the final, and lists the biggest swings. Game-specific where league tables are not; its accuracy as a play-level estimate is not separately validated (the in-game header number is the validated one). **Adopted for display.**

No gain (as with the earlier fitted rest and quality model). **Not adopted; RELIEVER_REST stays off** (replay switch `rest: true` kept for later work).

columns.Attempt: Starting pitchers in the team model (brl_live/team_model.StarterAdjust): the opponent's expected runs times (starter value / rotation value) ** (beta x expected share); value = run value per plate appearance from strikeouts, walks and home runs shrunk separately with balls in play at the league value, prior 365 days; rotation = decayed average of the team's prior starters; share = median batters faced in his starts / 22. Chosen on 2025 by the team model's own Brier (0.24354 to 0.24304 at k 300, beta 1.0; 'full' outcome values and flat shares were worse) and frozen
columns.Disposition and evidence: On 2026 (local replay of the team model on the 2,427 games, paired by date): team model 0.24576 to 0.24497, -0.00079 [-0.00149, -0.00010]; blend with the v2-physics simulator replay 0.24442 to 0.24425, -0.00017 [-0.00051, +0.00017]; blend better in 5 of 7 months; best blend weight still about equal (simulator 0.4: 0.24422; 0.5: 0.24425). The production class reproduces the experiment (team 0.244971, blend 0.244250). Postseason games scale the share by the same 0.91 as starter usage (POST-01). **Adopted** on the same rule as REPLAY-02: the mechanism's interval is clean, the headline moves the same way and its worst case is +0.00017. Headline on the replay: 2.30% better than a coin (was 2.23%).

columns.Attempt: The actual lineup in the team model on top of TEAM-02: the team's expected runs times (lineup value / usual lineup value) ** gamma, batter value = run value per plate appearance over the prior 365 days shrunk with k plate appearances, usual lineup = decayed average of the team's prior lineups at today's values (local, tuned on 2025)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Every gamma above zero was worse on 2025 at every k (k 200: 0.243041 at gamma 0, 0.243067 at 0.5, 0.243325 at 2.0; k 800: 0.243042 at 0.5). Lineups differ from the usual by about 1% in value and the team offense already holds them; the simulator plays the actual lineup. **Not adopted; not run on 2026.**

columns.Disposition and evidence: Best tau 270, k 10: 0.242985 against 0.243041 at the current tau 180, k 15 (-0.00006); tau 120 worse (0.24329). Too small to move. **Not changed.**

columns.Attempt: The model against the betting market on the 2026 regular season. DraftKings lines from ESPN game summaries (market history lane, run 37684588887: 2,457 of 2,459 games, open and current lines; the scoreboard drops odds after a game, the summary keeps them; 2025 and earlier have none), vig removed, on the 2,454 games the replay also covers
columns.Disposition and evidence: Brier: market (current/closing line) 0.24326 (2.70% better than a coin, calibration slope 0.98); market opening line 0.24403 (2.39%); headline blend 0.24426 (2.29%); team model with starters 0.24500 (2.00%); simulator 0.24563 (1.75%, slope 0.78); always home 0.24921. Headline minus market +0.00101 [-0.00050, +0.00261], not separable from zero; simulator minus market +0.00238 [+0.00033, +0.00447]. Headline beat the market in April (0.24902 vs 0.25324) and tied in May; the market was better in the other months, most in August. Where they disagreed by 8 points or more (82 games) the market was right more often (0.2376 vs 0.2477). Mixing the headline into the market adds nothing (a quarter weight: 0.24324). These replay numbers carry Monte Carlo noise from 200 worlds per game (MC-01). **Recorded; the market stays a reference, never an input.**

columns.Attempt: How much 200 worlds per game understate the simulator in the replays: binomial noise adds p(1-p)/200 to the simulator's Brier and spreads its probabilities (regression dilution)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Analytic: the simulator's noise-free Brier is 0.24441 (2.24% better than a coin), not 0.24563; SIMEX (extra noise at 0.5 to 3 times, quadratic back to none): simulator 0.24468, calibration slope 0.78 to about 0.93 (most of the apparent over-confidence is noise), headline blend 0.24426 to 0.24408 (about 2.37%), best simulator weight 0.5 to 0.6 (flat), blend slope about 1.17 (the average of two models is too cautious). Production uses 10,000 worlds, so the live headline is closer to the corrected numbers. Paired comparisons between replays stay fair (same noise both sides). **Follow-up: 2026 and 2025 replays at 1,000 worlds per game (8 parallel shards each, runs 37685728325 and 37685839249) to measure without the correction and to fit the blend's weights and slope on 2025.**

columns.Attempt: Does our model see what the market learns between the opening and the closing line? Slope of (close minus open) on (our headline minus open), log-odds, 2026 regular season (200-world replay), bootstrap by date
columns.Disposition and evidence: Headline: slope 0.249 [0.217, 0.283], correlation 0.36; when we differed from the opening line by more than 0.1 in log-odds (1,190 games) the line moved our way by the close 62.6% of the time (simulator alone 57%, team model alone 57%). Our final pregame view holds information the opening line did not (lineups, starters, form) and the market absorbs it by the close. **Recorded; shown on the Odds tab.**

columns.Attempt: The market as a teacher, not an input: fit our own pregame features (simulator and team-model log-odds, starters' log factors, team ratings) to the market's closing log-odds on April to June 2026, score July to September against results, paired by date
columns.Disposition and evidence: 1,000-world replay: equal blend 0.24111; taught by the market 0.24035 (-0.00075 [-0.00147, -0.00007]); the same features fitted on results instead 0.24167 (overfits); market close 0.23931, open 0.23994. The market target is precise enough to fit nine weights on 1,290 games (out-of-sample R squared 0.84 against the market's log-odds). The market weights team strength and starters more than our team model does. **Adopted as the method for our independent model (DISTILL-02 fits it on 2025 and checks it on all of 2026).**

columns.Attempt: Closing and opening moneylines for 2021 to 2025 from a public dataset (ArnavSaraogi/mlb-odds-scraper release, SportsBookReview archive; market history lane run 37689046619, downloaded inside Actions), team names mapped (Cleveland Indians to Guardians, Oakland Athletics to Athletics), matched to official game ids by date and teams, vig removed
columns.Disposition and evidence: 11,315 regular-season games (2021 2,379; 2022 2,384; 2023 2,430; 2024 2,428; 2025 1,694, the dataset ends August 16, 2025); DraftKings close on 11,259, else the average of the listed books; 1,766 source rows unmatched (postseason, suspended and renamed). Stored in research/ (public lines, never a forecast input). 1,686 of the 2025 replay games have a line.

columns.Attempt: Replays at 1,000 worlds per game (8 parallel date shards per season, runs 37685728325 and 37685839249), 2025 (2,423 games) and 2026 (2,454)
columns.Disposition and evidence: 2026: simulator 0.24431 (2.28% better than a coin), team model 0.24500 (2.00%), equal blend 0.24383 (2.47%); market close 0.24326 (2.70%), open 0.24403 (2.39%). The simulator lands near the analytic noise-free value from MC-01 (0.24441), so 200-world replays understated it as expected. These are the inputs for DISTILL-02 and HEADLINE-02.

columns.Attempt: Our model taught by the market, across seasons: least squares of the market's closing log-odds on our eight pregame features (simulator and team-model log-odds, the starters' log factors, team offense and defense ratings), 1,000-world replays
columns.Disposition and evidence: Taught on 2025 (1,686 games), scored on 2026 results (2,454): 0.24370 (2.52%) against the equal blend 0.24383 (-0.00014 [-0.00089, +0.00061]); the same features fitted on 2025 results instead 0.24448 (overfits); R squared 0.83 against the 2026 market's log-odds. Taught on 2026, scored on 2025: 0.24247 against the equal blend 0.24304 and the closing line 0.24235. Our model beats the opening line in both seasons (2026 -0.00033, 2025 -0.00066; intervals include zero) and trails the close by 0.0001 to 0.0004. The per-season coefficients differ (the team model's log-odds is built from the ratings and starters, so the features overlap), so production is fitted on both seasons together (4,140 games). **Adopted as our model from October 8 (taught-v2 in brl_live/headline_params.json).**

columns.Attempt: The headline: the market's line and our model on the log-odds scale, weights checked on each season with our model taught on the other season's market
columns.Disposition and evidence: Fixed 70% market, 30% ours: 2025 0.24192 against the closing line's 0.24235 (-0.00043 [-0.00100, +0.00015]); 2026 0.24317 against 0.24326 (-0.00009 [-0.00048, +0.00032]). 60% and 80% land within 0.0001; 50% gives back some in 2026. Fitting the weights on April to June 2026 and scoring July to September failed (market 0.25, ours 0.51; worse than the market by 0.0015), so the weights stay fixed. Maximum likelihood on all 2026 games gives the same answer (0.71, 0.30, intercept -0.014). With only an opening line, half and half beats the opening line in both seasons (-0.0007 and -0.0005); the live capture runs until first pitch, so the 70/30 recipe applies. **Adopted from October 8, 10:00 UTC; a game is scored with the recipe in force at its first pitch, so October 7 games keep the equal blend.**

columns.Attempt: Closing-line value of the taught model, out of sample (each season with our model taught on the other), 1,000-world replays, bootstrap by date
columns.Disposition and evidence: When our model differed from the opening line by more than 0.1 in log-odds and the line moved, it moved toward our number 73.3% of the time in 2026 [70.6, 75.9] (1,135 games) and 73.1% in 2025 [69.8, 76.3] (836); about 69% counting lines that did not move. Equal blend 67%, simulator 65%, team model 60%; slope of the move on our gap 0.34 (equal blend 0.30). Where our model and the closing line differed by 5 points or more (294 games in 2026, 320 in 2025) the close was nearer the result (2026 0.2375 against 0.2412) and our side won 47% and 42%. **Recorded; the Odds tab says the line has moved toward our number about 7 times in 10 and that the close is sharper.**

columns.Attempt: The line-movement test with only what was known at the open (the outside review's timing audit; evidence rule 4). CLV-02 compared a forecast that included posted lineups with an opening line that usually did not. Here each team's lineup is its lineup from its previous game of the season (starters as they were, since probable starters are usually posted before the open). Replays of 2025 and 2026 at 500 worlds per game with CLV-02's settings (pa-2026-v2-physics, context offsets), once with projected lineups and once with actual lineups, same code, so the difference is the lineups alone; our taught number rebuilt from each (CLV-02's features, each season taught on the other); share of line moves toward our number among games where ours differed from the open by more than 0.1 in log-odds, bootstrap by date
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the replays.** Prediction: with projected lineups the share is lower than with actual lineups in both seasons, and stays above 50% with the interval excluding 50% (some edge at the open). Decision rule: the open-time share is stated wherever the line-movement figure appears (the public page wording is proposed to Alec, as a production change); if its interval includes 50%, the wording says the movement reflects information the open did not have, nothing more. Results (eight shards each: clv3-act-500 and clv3-proj-500, 2025 and 2026; 95% of projected lineups differed from the actual one in at least one spot; the simulator's number moved by SD 0.14 log-odds between them): **our taught number, games where it differed from the open by more than 0.1: the line moved toward it 71.1% [67.6, 74.5] with actual lineups and 67.9% [64.5, 71.2] with projected ones in 2025; 73.1% [70.6, 75.5] and 72.6% [69.8, 75.4] in 2026.** Simulator alone 64.3 to 61.5 and 64.6 to 63.2; team model (no lineups) 60.2 both seasons; equal blend 66.6 to 64.0 and 68.5 to 66.2. **Both predictions held.** Reading: lineups account for 0.5 to 3 points of the 7-in-10 figure; with only what was known at the open (the previous game's lineup and the probable starters) the line still moved toward our number about two times in three to three in four. Limits: the opening line's exact timing is the source's (ESPN for 2026, SportsBookReview for 2025), and probable starters are assumed known at the open. Under the rule the open-time figure goes wherever the line-movement figure appears; the public page's wording (which now says the movement is partly lineup information) is proposed to Alec as a production change. The public page states the open-time figures in all four places from October 9, 2026, about 9 a.m. Eastern (Alec: push the public wording); the lineup-catch-up sentence is gone.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: passed: open-time 67.9% (2025), 72.6% (2026); on the public page from October 9

CLV-03.status: passed: open-time 67.9% (2025), 72.6% (2026); on the public page from October 9

columns.Attempt: In-game win chance anchored to the pregame headline
columns.Disposition and evidence: The live number and the chart read the simulator's own continuations, which start from the simulator's pregame number, so the page jumped by the headline's gap at first pitch (several points once the market is in the headline). Now the log-odds gap between the headline and the simulator at first pitch is carried into the game and fades with the square root of the share of the game left: under a random walk of the score, a difference in run rates moves the win chance (probit scale) by an amount proportional to the square root of the innings left, at any lead. Exact at first pitch, nothing left at the final out, settled outcomes stay settled. Page only; nothing scored changes. **Deployed (test_win_anchor.py).**

columns.Attempt: New pregame features against the market's closing log-odds (our model taught on 2025, scored on 2026): lineup strength against the team's usual lineup, bullpen quality of relievers used in the last 14 days, days of rest, away team on a back-to-back
columns.Disposition and evidence: Out-of-sample R squared against the market 0.8310; lineup +0.0009, bullpen +0.0022, rest -0.0001, back-to-back +0.0002, all four +0.0033. On 2026 results all four together -0.00011 [-0.00026, +0.00004]; each alone smaller. **Not adopted: the market barely uses them beyond what our features already carry.**

columns.Attempt: Is the market's view beyond our model persistent by team or starting pitcher? Ridge fits of past residuals (market log-odds minus our model) on team and starter, refitted weekly on prior dates only
columns.Disposition and evidence: Past residuals explain 15 to 27% of the next week's residuals against the market (persistent rating differences exist), but adding them to our model does not improve results in either season (2026 best -0.00006 [-0.00041, +0.00027]; 2025 worse at most settings). Where the market persistently rates a team or starter differently, the results do not side with it on average. **Not adopted; also keeps our model free of market inputs.**

columns.Attempt: Our total runs against the market's total (2026, 1,000-world replay, DraftKings closing totals from ESPN summaries)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Mean total: ours 8.89, market line 8.40, actual 8.95. Correlation with actual totals: ours 0.12, market line 0.21. Regressing actual on both: ours -0.15, line 0.96. P(over the line) from our distribution: Brier 0.2552, worse than a coin (0.25); the market's price 0.2498. Our park means are compressed (spread across parks 0.47 runs against 0.74 for the line and 0.96 actual; Sacramento 9.3 against 10.1 and 11.8 actual) and flat by month (the line rises with summer heat). **Totals are the clear gap; see TOTALS-02 and ENV-01.**

columns.Attempt: Totals and run lines kept with the moneylines: SBR dataset 2021 to 2025 (DraftKings totals on 11,241 games, run lines on 11,272; run 37697029392) and ESPN 2026 (total and both prices on all 2,457 games). The live capture now also stores the total's prices (p_over)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Data for the totals work.

columns.Attempt: Game conditions for 2021 to 2026 from MLB's public schedule (tools/brl_game_conditions.py, workflow brl-conditions, run 37697026337): temperature, wind speed and direction, sky or roof (Dome, Roof Closed), day or night, venue, roof type, home plate umpire
columns.Disposition and evidence: 14,580 regular-season games, temperature on 14,577, wind on 14,576, umpire on 14,577. Public game information, stored in research/.

columns.Attempt: The run environment taught by the market's totals: log of the market's implied mean total (line and both prices through a negative binomial) on log of our simulated mean, weather, roof, day or night, venue and umpire, fitted on one season and scored on the other
columns.Disposition and evidence: Against the market's log mean, R squared: our simulator alone 0.45 (2026) and 0.34 (2025); with weather 0.61 and 0.52; with weather and venue 0.65 and 0.60; the umpire adds nothing. Squared error against actual totals (2026): simulator 20.04, taught 19.72, market's implied mean 19.44. P(over the line) improves from 0.2553 to 0.2523 but stays worse than a coin. The simulator's spread of totals is too wide (coefficient on its log mean 0.70 to 0.73): temperature +3% runs per 10 F, wind out +2% per 10 mph, Wrigley wind out +9 to 14% per 10 mph. **Recorded; the market's total stays the better number. The fix belongs inside the simulator (ENV-01).**

columns.Attempt: Run environment at the plate-appearance level: per outcome class, observed against the locked model's out-of-sample probability (Poisson with offset) on temperature, wind out and in (Wrigley separately), roof closed, day game, venue residual (ridge) and home plate umpire (ridge)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Log loss per PA, fitted on 2025 and scored on 2026: weather alone +0.00022 nats better, weather and venue (ridge 1,600) +0.00028; the reverse direction (2026 to 2025) +0.00014 and +0.00018. Umpires overfit at every setting. Effects per 10 F: home runs +7.4%, walks -2%; wind out per 10 mph: home runs +3%; roof closed: home runs -4.5%, extra-base hits -3.5%; day games: home runs -8%; Wrigley wind out per 10 mph: home runs +42%. About a seventh of the physics gain (RESEARCH-01). **Built as brl_live/environment.py (weather and venue, centered, climate fallback), off until the replay check ENV-03.**

columns.Attempt: The run environment in the simulator, checked on full replays at 1,000 worlds per game (same seeds as the reference replays): 2026 with the table fitted on 2025 (v1, general wind terms included; run 37698236039) and 2025 with the v2 table (no general wind terms) fitted on 2026 (run 37699857535)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Win chance (simulator Brier): 2026 0.24431 to 0.24405 (-0.00026 [-0.00089, +0.00036]); 2025 0.24458 to 0.24420 (-0.00039 [-0.00093, +0.00017]). Total runs, squared error against the final: 2026 20.04 to 19.84 (-0.20 [-0.47, +0.07]); 2025 20.57 to 20.31 (-0.26 [-0.46, -0.06]). Correlation of our mean total with the market's line 0.66 to 0.73 (2026) and 0.58 to 0.68 (2025). P(over the closing total): 2025 0.2546 to 0.2513 (-0.0033 [-0.0058, -0.0009]); still short of the market's 0.2497. Spread of park means 0.47 to 0.70 runs (2026; actual 0.96). **Adopted October 8 (ADJUST['environment'], table env-v2 fitted on 2025 and 2026): forecasts and in-game continuations read the official feed's weather at forecast time, with the venue's usual weather when none is posted.**

columns.Attempt: Pitch-family matchup interactions in the PA model (research set 'matchup', run 37705384736): the batter's whiff weakness on fastballs, breaking balls and offspeed beyond his overall rate and the league's family rates, weighted by tonight's pitcher's family mix (mx_whiff), and his fastball weakness times the pitcher's velocity above the league (mx_velo); shrinkage 30, 60, 150
columns.Disposition and evidence: 2026 holdout log loss against v2 (1.458583): 1.458561, 1.458562, 1.458581 (at most -0.00002 nats per PA); 2025 validation +0.00002 (worse). Family-level matchups carry nothing the batter's and pitcher's own rates do not. **Not adopted.**

columns.Attempt: Matchup program M2 (discovery/MATCHUP_PROGRAM.md): does each hitter's own swing map, read where the pitch appears to be headed at the decision moment (gravity-only projection 260 ms before the plate, the Decision Horizon result estimated on 2025 and 2026), predict his swings beyond the league map and additive terms for the hitter and the pitcher (each one's earlier swing rate, shrunk)? Feed pitches 2023-2025 only (2026 locations use another reference): league maps (location bands by count, count, pitch group, speed, both propensities) and per-hitter maps (ridge logistic on 22 location bands and two strikes, offset by the league model, at least 300 training pitches), each on the true crossing and on the decision-moment crossing; shrinkage chosen on the second half of 2024 with maps from 2023 and its first half; maps refitted on 2023-2024 and scored on every 2025 decision, paired by game. Checked on synthetic worlds first: with planted hitter-specific maps the hitter maps gain 10.2 nats per 1,000 decisions, with none -0.2
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2025: decision-moment over true crossing, league maps, 25 to 50 nats per 1,000 decisions; hitter maps over the league map on the decision-moment crossing, 2 to 8 nats per 1,000 with the interval excluding zero; the decision-moment crossing beats the true one for hitter maps too, by at least 20. Decision rule: if hitter maps on the decision-moment crossing gain at least 2 nats per 1,000 with the interval excluding zero, they become the swing part of the pitch-level matchup engine (with whiffs from CONTACT-01 and called strikes), whose plate-appearance predictions are then tested against the simulator's model; below that, hitter-specific swing maps carry nothing a matchup model can use and the engine takes swing decisions from the league map. Results (run 37876160597, every 2025 swing-or-take decision, 87.7% by hitters with a map): log loss per decision, league map 0.50187 on the true crossing and 0.46899 at the decision moment; hitter maps 0.49373 and 0.45721 (shrinkage 10 chosen on held-out 2024 in both). Gains in nats per 1,000 decisions: decision moment over true crossing, league maps +32.9 [31.9, 33.8]; hitter maps over the league map +8.1 [7.8, 8.5] on the true crossing and **+11.8 [11.4, 12.2] at the decision moment**; hitter maps at the decision moment over the standard hitter heat map on the true crossing **+36.5 [35.5, 37.5]**. Matchups: 5,440 hitter-pitcher pairs with at least 10 pitches outside the zone in 2025 (70,618 pitches): the hitter-map model's predicted chase deviation from the additive model (SD 3.3 points across pairs) predicts the observed deviation with slope **0.98 [0.88, 1.09]** (correlation 0.25 against pair outcomes whose spread, 12.6 points, is mostly sampling noise). Every prediction held in direction; the hitter-map gain at the decision moment (11.8) is above the predicted 2 to 8. **Passes its rule: hitter decision-moment maps become the swing part of the matchup engine.** Reading: each hitter's swing decisions are sharper, and more his own, when read at the moment he commits than at the plate (the per-hitter gain is 45% larger there), and what a specific pitcher's arsenal looks like at that moment predicts how often that hitter chases it, calibrated, a year ahead. Before any claim leaves the lab: one scoring on the untouched set (2026 from August 1) once the 2026 location reference is settled (DATA-02).

MATCHUP-01.status: +36.5 nats/1000 over standard hitter maps; pair slope 0.98

columns.Attempt: Catcher effect (framing and game-calling) on outcomes beyond the pitcher and batter: per catcher (fielder_2), log of observed over the locked model's predicted rates per class over the PAs he caught, estimated on April to June 2026 with shrinkage, applied to July to September
columns.Disposition and evidence: All classes: worse at every shrinkage (-0.0018 to -0.00005 nats per PA); strikeouts and walks only: -0.00036 to +0.00007. No catcher signal that carries forward within a season once the pitcher is known. **Not adopted.**

columns.Attempt: Several sportsbooks instead of one. ESPN carries only DraftKings for MLB (books probe). SportsBookReview's public odds pages list eight books (bet365, BetMGM, BetRivers, Caesars, DraftKings, Fanatics, FanDuel, Hard Rock); 2026 backfilled by date (brl-market-books, run 37708481181: 2,287 games, 7.96 books on average) and read live once per run (brl_live/market_books.py)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Closing lines: the average of the books beat DraftKings alone in 2022 (-0.00054), 2023 (-0.00040), 2024 (-0.00111) and 2025 (-0.00013) on the SBR dataset (2021 is unusable: its DraftKings 'current' lines look like they were taken after the games); in 2026 the two are equal at the close (0.24338 both). At the open the average is better in 2026 (0.24365 against 0.24396). **Adopted: the market reference is the several-books average when at least three books are read, DraftKings otherwise; the live capture keeps both.**

columns.Attempt: Our model taught again on simulations with the run environment (replays v2-env2 for both seasons)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Taught on 2025, scored on 2026: 0.24354 (2.59% better than a coin) against the equal blend's 0.24370 and the closing line's 0.24326 (gap +0.00028, was +0.00044 without the environment); taught on 2026, scored on 2025: 0.24228 against the closing line's 0.24235, our model alone ahead of the close in 2025. The coefficients barely move (x_sim 0.517, starters -1.10/+1.17, ratings about 1). **Adopted as taught-v3.**

columns.Attempt: Headline weights with the environment-taught model
columns.Disposition and evidence: Fixed market weight, each season with our model taught on the other: 2025 best at 0.5 to 0.6 (0.6: 0.24177 against 0.24235, -0.00058 [-0.00135, +0.00019]); 2026 best at 0.6 (0.24311 against 0.24326, -0.00014 [-0.00065, +0.00037]); 0.7 is within 0.0001 in both. Maximum likelihood on 2026: market 0.63, ours 0.40. **Adopted: 60% market, 40% our model (taught-v3 replaces taught-v2 before taught-v2 took effect; both from October 8, 10:00 UTC).** Season replays on the page: headline 2.74% (2026) and 3.25% (2025) better than a coin against the several-books close's 2.68% and 3.11%.

columns.Attempt: Pitcher workload in the PA model (research set 'workload', run 37707699774), all known before the game: pitched yesterday, three or fewer days since his last outing, pitches in his last outing and pitches over the last 14 days
columns.Disposition and evidence: Log loss per PA against v2 (1.458583 on 2026): 1.458531 (-0.00005); 2025 validation 1.458843 against 1.458891 (-0.00005). With the matchup terms as well: 1.458508 on 2026 but no better on 2025. Largest effects: a heavy 14-day load lowers walks and raises other reaches on base; a long last outing raises home runs and lowers doubles and triples. Same direction in both seasons, about a thirtieth of the physics gain. **Held for the next PA model refit, not adopted on its own.**

columns.Attempt: Where the PA model's misses concentrate (locked model, 2026 out-of-sample predictions; observed minus predicted runs per 1,000 PA with linear weights)
columns.Disposition and evidence: By batter age: 23 and under +13.6 (SE 3.3), 23-25 +4.3, 25-27 +3.5, 27-29 -4.1, 29-31 -9.3, 31-33 -15.5, 33-35 -11.4, over 35 -22.6: young hitters beat their history, older ones fall short of it. By pitcher age the mirror image (25 and under -14, batters do worse than predicted; strikeouts 0.2415 against 0.2229 predicted for pitchers 23-25). Players with 1,200+ prior PA since 2023 -9.7 for batters. The player rates are all-history counts with no time decay, and the model's coefficients were fitted in 2023-2024 when histories were short. A correction on top of the locked predictions (fitted April-June 2026, scored July-September and the reverse): staleness and age-curve terms -0.00060 and -0.00050 nats per PA. **Research set 'aging' (AgingState: years since the PA-weighted mean date of the player's history, that gap times his distance from age 27, age squared; optional time-decayed rates) runs on the production feature set; see AGE-02.**

columns.Attempt: Team-level misses of the PA model (same predictions, summed by team)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Batting teams: spread across teams 0.29 runs per game against 0.20 from noise alone, split-half correlation 0.37, correlation with the lineup's average age -0.62 (Phillies -0.75 runs per game, Dodgers -0.44; Nationals +0.40, Marlins +0.40). Fielding teams: spread 0.35 against 0.20, split-half 0.52, unrelated to pitcher age; by class, outs on balls in play (split-half 0.62) and strikeouts (0.56). Offsets from prior-date residuals (log of observed over expected, k pseudo PA toward zero), applied to the next dates, May-September 2026: fielding team alone -0.00030 to -0.00033 nats per PA at k 2,000-8,000; batting and fielding together -0.00030 to -0.00036 at k 4,000-8,000. **Built as brl_live/team_offsets.py and TeamAdjust (off); scored on the production model in the 'aging' research run and in full replays (TEAM-02).**

columns.Attempt: Does the starter's pitch count explain his removal beyond batters faced? Hazard with cumulative pitches, pitches above his usual per-PA rate, 100+ pitches, strikeouts and walks so far; fitted 2023-2024
columns.Disposition and evidence: Decision log loss 2025: 0.10380 to 0.10253 (-0.00127 [-0.00153, -0.00098]); 2026: 0.10989 to 0.10913 (-0.00076 [-0.00103, -0.00045]). The start-level expected length barely moves (correlation with batters faced 0.922 both): the batters-faced hazard already carries most of it. Simulated starter outs against real (2026 replay): 15.09 against 15.41 for home starters, 14.79 against 14.88 away, slope of real on simulated 1.10 and 1.08 (slightly compressed). **Not built into the simulator; pitch counts stay bookkeeping.**

columns.Attempt: Tilt: after a pitcher gives up hits or runs, does he do worse than the PA model expects on the next batters? (2026 out-of-sample predictions, observed minus predicted runs per 1,000 PA)
columns.Disposition and evidence: After a baserunner on the previous batter -3.1 (SE 1.8) against -1.9 otherwise; after a home run -12.5 (5.8), better not worse; by baserunners among his last three batters -5.9, +1.9, -6.2, +4.8 (6.2); by runs he had allowed in the game 0 to 4+: -3.0, -2.6, +0.3, -4.6, +10.8 (6.2), -6.4 (6.4); by baserunners and runs already in the inning, no trend. Once the base-out state, the score and the times through the order are known, the next plate appearance does not depend on how the last ones went; big innings come from runners on base and chance, which the simulator already plays out, and managers remove pitchers who are struggling (the fitted hazard). **No tilt effect to build.**

columns.Attempt: Deserve-to-win team ratings: the team model rebuilt on BaseRuns (runs a team's plate-appearance outcomes are worth, ignoring their order) instead of runs scored, prior dates only, 2025 and 2026 regular seasons

Runs scored carry information the outcome counts do not: run conversion (runs minus BaseRuns) varies by about 0.075 runs per game across teams beyond noise, with a season-to-season correlation of 0.24 to 0.38 on offense (stolen bases, base running, situational hitting are not in the seven outcomes). **Not adopted; the team model keeps actual runs. Base running and steals go into the simulator instead (it now gives every runner the same speed and has no steals).**

columns.Attempt: Decision horizon (discovery/DECISION_HORIZON_PROTOCOL.md, frozen before results; tools/brl_discovery.py): when MLB hitters stop using the ball's flight for swing decisions, from 2.8 million rebuilt pitches 2023-2026
columns.Disposition and evidence: Within-type movement surprise with pitch-type location maps: 262 ms before the plate on 2026 (tau squared 0.0664 to 0.0702), 260 ms on 2025, 259 ms on primary fastballs; same sideways and vertically (258, 264), flat from 79 to 97 mph (fixed time, not distance), every count, inning and pitch type; fit turns back by 400 ms. Type level: gravity-only projection from 225 ms explains swings 40 nats per 1,000 decisions better than the true crossing. Contact (launch angle on balls in play): bat steered until about 100 to 125 ms (assumed geometry). Pre-run rule wanted 100-250 ms: recorded as not a clean pass; all later predictions met. **Continue; next: score pitch-pair tunneling at 260 ms against 175 ms.**

columns.Attempt: Tunneling at the measured horizon and the blind-window test (runs 37738936962, 37741128823, 37740908440)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Previous-pitch separation best predicts chases at 260 ms (1.31 nats per 1,000 against 1.03 at 175 ms; head to head +0.27 [0.22, 0.32] on 526,205 pitches); whiffs get nothing from tunneling. Reviewer's rival (expectation pull) rejected: movement surprise discounted 0.413 against 0.467 predicted by a 261 ms blind window, the line out of the hand -0.043. **Tunneling and deception should be scored at about 260 ms, not 150-175.**

columns.Attempt: Lever test: within-pitcher season-to-season changes in a pitch's early separation from its usual predecessors against its chase rate (runs 37741959956, 37742304034; 2,715 pitch types)
columns.Disposition and evidence: -0.51 points of chase rate per typical change in separation at 260 ms (-0.74 to -0.27), speed, movement, zone rate and height changes held fixed; 175 ms alone -0.64; together not separable (260: -0.03 [-0.57, 0.46], 175: -0.61 [-1.20, 0.02]). **Direction supported within pitcher; timing not resolved by this design.** Next: frozen spring-2027 prospective test.

columns.Attempt: Negative control for the horizon: umpires' called strikes on 1,477,048 taken pitches through the identical instrument (run 37751569525; predictions in addendum 11), heights standardized by each batter's zone recovered from the official zone numbers
columns.Disposition and evidence: Umpires: tau squared 0.0002 on 2025 (-0.0007 to 0.0014, about 15 ms), -0.0012 on 2026; best held-out fit at the true crossing, the hitters' value 19.6 nats per 1,000 calls worse, although calls are 3.6 times sharper in location than swings. Hitters through the same code: 0.0659 and 0.0653 (257 and 256 ms). Tracking error is ruled out as the source of the horizon; umpires are not fooled by late movement. **All three predictions held.**

columns.Attempt: Pitcher-level decision-moment tunneling (run 37775965368; predictions in addendum 12): each pitcher-season's average 260 ms separation of back-to-back pitches of different types against chase above expected
columns.Disposition and evidence: Stable (odd/even days 0.91, season to season 0.82); cross-sample link to chases above expected -0.209 points per SD (-0.401 to -0.001); nothing for next season beyond this season's chase above expected (+0.06, -0.09 to 0.23; prediction failed); 260 and 175 ms indistinguishable (correlation 0.93). **Descriptive, not a forecasting number.**

columns.Attempt: Ball-strike challenges as a second decision about the same pitch (discovery/DECISION_HORIZON_PROTOCOL.md addendum 13, committed before the run; run 37836217655): every 2026 player challenge on a called pitch, by who made it, through the umpire-test instrument
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered before the run.** Predictions: batters' decisions to challenge called strikes follow where the pitch looked about 260 ms out (tau squared 0.02 to 0.06 after the method's measured attenuation, interval above zero; synthetic: 0.034 at 260 ms, 0.004 on the crossing); catchers' challenges of called balls follow the crossing (interval including zero, estimate below 0.015). Results (370,808 called pitches; 3,468 batter, 4,294 catcher and 133 pitcher challenges): batters 0.0044 (0.0009 to 0.0079), the held-out fit best at the crossing and 3.5 nats per 1,000 worse at the swing horizon's value, the size synthetic batters judging the crossing give (0.004); catchers -0.0056 (-0.0081 to -0.0032), the synthetic null's value. Prediction 1 failed, prediction 2 held in size. **Reading: the horizon is when the swing is committed, not a limit on what hitters can know: taking a pitch, the same hitters judge its crossing as well as catchers (from watching it in or from the catch; not separable here).** Overturn rates: batters 57.8%, catchers 55.3%, pitchers 39.9%.

columns.Attempt: Uses of the horizon that failed (same lane): per-hitter horizon as a scouting number; pitcher shape variability as deception; hitter learning through the order
columns.Disposition and evidence: Per-hitter: split-half 0.84, tracks chase rate (0.49), adds nothing to 2025-2026 K, BB, chase or breaking-ball whiff beyond 2023-2024 discipline numbers. Pitcher: surprise stable (0.75 year to year) but predicts walks (+0.32 pts per SD) and fewer strikes, not chases or whiffs. Familiarity: horizon 259, 263, 268 ms first to third time through, flat with pitch-type exposure. Per-hitter steering limit (run 37743322069): split-half 0.18, under the 0.2 set in advance; the apparent late steerers are power hitters whose misses leave the ball-in-play sample. **All four dropped.**

columns.Attempt: Running low on ball-strike challenges (discovery/DECISION_HORIZON_PROTOCOL.md addendum 14, committed before the run; practitioner input: hitters down to their last challenge get hesitant and the zone widens on them). Every 2026 called pitch of innings 1-9 with each team's challenges left before it (two minus its failed challenges): challenge odds with one left against two at the same location against the batter's zone, count, inning and hand, with the batter's own habit and with the other team's challenges left as a placebo; overturn rates and clear misses left standing by challenges left; swings near the edge of the zone by challenges left
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered before the run.** Predictions: batters' odds ratio 0.45 to 0.80 with the interval excluding 1; their overturn rate at least 5 points higher with one left, and more clear misses left standing; catchers 0.45 to 0.90, interval excluding 1; placebo 0.85 to 1.15 with the interval including 1; two-strike swings near the edge up with no challenge left (1.00 to 1.25) and with one left (1.00 to 1.10); in the ninth, batters challenge clear misses with one left at least as often as with two. Falsifier: batters' odds ratio at or above 0.90 or an interval including 1. Results (run 37852742097; 714,483 pitches, 3,378 batter and 4,207 catcher challenges, 200 bootstrap draws): batters 0.72 (0.66 to 0.78), with the batter's own habit 0.71 (0.65 to 0.79); catchers 0.47 (0.42 to 0.51); clear misses left standing 77.8% to 81.6% (batters) and 62.1% to 75.3% (catchers, called balls inside the zone) with one left against two; overturn rate of the challenges made 59.1% to 53.8% (batters) and 55.8% to 53.7% (catchers), lower, not higher; placebo 1.11 (1.02 to 1.22) and 1.13 (1.05 to 1.23), so a team challenges a little more when the other team is down, and the own effect is unchanged with the placebo in the model (0.71, 0.46); two-strike swings near the edge unchanged (one left 0.99, 0.93 to 1.05; none left 1.01, 0.91 to 1.13); in the ninth, clear misses challenged less with one left (batters 22.9% against 27.6%). Predictions 1 and 3 held, the falsifier did not trigger; the overturn prediction failed (the sign is reversed: teams down to one are the ones that already misjudged), the placebo interval excludes 1 (a shared game factor, which pushes the own estimate toward no effect), the swing and ninth-inning predictions failed. **Reading: running low on challenges makes a team hold back on the challenge itself, not at the plate, so more of the calls that went against it stand: batting, the zone widens on its hitters (the practitioners' point); fielding, it shrinks on its pitchers, by more; and the remaining challenges are not better aimed.**

columns.Attempt: Does the own-spot edge fade as a hitter keeps facing a pitcher (a postseason series repeats the same matchups)? ADAPT-01 found no learning of own spots within a game; this asks across games. MATCHUP-05F's representation fitted on 2023-2024; every 2025 pitch outside the zone to a hitter with a map: his swing with the full map's prediction as offset, on his plate appearances against this pitcher in earlier games of 2025 (capped at 10), their product with the own part at this pitch (log-odds; negative means its pull fades with familiarity), earlier plate appearances against him in the game, and the pitch number; game-bootstrap intervals. Checked on synthetic seasons first: with the own part fading by a quarter per meeting the product's coefficient is -0.146 [-0.167, -0.128]; with no fading +0.008 [-0.007, +0.026]
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: no material fading: the product's coefficient at or above -0.02 per earlier meeting, interval's lower end above -0.04. Decision rule: if it holds, the scouting view says the edge holds across a series; if the coefficient is below -0.02 with the interval excluding zero, aim values are discounted by the fade for repeated meetings. Results (run 37901940710; 305,771 outside pitches, 65,571 after at least one earlier meeting, mean 0.5 meetings; own part SD 0.52 log-odds): **own part times earlier meetings -0.011 per meeting [-0.026, +0.008]**; at the hitter's highest own spots the observed swing runs 0.395, 0.399 and 0.407 after 0, 1-3 and 4-9 earlier meetings against map predictions of 0.427, 0.429 and 0.436 (a constant shortfall, no growing one). **The prediction held: a hitter does not learn a pitcher's way into his own chase spots over a season's meetings.** The scouting view says the edge holds across a series.

columns.Attempt: Do hitters decide differently under pressure? Hitter maps pool every game state; if hitters press or tighten with runners in scoring position or late in close games, their swings at the same apparent spots differ from the map, and a postseason aim plan should know it. MATCHUP-05F's representation fitted on 2023-2024; every 2025 pitch to a hitter with a map joined to its plate appearance's state (plate-appearance history: outs, runners, inning, score); his swing with the full map's prediction as offset, on runners in scoring position, late and close (seventh inning on, within one run), two outs, and the own part's product with the first two, outside and inside the zone; game-bootstrap intervals. Development data. Checked on synthetic seasons first: a planted +0.30 log-odds chase with runners in scoring position comes back +0.301 [0.276, 0.316]; with nothing planted, -0.004 [-0.025, +0.011]
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) outside the zone hitters chase more with runners in scoring position than their maps say (positive, interval excluding zero); (2) the own part pulls no less under pressure (both products' intervals reach zero or lie above it). Decision rule: descriptive; the scouting view states any state where hitters' chasing departs from their maps by more than a point. Results (run 37905862764; 305,771 outside and 311,856 inside pitches, all matched; runners in scoring position on 23%, late and close 11%): **outside the zone, with runners in scoring position hitters swing +0.193 log-odds [0.167, 0.219] more than their maps say, about +2.6 points of chase; late and close +0.068 [0.026, 0.096], +0.9 points; two outs nothing.** In the zone, scoring position +0.246 [0.222, 0.262] (+3.8 points of swing), late and close nothing. The own part's pull: times scoring position +0.005 [-0.048, +0.046] outside and +0.012 inside; times late and close +0.002 [-0.065, +0.063] outside and -0.126 [-0.170, -0.067] inside. **(1) held; (2) held outside the zone, where the edge is priced, and failed in the zone late in close games.** Reading: hitters get more aggressive everywhere with runners in scoring position (a state their pooled maps miss), and their own chase spots keep their pull. The scouting view says so.
