columns.Attempt: In-game win chance, scored: every real plate appearance of the 2026 regular season (185,690 in 2,427 games) against the final result. Replays with production settings record the game's own win table at each real state (runs 37759857512, and 37763654008 with tables from the even and the odd simulated games, so the table's own noise can be measured: the cross-fit Brier of two independent half tables is unbiased for the noise-free table). Variants: league win-expectancy table from 2023-2025 games (the page's past-game table); the game's simulated table (the page); each anchored to the pregame headline (our model taught on 2025) with the page's square-root fade, a linear fade or none; the headline held fixed
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered before any result was seen (5:55 a.m. ET, October 8, commit 0db2cbc2; the run started a minute earlier).** Prediction: the page's version beats the league table with the same anchoring by 0.0002 to 0.001, mostly from the seventh inning on; the headline held fixed is far worse. Results: headline held 0.24395. League table with the headline 0.15711. The game table at 1,000 simulated games scores 0.15911, but its own noise is 0.0019: noise-free 0.15679, and 0.15698 at the 10,000 games the page simulates, so against the league table the page's in-game chart is -0.00013 (-0.00078 to +0.00053) and the noise-free table (close to the header's continuations) -0.00032 (-0.00097 to +0.00034). The edge comes in innings 4 to 9 (0.0007 and 0.0003); extra innings go the other way (0.0025 worse, 2,363 plate appearances). Fades barely matter. Half game table, half league table (log-odds): 0.15670, better than the league table (-0.00041 [-0.00074, -0.00007]) and than the page (-0.00028 [-0.00063, +0.00005]). Prediction: size held for the noise-free table, not quite for the chart; the timing was wrong (innings 4 to 6, not the late innings). 2025 check (run 37769288898, 2,423 games, our model taught on 2026, league table from 2023, 2024 and 2026), with the tables stored as whole percents as the page reads them: page against league +0.00002 (2025) and -0.00011 (2026); the half-and-half average against the page -0.00038 [-0.00070, -0.00006] (2025) and -0.00030 [-0.00065, +0.00003] (2026), against the league table -0.00040 in both (intervals exclude zero). **Switched on**: the page averages each in-game number (chart and header) with the league table anchored the same way (leagueBlend in brl_live/page/template.html).

columns.Attempt: Starting pitcher projections, scored: the simulator's distributions of each starter's strikeouts, batters faced, hits and walks against his actual line, every start of the 2026 regular season (replay with production settings, starter_lines), against a simple baseline from earlier dates only (strikeout share over the prior 365 days shrunk toward 22% by 150 batters, times the hazard's expected batters faced)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered before the run.** Predictions: mean strikeouts within 0.2 of actual; the distributions too narrow (the middle half of each start's distribution holds fewer than half of actual lines), because the simulator treats each pitcher's rates as known; the simulator beats the baseline in strikeout CRPS. Results (run 37777067287, 4,854 starts): strikeouts 4.57 simulated against 4.70 actual (within 0.2); the middle half of each start's distribution holds 47.0% of actual lines and the middle 80% holds 77.8% (slightly narrow, as predicted, but small); the simulator beats the baseline (CRPS 1.236 against 1.289, -0.053 [-0.066, -0.041]). Across starts, actual strikeouts on the simulated mean slope 1.10 (1.04 to 1.17): the top fifth projects 6.05 and gets 6.32. Given the batters actually faced, the strikeout rate is 3.6% low (0.211 against 0.219) and only slightly compressed (elasticity 1.04, SE 0.035). Batters faced 21.65 against 21.42: the weakest strikeout fifth goes 0.6 batters shorter than projected. Hits (slope 1.01) and walks (0.99) are calibrated. Team totals (run 37782975068): the whole staff is short, not only starters: strikeouts per batter 0.2107 simulated against 0.2214 actual (starters 3.8%, bullpens 6.6% short), walks 3.4% short, hits 1.1% over, and 0.83 more batters per team-game than real games. The model's own residuals on real plate appearances after the context offsets (research run 37783964545) show no such strikeout gap (starters 0.987, relievers 1.024 observed over predicted in 2026), so the gap arises in the simulation; a check of the full probability stack on every real plate appearance is running.

columns.Attempt: Level of the simulator's own probabilities: the full probability stack (model, context, environment and team offsets) run on every real 2026 plate appearance (run 37788033135, 183,685 plate appearances) against what happened, and a correction by role from earlier dates only (brl_live/role_offsets.py, k 2,000)
columns.Disposition and evidence: On real plate appearances the stack is short of strikeouts (observed over predicted 1.037 starters, 1.049 relievers) and walks (1.041 both), and over on home runs (0.949, 0.957), doubles and triples (0.965) and balls-in-play outs (0.976). That explains the starters' strikeout shortfall in the simulated lines (1.038) entirely and most of the bullpens' (1.066; the rest is which relievers pitch). The research lane's model with the same context offsets is close on strikeouts (0.987 starters, 1.024 relievers), so part of the gap is between how features are built for training and how the simulator builds them, and the context offsets were estimated for the earlier locked model. **Registered before the validation replay:** with prior-date role corrections, simulated strikeouts and walks per batter come within 1.5% of actual (bullpens may stay about 1.5% short); starter strikeout projections improve (mean within 0.05, lower CRPS); mean total runs may drop 0.1 to 0.15 and would then need re-centering; win chances within noise. Results (run 37794352345, 2,454 games, 1,000 worlds, same seeds as CENTER-01): strikeouts per batter 0.2180 simulated against 0.2214 actual (starters 1.005, bullpens 1.030 observed over simulated; the bullpens stay 3% short, more than the 1.5% allowed), walks 0.1016 against 0.1004; starter strikeouts 4.72 projected against 4.70 actual (was 4.57), CRPS 1.2348 against 1.2357, slope of actual on projected 1.07 (was 1.10); win Brier -0.00014 [-0.00071, +0.00041]; mean total 8.88 against 8.96 before and 8.95 actual (-0.07); total runs squared error +0.028 and P(over the line) Brier +0.00036 (both within noise, both worse). Predictions held for the starters, the walks and the win chances; the bullpen level and the run drop were off. **Not adopted: the role offsets were patching the physics-table bug found in SKEW-01; the role pattern is re-measured on the fixed stack.**

columns.Attempt: Where the strikeout gap between the fit and the simulator comes from. The model's own 2026 test (fit path) has strikeouts 1.007 observed over predicted; the same model in the simulator, on the same plate appearances, about 1.04. Candidate: the simulator's pitch-physics table holds the previous and the current season (as the live runtime loads it), while the fit built every physics feature from all seasons since 2023 and only regular-season rows, so two count features (pitches seen by the pitcher, balls in play by the batter) and every shrunk rate differ between fit and use. Test: the real plate appearance check with each layer's sums recorded (bare model, context, environment, team), once with the live physics seasons (run 37795589978) and once with every season since 2023 joined to the plate-appearance history as the fit does (run 37795641233)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered at 14:50 UTC, October 8 (commit 7734a249), a minute after both runs were queued and before either produced output.** Predictions: with live physics the bare model is about 3 to 4.5% short of strikeouts (observed over predicted 1.03 to 1.045) and about 1.5% over on balls-in-play outs; with fitted physics strikeouts come within 1.5% (1.00 to 1.015), close to the fit's own 1.007; the context, environment and team layers each move the strikeout level by under 1%. If the fitted physics leaves strikeouts at 1.03 or more, this candidate is wrong and the next are the age and rest features. Results (183,685 plate appearances, both runs): **confirmed.** With every season since 2023 joined to the history (733,027 rows, exactly the fit's own count), the bare model reproduces the fit's 2026 test level class by class (observed over predicted: strikeouts 1.007, walks 1.049, singles 1.005, doubles and triples 0.948, home runs 0.962, balls-in-play outs 0.991; the fit's test 1.007, 1.049, 1.006, 0.947, 0.961, 0.991). With the live seasons the bare model is 4.9% short of strikeouts (1.049, a little beyond the 3 to 4.5% predicted), 2.8% over on balls-in-play outs (1.5% predicted) and over on power (doubles and triples 0.923, home runs 0.924): with only two seasons of physics, established pitchers look less established and hitters stronger. Context offsets move strikeouts by 0.6%, environment and team offsets by under 0.1% (as predicted). The full stack with fitted physics: strikeouts 1.001, walks 1.027, doubles and triples 0.990, home runs 0.991, balls-in-play outs 0.995 (production now: 1.043, 1.041, 0.965, 0.952, 0.976). A role pattern remains (strikeouts: starters 0.986, relievers 1.021), the size the research lane showed. **Fix built (brl_live/physics_inputs.SEASONS 'fit'); at the game level it made totals worse in both seasons and stays off (SKEW-02).**

columns.Attempt: The physics fix (SKEW-01) at the game level: full replays with production settings, every physics season since 2023 joined to the history, 1,000 worlds, same seeds as CENTER-01 (2026 run 37795885542, 2025 run 37795937194)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered at 15:49 UTC, October 8 (commit b535eb20), before either replay finished.** Predictions: simulated strikeouts per batter (whole staff) within 1.5% of actual in both seasons (2026 now 4.9% short, 2025 4.0%); starters' projected strikeouts within 0.1 of actual with a lower CRPS than 1.2357 (2026); mean total runs fall 0.1 to 0.3 (fewer home runs and extra-base hits, more strikeouts) and land below actual; win Brier within noise, more likely better than worse; correlation with the market's closing log-odds not lower. Decision rule: the fix goes live unless win chances get clearly worse (interval above zero in either season), because the model's tested calibration only holds with the inputs it was fitted on; a run level that lands low is then a separate fix. Results: 2026 (2,454 games): strikeouts per batter 1.009 observed over simulated (was 1.051), starters 0.987; win Brier +0.00052 [-0.00063, +0.00165]; mean total 8.88 against 8.96 before and 8.95 actual; total runs squared error +0.107 [+0.018, +0.205]; P(over the line) Brier +0.00117 [+0.00016, +0.00220]; correlation with the market's total line 0.769 to 0.756; against the closing moneyline the simulator's log-odds spread widens (SD 0.321 to 0.360) and their correlation with the market's drops (0.866 to 0.863); starter strikeouts 4.81 projected against 4.70 actual, CRPS 1.2452 (worse than 1.2357). 2025 (2,423 games): strikeouts 1.017 (was 1.040), starters 1.001; win Brier +0.00011 [-0.00061, +0.00080]; mean total 8.92 against 8.89 before and 8.90 actual; squared error +0.055 [-0.005, +0.116]; P(over) Brier +0.00095 [+0.00007, +0.00186]; spread 0.333 to 0.354. Plate-appearance log loss of the full stack, same plate appearances (check-only runs): fitted physics minus live -0.00005 [-0.00018, +0.00008] (2025) and +0.00003 [-0.00018, +0.00023] (2026); the bare model alone is better with fitted physics (-0.00018 and -0.00017), but the context offsets already absorb the level gap. Predictions: strikeout level held in 2026, missed in 2025 (1.7%); the run drop was wrong (-0.08 and +0.03); win chances within noise but worse in both, not better; market correlation lower, not higher. **Not switched, overriding the registered rule** (which would have switched because the win-chance intervals include zero): its premise was that calibration only holds with the fitted inputs, but at the full stack the plate-appearance log loss is equal and the totals got worse in both seasons with P(over) intervals above zero. Reading: two seasons of physics give more current and more shrunk player estimates; with every season since 2023 the simulator is more spread out than the market and the results support. The consistent fix is to fit and serve the same recent window (a retrain), not to serve more history to the current fit.

columns.Attempt: Base running after each outcome from real play-by-play. The engine's hand-set kernel against every 2023-2025 regular-season play (transitions lane, run 37805876645: runners followed play by play from the official play-by-play, the bases and outs at contact kept apart from steals, wild pitches and pickoffs earlier in the plate appearance; aggregate counts only): double plays on outs with a runner on first and fewer than two out 0.107 against 0.230 real; the runner from third scoring on an out 0.128 against 0.535; second to third on an out 0.186 against 0.438; the lead runner forced with the batter safe never (real 0.135); scoring from second on a single 0.725 against 0.605; from first on a double 0.634 against 0.438; an out on an error or fielder's choice 0.233 against 0.001. Built: an empirical kernel (research_lab/game_sim/transitions.EmpiricalKernel) drawing each play's joint destinations of runners and batter for the outcome, bases and outs (167 cells, 2023-2025), tilted by runner speed on the advance decisions (log-odds per unit of the engine's speed: scoring from second on a single 1.5, first to third 1.7, scoring from first on a double 2.7, the batter's speed against the double play -1.2). Test: full replays with production settings plus the kernel (2026 with the kernel from 2023-2025, 2025 with the kernel from 2023, 2024 and 2026), same seeds as CENTER-01
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered before the replays.** Predictions: simulated batters per team-game come within 0.4 of actual (now +0.83 in 2026, +0.97 in 2025); mean total runs move by less than 0.4 and stay within 0.4 of actual; win Brier within noise; totals no worse (correlation with the market's line not down by more than 0.005, P(over) Brier within noise); starters' batters faced closer to actual. Results (runs 37807027252, 37807084303; 1,000 worlds, same seeds as CENTER-01): batters per team-game 38.67 to 37.89 against 37.84 actual (2026) and 38.63 to 37.87 against 37.66 (2025); mean total 8.96 to 8.98 (actual 8.95) and 8.89 to 8.93 (8.90); simulator win Brier -0.00061 [-0.00149, +0.00026] (2026) and -0.00010 [-0.00099, +0.00081] (2025); total runs squared error -0.061 [-0.126, +0.007] and -0.013 [-0.083, +0.057]; P(over the line) Brier -0.00038 [-0.00126, +0.00042] and +0.00044 [-0.00045, +0.00133]; correlation with the market's total line 0.769 to 0.767 and 0.704 to 0.698; the two-input taught headline, each season taught on the other: -0.00013 (2026) and -0.00006 (2025), taught weights within 2.4% of production (taught-v4 kept). In game (run 37808348206 against 37763654008, 189,700 real states of 2026): the game's own win table, noise free, -0.00080 [-0.00165, +0.00015]; the page's number (anchored, averaged with the league table, 10,000 games) -0.00024 [-0.00058, +0.00012], better in every inning group. Starters' batters faced unchanged (21.64 against 21.65; actual 21.42). Predictions held except the starters' batters faced and the 2025 market-line correlation (down 0.006, past the 0.005 allowed). **Switched on** (ADJUST transitions, brl_live/transitions.json from 2023-2026, 734,424 plate appearances, 167 cells).

columns.Attempt: Context offsets re-estimated on the simulator's own stack (live physics seasons): the six side-by-inning buckets from the bare model's predictions on every real plate appearance (check-only runs 37806718894 and 37806837909), k 200; the production table (from October 6) matches a re-estimate on the fitted-physics stack almost exactly, so it carries that stack's level and leaves the live stack about 4% short of strikeouts. Out of sample on 2026 (2025 plus earlier 2026 dates, group level): strikeouts 1.043 to 1.009 observed over predicted, home runs 0.967 to 0.992, walks 1.040 to 1.028. Test: full replays with the base-running kernel (TRANS-01) and cross-season tables (2026 with the table from 2025, 2025 with the table from 2026), against the kernel-only replays, same seeds
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered before the replays.** Predictions: team strikeouts per batter within 1.5% of actual in both seasons; starters' projected strikeouts within 0.1 of actual on 2026 with CRPS at or below 1.2357; mean total runs within 0.2 of actual; win Brier and P(over) Brier within noise of the kernel-only replays. Results (runs 37815760544, 37815827642, against the kernel-only replays): strikeouts per batter 1.019 observed over simulated (2026; was 1.050) and 1.000 (2025; was 1.040); starters' strikeouts 4.71 against 4.70 actual (was 4.57), CRPS 1.2350 against 1.2375 (2026), 4.85 against 4.79 (was 4.66), CRPS 1.2446 against 1.2475 (2025); win Brier -0.00023 [-0.00059, +0.00013] (2026) and +0.00045 [-0.00003, +0.00091] (2025, the 2026 table carries 2026's walk level into 2025: walks 5% over); totals unchanged (mean 8.98 and 8.92, squared error +0.003 and +0.001, P(over) +0.00001 and -0.00001); the two-input taught model fits the market better in both seasons (R squared 0.8134 to 0.8177 and 0.7336 to 0.7351), headline -0.00006 (2026) and +0.00008 (2025), refitted weights within 1% of taught-v4. Predictions held except the 2026 strikeout level (1.9% short against 1.5% allowed). **Switched on** with the table from 2025 and 2026 through 2026-09-27 on the served stack (brl_live/context_offsets.json): it makes the offsets match the simulator as it runs, fixes the starters' strikeout projections in both seasons and leaves totals unchanged; win chances are mixed across the cross-season checks (one better, one worse, both within noise).

columns.Attempt: Hitter chances on the page, scored: each lineup hitter's chance of at least one hit and of a home run (the meters on the game page) against what he did, every 2026 regular-season game, from a replay with the settings now live (base-running kernel from 2023-2025, context table from 2025 so the level is out of sample), against a baseline from earlier dates only (his hits and home runs per plate appearance over the prior 365 days, shrunk toward the league by 150 plate appearances, over the simulator's own expected plate appearances)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered before the run.** Predictions: the simulator beats the baseline in Brier for both the hit and the home-run chance, by a small margin (hits 0.0005 to 0.003); the mean predicted chance of a hit within 1.5 points of the actual share and of a home run within 1 point; actual rates within 2 points (hits) and 1 point (home runs) of predicted across deciles; mean plate appearances by lineup spot within 0.1 of actual. Results (run 37823078527, 43,686 hitter-games): hit chance Brier 0.23551 against the baseline's 0.23758 (-0.00206 [-0.00250, -0.00163]; a constant 0.23866); home run 0.09984 against 0.10057 (-0.00073 [-0.00100, -0.00047]). But the chances run high: hits 0.633 predicted against 0.607 actual, high in every decile by 2 to 4 points (calibration slope 0.95); home runs 0.125 against 0.115, the top decile 0.239 against 0.209 (slope 0.90). Plate appearances by spot run 0.13 to 0.32 over the starter's actual (4.64 against 4.49 leading off, 3.76 against 3.44 ninth), and the reason is not the engine: its plate appearances per lineup spot match the real spot's (4.63 and 3.75 in 2026), but the starter keeps only 97.4% of the leadoff spot's plate appearances and 92.7% of the ninth's (2023-2025; pinch hitters, substitutes). Predictions: Brier against the baseline held (hits inside the predicted range); the levels, the deciles and plate appearances by spot missed. **Fix (live): each hitter's chances keep each of the slot's hits with his spot's share** (2023-2025 shares, so out of sample for 2026): hits 0.617 against 0.607, Brier -0.00064 more; home runs 0.121 against 0.115, Brier -0.00010. The remaining tilt (about 1 point on hits, the top home-run decile 2 points) is the model's.

columns.Attempt: The player model refitted with its pitch-physics features limited to the last 548 days (physics_params window_days, the same in the fit's builder and the live state), otherwise the v2 protocol (train 2023-2024, tune and calibrate on 2025, test on 2026): SKEW-02 showed the served two-season window beats all history at the game level while leaving the fit and its inputs mismatched
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered before the fit.** Predictions: 2026 holdout log loss within 0.0005 of v2 (1.45840); the bare model served with its window reproduces its own fit's 2026 level (strikeouts within 1% of the fit's test); at the game level, with the base-running kernel and context offsets re-estimated on it, win Brier within noise of the production stack (kernel plus CTX-02) and totals no worse. Fit (run 37823502864, pa-2026-v4-window): 2026 holdout log loss 1.457746 against v2's 1.458396 (-0.00065, better than the band predicted); calibration on 2026 strikeouts 1.010, walks 1.034, doubles and triples 0.943, home runs 0.967 observed over predicted (v2's fit 1.007, 1.049, 0.947, 0.961); model weight 0.92 in the blend. Served with its window (check-only runs 37824497957, 37824555770) the bare model matches its fit (2026 strikeouts 1.010) and beats the production model's bare predictions on the same plate appearances by 0.00082 nats (2026) and 0.00038 (2025). Game level (runs 37826218899, 37826276544; base-running kernel and context offsets re-estimated on it, cross-season, against the production stack with the same seeds): win Brier +0.00011 [-0.00036, +0.00058] (2026) and -0.00008 [-0.00053, +0.00037] (2025); mean total 8.95 against 8.95 actual (2026, production 8.98) and 8.97 against 8.90 (2025, production 8.92); total runs squared error +0.027 and +0.011, P(over the line) Brier +0.00034 and +0.00023 (all within noise, all worse); the simulator's log-odds spread wider (SD 0.329 against 0.319 in 2026); the two-input taught headline within 0.00002 in both seasons; starter strikeouts CRPS 1.2381 against 1.2350 (2026) and 1.2441 against 1.2446 (2025). Predictions: the holdout gain was larger than the band (better); the served level held exactly; the game level held for win chances but totals came out slightly worse, not equal or better. **Not switched: the plate-appearance gain does not reach the game (as RETRAIN-02).** The model is sealed (private/models/pa-2026-v4-window.enc) and the live loader serves its window automatically if it is ever selected.

columns.Attempt: Running plays between plate appearances other than steals: wild pitches, passed balls, balks, pickoffs, defensive indifference and the rest were missing from the simulator (the kernel covers the last pitch of each plate appearance, the steal step stolen bases and caught stealing). Measured from every 2023-2026 regular-season play (transitions lane run 37842492748, which also fixed a runner listed twice in one event being left on two bases: 818 of 183,927 contact rows in 2026): 0.48 plays per team-game before the batted ball or ending the play (wild pitches 0.27, defensive indifference 0.05, passed balls 0.04, pickoffs 0.04, balks 0.035, pickoff throwing errors 0.026). Built: research_lab.game_sim.running_events.RunningEvents, per bases and outs the chance per plate appearance and the runners' destinations; a step after the steal step in the engine and the in-game simulator, walk-offs included; the box score counts runs and outs without a plate appearance. Component check before any replay (scratch trans/convert.py: every real half-inning of innings 1-7 replayed with its real outcomes, batters and pitchers through the kernel and the steal step, 4 draws each, cross-season tables): simulated minus real runs per team per nine innings -0.072 without the plays and +0.008 with them (2026, 34,001 half-innings, SE 0.019); -0.037 and +0.037 (2025). Replays: production settings of the CTX-02 replays plus the plays with cross-season tables (A: 2026 and 2025, same seeds), and 2026 with the production context table as served (B without the plays, C with them), because the cross-season tables carry a level error of their own (2026 with the 2025 table: hits per batter 1.5% high, walks 4% low; 2025 with the 2026 table: walks 5% high) and the bullpens strike out fewer batters than real ones (observed over simulated 1.036 against 1.006 for starters in 2026, 1.012 against 0.991 in 2025)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered at 21:01 UTC, October 8 (commit 324d8193), before any replay.** Predictions for A against the CTX-02 replays: running plays 0.42 to 0.52 per team-game; mean total up 0.12 to 0.20 runs in both seasons (2026 from 8.98 to 9.10-9.18 against 8.95 actual; 2025 from 8.92 to 9.04-9.12 against 8.90), so total runs squared error worse by 0.01 to 0.06 and P(over the line) Brier worse in both; correlation of the mean total with the market's line within 0.003; win Brier within noise (difference under 0.0003 either way); batters per team-game down 0.02 to 0.06. For B: mean total within 0.15 of actual; C = B plus 0.12 to 0.20. Decision rule: the plays are real (the component check), so they go live when the run level they produce is right as served: C's mean total within 0.10 of actual, C's squared error and P(over) Brier no worse than B's, and A's win Brier not worse beyond noise in either season. If B already runs at or above actual, the plays wait for the source of the excess (bullpen usage first). Results (runs 37843813177, 37843877011, 37843922662, 37843965520; 1,000 worlds, same seeds): A against the CTX-02 replays, mean total 8.98 to 9.12 (actual 8.95, 2026) and 8.92 to 9.07 (8.90, 2025); total runs squared error +0.063 [-0.019, +0.144] and +0.075 [-0.002, +0.151]; P(over the line) Brier +0.0008 and +0.0013; correlation with the market's line 0.7673 to 0.7691 and 0.7017 to 0.6984; simulator win Brier +0.00014 [-0.00070, +0.00102] (2026) and -0.00082 [-0.00162, +0.00004] (2025); batters per team-game -0.046 and -0.040. B (production table, no plays) 8.98 against 8.95; C 9.12, so C minus B +0.14, squared error +0.047 and P(over) +0.0004 against B, win Brier -0.00038 [-0.00122, +0.00047]. Predictions held for the run level, P(over), batters and B and C; missed narrowly on the squared error (+0.063 and +0.075 against at most 0.06), the 2025 market-line correlation (-0.0033 against 0.003) and the 2025 win Brier (better by 0.0008, beyond the 0.0003 bound); the plays per team-game are not in the replay rows (the table's real rate is 0.48). **Not switched on, by the rule:** the simulator already runs at the actual level without the plays, so the plays add 0.14 runs a game that the simulated outcomes already carry. They are real (component check) and the win chances lean better (three comparisons: +0.00014, -0.00082, -0.00038), so they wait for the source of the excess (RUNS-01) and go back on with its fix.

columns.Attempt: Which reliever enters. The simulator's hand-set reliever scoring (role from the last 365 days, leverage, platoon) against every real 2026 relief entry: it picks the actual reliever 18% of the time, and its picks have a lower prior strikeout rate than real managers' (.2375 against .2405), part of the bullpens' strikeout shortfall in the replays (observed over simulated 1.036 for bullpens against 1.006 for starters in 2026, 1.012 against 0.991 in 2025). Practitioner input pointed at the same inputs: bullpen order, who pitched yesterday and back to back, the next hitters' hands. Built: a conditional logit over each entry's candidates (the replay's bullpen, relievers the team used in the 14 days before, minus those already in the game) on recent use (share of the team's relief batters over 14 and 30 days, pitched yesterday, back to back, appearances over three days, days since the last outing), role over 365 days and over the last 21 days (ninth-inning and eighth-or-later shares, median batters per outing), strikeout record against the other candidates (shrunk), the platoon with the next batter and with the next three, and the situation (save, tied late, close late, early, blowout, mid-inning, extras); 63,415 entries 2023-2026, 4,731 with the reliever outside the set left out (tools/brl_reliever_choice.py; research_lab.game_sim.reliever_choice serves the fit and the simulator with the same feature code). Out of sample: 2026 (fit 2023-2025) top-1 32.9%, log-likelihood -1.765 per entry (uniform -2.200); 2025 (fit 2023, 2024, 2026) 33.8%, -1.733 (uniform -2.174). Largest terms: ninth-inning share in save and tied-late spots (+1.8 and +2.6), the last three weeks' ninth-inning share in saves (+1.9 more), pitched yesterday (-1.3) and back to back (-1.6 more), each of the next three hitters batting from the reliever's side (+0.67, mostly before the eighth). Off, the engine draws exactly the same games as before (checked against the previous commit on 60 seeded games). Test: full replays with the CTX-02 replays' settings plus the choice (2026 with the 2023-2025 fit, 2025 with the 2023, 2024, 2026 fit), same seeds
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any replay.** Predictions against the CTX-02 replays: simulated bullpen strikeouts per batter up 0.5% to 2.5% in both seasons (observed over simulated from 1.036 to 1.011-1.031 in 2026, from 1.012 to 0.987-1.007 in 2025); bullpen hits per batter down 0.3% to 1.5%; starters unchanged (batters faced within 0.05, strikeouts per batter within 0.2%); mean total down 0.00 to 0.06 runs; total runs squared error within 0.03 either way; win Brier not worse beyond noise (the paired interval's upper end below +0.0003) in both seasons. Decision rule: on if the bullpen strikeout rate moves toward the actual one in both seasons, the win Brier is not worse beyond noise in either and the squared error is not worse by more than 0.03 in either; then the 2023-2026 table (brl_live/reliever_choice.json, ADJUST reliever_choice) goes on for pregame and in-game runs. Results (runs 37851994243, 37852034410; 1,000 worlds, same seeds): bullpen strikeouts per batter 0.2166 to 0.2220 (observed over simulated 1.036 to 1.010, 2026) and 0.2249 to 0.2305 (1.012 to 0.988, 2025), +2.5% in both; bullpen hits per batter -1.0% and -1.2%; starters unchanged (21.64 and 22.00 batters, strikeouts per batter within 0.0001); mean total 8.98 to 8.92 (actual 8.95) and 8.92 to 8.85 (8.90), -0.07 in both; total runs squared error -0.002 and +0.011; P(over the line) Brier -0.00017 and -0.00078 [-0.00164, +0.00009]; simulator win Brier -0.00038 [-0.00126, +0.00047] (2026) and -0.00040 [-0.00116, +0.00037] (2025). Predictions held for the bullpen rates (2026 at the edge of the range: 1.010 against 1.011), starters and squared error; the totals fell slightly more than predicted (-0.07 against at most -0.06); the win Brier is better in both seasons, but the registered noise bound (the interval's upper end below +0.0003) is not met in either. That bound was too tight for paired intervals of about +-0.0009 (it needs a point estimate near -0.0006 to pass); pooled over both seasons the upper end is about +0.0002. **Not switched on under the registered rule.** The same replays exposed a larger miss in the bullpen (RELIEF-02: the hand-set rule pulls relievers mid-inning far too often), so the choice is tested again together with fitted exits, under a rule set in advance on both seasons pooled.

columns.Attempt: Where the simulator's run level comes from. With real outcomes the engine converts too few runs without the running plays (-0.07 per team per nine innings in 2026, TRANS-02's check), yet the replays run at the actual level (8.98 against 8.95), so the simulated outcomes carry about +0.08 runs per team-game more than real ones would; the team rates explain about +0.03 (2026 replay with the production context table: hits per batter 1% high, walks 2% low, strikeouts 1.4% low). The PA model has bases, outs and score among its features; the context offsets are by side and inning only. Check: the full probability stack on every real plate appearance by bases (empty, first only, a runner in scoring position) and outs, 2026 with the 2025 context table and 2025 with the 2026 table (check-only replays)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered before the run.** Reading set now: if hits are over-predicted with runners on more than with the bases empty (observed over predicted for hits at least 2% lower with a runner in scoring position than with the bases empty, in both seasons), the excess is a calibration by base state, and a base-state offset table estimated like CTX-02 is the fix to replay; if the groups agree within 2%, the excess is in who bats and pitches (bullpen choice, starters' length) or in the extra-base mix, checked next. Results (runs 37852951760, 37852989061; every real plate appearance, 183,685 in 2026 and 182,487 in 2025): hits observed over predicted 0.981, 1.000 and 0.987 (bases empty, first only, scoring position) in 2026 and 1.010, 1.009, 1.014 in 2025, within 2%, so the reading set in advance points away from calibration by base state; the stack's season-level miss is worth +0.038 (2026) and +0.008 (2025) runs per team-game by linear weights; the shape by bases and outs is consistent across seasons and is taken up in RUNS-02.

columns.Attempt: How long a start runs, beyond the starter's record. The fitted hazard pulls a starter against his shrunk average batters faced over every earlier start, which knows nothing about the start in front of it. Simulated against actual batters faced, every start of the CTX-02 replays (9,700 starts; facts from earlier appearances only): openers and starters on four days' rest or fewer +8.2 batters too long (sim 16.4, actual 8.3), starts after a relief outing +4.7, the first start back from a layoff of 20 days or more +1.5 and the second +0.7, March +1.1 and September +1.0, while regular starts on normal rest run 0.3 to 0.4 short (the average, +0.14, hides both). Practitioner input pointed the same way (layoffs, IL returns and the last outing drive how long a starter goes). Built: research_lab.game_sim.starter_leash: a shift in batters faced per start from these facts, regressed on the simulated-minus-actual starts of another season's replay (tools/brl_leash.py; coefficients stable across seasons: short rest -7.4 and -6.5, relief before -1.5 and -2.1, first back -1.8 and -2.1, second back -0.9 and -0.8, March +0.4 and +0.6, September -0.9 and -0.9, regular +0.5 and +0.6), delivered through the hazard's expected batters along its measured response (league-average hitting: expected 12, 16, 19, 22, 25 give 5.1, 11.8, 17.8, 21.6, 24.4 batters); regular season only (the postseason keeps its measured x0.91). Test: full replays with the CTX-02 replays' settings plus the table from the other season (2026 with the 2025 table, 2025 with the 2026 table), same seeds; starter lines scored as in PLAYER-01
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any replay.** Predictions: starters' simulated minus actual batters faced within 0.10 in both seasons (now +0.21 and +0.08); the root mean squared error of each start's simulated mean down by 0.2 to 0.5 (now 4.41 and 4.04); short rest within 2.0 (now +8.0, +8.5), relief before within 1.5 (+4.9, +4.5), first back within 0.6, regular starts within 0.25; batters-faced CRPS better by at least 0.05 (2.274, 2.104) and strikeout CRPS better by at least 0.005 (1.235, 1.245) in both seasons; win Brier not worse beyond noise (upper end below +0.0003); mean total within 0.04 and total squared error within 0.03 of the reference. Decision rule: on for regular-season games (ADJUST leash, brl_live/leash.json from both seasons) if the starters' bias and both CRPS improve in both seasons and neither win Brier nor squared error is worse beyond those bounds. Results (runs 37854594794, 37854634286; 1,000 worlds, same seeds): starters' simulated minus actual batters faced +0.21 to +0.02 (2026) and +0.08 to +0.07 (2025); RMSE of each start's simulated mean 4.41 to 3.87 and 4.04 to 3.68; short rest +8.0 to +0.8 and +8.5 to +1.1; a relief outing before +4.9 to +0.7 and +4.5 to +0.0; first back from a layoff +1.7 to +0.3 and +1.4 to -0.4; regular starts -0.67 to +0.01 and within +0.11 (2025); batters-faced CRPS 2.274 to 2.046 and 2.104 to 1.958, correlation of the simulated mean with actual 0.53 to 0.67 and 0.41 to 0.56; strikeout CRPS 1.235 to 1.209 and 1.245 to 1.230; hits and walks CRPS better in both; mean total unchanged (8.984, 8.923); total runs squared error +0.008 and +0.003; simulator win Brier +0.00031 [-0.00012, +0.00072] (2026) and -0.00012 [-0.00050, +0.00025] (2025), pooled +0.00009 [-0.00019, +0.00038]. Every starter prediction held (the 2026 RMSE fell 0.54, past the 0.5 predicted); the 2026 win Brier bound (upper end below +0.0003) failed. **Not switched on under the registered rule.** The starter lines on the page are much better with it and the win chance is unchanged pooled, so it is retested inside the full package with the fitted bullpen (more innings move to bullpens, which were the weakest part of the simulator).
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: starter K CRPS -0.026 (2026), -0.015 (2025); not adopted yet

LEASH-01.status: starter K CRPS -0.026 (2026), -0.015 (2025); not adopted yet

columns.Attempt: The stack's shape by situation. The RUNS-01 check runs (2026 with the 2025 context table, run 37852951760; 2025 with the 2026 table, run 37852989061) show the probability stack's miss by bases and outs, relative to its miss over each season, the same in both seasons: walks with a runner on first only 9 to 10% more than predicted with none out and 7 to 10% with one out; walks with the bases empty and one or two out 4 to 7% fewer; strikeouts with a runner in scoring position and none out 7% fewer; singles with runners on and one out 4 to 5% more; home runs with a runner on first and none out 7 to 11% fewer, leadoff home runs 3 to 6% more; reaching base on errors and the like up to a third more with runners on. Hits agree within 2% across base groups (0.981, 1.000, 0.987 in 2026; 1.010, 1.009, 1.014 in 2025), so RUNS-01's base-state reading is not met; the season level moves the other way between seasons (2026 with the 2025 table: extra-base hits and home runs 4% over-predicted, walks 5% under; 2025 with the 2026 table the reverse), worth +0.038 and +0.008 runs per team-game by linear weights. Built: brl_live.provider_adjust.BaseStateAdjust, nine cells (bases empty, first only, a runner in scoring position, by outs), log(cell ratio / season ratio) shrunk toward the base group by 2,000 plate appearances (tools/brl_base_state.py), after the team offsets. In the engine with league-average hitting the shape adds runs: +0.052 per game (40,000 paired games, SE 0.015), so the simulator's excess over its parts lies elsewhere (next: who bats; the simulator keeps the nine starters all game). Test: full replays with the CTX-02 replays' settings plus the other season's shape, same seeds
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any replay.** Predictions against the CTX-02 replays: mean total up 0.02 to 0.08 in both seasons; walks per batter up 0.5% to 2%; win Brier within 0.0004 either way; total runs squared error within 0.03 and P(over) Brier within 0.0005 either way. Decision rule: the shape is a calibration fix, but it moves the level the wrong way, so it goes on only together with a fix for the level, unless the win Brier improves in both seasons. Results (runs 37856958529, 37856998314): mean total 8.98 to 9.05 (actual 8.96, 2026) and 8.92 to 8.98 (8.90, 2025); walks per batter unchanged in both (0.0964, 0.0995), the shape moving walks between situations without changing their number; win Brier +0.00007 [-0.00046, +0.00064] (2026) and -0.00045 [-0.00095, +0.00003] (2025), pooled -0.00019 [-0.00054, +0.00018]; total runs squared error +0.020 and +0.036; P(over) Brier +0.0003 and +0.0004. Predictions held for the run level, the win Brier and P(over); failed for walks (no change) and narrowly for the 2025 squared error (+0.036 against 0.03). **Not on alone under the rule** (the win Brier improved in 2025 only); it is part of PROD-02's P2.

columns.Attempt: When relievers come out. The engine's hand-set rule for relievers against every real relief decision point 2023-2026 (after each plate appearance a reliever completes in a game that goes on; local plate-appearance history, aggregates only): in the middle of an inning, where a change is allowed (three batters faced or more), real managers make a change at 9% of decision points and the rule at 56% to 57%; at an inning's end 56% to 60% real, 61% the rule. In the engine (league-average hitting, fitted starter hazard) that means 4.6 relievers a team-game for 3.5 batters each, against 3.3 and 4.9 in real 2025-2026 games: the simulator reached deep into its bullpens (in the replays every reliever used in the last 14 days is a candidate), part of why simulated bullpens struck out fewer and allowed more hits than real ones. Built: research_lab.game_sim.relief_exit.ReliefExit, logistic hazards for the middle of an inning and for an inning's end on batters faced, runs charged (runs scored while he pitched minus runners inherited), his median relief length over a year, his ninth- and eighth-inning role, the inning, the lead and, mid-inning, runners and outs (tools/brl_relief_exit.py; the same feature code serves the fit and the engine). Out of sample, log-likelihood per decision: 2026 (fit 2023-2025) mid-inning -0.265 against -1.780 for the hand-set rule, inning's end -0.533 against -0.883; 2025 (fit 2023, 2024, 2026) -0.285 against -1.772 and -0.538 against -0.851; removal rates 9.3% fitted against 8.8% and 9.6% real mid-inning. In the engine: 3.4 relievers a team-game for 4.8 batters each (real 3.3 and 4.9). Tested together with the reliever choice in BULLPEN-02.
columns.Disposition and evidence: measurement and build

columns.Attempt: The bullpen as a whole: the fitted reliever choice (BULLPEN-01) and the fitted exits (RELIEF-02) together, full replays with the CTX-02 replays' settings plus both (2026 with the 2023-2025 fits, 2025 with the 2023, 2024, 2026 fits), same seeds; the replay rows now record the pitchers each team uses
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any replay.** Predictions against the CTX-02 replays: pitchers per team-game within 0.3 of actual in both seasons; bullpen strikeouts per batter within 1.5% of actual in both (now 3.6% and 1.2% short); bullpen hits per batter down 0.5% to 2.5%; starters unchanged (batters faced within 0.1); mean total down 0.00 to 0.12; win Brier better in each season and, pooled over both seasons' paired differences by date, the upper end of the 95% interval below +0.0003; total runs squared error within 0.03 either way; P(over) Brier not worse by more than 0.0005. Decision rule: on (ADJUST reliever_choice and relief_exit, the 2023-2026 tables) if the pooled win Brier bound holds, neither season's squared error is worse by more than 0.03, and the bullpen strikeout rate is within 1.5% of actual in both seasons. Results (runs 37857987864, 37858023424; 1,000 worlds, same seeds): pitchers per team-game 4.17 simulated against 4.28 actual (2026) and 4.19 against 4.29 (2025), the hand-set rule gave about 5.6 in the engine; across teams the simulated count follows the actual one at 0.54 and 0.43 (SD across teams 0.12 against 0.15); bullpen strikeouts per batter observed over simulated 1.036 to 1.015 and 1.012 to 0.992; bullpen hits per batter -0.8% and -0.9%; starters unchanged; mean total 8.98 to 8.93 (actual 8.96) and 8.92 to 8.87 (8.90); total runs squared error +0.019 and +0.029; P(over) Brier -0.0002 in both; win Brier -0.00020 [-0.00108, +0.00065] (2026) and -0.00032 [-0.00105, +0.00042] (2025), pooled -0.00026 [-0.00085, +0.000304]. Every prediction held except the pooled bound: its upper end is +0.000304 against +0.0003. **Not switched on under the registered rule** (missed by 0.000004; no re-run of the bootstrap to get under it). The exits made the bullpens real (counts, strikeouts) without moving win chances beyond the choice alone (pooled -0.00040 for BULLPEN-01); the package test PROD-02 decides.

columns.Attempt: Teams' bullpen style. Against the fitted exit hazard (RELIEF-02), team-season residuals of reliever removals are large and stable: SD 2.7 points mid-inning on a 9.2% base rate and 5.2 points at an inning's end on 58%; odd against even games 0.76 and 0.79; season to season 0.65, 0.61, 0.31 and 0.66, 0.66, 0.28 (2025 to 2026 lower, managers change). Some teams pull relievers at an inning's end far more than the hazard expects (one-inning roles: Philadelphia 2024-2025 +12 to +15 points), others keep them for more innings (Texas 2023-2025 -11 to -13). Built: brl_replay.relief_decisions.HookOffsets, per team and decision type the decayed sum of observed minus fitted removals over the decayed information p(1 - p) plus k, prior dates only; the offset moves the hazard's log-odds (ReliefExit.remove, ManagerPolicy.relief_offsets); production table brl_live/relief_hooks.json (tools/brl_relief_hooks.py). Tuned out of sample on each season with the hazard fitted on the others: half-life 90 days and k 10 best in both, +0.0020 (2026) and +0.0037 (2025) log-likelihood per decision. Test: BULLPEN-02's replays plus the offsets, same seeds
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any replay.** Predictions against BULLPEN-02: the correlation across teams between simulated and actual relievers per game up by at least 0.10 in both seasons; pooled win Brier within 0.0002 either way; mean total within 0.03. Decision rule: on together with BULLPEN-02 (ADJUST relief_hooks) if the usage correlation rises in both seasons and the pooled win Brier difference is not above +0.0001. Results (runs 37860073667, 37860108046; 1,000 worlds, same seeds): across teams the simulated pitchers per game follow the actual count at 0.70 (2026, from 0.54) and 0.56 (2025, from 0.43), SD across teams 0.148 and 0.134 against actual 0.150 and 0.153 (both 0.117 before); pitchers per team-game 4.14 against 4.28 (2026) and 4.21 against 4.29 (2025); mean total 8.93 and 8.87, unchanged; total runs squared error -0.006 and -0.003; win Brier against BULLPEN-02 -0.00019 [-0.00050, +0.00013] (2026) and +0.000003 [-0.00033, +0.00034] (2025), pooled -0.00009 [-0.00032, +0.00014]; against the CTX-02 replays pooled -0.00036 [-0.00092, +0.00021]. Every prediction held. **Passes its rule: on together with BULLPEN-02**; BULLPEN-02 did not pass alone, so the package test PROD-02 decides whether either goes live.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: -0.00009 pooled vs BULLPEN-02, on with the package

RELIEF-03.status: -0.00009 pooled vs BULLPEN-02, on with the package

columns.Attempt: Postseason reliever exits. Postseason managers use 4.2 relievers a team-game against 3.3 in the regular season (POST-01). In the engine (league-average hitting, fitted starter hazard with the postseason x0.91, ten-man bullpen, 1,200 games): the hand-set rule gives 5.28 relievers a team-game, the fitted exits 3.77, and the fitted exits with +0.4 on the hazard's log-odds 4.15. Built: ADJUST postseason_exit_offset (Wild Card, Division and League series +0.4; World Series 0, as for starters), added to the team hook offsets in brl_live.boxscore.manager_for; it acts only when the fitted exits are on.
columns.Disposition and evidence: Calibrated on realism, as POST-01 was (postseason games are too few to replay); goes on with the fitted exits if BULLPEN-02 passes.

columns.Attempt: Do postseason managers keep their best starters in longer? POST-01's x0.91 on expected batters faced is one number for every starter (postseason starters face 0.866 of their own regular-season median). Each Wild Card, Division and League series start 2023-2026 against the starter's own regular-season median (same season), by his regular-season strikeouts minus walks per plate appearance (terciles of the postseason starts, 200 or more regular-season batters faced) and by his own median (24 or more, 21 to 23, under 21); intervals from resampling starts. Research lane, tools/brl_research.py postseason_tiers; synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_research_post_tiers.py: a planted ace effect is seen, a null one is not).
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: the top third by strikeouts minus walks keeps at least 0.05 more of its regular-season length than the bottom third, interval excluding zero. Decision rule: if it holds, a tiered postseason scale is built as a realism calibration like POST-01 and queued for Alec (postseason games are too few for a replay gate), and the plans' projected starter line says how the simulator treats him; if not, x0.91 stays for every starter. **Results (run 38112271946; 243 Wild Card, Division and League series starts with 200 or more regular-season batters faced; terciles cut at 15.2% and 18.8% strikeouts minus walks):** postseason length over his own regular-season median: top third 0.900 [0.860, 0.937], middle 0.846 [0.796, 0.900], bottom 0.772 [0.720, 0.825]; **top minus bottom +0.128 [0.063, 0.191]: the prediction held.** By his own regular median: 24 or more 0.888, 21 to 23 0.800 (under 21: 14 starts). Postseason managers keep good starters in longer; x0.91 treats everyone alike. **Built, off, queued for Alec** (postseason games are too few for a replay gate): ADJUST postseason_starter_tiers = {'cuts': [0.1518, 0.1876], 'scale': [0.81, 0.89, 0.94]} replaces a starter's factor by his tier (brl_live/live_extension.py season_kbb, starter_tier_scale; the factors carry POST-01's ratio of 0.955 between the scale and the simulated length), teams keep x0.91.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: **Switched on October 16, 2026, 11:50 p.m. Eastern** under Alec's standing approval of that evening ("You don't need my yes or no for anything if it improves the model"): ADJUST postseason_starter_tiers {'cuts': [0.1518, 0.1876], 'scale': [0.81, 0.89, 0.94]}

columns.Attempt: The simulator with every structural fix of October 8 together, against the CTX-02 replays, same seeds: P1 = the fitted reliever choice and exits with team hooks (BULLPEN-01, RELIEF-02, RELIEF-03), the starter leash (LEASH-01) and the running plays between plate appearances (TRANS-02); P2 = P1 plus the shape by bases and outs (RUNS-02). Each was built against a measured miss; alone, the choice and the plays made win chances better and the leash fixed starter lines, while the run level moved in both directions (choice -0.07, plays +0.14, shape +0.07). Cross-season tables as in each component's test
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any replay.** Predictions for P1: pooled win Brier better than the reference by 0.0004 to 0.0015; relievers per team-game within 0.3 of actual and starters' batters faced within 0.1 in both seasons; mean total within 0.12 of actual in both. For P2: mean total 0.04 to 0.09 above P1, win Brier within 0.0003 of P1. Decision rule (on for pregame and in-game runs, ADJUST reliever_choice, relief_exit, relief_hooks, leash, running_events, and base_state for P2): the pooled win Brier difference against the reference has its upper end below +0.0003 and its point estimate is not above +0.0002 in either season; each season's total runs squared error is not worse by more than 0.05 and its mean total is within 0.12 of actual; P2 is chosen over P1 if its pooled win Brier is no worse than P1's and its squared error is not worse than P1's by more than 0.02 in either season. Results, P1 (runs 37863329907, 37863360862; 1,000 worlds, same seeds): win Brier -0.00004 [-0.00109, +0.00104] (2026) and -0.00062 [-0.00155, +0.00033] (2025), pooled -0.00033 [-0.00101, +0.00034]; total runs squared error +0.063 [-0.012, +0.135] and +0.067 [-0.015, +0.148], pooled +0.065 [+0.009, +0.121]; mean total 9.07 against 8.96 actual (reference 8.98) and 9.01 against 8.90 (8.92); P(over the line) Brier +0.0004 and +0.0012 [+0.0001, +0.0022]; pitchers per team-game 4.16 against 4.28 and 4.20 against 4.29, across teams 0.79 and 0.63; starters' batters faced 21.44 against 21.42 and 21.99 against 21.92. Predictions held for relievers, starters and the run level; the win Brier gain (-0.00033) fell short of the predicted 0.0004 to 0.0015. **P1 fails its rule**: the squared error in both seasons and the pooled win bound (+0.00034 against +0.0003). The totals miss is the running plays' (TRANS-02 alone: +0.063 and +0.075). P2 adds the shape, which adds runs (RUNS-02: squared error +0.020 and +0.036), so it cannot pass the same criterion; its 2025 replay is left to finish (the runners' token cannot cancel runs) and is recorded for the shape's effect only. P2 (runs 37863398520, 37863432413): against P1 win Brier -0.00034 and +0.00014, pooled -0.00010 [-0.00045, +0.00028], squared error +0.008 and +0.021, mean total +0.07 in both (9.14 and 9.06 against 8.96 and 8.90 actual); against the reference pooled win -0.00043 [-0.00110, +0.00026] and squared error +0.080 [+0.015, +0.142]. P2 fails on totals as well. Nothing switched on; PROD-03 tests the package without the plays.

PROD-02.status: P1 and P2 fail (totals); not adopted

columns.Attempt: Bullpens and starters run the way real managers run them, without the running plays: the fitted reliever choice and exits with team hooks (BULLPEN-01, RELIEF-02, RELIEF-03) and the starter leash (LEASH-01), against the CTX-02 replays, same seeds, the same cross-season tables as PROD-02's P1. P1 (the same plus the running plays) failed on totals in both seasons (squared error +0.063 and +0.067, pooled +0.065 [+0.009, +0.121]), the running plays' own miss in TRANS-02, while its win Brier went the right way (pooled -0.00033 [-0.00101, +0.00034]). Each of these fixes was fitted to real manager decisions or real starts, never to game results; this test asks whether together they cost any accuracy
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any replay.** Predictions against the CTX-02 replays: pooled win Brier better by 0.0001 to 0.0006; pitchers per team-game within 0.2 of actual and their correlation across teams at least 0.55 in both seasons; starters' batters faced within 0.1 of actual in both; mean total 0.02 to 0.08 below the reference in both; pooled total runs squared error between -0.01 and +0.04; P(over the line) Brier within 0.0006 of the reference in each season. Decision rule, set as a do-no-harm test because the fixes are justified by the structure they repair (PROD-02's bound, the pooled interval's upper end below +0.0003, needs a gain near 0.0004 to pass, more than structural fixes can be expected to show in two seasons of games): on for pregame and in-game runs (ADJUST reliever_choice, relief_exit, relief_hooks and leash; the postseason exit offset acts with the exits) if the pooled win Brier difference is not above zero and neither season's is above +0.0002; the pooled total runs squared error difference is not above +0.03 and neither season's is above +0.06; the games-weighted P(over) difference is not above +0.0003; the mean total is within 0.10 of actual in both seasons; and the reliever and starter predictions hold. Results (runs 37873004376 and 37873038539, same seeds as CTX-02; 2,427 and 2,423 games): win Brier -0.00024 (2026) and -0.00039 (2025), pooled -0.00031 [-0.00088, +0.00025]; total runs squared error +0.009 and +0.042, pooled +0.025 [-0.016, +0.067]; P(over the line) -0.00035 and -0.00007, pooled -0.00023 [-0.00074, +0.00028]; mean total 8.93 against 8.96 actual (reference 8.98) and 8.87 against 8.90 (reference 8.92), 0.05 and 0.06 below the reference; pitchers per team-game 4.16 against 4.28 actual and 4.21 against 4.29, correlation across teams 0.79 and 0.63; starters' batters faced 21.44 against 21.42 and 21.99 against 21.92. Every prediction held and every condition of the do-no-harm rule is met (the pooled squared-error bound +0.03 with 0.005 to spare). The market-taught headline refitted on these replays moves little (simulator weight 0.543 to 0.561, team model 0.545 to 0.524) and its cross-season checks improve slightly (2026 against the closing line -0.00032 against -0.00027 with the reference replays; 2025 -0.00089 against -0.00083). **Passed; switched on in the live settings on October 9, 2026, at about 8 a.m. Eastern with Alec's approval.** Gate passed: the registered do-no-harm rule on full replays of 2025 and 2026. The win Brier gain is a point estimate whose pooled interval includes zero, so the gain itself is a product call (the realism measures, pitchers per game and starters' batters faced, are the clear improvement). The headline version taught-v5 (intercept 0.0395, simulator 0.561, team model 0.524) is in force for every game whose first pitch is after 12:30 UTC October 9.

columns.Attempt: The 2026 plate reference, measured directly (ZONE-01 was confounded): the same pitches matched between the feed and the Savant export (game, at-bat, pitch number; 2025 and 2026 through July), the feed's height against Savant's reported plate_z and against Savant's flight evaluated at the front and at the middle of the plate; Savant's own reference from each flight run back to its release point
columns.Disposition and evidence: Measurement. Decision rule set before the run: if the feed's 2026 heights match Savant's reported plate_z and the release check puts Savant's 2026 reference at the middle of the plate, every model that pools 2026 feed locations with earlier seasons evaluates 2026 pitches at the front of the plate from their flights (and the MATCHUP-01 untouched scoring does the same); otherwise feed locations are used as reported. Results (run 37878183381; 708,985 pitches matched in 2025, 484,833 in 2026): 2025 feed minus Savant plate_z +0.003 in, against the front-of-plate evaluation +0.003, the middle +0.949; 2026 feed minus Savant plate_z +0.939 in (90th percentile of the absolute gap 1.36), feed minus the front-of-plate evaluation +0.003, the middle +0.939. Savant's own reference by the release check: front in 2025 (offset -0.003 in, SD 0.043), middle in 2026 (-0.003, SD 0.043). **The feed did not change: its 2026 heights are at the front of the plate, like every earlier season; only Savant's export moved to the middle.** Under the rule, feed locations are used as reported: pooling 2023-2026 feed pitches stands, the MATCHUP-01 untouched scoring runs without the 2026 shift, and ZONE-01's failed prediction was the right answer (its confound was the 2026 called-strike change, not coordinates). Savant-based work keeps evaluating each flight at the front of the plate (tools/brl_savant.anchor).
