columns.Attempt: Savant pitch-by-pitch data for the matchup program (discovery/MATCHUP_PROGRAM.md): every regular-season pitch of 2024 to 2026 from the public search export, one day at a time, inside Actions (experiment savant_pull): fitted flight (vx0 to az at 50 ft), plate location, ABS zone, arm angle, run value, batted ball and spray, and bat tracking on swings (bat speed, swing length, attack angle and direction, swing path tilt, intercept point). Sealed with the package key, private/savant/pitches-YEAR-PART.enc on the ledger branch; the receipt carries coverage counts and league summaries only. The 2026 postseason is not pulled yet (untouched set)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Data acquisition, no hypothesis. The receipt also settles which plate reference the export uses each season: anchoring each flight on the reported crossing, front or middle of the plate, and running it back to the reported release point (the right reference leaves the same offset every season). Results (run 37875412419): 2025 and 2026 regular seasons pulled, sealed and stored (private/savant/pitches-2025-a and -b, 2026-a and -b, 18 to 20 MB each); the 2024 pull was refused by the server (HTTP 403) after about 22 minutes, which ended the job before its receipt summaries were written. Coverage and the plate-reference check are reported by the next job that reads the stored files (CONTACT-01). 2024 is retried later with fewer parallel requests. Coverage (CONTACT-01 run 37877565820): 712,528 pitches in 2025 and 487,063 in 2026 through July; bat tracking filled on 96 to 98% of swings every month, whiffs included (attack angle on 98.7% of whiffs, contact point on 98.3%); league attack angle 9.1 degrees (SD 11.9), swing path tilt 32.2, bat speed 69.6 mph; arm angle on 99%. **Plate reference, settled per pitch**: running each flight back to its release point, the front-of-plate reference leaves no offset in 2025 (-0.003 in, SD 0.04) and the middle-of-plate one 0.94 in; in 2026 exactly the reverse (middle -0.003, front -0.94). Savant's plate_x and plate_z are measured at the front of the plate through 2025 and at the middle from 2026, as documented; the average pitch drops 0.94 inches between the two.

columns.Attempt: Pitch location across the 2026 definition change. Statcast documents that plate_x and plate_z moved from the front of the plate (through 2025) to the middle (2026) and that sz_top and sz_bot became the ABS zone. Our discovery work trains location models on 2023-2025 and tests on 2026 locations (Decision Horizon), and the player model's zone, chase and in-zone contact rates read the Statcast zone field across seasons. Test (discovery lane, experiment zone_audit, 2023-2026 feed pitches, aggregates only): for the same pitcher and pitch type in consecutive seasons (at least 50 pitches each), the change in mean height at the plate against the drop each pitch makes between the front and the middle of the plate, computed from its own rebuilt flight in a third season (a change of definition scales with how steeply the pitch arrives; a change in where pitchers aim does not); the zone field's in-zone share and called strikes by zone and height, by season
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: 2025 to 2026, the slope of the change on the computed drop between 0.7 and 1.3 with its interval excluding zero, the mean change between -0.5 and -1.2 inches, curveballs dropping at least 0.4 inches more than four-seamers; 2023 to 2024 and 2024 to 2025, slopes within -0.35 and +0.35. Decision rule: if the 2025 to 2026 prediction holds, every location model that pools 2026 with earlier seasons uses front-of-plate heights for 2026 (each pitch's measured height minus its computed drop, and the same for side), and the Decision Horizon results that tested on 2026 locations are rechecked with corrected locations; if not, the documented change is not in the feed's coordinates and pooling stands. Results (run 37874888511, 2,874,000 feed pitches, 1,057 to 1,095 pitcher-type pairs per season step): computed drop between front and middle of the plate four-seam 0.70, sinker 0.87, slider 1.14, curveball 1.44 inches. 2025 to 2026 the same pitcher-type mean height rose 0.15 inches (four-seam -0.10, curveball +0.50), slope on the computed drop -0.84 [-1.31, -0.43]; controls 2023 to 2024 +0.54 [0.00, 0.98] and 2024 to 2025 -0.38 [-0.88, +0.17], mean changes +0.19 and +0.34. **The prediction failed**: no drop of the documented size appears. But the test is confounded in exactly the season it targets: called strikes moved sharply in 2026 (taken pitches over the middle third at 1.4 to 1.6 ft called strikes 25% against 45 to 52% before, at 3.4 to 3.6 ft 33% against 40 to 49%; in zones 1 to 9 93% against 88 to 90%, outside 4.1% against 4.6 to 7.3%), so pitchers had reason to change where they aim, and the year-to-year controls swing by as much as the effect sought. Recorded as not settling the feed's reference; the release-point check in DATA-02 (no dependence on where pitchers aim) decides it. Until then no experiment pools 2026 feed locations with earlier seasons (MATCHUP-01 uses 2023 to 2025). Side result: the 2026 ABS-era zone is tighter at both edges in feed coordinates.

columns.Attempt: MATCHUP-01 scored once on the program's untouched set: every 2026 pitch from August 1 (the regular season's last two months and any postseason pitches in the feed data), never fitted, tuned or inspected by any model of the program. The frozen code is matchup_final in tools/brl_discovery.py as of commit 45576a52 (unchanged since; checked line for line): league swing maps on the true crossing and at the decision moment (gravity-only projection 260 ms out), per-hitter ridge maps with shrinkage 10 and at least 300 training pitches, all fitted on 2023-2025; 2026 feed locations used as reported (ZONE-02: the feed stayed at the front of the plate). Pairs: hitter-pitcher pairs with at least 10 pitches outside the zone in the test set
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run; one scoring, a second look needs a new registration.** Predictions on the untouched set: (a) hitter maps over the league map at the decision moment gain at least 2 nats per 1,000 decisions with the interval excluding zero (MATCHUP-01's own threshold); (b) the decision moment beats the true crossing for the league map, interval excluding zero; (c) hitter maps at the decision moment beat the standard hitter heat map on the true crossing, interval excluding zero; (d) the pair chase slope's interval includes 1 and excludes 0. The test set differs from development in ways that work against the claim: maps are seven to nine months old, and 2026 called strikes moved under the challenge system (ZONE-01), which hitters may have answered by changing what they swing at. Decision rule: if (a) and (d) hold, the decision-moment swing map is credited as a forward-tested result (a hitter's swing decisions and his chases against a specific pitcher's arsenal predicted from earlier seasons, calibrated) and can be stated outside the lab with these numbers; if (a) fails, the development result is not credited and the engine's swing part falls back to the league map plus the hitter's rate. Results (run 37881498012, frozen commit 45576a52; 226,679 untouched decisions from August 1, 2026, 81.3% by hitters with a map; maps from 2023-2025): gains in nats per 1,000 decisions: (a) hitter maps over the league map at the decision moment **+11.2 [10.4, 11.9]** (development +11.8); (b) decision moment over true crossing, league map +36.8 [35.1, 38.5] (development +32.9); (c) hitter maps at the decision moment over the standard hitter heat map on the true crossing **+40.2 [38.5, 41.8]** (development +36.5); hitter maps on the true crossing +7.8 [7.1, 8.4]. Pairs: 820 hitter-pitcher pairs with at least 10 pitches outside the zone, chase slope on the predicted pair deviation **0.95 [0.66, 1.19]**. **Every prediction held on data no model had seen, with frozen code: the result is credited.** A hitter's swing decisions, read where each pitch appears to be headed 260 ms before the plate, are predicted from earlier seasons 40 nats per 1,000 decisions better than by the standard heat map of where pitches cross the plate, the gain is larger than in development, and what a specific pitcher's arsenal looks like at that moment predicts that hitter's chases against him, calibrated (slope near 1), in the two months after the models were frozen.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: credited on untouched data: +40.2 over standard maps; pair slope 0.95

MATCHUP-01F.status: credited on untouched data: +40.2 over standard maps; pair slope 0.95

columns.Attempt: MATCHUP-01 for misses. On swings (feed 2023-2025), each hitter's own whiff function over where the pitch appeared to be headed at the decision moment, the late drop he could not see (true crossing minus that projection) and pitch family, against the league whiff model (location bands by count, family, speed, late movement, both players' earlier whiff rates shrunk, platoon); per-hitter ridge maps offset by the league model (at least 250 training swings), shrinkage chosen on held-out 2024, scored on 2025, paired by game; the same on the true crossing (with height in place of late drop) for comparison. Checked on synthetic data first: planted hitter-specific sensitivity to late drop gains 2.9 nats per 1,000 swings; with none, hitter maps cost 0.6 to 0.7 (overfitting to clear)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2025: hitter whiff maps at the decision moment gain at least 1.5 nats per 1,000 swings over the league model, interval excluding zero; at least as much as hitter maps on the true crossing. Decision rule: if the gain holds, hitter whiff maps become the miss part of the matchup engine (with MATCHUP-01's swing maps), and their pair effects are tested on strikeouts as in MATCHUP-02; if not, misses in the engine come from the league model and the hitter's whiff rate. Results (run 37877789480; 336,383 swings of 2025, whiff rate 23.2%, 84.6% by hitters with a map; shrinkage 30 chosen in both representations): log loss per swing, league 0.44011 on the true crossing and 0.47083 at the decision moment; hitter maps 0.43361 and 0.46716. **Hitter whiff maps add 6.5 nats per 1,000 swings [6.1, 6.9] on the true crossing and 3.7 [3.3, 4.0] at the decision moment; the decision moment is worse than the true crossing by 30.7 [29.8, 31.4] (league) and 33.6 [32.7, 34.3] (hitter maps).** The gain prediction held (3.7 against at least 1.5); the second failed (the decision moment is far worse for misses). Under the rule, hitter whiff maps join the matchup engine, on the true crossing, where they are better. Reading, after the fact and to be confirmed: a double dissociation. Whether a hitter swings follows where the pitch appears to be headed when he commits (MATCHUP-01: the decision moment wins by 32.9 per 1,000 decisions); whether he makes contact follows where it actually arrives (here the true crossing wins by 30.7 per 1,000 swings). It fits the Decision Horizon's two clocks (the swing committed about 260 ms out, the bat steered until about 110 ms). Registered next: whiffs profiled over the projection time, which should be best near the steering limit, not at the decision moment.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: whiff maps +6.5 (true crossing); decision moment -30.7 for misses

MATCHUP-03.status: whiff maps +6.5 (true crossing); decision moment -30.7 for misses

columns.Attempt: Hitter maps by pitch family at the decision moment. MATCHUP-01's maps are one surface over where the pitch appears to be headed for every pitch family; if hitters answer the same apparent location differently for a fastball and a breaking ball (some chase sliders low and away but lay off fastballs there), a map with a family part (the location bands times breaking and times offspeed, plus family levels, on top of the shared surface: 64 columns against 22) predicts better. Data, league model and protocol as MATCHUP-01 (train 2023-2024, shrinkage from 3 to 100 chosen on the second half of 2024, score 2025, paired by game); gains also by subset (fastball, breaking and offspeed pitches outside the zone; all pitches inside). Checked on synthetic seasons first: a planted hitter-specific breaking-ball shift gains 3.17 nats per 1,000 decisions [2.87, 3.44] (6.4 on breaking balls outside); with none the extra columns cost 0.66 [0.53, 0.78], so a real family effect has to clear that
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: family maps beat location maps by at least 1 nat per 1,000 decisions with the interval excluding zero, most of it on breaking and offspeed pitches outside the zone. Decision rule: if it holds, family maps replace location maps in the matchup engine and the scouting view, and the run value of aiming is re-estimated with them (development first, then a frozen scoring that says it is another look at the untouched months); if not, hitters' chase spots are shared across pitch families at this resolution. Results (run 37889588250; 2025 scored, 87.7% of decisions with a hitter map): shrinkage chosen 10 for location maps and 3 for family maps (validation log loss 0.45157 against 0.44696; location maps at 3 validate worse, 0.45191, so the gain is not lighter shrinkage). **Family maps over location maps +4.68 nats per 1,000 decisions [4.37, 4.99]**; location over league +11.74 [11.33, 12.17]; family over league +16.42 [15.84, 16.99]. By subset: fastballs outside the zone +5.31 [4.94, 5.75], breaking balls outside +3.84 [2.93, 4.71], offspeed outside +5.90 [4.65, 7.13], all pitches in the zone +4.47 [4.07, 4.90]. **The main prediction held (4.7 against at least 1, interval clear of zero, the synthetic null cost 0.66); the second part failed: the gain is spread across families and both sides of the zone edge, not concentrated on breaking and offspeed pitches outside.** Reading: one surface averages a hitter's answers to fastballs and to spin, so it misreads both; separating them helps fastballs as much as anything. Under the rule, family maps are the candidate representation: the run value of aiming is re-estimated with them (VALUE-06, development), and the maps are scored once on the untouched months (MATCHUP-04F) before the scouting view and the engine switch.

columns.Attempt: MATCHUP-04 scored once on the untouched months: the league model and both hitter maps (location only, and location by pitch family) fitted on 2023-2025 at the shrinkage MATCHUP-04 chose on its validation half (10 and 3), scored on every 2026 regular-season pitch from August 1 to September 27 (the feed table holds regular-season games only; the postseason stays untouched), paired by game; gains overall and by subset as MATCHUP-04. The untouched months have been scored before for other frozen candidates (MATCHUP-01F, VALUE-01F, VALUE-02F, TIMING-03F, DAMAGE-01F); this is the family maps' only look. Checked on synthetic seasons first (the last season relabeled as the untouched months; the run refuses without a frozen commit): a planted breaking-ball shift gains 2.04 [1.65, 2.39] (5.7 on breaking balls outside); with none the family part at the fixed light shrinkage costs 3.06 [2.82, 3.31], so a real gain has to clear that cost
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: family maps beat location maps by at least 1 nat per 1,000 decisions with the interval excluding zero (development value 4.68). Decision rule: if it holds, family maps are credited and replace location maps in the scouting view and the engine's pair parts; if not, they stay a development result and the credited location maps stand. Results (run 37890575360, frozen fdb61e9; 226,679 untouched decisions, 81.3% with a hitter map): **family maps over location maps +3.91 nats per 1,000 decisions [3.34, 4.44]**; location over league +11.16 [10.44, 11.89]; family over league +15.06 [14.12, 15.95]. Subsets: fastballs outside the zone +4.84 [4.18, 5.62], breaking balls outside +4.05 [2.46, 5.52], offspeed outside +7.04 [4.84, 9.19], in the zone +2.92 [2.23, 3.66]. **The prediction held on the untouched months: credited as registered, family maps predict swing decisions better than location maps.** What the credit does not establish: the league model has no family-by-location terms, so part of the gain can be a league-wide pattern that every hitter's family part learns (VALUE-06's placebo found such a shared part the same hour). Because of that, the switch in the scouting view and the engine waits for MATCHUP-05, which gives the league its own family-by-location part and asks what hitter-specific family parts add on top.

columns.Attempt: Hitter-specific family parts, net of a league-wide family pattern. MATCHUP-04's league model has no family-by-location terms, so each hitter's family part can learn a pattern all hitters share (VALUE-06's placebo found one). Here the league model gets the same family-by-location part as the maps (the map's location bands times breaking and times offspeed), and the question is what hitter-specific family parts add over hitter location maps, both against that league; also the league-wide pattern's own gain (league with the part over the plain league). Data and protocol as MATCHUP-04 (train 2023-2024, shrinkage chosen on the second half of 2024 from 3, 10, 30 and 100, score 2025, paired by game). Checked on synthetic seasons first: with a league-wide breaking-ball shift and no hitter-specific one, the plain league shows a false family gain of 3.85 [3.50, 4.12], which the league's own family part removes (0.20 [0.05, 0.36]; the league part gains 4.88); a hitter-specific shift is still found against that league (2.86 [2.64, 3.05]); with neither, -0.64 [-0.77, -0.51]
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: hitter family parts over hitter location maps, both against the league with its family part, at least +1 nat per 1,000 decisions with the interval excluding zero. Decision rule: if it holds, the frozen version is scored once on the untouched months (MATCHUP-05F) and, if confirmed, family maps with the league's family part replace location maps in the scouting view and the engine; if not, MATCHUP-04F's gain was mostly a league-wide family pattern: the league model takes the family part and hitter maps stay location-only. Results (run 37891547233; 2025): the league's own family part gains +4.80 nats per 1,000 decisions [4.55, 5.07] over the plain league; against that league, hitter location maps +11.68 [11.25, 12.10], and **hitter family parts over hitter location maps +2.55 [2.35, 2.75]** (shrinkage 10 for both). Subsets: fastballs outside +2.15 [1.89, 2.40], breaking balls outside +3.88 [3.32, 4.45], offspeed outside +0.52 [-0.26, +1.25], in the zone +2.63 [2.36, 2.87]. **The prediction held: hitter-specific family differences are real, about half of MATCHUP-04's +4.68 (the rest was the league-wide pattern), most of it on breaking balls outside the zone.** Under the rule the frozen version is scored once on the untouched months (MATCHUP-05F).

columns.Attempt: MATCHUP-05 scored once on the untouched months: the league with its own family part and both hitter maps fitted on 2023-2025 at MATCHUP-05's chosen shrinkage (10 and 10), every 2026 regular-season pitch from August 1 to September 27 (the feed table holds regular-season games only; the postseason stays untouched), paired by game; subsets as MATCHUP-04. Another look at the untouched months, and this candidate's only one. Checked on synthetic seasons first (last season relabeled as the untouched months; the run refuses without a frozen commit): a league-wide family pattern alone gives no hitter family gain (-0.46 [-0.67, -0.26]); hitter-specific family shifts give +3.05 [2.74, 3.31] (6.1 on breaking balls outside)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: hitter family parts over hitter location maps, both against the league with its family part, at least +1 nat per 1,000 decisions with the interval excluding zero (development +2.55). Decision rule: if it holds, credited: hitter-specific family maps, with the league's family part, replace location maps in the scouting view and the engine's pair parts; if not, the scouting view keeps location maps and only the league takes the family part. Results (run 37892797144, frozen 9f2f971; 226,679 untouched decisions, 81.3% with a hitter map): the league's own family part +4.67 nats per 1,000 [4.28, 5.08] over the plain league; against it, hitter location maps +11.20 [10.48, 11.90] and **hitter family parts over hitter location maps +2.16 [1.78, 2.52]**. Subsets: breaking balls outside +3.95 [2.78, 5.00], fastballs outside +2.10 [1.64, 2.57], offspeed outside +1.44 [0.17, 2.58], in the zone +1.78 [1.32, 2.24]. **The prediction held on the untouched months: credited.** Hitters answer a breaking ball and a fastball headed to the same apparent spot differently, each in his own way, beyond the league-wide difference; the league model takes the family part, and hitter maps with family parts replace location maps in the scouting view and the engine's pair parts.

columns.Attempt: Hitter maps by pitcher hand. A slider from a same-side pitcher breaks away from the hitter and one from the other side breaks in; the release angle changes how a pitch appears headed. If hitters answer the same apparent spot differently by the pitcher's hand, each in his own way, a map with a platoon part (the location bands times same-hand, plus its level) on top of the family map predicts better; the league model gets its own platoon-by-location part, so a league-wide platoon pattern is not counted (MATCHUP-04's lesson). MATCHUP-05's data and protocol (train 2023-2024, shrinkage chosen on the second half of 2024, score 2025, paired by game). Checked on synthetic seasons first: a planted hitter-specific platoon shift gains +3.83 [3.65, 3.99]; a league-wide one -0.28 [-0.37, -0.20] (absorbed by the league's part); none -0.27 [-0.36, -0.19]
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: the platoon part over family maps at least +1 nat per 1,000 decisions with the interval excluding zero. Decision rule: if it holds, the frozen version is scored once on the untouched months (MATCHUP-06F) and, if confirmed, the scouting maps split by pitcher hand; if not, hitters' own maps are shared across pitcher hands at this resolution. Results (run 37898968465; shrinkage 10 for both): **platoon part over family maps +0.16 nats per 1,000 [0.06, 0.25]**; on same-hand decisions alone -0.15 [-0.32, +0.02]. **The prediction failed: a hitter's own map does not change with the pitcher's hand beyond what the league's platoon pattern carries.**

columns.Attempt: Hitter maps with two strikes. Hitters widen their zone with two strikes; if each widens in his own way (some protect low, some away), a map with a two-strike part (the location bands times two strikes) on top of the family map predicts better. The league model is already split by count, so a league-wide two-strike shape is not counted. Protocol as MATCHUP-06. Checked on synthetic seasons first: a planted hitter-specific widening gains +0.58 [0.48, 0.68]; a league-wide one -0.36 [-0.44, -0.30]; none -0.24 [-0.32, -0.17]
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: the two-strike part over family maps at least +0.5 nats per 1,000 decisions with the interval excluding zero. Decision rule: if it holds, the frozen version is scored once on the untouched months (MATCHUP-07F) and, if confirmed, the scouting maps add a two-strike view; if not, hitters' two-strike shapes are not individual at this resolution. Results (run 37899171879; shrinkage 10 for both): **two-strike part over family maps +0.11 nats per 1,000 [0.04, 0.20]**; on two-strike decisions alone +0.35 [0.11, 0.55]. **The prediction failed (below +0.5): hitters' own two-strike shapes are real but small**; the scouting maps keep one map per family. With MATCHUP-06, the hitter-specific structure at this resolution is location by pitch family; hand and count add little.

columns.Attempt: Are a hitter's own chase spots a trait? MATCHUP-05F's family maps, own part (minus the same-side mean map), fitted separately on 2023-2024 and on 2025, and on the odd and even games of 2025; each read on the scouting grid (7 by 7 cells, three families, first pitch); per hitter, the correlation between periods; the 2025 split-half correlation (stepped up to a full season) bounds what one season's map can repeat; the ratio is the trait share. Development data. Checked on synthetic seasons first: with stable hitter shifts the trait share is 0.94 (all cells) and 0.96 (outside); with shifts redrawn each season, -0.17 and -0.23
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: on cells outside the zone the trait share is at least 0.6 and the 2025 split-half median at least 0.3. Decision rule: descriptive; at 0.6 or more the scouting view describes own chase spots as stable traits, under 0.3 it warns they are season-specific. Results (run 37900836285; 398 hitters with maps in both periods, 368 in both 2025 halves): between 2023-2024 and 2025 the own part correlates at a median 0.66 on cells outside the zone (quartiles 0.41 and 0.82) and 0.61 on all cells; the 2025 split halves 0.62 and 0.59; **trait share 0.86 outside the zone and 0.82 overall. The prediction held: a hitter's own chase spots are mostly a lasting trait**, about as repeatable across seasons as within one.

columns.Attempt: Forward in time: the credited swing representation scored on pitches nobody had thrown when it was frozen, every pitch from October 9, 2026 (the rest of the postseason). Code frozen in the commit that adds this row; trained on everything before October 9. Re-frozen at about 3:40 a.m. October 9, still before any of its pitches existed: the first frozen commit (acc61517) built the pitch table from regular-season games only and could not score the postseason; the re-frozen code adds the postseason rounds when the run asks for them (game_types R, F, D, L, W), and nothing else changed. (a) matchup_final with forward_from 2026-10-09: hitter maps at the decision moment against hitter maps on the true crossing (MATCHUP-01F's comparison); (b) matchup_family with the league family part and forward_from 2026-10-09: hitter family parts over location maps (MATCHUP-05F's comparison). Runs after the World Series; any earlier run is an interim look, labeled so, and does not decide. Checked on synthetic seasons first: the forward mode reproduces planted effects (family parts +3.25 [2.61, 3.83]; decision moment over true crossing, hitter maps, +33.3 [31.7, 34.8])
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any of its pitches existed.** Predictions: (a) decision-moment hitter maps beat true-crossing hitter maps by at least 15 nats per 1,000 decisions with the interval excluding zero; (b) family parts over location maps positive (point estimate; one postseason is too small to expect its interval to clear zero). Decision rule: if (a) holds, the decision-moment representation is confirmed forward in time; if (a) fails, MATCHUP-01F's credit is questioned and the scouting view says so.

columns.Attempt: Can a hitter answer a breaking ball differently from a fastball only when he can tell them apart early? MATCHUP-05F found hitter-specific family parts at the decision moment. If the cue is the release, those parts should matter more against pitchers whose breaking balls leave from a different point than their fastballs and less against pitchers who hide them. Each pitcher's separation between his fastballs (groups 0-2) and breaking balls (3-4) at release (x0 and z0 at 50 ft, and extension), in units of his own within-family scatter (training pitches 2023-2024, at least 60 of each); MATCHUP-05's models (league with its family part, development, 2025 scored); the family parts' gain over location maps by thirds of the pitcher's separation, and the difference between the separated and tight thirds, paired by game. Checked on synthetic seasons first: with family answers planted only when releases separate, separated minus tight +1.81 nats per 1,000 [1.46, 2.18]; with answers regardless of release, -0.38 [-0.76, +0.04]
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: the family parts' gain against the separated third exceeds the tight third by at least 0.5 nats per 1,000 decisions with the interval excluding zero. Decision rule: if it holds, release concealment (the separation in units of the pitcher's own scatter) becomes a pitcher scouting measure and a candidate scale on the family parts, scored once on the untouched months (PERCEPT-01F); if not, hitters' family answers do not depend on release cues at this resolution (they read the type from the flight before the decision moment). Results (run 37897866419; 801 pitchers measured, thirds cut at 0.98 and 1.50 scatter units): the family parts gain +2.66 [2.29, 3.06] against tight releases, +2.40 [2.04, 2.75] in the middle third, +2.72 [2.36, 3.11] against separated releases; **separated minus tight +0.06 [-0.52, +0.65]**; on breaking balls outside +3.49, +4.11, +4.22; the league-wide family pattern +5.06, +4.72, +4.98. **The prediction failed: hiding the breaking ball's release does not blunt a hitter's family-specific answer at the decision moment.** Reading: by 260 ms before the plate the type is readable from the flight whatever the release; PERCEPT-02 asks the same question of the flight itself (the two families' separation where they appear headed at the decision moment).

columns.Attempt: PERCEPT-01 with the plainest type cue in flight instead of the release: each pitcher's speed gap between his fastballs and breaking balls, in units of his own within-family speed scatter (a hard slider a few mph under the fastball against a curveball 15 mph under). Same models and split as PERCEPT-01 (development, 2025). No new synthetic check (PERCEPT-01's split with a different separation measure)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: the family parts' gain against the third with the largest speed gaps exceeds the third with the smallest by at least 0.5 nats per 1,000 decisions, interval excluding zero. Decision rule: if it holds, speed-gap concealment becomes a pitcher scouting measure and a candidate scale on the family parts (PERCEPT-02F on the untouched months); if not, neither release nor speed gap governs whether hitters answer types differently. Results (run 37898229237; thirds cut at 4.7 and 6.8 scatter units): family parts +2.38 [2.03, 2.72] against the smallest speed gaps, +2.55 [2.16, 2.91] middle, +2.95 [2.48, 3.37] largest; **largest minus smallest +0.58 [0.03, 1.14]**; on breaking balls outside +3.01, +4.57, +4.58; the league-wide family pattern flat (+4.98, +4.86, +4.89). **The prediction held, barely.** Reading, with its limit: hitters' own answers to breaking balls are clearer against pitchers whose breaking balls are much slower than their fastballs, as if speed were the cue; but the speed gap also separates curveballs from hard sliders, so the pitch kind may carry it rather than perception. Under the rule, PERCEPT-02F scores it once on the untouched months, with a sliders-only split reported beside it.

columns.Attempt: PERCEPT-02 scored once on the untouched months (another look at them; this candidate's only one): models fitted on 2023-2025 at MATCHUP-05's shrinkage (10 and 10), speed gaps from 2023-2025 pitches, every 2026 regular-season pitch from August 1 to September 27. Two scorings from the same frozen code: (a) the registered measure (fastballs against breaking balls, groups 3-4), which decides; (b) sliders and sweepers only (group 3), reported to see whether the pitch kind rather than the speed cue carries it
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction for (a): the family parts' gain against the largest-gap third exceeds the smallest-gap third with the interval excluding zero (development +0.58 [0.03, 1.14]; the untouched months hold about a third as many decisions, so the interval will be wider). Decision rule: if it holds, speed-gap concealment is credited as a pitcher scouting measure (how much a pitcher's breaking ball blunts hitters' type-specific answers); if not, it is not confirmed and stays a development result. Results (runs 37898561350 and 37898583663, frozen f7dba16; 226,679 untouched decisions; 965 pitchers measured): (a) family parts +2.21 [1.66, 2.80] against the smallest speed gaps, +2.81 middle, +1.64 [0.85, 2.38] largest; **largest minus smallest -0.58 [-1.49, +0.33]**; (b) sliders and sweepers only -0.20 [-1.15, +0.83]. **The prediction failed: the development difference did not hold up (it reversed sign).** With PERCEPT-01, neither the release nor the speed gap governs whether hitters answer a breaking ball differently from a fastball at the decision moment.

columns.Attempt: What changes before strikeouts and walks do. Each hitter's swing map at the decision moment refitted on each 30-day window of a season (ridge, offset by a league map fitted on 2023), read on one fixed set of 4,000 pitches outside the zone: a chase propensity free of what he was thrown. Its change in the latest window against his earlier windows of the season, next to the raw chase rate's change, as predictors of strikeouts and walks in the following window beyond his rates in the latest window and earlier in the season (feed 2023-2025; logistic models trained on 2023-2024 plate appearances, scored on 2025, paired by game). Checked on synthetic seasons first: with a planted drift in chase propensity both changes predict next-window strikeouts (about 1 nat per 1,000 plate appearances); with none, 0.00
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2025: the map-based change predicts next-window strikeouts beyond the rates (gain at least 0.2 nats per 1,000 plate appearances, interval excluding zero; coefficient positive) and walks (coefficient negative); it adds to the raw chase rate's change (interval excluding zero), since the raw rate moves with the pitches a hitter happens to see. Decision rule: if it holds, a hitter's decision-moment chase propensity, kept current by window, becomes an input to the player model's next refit and a scouting signal (whose approach is changing before his line shows it); if it adds nothing beyond the raw chase rate, the decision-moment map is a matchup tool, not an early-warning one. Results (run 37878336284; 270,377 plate appearances in 2025, 6,066 window maps): the map-based chase change has SD 1.9 points against 5.1 for the raw chase rate's change, correlation 0.65. Strikeouts: map change gain -0.002 nats per 1,000 plate appearances [-0.037, +0.034], coefficient -0.007 per point (the wrong sign); the raw change +0.024 [-0.005, +0.053]; map over raw -0.019 [-0.041, +0.003]. Walks: map change coefficient -0.012 per point (the predicted sign) but gain -0.001 [-0.045, +0.039]; map over raw +0.018 [-0.012, +0.048]. **Every prediction failed.** Under the rule the decision-moment map is a matchup tool, not an early-warning one: a month-to-month change in how a hitter chases, measured free of what he was thrown, does not tell where his strikeouts and walks go next beyond his recent rates. What changes first, if anything, has to be looked for in the swing itself (bat speed, timing) rather than in swing decisions.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: failed; maps are not an early warning

DRIFT-01.status: failed; maps are not an early warning

columns.Attempt: Where the bat aims, read from misses. MATCHUP-03 found misses follow the true crossing far better than the decision-moment projection. If the bat is steered until a later moment and no further (the Decision Horizon's second clock, 100 to 125 ms, estimated from launch angles under an assumed bat-ball geometry), misses should be best explained by the flight as it looked then. Whiffs on 2023-2025 swings (feed), one location map shared by all pitch types (as in the horizon's first run) on the gravity-only projection from tau seconds out, with pitch family, speed, two strikes, the hitter's whiff habit and platoon; fitted on 2023-2024, held-out log loss on 2025 for tau from 0 (the true crossing) to 0.26 s; bootstrap over games for the best tau. Checked on synthetic swings first: planted at 0.11 s the profile peaks at 0.11; planted at the true crossing it peaks at 0.03 and is flat to 0.05
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: the profile peaks between 0.07 and 0.15 s, its gain over the true crossing positive with the interval excluding zero, and at least 80% of bootstrap draws pick a tau in that range. Falsifiers: the best tau at 0.03 or below (the bat follows the whole flight) or at 0.18 or above (contact is set at the decision). Decision rule: if it holds, the steering limit is confirmed from misses, independently of the launch-angle estimate, and the matchup engine's miss model reads location at that moment; if the bat follows the whole flight, the engine's miss model uses the true crossing. Results (run 37879657819; 336,383 swings of 2025): whiff log loss rises monotonically as the projection moves back from the plate: against the true crossing -0.09 nats per 1,000 swings at 0.03 s, -0.27 at 0.05, -0.61 at 0.07, -1.13 at 0.09, -1.96 at 0.11, -3.20 at 0.13, -5.0 at 0.15, -9.3 at 0.18, -18.5 at 0.22, -31.6 at 0.26; the true crossing is best in every bootstrap draw. **The falsifier triggered (best tau at 0.03 or below): read as one location map, misses follow where the ball actually arrives.** Under the rule the engine's miss model uses the true crossing (as it already does). What it does not settle: a single map cannot separate where the bat aims from where the ball ends; the steering idea predicts that the movement after the steering limit (unseen by the hitter) adds to the true crossing, which is a different model (true crossing plus the late movement after tau, profiled over tau) and needs its own registration.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: falsifier triggered: misses follow the true crossing

STEER-01.status: falsifier triggered: misses follow the true crossing

columns.Attempt: Do decision-moment matchups move plate-appearance outcomes? Hitter maps and the league map at the decision moment as in MATCHUP-01 (2023-2024, shrinkage 10). For each 2025 hitter-pitcher pair, the pitcher's 2024 pitches (to the hitter's side when there are enough) are run through both: the pair's expected extra swing rate outside the zone (chase deviation) and inside it (zone-swing deviation), beyond the additive terms, all from data before 2025. Strikeouts and walks of every 2025 plate appearance on both players' earlier strikeout or walk rates (shrunk) and platoon, with and without the two deviations; game-parity cross-fitting for out-of-sample log loss, game-bootstrap intervals for the coefficients. Checked on synthetic data first: with planted hitter-specific zones the strikeout coefficient is +0.013 per point [0.007, 0.021] and the gain +0.24 nats per 1,000 plate appearances; with none, 0.005 [-0.012, 0.025] and 0.00
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2025: strikeouts rise with the chase deviation (+0.005 to +0.03 log-odds per point, interval excluding zero) and gain at least 0.1 nats per 1,000 plate appearances out of sample with the interval excluding zero; walks fall with it (interval excluding zero); the strikeout rate across chase-deviation quintiles rises beyond the base model, top against bottom by at least 0.5 points. Decision rule: if the strikeout prediction holds, a matchup layer is built for the simulator (each lineup hitter against each pitcher he may face, strikeout and walk chances moved by the fitted coefficients, from maps and arsenals of earlier seasons) and replayed with paired streams like any other change. Results (run 37877030474): 119,264 of 182,484 plate appearances in 2025 have pair features (55,084 pairs); chase deviation SD 2.6 points, zone-swing deviation 3.0. **Strikeouts: no effect** (chase coefficient -0.0037 per point [-0.0096, +0.0008], the wrong sign; gain -0.03 nats per 1,000 plate appearances [-0.07, +0.01]; across chase quintiles the observed rate, 22.6 to 19.6%, follows the base model, 23.1 to 20.3%). **Walks fall with the chase deviation**: -0.0176 per point [-0.0284, -0.0093], zone-swing deviation +0.0084 [0.0023, 0.0154], gain +0.07 [0.00, 0.14]; the top chase quintile walks 7.1% against 7.7% expected, the bottom 10.2% against 9.8%. Predictions failed for strikeouts and held for walks. **No matchup layer under the rule** (it was keyed on strikeouts). Reading: the pair-specific chasing MATCHUP-01 predicts is real and shows up where chasing acts directly (fewer balls, fewer walks); its net effect on strikeouts cancels (chased pitches end in weak contact as often as in misses, and plate appearances get shorter). Swing maps alone are too small a lever at the plate-appearance level; misses (MATCHUP-03) and contact are where a strikeout matchup effect would have to come from.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: walks -0.0176/pt; no K effect; no layer

MATCHUP-02.status: walks -0.0176/pt; no K effect; no layer

columns.Attempt: The matchup engine played pitch by pitch. For each 2025 hitter-pitcher pair (to the hitter's side), the pitcher's 2024 pitches in each count are run through the hitter's swing map at the decision moment (MATCHUP-01) and his whiff map on the true crossing (MATCHUP-03), with league models for called strikes on takes and fouls on contact (all fitted on 2023-2024); a count-by-count chain from 0-0 gives the pair's strikeout and walk chances with his maps and with the league maps. The difference is split over the 2025 plate appearances into a hitter part, a pitcher part and the pair part (what the two averages hide), and the pair part into what the chain makes of his tendencies as constants and what the shape of his maps adds against this arsenal. Outcomes of every 2025 plate appearance on both players' earlier rates and platoon, then plus the hitter and pitcher parts, then plus the pair part; game-parity cross-fitting for out-of-sample log loss, game bootstrap for coefficients. Checked on synthetic games played pitch by pitch first: the chain's league strikeout chance matches the observed rate (42.63% against 42.64%); with planted hitter weaknesses up in the zone and pitchers who live high or low, the strikeout pair part gains 0.39 nats per 1,000 plate appearances [0.21, 0.58] and its shape part has coefficient 0.060 per point [0.048, 0.078]; with hitters differing only in level, the shape part is 0.037 [-0.036, 0.102] with no gain, while the undivided deviation showed a false 0.019 [0.001, 0.039] (it carries level information the earlier rates miss), which is why the split is the test
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2025: (1) the strikeout pair part's coefficient positive with the interval excluding zero, and its shape part likewise; (2) the pair part's out-of-sample gain over the levels model positive with the interval excluding zero; (3) the pair part's coefficient at or above the calibrated 0.058 per point (1/(p(1-p)) per 100 at a 22% strikeout rate; the synthetic check ran 1.5 times calibrated, as ridge maps shrink); (4) the chain's league strikeout chance within 1.5 points of the observed rate and its walk chance within 2 points (the chain has no hit-by-pitch). Walks: the pair part's coefficient positive (MATCHUP-02 found chasing lowers walks). Decision rule: if (1) and (2) hold for strikeouts, the simulator gets a matchup layer from the engine's pair parts (strikeout and walk log-odds moved by the fitted coefficient times the pair points, maps and arsenals from earlier seasons only), replayed on 2025 and 2026 with paired streams against the production reference, then frozen and scored once on the untouched set; if only (1) holds, the effect is real but too small to move forecasts, the engine becomes a scouting view and contact quality is next; if (1) fails, strikeout matchups are additive in these maps and the program moves to batted-ball quality. Results (run 37880940236; 2025: 111,535 of 182,484 plate appearances in 50,727 pairs with maps and arsenals): the chain's league strikeout chance 23.9% against 22.2% observed (1.7 points high, prediction 4 missed by 0.2; the chain has no bunts, hit batters or catcher's interference and real counts do not run from the arsenal's mix), walks 7.6% against 9.0% (within 2). Strikeouts: SD of the engine deviation 2.1 points, hitter part 1.8, pitcher part 0.5, pair part 1.0 (shape 0.94, chain 0.24). **The pair part predicts strikeouts beyond both players' levels: coefficient +0.023 per point [0.008, 0.038], its shape part +0.021 [0.010, 0.034]**; out-of-sample gain +0.035 nats per 1,000 plate appearances [-0.018, +0.094]; the levels add nothing beyond the rates (-0.014). Walks: pair part +0.065 per point [0.039, 0.093], shape +0.069 [0.037, 0.093], gain +0.014 [-0.074, +0.085]. Across pair quintiles the observed strikeout rate runs 22.1% to 22.9% where the levels model says 22.4% at both ends; walks 8.8% to 9.9% against 9.3% at both ends. Predictions (1) and the walk sign held; (2) failed (the gain's interval includes zero); (3) failed: the coefficients are 40% (strikeouts) and 53% (walks) of calibrated, so the engine's pair deviations are about two and a half times too wide (maps tuned for pitches are noisy when summed over an arsenal). **Under the rule only (1) holds: the matchup effect is real but too small to move forecasts; no simulator layer; the engine becomes a scouting view (scaled by the fitted coefficients) and contact quality is next.** Measured on the way: what player averages hide about a specific matchup, from swing and miss maps, is a strikeout-rate SD of about 0.4 points and a walk-rate SD of about 0.35 points across pairs (pair part SD times coefficient over calibrated).
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: pair effect real (K +0.023/pt, BB +0.065/pt); too small for a layer

ENGINE-01.status: pair effect real (K +0.023/pt, BB +0.065/pt); too small for a layer

columns.Attempt: ENGINE-01 with MATCHUP-05F's swing representation (the league with its family part, hitter family maps), as MATCHUP-05F's rule requires for the engine's pair parts: a slider-heavy arsenal against a hitter who chases sliders is a pitcher-hitter interaction a location-only map cannot see. Everything else as ENGINE-01 (2025 pairs, arsenals from 2024, maps from 2023-2024, whiff maps on the true crossing, the count chain, the two-way split, cross-fitted log loss, game bootstrap). Checked on synthetic seasons first with the family option: planted pair effects give a pair coefficient of 0.082 [0.070, 0.097] and a gain of 0.70 [0.35, 1.02]; with none, 0.024 [-0.019, +0.095] and 0.01 [-0.02, +0.04]
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) the strikeout pair part's coefficient positive with the interval excluding zero; (2) the calibrated pair spread (pair SD times coefficient over the calibrated 0.058) larger than ENGINE-01's 0.40 points; (3) the pair part's out-of-sample gain positive with the interval excluding zero. Decision rule: if (1) and (3) hold, a simulator matchup layer becomes a candidate (replayed with paired streams, frozen, scored on the untouched months); if (1) and (2) hold without (3), the scouting view's matchup numbers use family maps and there is no simulator layer; if (1) fails, family maps add nothing to plate-appearance matchups. Results (run 37896232285; same 111,535 plate appearances in 50,727 pairs as ENGINE-01): strikeouts: pair part SD 1.07 points (ENGINE-01 1.00), **coefficient +0.019 per point [0.004, 0.031]** (ENGINE-01 +0.023), calibrated spread 0.35 points (ENGINE-01 0.40), out-of-sample gain +0.013 nats per 1,000 [-0.044, +0.069]; walks: pair part +0.060 [0.037, 0.088], gain +0.063 [-0.019, +0.132]. **(1) held, (2) and (3) failed: pitch-family maps do not enlarge what player averages hide about a plate-appearance matchup** (about 0.35 to 0.40 points of strikeout rate either way). No simulator layer; the scouting view keeps its pair numbers as they are (now from family maps, which change them little).
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: (1) held; (2), (3) failed: no larger pair effect

ENGINE-02.status: (1) held; (2), (3) failed: no larger pair effect

columns.Attempt: From the pitch-level discovery to the player model: do a hitter's decision-moment swing map and true-crossing whiff map, read on one standard set of pitches (40,000 from the same season, to his side, his own swing and whiff levels entering through the league models' propensity terms), project his next season's strikeouts and walks better than his own rates and raw plate-discipline numbers (chase rate, zone-swing rate, whiffs per swing, all shrunk)? Each source season's maps and league models fitted on that season only (feed, at least 600 pitches); targets every plate appearance of the next season; logistic models trained on 2023 to 2024 and scored on 2024 to 2025 and on 2025 to 2026 (through July), intervals clustered by hitter. Checked on synthetic seasons first (hitters seeing similar pitches): map and raw measures correlate 0.95 to 0.99 and the three map terms cost 0.09 to 0.21 nats per 1,000 plate appearances out of sample (fitting three hitter-level terms on 200 hitters), so a real effect has to clear that
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: the map terms gain on strikeouts with the interval excluding zero in both test pairs (a hitter's swing and miss tendencies measured free of the pitches he saw); walks reported. Decision rule: if the strikeout gain holds in both, the map measures enter the player model's batter features (a refit, then the replay gates); if not, the maps' value stays at the pitch and matchup level and the player model keeps its raw discipline numbers. Results (run 37883784534; 393, 400 and 388 hitters with maps in 2023, 2024 and 2025; 140,410 training plate appearances, 142,170 in 2025 and 97,881 in 2026 through July): the map measures correlate with the raw ones at 0.92 (chase), 0.90 (zone swing) and 0.98 (whiffs per swing). **Strikeouts: the map terms cost -0.37 nats per 1,000 plate appearances [-0.57, -0.18] (2025) and -0.49 [-0.74, -0.27] (2026)**; walks -0.03 and -0.02 (zero). **The prediction failed: under the rule the maps' value stays at the pitch and matchup level and the player model keeps its raw discipline numbers.** With DRIFT-01 (no early warning) and ENGINE-01 (pair effects about 0.4 points of strikeout rate), the pattern is consistent: the decision-moment representation predicts individual pitches far better (credited, MATCHUP-01F), but what it adds to a season's rates is already in the rates, and what it adds about a specific matchup is real and small.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: failed: maps do not improve projections

DISCIPLINE-01.status: failed: maps do not improve projections

columns.Attempt: Do pitchers already aim at a hitter's own swing map? Hitter maps at the decision moment fitted on 2023-2024 (MATCHUP-01), read on 2025. For each 2025 hitter-pitcher pair and count group (two strikes, behind, other), the hitter's extra swing chance from his map on the pitches the pitcher actually threw him, against the same pitcher's 2025 pitches to other hitters of the same side in the same count group read through this hitter's map, with this hitter's own swing level (what he would have seen if pitched like everyone else). Outside the zone, a positive difference means more pitches where he chases; inside, aiming means more pitches where he takes. Reported in points of swing chance with intervals over hitters; whether it grows with how distinct the hitter's map is against that pitcher (slope on the generic deviation); and an oracle bound (the same pitcher's best pitches for him, as many as he was thrown), which picks extremes and so only bounds the headroom from above. Checked on synthetic seasons first: with pitchers aiming low at low-chasers, outside targeting +1.64 points [1.39, 1.86] and slope +0.25; with no aiming, -0.02 [-0.05, +0.01] and inside -0.01 (a first version compared pitches at other hitters' swing levels and showed a false +0.11 inside; fixed before registering)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: outside the zone, targeting positive, 0.1 to 1.0 points, interval excluding zero (advance scouting aims a little at chase zones), and growing with the hitter's generic deviation (positive slope); inside the zone, reported. Decision rule: if outside targeting is under a quarter of the spread of hitters' generic chase deviations against the pitchers they face, most hitter-specific chase information is unexploited, and the scouting view lists each hitter's chase zones that pitchers are not reaching and the arsenals that reach them; if it is at least half, pitchers already use it and the view says so. Results (run 37884495989; 2025: 298,455 pitches outside the zone and 304,607 inside in 133,043 and 145,324 pair-count cells, 476 hitters with maps): **outside the zone, targeting -0.09 points [-0.14, -0.03]**: pitchers put slightly fewer pitches where a hitter personally chases than they put there for other hitters, against a spread of hitters' generic chase deviations of 3.65 points; slope on the generic deviation -0.01 (no aiming at more distinct hitters); inside the zone -0.02 [-0.05, +0.02]; the oracle bound 14.4 points (an upper bound only). **The prediction failed (no targeting at all)**. Under the rule (targeting under a quarter of the spread), the hitter-specific chase information in the decision-moment maps is unexploited: pitchers' locations against a hitter do not follow his own map, so the scouting view lists each hitter's chase zones and the pitchers whose arsenals reach them. Caveat: pitchers may aim at weaknesses described another way (pitch types, true-crossing heat maps), which these maps beat for predicting swings (MATCHUP-01F) but which would not show as targeting here.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: no targeting (-0.09 pts): map information unexploited

EXPLOIT-01.status: no targeting (-0.09 pts): map information unexploited

columns.Attempt: Do pitchers aim at a hitter's own whiff holes? EXPLOIT-01 found no aiming at decision-moment swing maps. Misses follow where the ball arrives (MATCHUP-03), and whiff holes are what scouting reports describe, so the league may already aim at them. Both maps as each hitter's own part (his map minus the same-side mean map of the other hitters, VALUE-08): the whiff map on the true crossing (MATCHUP-03's representation, shrinkage 30, at least 250 swings) and the swing map at the decision moment (MATCHUP-05F's). Maps from 2023-2024; for each 2025 hitter-pitcher pair, zone side and count group, the own-part deviation at the pitches thrown to him against the same pitcher's pitches to other hitters of that side read through his maps at his own levels; headroom from the best of the same pool; bootstrap over hitters. Checked on synthetic seasons first: with pitchers aiming higher at hitters who miss high, whiff targeting +0.89 points [0.76, 1.04] outside the zone (11% of the headroom) and +0.25 [0.19, 0.29] in it, chase targeting nil (-0.04 [-0.21, +0.12]); with no aiming, all nil (0.00 [-0.02, +0.02])
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: whiff targeting positive with the interval excluding zero both outside and inside the zone, using at least 5% of the headroom; chase targeting's interval includes zero on both sides (as EXPLOIT-01). Decision rule: if both hold, the league already aims at where a hitter misses but not at where he chases at the decision moment, which the scouting view states; whiff holes then cannot be priced by this natural experiment. If whiff holes are not targeted either, VALUE-12 prices the whiff own part with VALUE-08's design. Results (run 37894956341; 2025, 439 hitters with whiff maps, 476 with swing maps): **whiff holes: targeting +0.153 points [0.112, 0.193] outside the zone, 1.6% of the headroom (9.4 points); +0.091 [0.063, 0.121] in the zone, 1.3% of 7.1.** Chase spots (own part): outside -0.082 [-0.140, -0.029], -0.5% of 16.0; inside -0.021 [-0.060, +0.017]. Predictions: whiff targeting positive held, but its share of the headroom (1.3 to 1.6%) fell short of 5%; chase targeting nil held inside and failed outside (slightly negative, as EXPLOIT-01's -0.09). **Reading: pitchers lean very slightly toward a hitter's own whiff holes and very slightly away from his own chase spots; both use almost none of what is available.** Under the rule, whiff holes are close enough to untargeted for VALUE-08's design (its placebo, within-hitter and same-spot checks guard the rest): VALUE-12 prices them.

columns.Attempt: Is the edge left on the table even in October? EXPLOIT-01 found no regular-season aiming at hitters' own chase spots (-0.09 points), EXPLOIT-02 a little at whiff holes; postseason staffs prepare for one lineup with far more advance scouting. EXPLOIT-01's design with hitter maps at the decision moment fitted on the 2023-2025 regular seasons (MATCHUP-01, shrinkage 10) and targeting measured on every 2023, 2024 and 2025 postseason pitch (feed, game types F, D, L and W; development data, the 2026 postseason stays untouched). For each postseason hitter-pitcher pair, count group and zone side: the hitter's extra swing chance from his map on the pitches the pitcher threw him, against the same pitcher's pitches to other same-side hitters read through this hitter's map at his own swing level. Two comparison pools: (a) the pitcher's postseason pitches of that year to other hitters (pure targeting within October); (b) his regular-season pitches of that year to other hitters (October's pitching to this hitter against how he pitched everyone all season). columns.Attempt: What a hitter's own swing map is worth to a pitcher, in runs. Pitchers do not aim at it (EXPLOIT-01), so where a pitch falls on the hitter's map, beyond the league's map at the same spot, is as good as chance with respect to the rest of the plate appearance: a natural experiment. Every 2025 pitch to a hitter with a map (fitted on 2023-2024): d = his extra swing chance there, in points. The plate appearance's run value (linear weights of its final outcome) on d outside and inside the zone, holding the count (twelve categories), the league's swing chance at that spot and its log-odds, zone-distance bands, pitch group, both players' earlier run values and platoon fixed; game-clustered bootstrap. Placebo: d from another hitter's map of the same side. Worth of aiming: within each pitcher's own outside pitches to that side and count group, and within thirds of the league swing chance (so the spot stays as good in general), his best third for this hitter against the average, times the outside coefficient and the outside pitches per plate appearance, scaled to 6,200 plate appearances (a team's season). Checked on synthetic seasons first (strikeouts driven by chases, no aiming by pitchers): planted hitter-specific zones give -0.00031 runs per point outside [-0.00050, -0.00005], placebo +0.00003, aiming -19.6 runs per 6,200 [-32.4, -2.9]; with no hitter-specific zones +0.00009 and +2.6 [-14.7, +17.4] (one of the null placebo intervals excluded zero, -0.00063, the expected rate of chance excursions over the six intervals)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) the own-map outside coefficient negative with the interval excluding zero (a hitter does worse when pitches land where he personally chases), the placebo's interval including zero; inside reported; (2) the worth of aiming negative with the interval excluding zero, between -5 and -40 runs per 6,200 plate appearances. Decision rule: if (1) holds, the maps carry run value for pitchers, sized by (2); the estimate is frozen and scored once on the untouched set (maps from 2023-2025, the 2026 pitches from August 1) before any figure is stated outside the lab, and the scouting view carries it; if (1) fails, a hitter's chase zones do not cost him runs beyond the league's map, and the scouting value is descriptive. Results (run 37885781639; 617,627 pitches of 2025, 49.5% outside the zone; the hitter's own deviation d has SD 7.8 points outside and 7.3 inside): **outside the zone -0.000694 runs per point [-0.000901, -0.000526]**: a pitch that lands where this hitter personally chases, by 10 points more than the league, costs him 0.007 runs over the plate appearance; inside the zone +0.000826 [0.000629, 0.001037] (a strike where he swings more than the league helps him). Placebo with another hitter's map: outside -0.000124 [-0.000298, +0.000091], inside -0.000025: the effect is his own map's. Aiming: the best third of each pitcher's own outside spots for this hitter, within thirds of the league's swing chance, is 6.1 points above their average; with 1.93 outside pitches per plate appearance, **-0.0081 runs per plate appearance [-0.0106, -0.0062], -50.4 runs per 6,200 [-65.4, -38.2]**. Prediction (1) held; (2) failed by size (beyond the predicted -5 to -40). **Under the rule the estimate is frozen and scored once on the untouched set (VALUE-01F) before any figure is stated outside the lab.** Reading, with its limits: this is what perfect placement within each pitcher's own outside spots would be worth (real command scatters pitches around the aim, so a realistic share is lower), it counts outside pitches only (moving strikes to where a hitter swings less would add the inside term), and hitters could adapt once pitched this way. Even a fifth of it is about 10 runs a season, and EXPLOIT-01 says nobody is collecting it.

Decision rule: if (a) and (b) hold, it is credited: a hitter's own decision-moment chase map is worth up to that many runs a season to pitchers able to place each outside pitch at that hitter's best spots among their own, an upper bound under perfect placement, and no pitcher is collecting it (EXPLOIT-01); the scouting view states it with that bound. If (a) fails, the development estimate is not confirmed. Results (run 37886038190, frozen commit 63623e0f; 184,318 untouched pitches to hitters with maps, August 1 to September 27, 2026; d SD 8.1 points outside, 7.5 inside): **(a) outside -0.000946 runs per point [-0.00122, -0.00061]**, placebo -0.000186 [-0.000535, +0.000173]; **(c) inside +0.000384 [0.000025, 0.000843]**, placebo -0.000132; **(b) aiming: best third 6.3 points above the average of each pitcher's own outside spots, -0.0111 runs per plate appearance [-0.0143, -0.0071], -68.8 runs per 6,200 [-88.7, -44.2]**. Every prediction held: credited. Stated with its bound: a hitter's own decision-moment chase map, fitted on earlier seasons, tells a pitcher where among his own outside spots that hitter is most likely to chase, and on data no model had seen, putting pitches there cost hitters runs at a rate that, if every outside pitch could be placed at the best third of those spots, would be worth about 69 runs over a team's season (44 to 89). columns.Attempt: VALUE-01 with real command (development, 2025). Each aim point (one of the pitcher's own 2025 spots to that side and count group) is scattered by command error, a two-dimensional normal offset with SD sigma per axis (the decision-moment picture shifts with it), and the hitter's own deviation is averaged over the scatter; the pitcher takes the best third of his aim points for the hitter by that expected deviation (outside the zone the highest; inside the lowest, since there a higher deviation helps the hitter), within thirds of the league's swing chance; the gain times the run value per point (VALUE-01's regression re-estimated on the same pitches) and the pitches per plate appearance. Sigma 0, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 ft (typical misses from a catcher's target run about a foot, near 0.6 to 0.8 per axis). A pitch that scatters across the zone edge keeps the coefficient of where it was aimed. Checked on synthetic seasons first: planted, the outside gain falls from 4.9 points at sigma 0 (-19.7 runs per 6,200, matching VALUE-01's synthetic -19.6) to 2.6 at 0.9 (-10.5), outside and inside together -29.8 to -15.1; null, +6.4 to +2.4
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: at sigma 0 the outside-only value reproduces VALUE-01's -50 within 5 runs; at sigma 0.6 the outside-only value keeps 40 to 75 percent of it; outside and inside together at sigma 0.6 between -15 and -50 runs per 6,200 plate appearances. Decision rule: development measurement of the realistic edge; if outside and inside together at sigma 0.6 is beyond -10 runs (a win or more a season), the frozen version gets its own scoring on the untouched set (a second look at those months, registered as such) before it is stated outside the lab; otherwise the edge is stated as the perfect-placement bound only. Results (run 37886531947; the same 2025 pitches, coefficients -0.000694 outside and +0.000827 inside per point; 1.93 outside and 1.97 inside pitches per plate appearance): runs per 6,200 plate appearances, outside only / inside only / both: **sigma 0: -50.4 / -57.8 / -108.2; 0.3: -41.8 / -48.1 / -89.9; 0.6: -31.1 / -34.4 / -65.6; 0.9: -23.8 / -26.7 / -50.5** (gains outside 6.1, 5.0, 3.7, 2.9 points; inside -5.7, -4.8, -3.4, -2.6). Predictions: sigma 0 reproduced VALUE-01 (held); outside at 0.6 kept 62 percent (held); both at 0.6 -65.6, beyond the predicted -15 to -50 (failed by size). Under the rule (beyond -10), the frozen version gets a second look at the untouched months (VALUE-02F). Caveats carried forward: the inside coefficient on the untouched months was half its development size (VALUE-01F: +0.00038 against +0.00083), so the inside part is the less certain half; ADAPT-01 found hitters chase less at all outside pitches after being shown more tempting ones than chance, which this calculation does not net out.

The prediction held (50 to 90 percent). Checked on synthetic seasons first: with a planted breaking-ball shift the family maps' gain in points rises from 2.84 to 4.18; the placebo's intervals include zero in every world; with no family effect the family maps' larger point gains are offset by a smaller coefficient (outside -6.3 against -7.3 runs per 6,200), so lighter shrinkage does not inflate the value (that synthetic outcome effect is weak, so its run intervals include zero for both kinds of map)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) the outside value at 0.6 ft at least 10% larger than VALUE-05's -26.3 runs per 6,200 (beyond -28.9); (2) the placebo's outside coefficient interval includes zero; (3) the within-hitter coefficient's outside interval excludes zero. Decision rule: if all three hold, family maps become the aiming basis of the scouting view once MATCHUP-04F holds, and the frozen version is scored once on the untouched months (VALUE-06F, registered as another look at them); if (1) fails, family maps predict decisions better but do not add aiming value, and aiming stays on location maps; if (2) or (3) fails, the run value per point is questioned and VALUE-02F's reading is re-examined. Results (run 37890596403; 617,627 test pitches): outside -40.0 runs per 6,200 [-47.9, -32.0] (VALUE-05 -26.3), both sides -63.9 [-73.7, -53.0]; gain 4.26 points outside (3.17 with location maps); run value per point outside -0.000783 [-0.000939, -0.000627]. **Placebo: another same-side hitter's family map gives -0.000375 [-0.000522, -0.000221], about half the own map.** Within hitter, pitch group and zone side -0.000637 [-0.000801, -0.000481]. Prediction (1) held, (2) failed, (3) held. Reading: at light shrinkage every hitter's family part carries a shared family-by-location pattern the league model lacks; that shared part predicts outcomes for any hitter, and a league-wide pattern is something pitchers can and do aim at, so it is neither hitter-specific nor as good as chance. **Under the rule the run value per point is questioned: the family-map value (-40) is not usable as is.** Next: VALUE-07 re-examines VALUE-02F's reading on location maps with the placebo, the within-hitter check and a new check that one pitch's coefficient is not counting its neighbors in the plate appearance; the family version is redone against a league with its own family-by-location part.

columns.Attempt: Re-examining the run value per point (development, 2025, 0.6 ft, aiming within pitch type). A swing on a pitch outside the zone, against a take in the same count, distance band and pitch group, cost -0.112 runs per plate appearance [-0.115, -0.109] in 2025 and -0.123 [-0.126, -0.120] in 2026, a change of -0.011 [-0.016, -0.007]. **The prediction held.** Reading: the 2026 challenge system took away most of the borderline strikes a hitter used to get for taking, so chasing costs more; this is a candidate part of why a hitter's own chase spots are worth more in 2026, but the price of a chase rose about 10% while the per-point value rose about 65%, so it does not account for all of it.

Decision rule: if both hold, bat speed against norm becomes a recent-form input candidate for the player model (a refit and the replay gates) and a scouting flag, frozen and scored once on the untouched months first; if not, short-term bat-speed changes do not run ahead of results either. Results (run 37888985847; 111,564 training and 62,261 test plate appearances; deviation SD 0.98 mph): **+0.0019 runs per plate appearance per mph [-0.0002, +0.0043]; squared-error reduction on 2026 +0.007 per 1,000 [-0.005, +0.021]**; fitted on 2026 alone +0.0029. By band on 2026: 1.5 mph or more below norm -0.016 against the base model (1,851 plate appearances), 1.5 or more above +0.010 (6,163), the middle bands flat. **Both predictions failed (the intervals include zero).** Under the rule, short-term bat-speed changes do not run ahead of results at a useful size either: only the extremes lean the expected way. With DRIFT-01, the early-warning question is answered no for both swing decisions and bat speed at two-week resolution.

columns.Attempt: Would hitters adapt if pitchers aimed at their own chase spots? Pitchers do not aim today (EXPLOIT-01), so how many of a hitter's high spots he has already been shown in a game is chance. Every 2025 pitch outside the zone to a hitter with a map (2023-2024): his swing, with the map's prediction as offset, on the number of earlier pitches in the game that fell in his high spots (outside, his own deviation in the top quarter) beyond what his own share of high spots gives by chance among the outside pitches he has seen, and its product with this pitch's deviation (does his excess chasing at his own spots shrink after he has been shown them?), with outside pitches seen, his share of high spots times deviation, outside pitches seen times deviation, earlier high spots chased (secondary: a hacking day raises both) and their product, earlier plate appearances and pitch number. Game-bootstrap intervals. Checked on synthetic games first: with adaptation planted (15 percent of the excess lost per earlier high spot) the key product is -0.083 [-0.099, -0.068]; with none -0.010 [-0.021, +0.002] (a first version that counted high spots without the chance adjustment showed a false +0.017 with none, because hitters with more distinct maps have more high spots; fixed before registering)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: the key product (high spots seen beyond chance times deviation) negative with the interval excluding zero: hitters lose some of their excess chasing at their own spots after being shown them within a game. Decision rule: if it holds, the realistic edge (VALUE-02) is discounted for repetition within a game and the scouting view says to spread the pitches into a hitter's spots across the game; if the interval includes zero or is above it, the edge does not wear off within a game at today's exposure levels. Results (run 37886804864; 305,771 outside pitches of 2025, high spots above 3.2 points): **the key product, high spots seen beyond chance times deviation, +0.009 [-0.004, +0.024]: hitters do not lose their excess chasing at their own spots after being shown them.** But the main term is clearly negative: **each extra high spot seen beyond chance lowers the log-odds of chasing any outside pitch by 0.065 [0.054, 0.074]** (about 1.4 points of chase rate at a 30 percent base), a general tightening rather than learning the spots; outside pitches seen -0.015 per pitch; earlier high spots chased +0.082 (a hacking day raises both, as expected); earlier plate appearances +0.051; pitch number -0.025. The prediction failed. Under the rule the spot-specific edge does not wear off within a game; the general tightening is an unregistered finding that bears on any aiming strategy: a pitcher who aims at a hitter's spots shows him more of them than chance, and each extra one costs about 1.4 points of chasing everywhere outside, so repeated aiming within a game gives back part of the gain. Netting the two needs its own registration (VALUE-03).
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: no spot learning; general tightening -0.065 per extra spot

ADAPT-01.status: no spot learning; general tightening -0.065 per extra spot

columns.Attempt: The third part of the matchup engine: where a hitter does damage, and which clock it follows. Each 2023-2025 ball in play's expected run value from its launch speed and angle (a league table of run value by speed and angle bins fitted on 2023-2024, so fielding and luck on where it lands drop out). League model: location bands by count, pitch group, speed, platoon and the hitter's earlier damage (shrunk), linear. Hitter damage maps: ridge regression of the residual on the 22-column hitter basis (at least 150 training balls in play), shrinkage chosen on the second half of 2024 from 10 to 10,000. Each on the true crossing and at the decision moment; trained 2023-2024, scored on 2025, squared-error reduction per 1,000 balls in play, paired by game; calibration across quintiles of the map deviation. Checked on synthetic balls in play first: planted hot zones (up in the zone, SD 3 mph of launch speed) gain 0.100 [0.061, 0.138] on the true crossing and 0.041 at the decision moment (true better by 0.061 [0.023, 0.097]), calibrated across quintiles; with none, the validation picks the largest shrinkage and the maps gain -0.0004 [-0.0026, +0.0017] (a first grid that stopped at 300 overfit the null at -0.10; widened before registering)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) hitter damage maps on the true crossing reduce the squared error on 2025 with the interval excluding zero; (2) the true crossing beats the decision moment for damage maps, interval excluding zero; (3) observed damage beyond the league model follows the map deviation across quintiles. Decision rule: if (1) holds, damage maps join the matchup engine (swings at the decision moment; misses and damage at the true crossing) and the scouting view gets a damage grid; (2) holding extends the two-clock reading to contact quality. If (1) fails, a hitter's damage is his level plus the league's map, and the engine's contact value comes from the league. Results (run 37886945666; 123,561 balls in play of 2025, 79.8% by hitters with a map; expected run value SD 0.309): squared error per ball in play, league 0.091977 and hitter maps 0.091770 on the true crossing (shrinkage 300), 0.093466 and 0.093432 at the decision moment (1,000). **(1) Hitter damage maps on the true crossing reduce it by 0.207 per 1,000 [0.151, 0.260]; (2) the true crossing beats the decision moment for hitter maps by 1.66 per 1,000 [1.53, 1.79]** (the league model alone is better on the true crossing by 1.49); (3) across quintiles of the map deviation the observed damage beyond the league runs -0.011, 0.000, +0.006, +0.011, +0.025 against map deviations -0.016, -0.002, +0.001, +0.006, +0.023. **Every prediction held: damage maps join the matchup engine on the true crossing, and the two-clock reading extends to contact quality: swing decisions follow where the pitch appears to be headed 260 ms out, misses and damage follow where it actually arrives.** The hitter maps' share of the variance is small (0.2 percent of the squared error: most of a ball in play's value is the swing itself), which is why they help most as a map of where a hitter does damage, not as a forecaster of single balls in play. A one-time scoring on the untouched months is registered as DAMAGE-01F.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: damage maps +0.21 (true crossing); true beats decision moment by 1.66
