columns.Attempt: Stress test of the run-value estimator and the aiming figure in synthetic worlds with known truth (the audit's priority 2). tools/brl_synth.py generates seasons pitch by pitch (count progression, a league swing model with each hitter's own shifts, levels and miss holes, pitchers with their own spots who may target or pitch away from a hitter's spot, foul, called strike, ball-in-play damage), 2023-2024 as map seasons and 2025 as the test season, 200,000 plate appearances, 240 hitters, 120 pitchers; eight kinds: null (hitters swing alike, so any coefficient is a false positive), level (hitters differ only in how much they swing), effect, small (40% of effect's spreads, nearer the real own-part spread), target (every pitcher aims 30% of pitches at the hitter's true chase spot), opposing (half target it, half pitch away), coincident (the miss hole sits on the chase spot), noisy (three times the hitters on the same pitches). The generator prices the truth: per point of a hitter's own part, 0.01 times (value if swing minus value if take) under its own probabilities and count values; and the true value of the estimator's actual aim choices (the chosen third's hitter-specific expected value against the pool's, the generator's oracle choice beside it). value2_study runs on each world with the audit's four code findings as options, all on: the 'pitch' estimand (each pitch's realized telescoping value, only earlier pitches of the plate appearance as controls) beside the 'pa' estimand; aim menus from the pitcher's training-season spots; a scattered pitch priced by the side of the zone it crosses ('side') and by the distance band it crosses in ('bands', six bands, the regression split by band). Smoke results before registration (one 60,000-plate-appearance effect world, local, disclosed): the own-part coefficient came out -0.00112 (pitch estimand; -0.00143 pa) against a truth of -0.00084 per true point, and 1.25 true points per fitted point (shrinkage), so the fitted part's one-standard-deviation value was 82% of the truth's; **the aiming figure (coefficient times the fitted gain) read -63.5 runs per 6,200 at zero scatter and -41.2 at 0.6 ft against true values of the chosen spots of -42.2 and -21.9 (ratios 1.5 and 1.9); priced by side -31.4 against -24.4 (1.3), by band -33.4 against -24.4 (1.4); the oracle -85.3 and -54.1.** The cause, measured: the run value per point differs across pitches, and the chosen spots (where a hitter's own part is largest, near his region's edge) carry a smaller value per point than the regression's average (-0.00069 against -0.00095 per fitted point at the test pitches), with the scatter adding sign flips the side pricing only partly catches
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the lane runs (ten worlds per kind, seeds 100-109).** Predictions: (1) null: the own, within-hitter, neighbor-held and placebo intervals exclude zero in at most 10% of worlds for each estimand (false-positive rate at the nominal 5%, allowing for ten reps); (2) effect and small: the pitch estimand's one-standard-deviation value is within 25% of the truth's in both kinds, and the pa estimand's own coefficient is larger in magnitude than the pitch estimand's in at least eight of ten worlds (the plate appearance's other pitches inflate it); (3) effect: the points figure at 0.6 ft overstates the true value of the chosen spots by a ratio between 1.3 and 2.0 on average, and neither the side nor the band pricing brings the ratio under 1.2; (4) target, opposing, coincident: the pitch estimand's one-standard-deviation value within 25% of effect's (the design's controls carry pitcher targeting), placebos nil (at most 10% excluding zero); (5) noisy: a smaller one-standard-deviation value than effect's with intervals still excluding zero in at least eight of ten worlds. Decision rule: if (1) fails, every ledger row that rests on the coefficient's interval (VALUE-08F, VALUE-11, VALUE-15, VALUE-16) carries a false-positive note and the stated interval is widened by the null's observed spread; if (3) holds, the stated 32 runs is relabeled as the regression's figure with the synthetic overstatement factor beside it until VALUE-18 (structural pricing: the per-point value computed at each aim from the engine's whiff, called-strike, foul and contact components and the count values, not one regression coefficient) is registered and tested in these same worlds; if (2) fails for the pitch estimand, the estimand itself is at fault and the structural pricing becomes the only stated figure. Receipts: research/discovery-value_synth-<run>.json, one per kind; no sealed data is read. Results (runs 37962478538 null, 37962521079 level, 37962566027 effect, 37962608258 small, 37962651070 target, 37962694526 opposing, 37962740015 coincident, 37962784613 noisy; ten worlds each, both estimands): **(1) failed for the plate-appearance estimand's own-map coefficient, which excluded zero in 3 of 10 null worlds (mean +0.00025, spread 0.00055 per point across worlds); held for everything else: the plate-appearance estimand's within-hitter neighbor-held coefficient 1 of 10 and placebo 0 of 10, the pitch estimand's own 1 of 10, neighbor-held 1 of 10, placebo 0 of 10.** (2) held on size, failed on the ordering: the pitch estimand's one-standard-deviation value was 85% of the truth's in effect (-0.0088 against -0.01035) and 85% in small (-0.00373 against -0.0044); the plate-appearance own coefficient exceeded the pitch estimand's in 7 of 10 worlds in both kinds (8 to 10 of 10 in the other kinds). **(3) held on the points figure: in effect worlds the regression figure at 0.6 ft was 1.72 (plate-appearance estimand) and 1.49 (pitch estimand) times the true value of its chosen spots (-52.5 and -45.7 against -30.6); held on side and band pricing for the plate-appearance estimand (1.23 and 1.24), failed for the pitch estimand (1.07 and 1.06, so with the pitch estimand the repricing removes most of the overstatement when the maps are good).** In small worlds (nearer the real spreads) the ratios were 2.03 and 1.63 for points, 1.48 and 1.19 by side, 1.46 and 1.11 by band. (4) held on size (one-standard-deviation values 78 to 104% of the truth in target, opposing and coincident); failed on the placebo's interval for the pitch estimand, which excluded zero in 2, 3 and 3 of 10 worlds (4 of 10 in effect) with means within 0.00002 of zero: the game bootstrap of one random reassignment is too narrow for the pitch estimand, so the placebo check must read the spread across reassignments (already reported as outside_more_reassignments) rather than that interval; the plate-appearance placebo 1, 0 and 2 of 10. (5) held: noisy one-standard-deviation value 83% of the truth, below effect's, excluding zero in 10 of 10. Level worlds (hitters differ only in how much they swing): the within-hitter coefficient read zero (-0.00002), correctly finding no location structure, while the own-map coefficients read -0.00055 and -0.00038 and the points figure excluded zero in 4 and 7 of 10 (the own part carries a swing level that also moves misses). **Under the rules set in advance: the own-map figures in VALUE-08F, VALUE-11, VALUE-15 and VALUE-16 carry a false-positive note (their primary estimator, within hitter and neighbor-held, passed); the stated 32 runs is the regression's figure, overstating the true value of its choices by 1.3 to 2.0 in these worlds, and is replaced by VALUE-18F's structural figure when scored.** The regression keeps its place as the check on the structural pricing (its per-point value is unbiased to within 15% on the one-standard-deviation scale in every world with location structure).

columns.Attempt: Structural pricing of the aiming edge (the fix VALUE-17's smoke results called for). Instead of one regression coefficient times the fitted gain, each scattered aim is priced by the engine's own components: the hitter's own swing part at that point, scaled by its out-of-sample calibration (the test season's swing residual regressed on the own part in probability units, by side of the zone; near 1 when the maps are real, near 0 when they are noise), times the value if he swings minus the value if he takes, built from the whiff model with his whiff map, the called-strike, foul and ball-in-play value models with his and the pitcher's terms (PAModels, the planner's fitted pieces) and the training seasons' count values. The pitcher's best third is chosen by that structural value, so the choice weighs where an extra swing is expensive, not only where the hitter swings most. Interval: hitters resampled and the calibration slope resampled by game. No regression coefficient enters; the regression stays beside it as the check. Smoke results before registration (60,000-plate-appearance worlds, local, disclosed): effect world at 0.6 ft, structural -41.6 against the true value of its own choices -41.5 (points -41.2 against -21.9), at zero scatter -69.1 against -59.8; the structural choices were worth more than the points choices (-41.5 against -21.9; oracle -54.1); small world (40% effects) -11.1 against -12.2 (points -7.4 against -6.2; bands -7.6 against -4.0), calibration 0.56; null world -0.1 with the calibration slope 0.0002 [-0.11, +0.14] and the interval covering zero; the engine's structural per-point value correlated 0.93 with the generator's at the test pitches
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the lane runs (ten worlds per kind, seeds 100-109, the structural option on; and one development run on the real 2025 test season with maps from 2023-2024).** Predictions, synthetic: (1) null: the structural figure's interval covers zero in at least nine of ten worlds and the calibration slope's interval covers zero in at least nine; (2) effect, small, target, opposing, coincident: the structural figure at 0.6 ft is within 20% of the true value of its own choices on average (ratio 0.8 to 1.2) in each kind; (3) the structural choice's true value beats the points choice's in at least eight of ten worlds in each of those kinds; (4) noisy: the calibration slope below effect's, the ratio within 0.7 to 1.3. Real data (development, descriptive, no prediction registered on its size): the 2025 structural figure, its calibration slopes, and the regression's figure beside it. Decision rule: if (1) and (2) hold, VALUE-18F is registered: the structural pricing scored once, frozen, on the untouched months (maps from 2023-2025), and its figure replaces the regression's 32 runs as the stated value of the aiming edge, the regression's figure kept as the check; if (2) fails, the structural figure is not stated and VALUE-17's overstatement factor is written beside the 32 runs; if (1) fails, the calibration does not protect against noise maps and the pricing is set aside. Development result, real 2025 (run 37964377494; 617,627 test pitches; maps 2023-2024; pitch estimand; menus from the pitcher's 2023-2024 spots): the own part's calibration on 2025 swings 0.954 [0.932, 0.978] outside and 0.820 [0.797, 0.848] inside (the maps are real: a fitted point is 0.95 of a real point); the regression's per-point value -0.000731 [-0.000817, -0.000658] (pitch estimand; the plate-appearance estimand gave -0.000553), placebo +0.000053 [-0.000034, +0.000119]; by distance band, 0 to 1 inch outside -0.000168 (nil), 1 to 2 -0.000422, 2 to 4 -0.000576, over 4 -0.001055, deep inside +0.000969; aiming at 0.6 ft, outside only, per 6,200: **points -25.7 [-28.7, -23.1], by side -21.5, by band -25.9, structural -43.3 [-45.6, -41.1]** (inside, structural -21.7); 476 hitters priced. columns.Attempt: The planner priced by the generator (synthetic worlds only; diagnostic, no real data): PLAN-01's machinery (PAModels fitted on the world's 2023-2024, pools of each pitcher's pitches, value iteration over counts and expectation states) run on 60,000-plate-appearance worlds, 40 pairs each, and every policy's true value computed with the generator's own probabilities (tools/brl_synth.py: true_probs_for_pool, policy_value, planner_truth; scratch synth/plan_truth.py and plan_truth2.py): the pitcher's actual mix, the league plan, the hitter plan, the oracle; the planner's own claim beside the truth; then the policy softened to a uniform choice among the best fraction of the pool in each state, and the hitter's maps scaled by the out-of-sample calibration slope VALUE-18 measures (1.07 effect, 0.74 small, 0.03 null)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **The single-best-pitch planner's hitter-specific claim does not track the truth at realistic sizes: effect world true +41.8 runs per 6,100 plate appearances over the league plan (claimed +37.3), small world true -8.2 (claimed -0.4), null world true -10.1 (claimed +14.8); following noise maps costs runs while the planner believes it gains.** Softening alone (best 10% of the pool) helps where effects are large (effect +57.7 true, 90% of pairs) but not elsewhere (small +0.7 true against +12.6 claimed; null -11.4 true against +12.4 claimed). **Calibrated maps with the soft policy track the truth in all three worlds: effect true +59.0, claimed +40.6; small true +5.1, claimed +4.6; null true +0.2, claimed -0.1.** The league plan's value over the actual mix (0.21 runs per plate appearance in every world) is the planner exploiting hitters who never adapt and is not a claim about anything real; the same figure in PLAN-01's real-data run (114.9 per 6,100) is read the same way. Reading: the planner stays set aside for the product; PLAN-03, when taken up, is the calibrated soft planner (own part scaled by its measured calibration, the best tenth of the pool per state) with a sequential off-policy evaluation checked first in these worlds, where a plan's true value is known. The hitter-specific increment of a plan over the league plan at realistic map sizes is small here (about 5 runs per 6,100) beside the structural aiming edge, which is a different quantity (the best third of outside spots against the pitcher's own mix, hitter-specific part only). A first off-policy check (scratch synth/ope_synth.py; logged 2025 pitches reweighted by the target policy's share of the pitch's family-by-zone bin over the pitcher's share, 150 pairs, 2,860 pitches, median effective sample size 6 per pair) read a one-step increment of 11 runs per 6,100 against a true 64 and the model's 58: the planner's gains come from placement inside a bin (the exact corner among the pitcher's pitches) that logged data cannot resolve and that command scatter would erase, so **PLAN-03's actions must be aims under command scatter, the policy a landing cloud over bins, and the planner solved on scatter-averaged transitions**, which also keeps it from exploiting corners no pitcher can hit on purpose. A second cut with aims under 0.6 ft of scatter (scratch synth/ope_scatter.py; the policy's landing cloud over 75 family-by-location bins against the pitcher's landing shares, 120 pairs, 2,320 logged pitches): the off-policy levels of the league-aim and hitter-aim policies now track the truth (-0.0218 against -0.0229 and -0.0265 against -0.0236 runs per pitch), but the hitter-specific increment is small (true 0.0007 runs per pitch) and the estimate's noise at this size is several times that; a real-data version needs the full season's pairs and should state the increment with its interval and abstain below an effective sample size.

columns.Attempt: Where the totals distribution goes wrong (the audit's priority 3; diagnostic, descriptive, development replays only: PROD-03's v2-prod3-1000 replays, 2,423 games of 2025 and 2,427 of 2026; scratch harness/totals_diag.py): combined and team-level PIT coverage, tails, CRPS and log score; predictive against residual variance; first five innings against the rest and the inning profile; home-away residual dependence; extras; subsets by day or night, roof, temperature, wind speed and direction (public game conditions); park bias; and a negative-binomial challenger on the simulator's own team mean (mean a + b times the simulator's, dispersion fitted by maximum likelihood on one season, scored on the other) against the simulator's histogram and a Poisson
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Means are right everywhere they were checked**: combined total bias -0.03 runs in both seasons, home -0.06 and -0.05, away +0.03 and +0.02; first five innings -0.03 and -0.01 against after the fifth +0.00 and -0.02 (the inning profile matches within 0.04 runs per team-inning through the seventh); the home-away residual correlation is 0.00 and -0.01, so the independence the convolution assumes holds. **The shape is slightly narrow**: predictive variance of a team's runs 9.2 against a residual variance of 10.0 to 10.1 (8 to 10% short); middle-half coverage 0.48 against 0.50 and 10.4 to 11% in each tail against 10%. **The negative-binomial challenger on the simulator's own mean (dispersion 3.4 to 3.6, slope 0.98 and 0.84, intercept 0.12 and 0.73) matches the histogram on CRPS (1.7143 against 1.7145 and 1.7250 against 1.7238 per team-game; combined 2.4643 against 2.4659 and 2.4856 against 2.4862) but beats it on the log score by 0.047 nats per team-game (2.452 against 2.499; 2.455 against 2.503) with coverage 0.497 and tails 8 to 10%**; a Poisson on the same mean is far worse (coverage 0.34 to 0.36, tails 17 to 21%). Reading: the simulator's mean carries the information; its 1,000-world histograms carry Monte Carlo noise in the bins (a log-score cost, not a CRPS one) and a little too little spread. Subsets: no condition shifts the mean consistently across both seasons beyond noise except wind of 12 mph or more (-0.24 and -0.22, the simulator low); park biases have a standard deviation of 0.59 and 0.64 runs across parks against about 0.5 expected from noise alone, with Colorado -1.25 (2025) and Sacramento -1.53 (2026) at the low end (the simulator under those parks) and Kansas City +1.62 (2025) and Los Angeles Angels +1.07 (2026) at the high end. Extras (8.6% of games): the simulator's mean is 0.57 and 0.93 runs under those games' totals, as a pregame number must be. Decisions: (1) the published run distributions should be smoothed (TOTALS-05: a negative-binomial fit with the simulator's mean and its own variance inflated to the residual variance, or more worlds; registered before any change to the page); (2) a park adjustment is the one feature with a visible target (TOTALS-06, registered with a prediction before its run); (3) the page keeps stating no over chance of its own (TOTALS-03).

columns.Attempt: A park adjustment to the simulator's mean total (TOTALS-04's one feature with a visible target). Per-park offsets of the residual (actual total minus the simulator's mean) on one season of the PROD-03 replays (v2-prod3-1000), shrunk toward zero by the between-park variance against the noise of each park's mean (empirical Bayes), applied to the other season's games: the simulator's own mean total, then the taught expected total with TOTALS-03's fixed weights (0.32 simulator, 0.78 line, -0.543). Paired squared error, intervals by date bootstrap. Also whether the market line's park residuals have structure beyond noise. tools/totals_park.py; data-branch aggregates only. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: the simulator's own squared error improves by 0.05 to 0.15 runs squared in each season, with at least one season's interval reaching zero (TOTALS-04 found park biases with a standard deviation of 0.59 to 0.64 runs against about 0.5 from noise, so the true park spread is about 0.3 runs); the taught expected total improves by under 0.03 (below the floor); the line's park residuals show no structure (standard deviation under 0.5). Gate: the offsets enter the simulator's own mean total (the number the page shows beside the taught total) only if the paired improvement excludes zero in both seasons; the taught total changes only if its own improvement clears the floor, which is not expected. **Results (tools/totals_park.py, run October 9): the prediction failed in the other direction.** Offsets from 2025 (shrinkage factor about 0.3; largest KC -0.47, PIT -0.36, DET +0.31, COL +0.36) make the 2026 simulator mean worse by 0.125 runs squared [0.069, 0.184]; offsets from 2026 (LAA -0.43, DET -0.32, PIT +0.45, ATH +0.62) make 2025 worse by 0.202 [0.120, 0.287]; the taught total worsens by 0.028 and 0.044, both intervals excluding zero. The park residual reverses between seasons: the correlation of a park's mean residual in one season with the next is -0.46 (30 parks, both directions), while the same teams' away-game residuals do not reverse (+0.09) and within a season a team's home and away residuals are negatively related (-0.22 and -0.29), so this is not a team effect and not a stable park effect. The market line's park residuals have a spread of 0.57 and 0.65 against 0.49 and 0.59 from noise (little structure). Reading: TOTALS-04's park biases are one-season noise that the model's park feature then carries into the next season with the wrong sign (an all-time online counter with a 1,000-PA prior, so one season's outcomes move a park's rating by about a third, and the fitted coefficient on the park log-ratio can amplify that); a fixed park table would make the totals worse. **Nothing adopted; the simulator's park feature is the suspect, tested next by refitting with a stronger park prior (TOTALS-07).**
columns.Disposition and evidence: failed; park residuals reverse across seasons (corr -0.46)

TOTALS-06.status: failed; park residuals reverse across seasons (corr -0.46)

columns.Attempt: Does the simulator's park feature chase one-season noise (TOTALS-06)? The PA model refitted exactly as pa-2026-v2-physics (train 2023-2024, validation 2025, test 2026, the same physics parameters) with park_prior_pa 6,000 instead of 1,000 (tools/fit_model_params.json, name pa-2026-v5-parkprior; the fit tool reads the prior from its settings), then both seasons replayed with the PROD-03 recipe (1,000 worlds, paired streams against v2-prod3-1000-2025 and -2026), scored on the mean total's squared error, the cross-season correlation of park mean residuals, the P(over) Brier and the win Brier. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the fit and the replays.** Prediction: the cross-season correlation of park residuals moves from -0.46 to above -0.2; the mean total's squared error improves by 0.03 to 0.10 runs squared in each season; the win Brier moves by less than 0.0002 pooled; the PA model's own held-out log loss (the fit receipt's locked-final block) changes by less than 0.001 nats. Gate: adopt as the production PA model if the pooled squared-error improvement's interval excludes zero with neither season worse, the pooled win Brier is not worse than +0.0002, and the fit's held-out log loss is not worse by more than 0.0005; the taught headline is then refitted on the new replays (a new headline version) before the switch. **Results (fit run 37998079379; replays 37999075249 and 37999145650, tools/replay_compare.py): the prediction failed and the gate is not met.** The refit's held-out log loss is unchanged (1.45843 against 1.45840 nats; the empirical-Bayes baseline's tuned park weight rose from 0.51 to 0.68 to compensate for the shrunken feature). Against the production replays, paired by game: mean-total squared error worse by 0.030 [-0.019, +0.076] in 2025 and 0.055 [-0.010, +0.118] in 2026, pooled +0.043 [+0.002, +0.082]; the cross-season correlation of park residuals moved only from -0.45 to -0.38 (predicted above -0.2); win Brier +0.00003 and +0.00028, pooled +0.00015 [-0.00005, +0.00036]; P(over) Brier +0.0003 and +0.0005. **Not adopted; the PA model's park feature is not the source of the reversal.** The source was found in the replay recipe itself: the run-environment table (ENV-02) carries a shrunk venue residual (ridge 1,600) fitted on one season and applied to the other, and the two seasons' venue terms are uncorrelated (-0.02 across 29 venues) with a spread of 0.17 runs per game, so each replay inherits the other season's venue noise and the park residuals reverse by construction; the PA-level log loss that chose ridge 1,600 (ENV-01) is nearly indifferent to the venue term (+0.00005 nats, scratch harness/env_ridge_scan.py), while at the run level it is noise. That is TOTALS-08.
columns.Disposition and evidence: failed; the reversal is the environment table's venue term

columns.Attempt: The run-environment table without its venue residual (TOTALS-07's finding): the production replays repeated with the same tables minus the venue term, the center recomputed on the fit rows (brl_replay/environment_fit2025_weather.json for the 2026 replay, environment_fit2026_weather.json for 2025; the production candidate brl_replay/environment_weather.json is env-v2 fitted on both seasons without venues), PROD-03 recipe otherwise unchanged, 1,000 worlds, scored against v2-prod3-1000 by tools/replay_compare.py. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the replays.** Prediction: the mean total's squared error improves by 0.02 to 0.06 runs squared in each season (the venue noise's variance is about 0.028); the cross-season correlation of park residuals rises from -0.45 to above -0.15; the win Brier moves by less than 0.0002 pooled; the P(over) Brier improves by up to 0.0005. Gate: the weather-only table replaces brl_live/environment.json (ADJUST['environment'] stays on) if the pooled squared-error improvement's interval excludes zero with neither season worse and the pooled win Brier is not worse than +0.0002; the taught headline is refitted on the new replays before the switch. **First result (replays 38004874163 and 38004938036 against v2-prod3-1000, independent streams):** mean-total squared error -0.049 [-0.111, +0.013] in 2025 and -0.027 [-0.091, +0.037] in 2026, pooled -0.038 [-0.080, +0.005]; the cross-season correlation of park residuals -0.449 to -0.026; win Brier -0.00008 and +0.00047 [+0.00015, +0.00079], pooled +0.00019 [-0.00004, +0.00042]; P(over) -0.00007 and -0.00039, pooled -0.00026. The predictions held (both squared-error points inside 0.02 to 0.06, the reversal gone, win Brier within 0.0002 pooled, P(over) better) but the pooled squared-error interval reaches zero, so the gate is not met on these runs; the per-game simulation noise of two independent 1,000-world runs is of the size of the effect. Declared before the runs: the same comparison is repeated with paired streams (METHOD-01, which cuts that noise by 71 to 84 percent), reference v2-prod3-ps-1000 (the PROD-03 recipe with streams) against v2-prod3-weather-ps-1000, both seasons, and the gate above is applied to that comparison. **Paired-streams result (runs 38009451097, 38009502287, 38009551022, 38009599322):** mean-total squared error -0.040 [-0.095, +0.016] in 2025 and -0.019 [-0.079, +0.039] in 2026, pooled -0.029 [-0.069, +0.011]; the park reversal -0.44 to -0.02; win Brier -0.00004 and -0.00005, pooled -0.00005 [-0.00019, +0.00009] (the pairing cut that noise as METHOD-01 says); P(over) +0.0002 and -0.0003, pooled -0.0001. The totals gain is in the predicted direction in both seasons and both runs, but its interval reaches zero again: the pairing removes simulation noise, not the noise of the games themselves, and 0.03 runs squared on 20 is below what two seasons can resolve. **Gate not met; nothing switched.** What is established: the venue term is one-season noise applied across seasons, it manufactures the park reversal, and removing it costs nothing on win chances or P(over). Removing it from the production table is a product call under the do-no-harm standard (rule 3, as PROD-03 was adopted), not an evidence-gated improvement; it waits for Alec.

columns.Attempt: Matchup program M4, how unexpected a pitch is. What a hitter can know: how often this pitcher throws each pitch type in this count bucket (first pitch, ahead, even, behind, full), after this previous pitch in the plate appearance, to this side, on earlier days, shrunk toward the league in the same context (70 contexts). Surprise = -log of the probability of the type actually thrown. Feed pitches 2023-2025; gradient boosting with and without surprise, the context's entropy and the six type probabilities, on top of speed, movement, location, spin, release, extension, count, type, platoon, the hitter's swing habit and the previous type; trained on 2023-2024, scored on 2025, paired by game, for swings, whiffs on swings and called strikes on takes. Checked on synthetic data first: a planted whiff effect gains 4.6 nats per 1,000 swings; with none the extra features cost 0.15 to 0.31 (so a real effect must clear that)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2025: whiffs on swings gain at least 0.5 nats per 1,000 swings with the interval excluding zero, and the observed whiff rate rises across surprise quintiles beyond the model without it; called strikes on takes gain at least 0.5 per 1,000 takes (hitters take what they did not expect); swing decisions gain less than whiffs. Decision rule: if the whiff gain holds, surprise enters the pitch-level matchup engine (its pitch-selection part is this same usage model) and a pitcher-level predictability cost is computed for scouting; if no gain clears 0.5, the hitter's expectation by count and sequence carries nothing beyond the pitch itself at this resolution. Results (run 37876755436; 2025: 705,553 pitches, 337,416 swings, 368,137 takes): surprise averages 1.93 bits (SD 0.91) against a context entropy of 2.06 bits. Gains in nats per 1,000: swings -0.29 [-0.43, -0.16], whiffs on swings -0.44 [-0.65, -0.23], called strikes on takes -0.88 [-1.03, -0.72], all at or below the cost of the extra features in the null synthetic world. Across surprise quintiles (0.9 to 3.4 bits) the observed whiff rate (21.5 to 23.5%) follows the model without surprise (22.2 to 23.5%) within half a point. **Every prediction failed: how unexpected a pitch type is, given the pitcher's habits in that count, after that pitch, to that side, adds nothing to swings, whiffs or called strikes beyond the pitch's own physics and location.** Ruled out at this resolution: the hitter's count-and-sequence expectation of the pitch type as a source of whiffs (consistent with pitchers mixing well enough to leave nothing to exploit, or with hitters not acting on type expectations); together with tunneling's weak result (DISC), deception has to be sought in the flight at the decision moment, not in the choice of pitch.

columns.Attempt: What the times-through-the-order penalty is, if not velocity (FATIGUE-01) or reading the flight better (Decision Horizon): familiarity with this pitcher's pitch types. For each pitch: how many pitches of the same type this hitter has already seen from this pitcher in the game, how many of any type (total exposure), and how many of the same type from other pitchers in the game (control: learning one pitcher's pitch should not transfer fully). Feed pitches 2023-2025, gradient boosting trained on 2023-2024 and scored on 2025, paired by game: whiffs on swings, chases, launch speed on balls in play, beyond the pitch's physics, location, count, the pitcher's pitch count, times through the order, total exposure and the hitter's swing habit. Checked on synthetic games first: a planted learning effect gains 1.07 nats per 1,000 swings (three more same-type pitches: -3.4 points of whiff rate); with none, -0.34 and 0.0
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2025: three more same-type pitches from this pitcher lower the whiff rate on swings by 0.5 to 2.0 points, with a gain of at least 0.5 nats per 1,000 swings (the interval excluding zero); the same exposure from other pitchers moves it less than half as much; chases fall 0.3 to 1.5 points per three; launch speed on contact rises 0.2 to 1.0 mph per three. Decision rule: if the whiff and chase effects hold, pitch-type familiarity replaces the fixed times-through-the-order term in the matchup engine (pitch-mix order then matters, and a scouting view shows which pitches a starter has already shown each hitter); if not, familiarity at the pitch-type level is ruled out as the penalty's source. Results (run 37877474263; 2025: 336,846 swings, 347,997 pitches outside the zone, 124,100 balls in play): whiffs on swings fall steeply with same-type exposure (25.3% at none, 20.2% at three, 15.9% at seven) but the model without it predicts nearly the same (25.5, 20.8, 17.7: total exposure, times through the order and pitch count carry it); gain -0.06 nats per 1,000 swings [-0.23, +0.11]; three more same-type pitches from this pitcher -0.74 points, from other pitchers -0.63 (not specific to the pitcher). Chases: gain -0.08 [-0.26, +0.10], three more same-type pitches +0.96 points (the wrong direction). Launch speed on contact: +0.20 mph per three [mean squared error down 0.19, 0.10 to 0.27]. Predictions held only for the size of the whiff effect and, at its lower edge, launch speed; the gain, the pitcher-specific contrast and the chase direction failed. **Under the rule, pitch-type familiarity with the pitcher is ruled out as the source of the times-through-the-order penalty**: hitters do miss less as a game goes on, but seeing the same pitch type from any pitcher counts as much as seeing it from him, and none of it adds to total exposure. With FATIGUE-01 (velocity, 1.4% of the penalty) and the Decision Horizon (no better reading of the flight), three explanations are now out; remaining candidates are command that degrades without speed loss and timing that adapts to the game in general.

columns.Attempt: Which part of a hitter's swing geometry carries the miss information CONTACT-01 found, and is it more than training noise? Same data and split as CONTACT-01 (Savant: train 2025, score 2026 through July). (1) The flexible comparisons refitted three times on bootstrap resamples of training games with feature subsampling (the game bootstrap on the test set does not see how much a boosted model's gain moves when it is refitted; a synthetic check with two pure-noise hitter features showed +0.66 nats per 1,000 at a smaller sample). (2) Nine parametric terms on the rates model's cross-fitted logits, all together, each left out and each alone: timing spread alone, with speed, and with the late change in approach angle (the plane at the steering limit, 110 ms, against the plane at the plate); usual attack angle with height, with approach angle, with vertical movement; the plane formula F; the hitter's attack-angle spread alone and with height. (3) The flexible model with more geometry (attack-angle spread, swing path tilt, attack direction)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: the geometry gain over the rates model averages at least 0.5 nats per 1,000 swings across refits and is positive in every refit; the parametric terms together recover at least half of it; the two largest drop-one losses are attack angle with height and timing spread with the late plane change; the extra geometry adds at least 0.2 on average. Decision rule: if the gain survives the refits, the parametric terms that carry it (drop-one loss at least 0.05 each) form a frozen swing-geometry miss model scored once on the untouched set; if it does not survive, CONTACT-01's geometry gain is recorded as within training noise. Results (run 37879352713; train 309,477 swings, test 225,466): the geometry gain over the rates model in three refits on resampled training games: 0.39, 0.66, 0.55 nats per 1,000 swings (mean 0.53, every refit positive; the single fit's 1.04 sat at the high end); the extra geometry (attack-angle spread, path tilt, attack direction) adds 0.26, 0.59, 0.92 (mean 0.59). The nine parametric terms together gain 0.19 [0.07, 0.32], 18% of the single fit's flexible gain. Drop-one losses: timing spread 0.169, attack angle with approach angle 0.013, F 0.013, timing spread with speed 0.012, the rest at or below 0.006 (attack angle with height -0.022). Alone: timing spread 0.22 (coefficient -0.90: hitters with a wider spread of contact depth miss less, beyond their whiff rate), attack angle with height 0.07, F 0.11, attack angle with approach angle 0.04. Predictions held for the refit mean and sign and for the extra geometry; failed for the parametric share (18% against at least half) and for which terms carry it. **Under the rule the gain survives refitting, and the frozen miss model is the rates model plus the one term with a drop-one loss of at least 0.05, the hitter's contact-depth spread; it is scored once on the untouched set (CONTACT-03).** Reading, to be tested: the spread of contact depth is not timing error as the M1 equation assumed. Contact depth is only seen when contact is made, so a hitter who still meets the ball when early or late shows a wide spread and one who misses when off time shows a narrow one: it measures his contact window, and a wide window means fewer misses. If so, hitters with wide windows should lose less to changes of speed (an offspeed pitch after fastballs), a matchup-specific prediction for the next registration.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: gain survives refits (0.53); timing spread carries it, sign reversed

CONTACT-02.status: gain survives refits (0.53); timing spread carries it, sign reversed

columns.Attempt: How much of the previous pitch's timing a hitter carries into his next swing, measured where contact happens. A hitter times his swing to the flight he expects; if a share alpha of that expectation is carried from the previous pitch of the plate appearance, a pitch whose flight from release to the front of the plate is longer by dt finds him early by alpha times dt, and contact is made farther in front of him by u times alpha times dt (u = v_s v_b / (v_s + v_b), the speed at which the meeting point moves along the flight per unit of timing error, about 56 ft/s or 6.7 inches per 10 ms at 70 mph bat and 85 mph ball; the M1 equation wrote the denominator as a difference, the numbers there used the sum). Savant contact swings (contact depth: intercept, inches toward the pitcher) with a previous pitch in the same plate appearance, the hitter's usual depth (earlier days, shrunk) removed, against dt with the pitch's own flight time, type, side and height, count and platoon held fixed, fitted on 2025 and repeated on 2026 through July: the slope over 6.7 inches per 10 ms is the carryover share. Also: after swings against after takes, two pitches back beyond the previous one, each hitter's own carryover (shrunk slope; its correlation between the first and second halves of 2025), and misses on speed changes: on top of a flexible whiff model that already sees the speed change (flight time, dt, its size, the previous pitch's type and whether he swung, the hitter's whiff rate), each hitter's carryover and contact window (CONTACT-02) with their products with the size of the speed change, coefficients fitted on 2025 and scored on 2026 through July. Checked on synthetic plate appearances first: with a planted carryover share of 0.25 (between-hitter SD 0.12) the depth slope is 1.56 inches per 10 ms (share 0.23), hitters' own carryover correlates 0.96 between halves, and misses on speed changes gain 1.25 nats per 1,000 swings [0.77, 1.73] with carryover times speed change +0.032 [0.028, 0.039]; with none, the slope is 0.002 [-0.012, 0.017], the halves correlate 0.05 and nothing gains
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) the depth slope positive with the interval excluding zero in 2025 and in 2026, a carryover share between 0.03 and 0.30; (2) two pitches back adds less than half the previous pitch's slope; (3) after a swing against after a take: no direction predicted, reported; (4) each hitter's carryover correlates at least 0.2 between the halves of 2025; (5) misses: carryover times speed change positive with the interval excluding zero, and its gain positive with the interval excluding zero on 2026; (6) contact window times speed change negative (a wide window blunts a speed change) with the interval excluding zero. Decision rule: (1) holding makes timing carryover a measured relationship of the program (the share of the previous pitch's timing in the next swing); (4) and (5) together make each hitter's carryover a matchup input (pitchers whose speeds differ most against hitters who carry most) and a scouting number, frozen and scored once on the untouched set before it is used; if (1) fails, hitters re-time every pitch, and speed sequencing does not act through carried timing. Results (run 37882064459; contact swings with a previous pitch: 197,598 in 2025, 141,042 in 2026 through July; speed change SD 37 ms): depth slope **+0.038 inches per 10 ms [0.021, 0.051] (2025) and +0.043 [0.027, 0.060] (2026)**, a carryover share of 0.006, ten times below the predicted range. **After a take the slope is zero (+0.002 [-0.015, +0.016]; 2026 +0.012); after a swing it is +0.11 more [0.091, 0.129] (2026 +0.095 [0.073, 0.115])**: timing carries over only from a pitch the hitter swung at, a share of about 1.7%. Two pitches back (pitch three on): the previous pitch's own coefficient nearly vanishes (-0.02 per 10 ms of its flight time) while the pitch two back carries -0.16, the opposite of a decaying memory. Each hitter's slope: between-hitter SD 0.16 inches per 10 ms, four times the pooled mean, **correlation between the halves of 2025: 0.60**. Misses (263,153 training swings, 171,651 test): the hitter's slope as a main term -0.51 [-0.62, -0.43] (hitters whose contact moves out front on slower pitches miss less overall) and times the size of the speed change **+0.055 [0.028, 0.078]**, gain 0.17 nats per 1,000 swings [0.09, 0.28]; contact window main term -0.91 (as in CONTACT-02) but times the speed change +0.010 [-0.049, +0.054]. Predictions: (1) held for the sign in both seasons, failed for the size; (2) failed; (3) carryover after swings only; (4) held (0.60); (5) held; (6) failed (the window does not blunt speed changes). Reading, before any use: the after-swing contrast is the cleanest result (the same speed change, after a swing against after a take); the pooled and per-hitter slopes are open to an artifact, because the pitch's own flight time enters linearly with its type, so any curvature in how depth follows a pitch's own speed is picked up by the speed change and by the pitch two back (pitchers alternate types, so the pitch two back resembles the current one). The per-hitter number may be how a hitter's contact depth follows pitch speed in general (an adjustability trait) rather than carried timing. **Under the rule (4) and (5) make the hitter's slope a matchup input to be frozen and scored on the untouched set; the freeze waits for TIMING-02, which removes the artifact (within each pitcher's pitch type) and separates the two traits, so the one untouched scoring is spent on a measure whose meaning is known.**
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: after-swing carryover +0.11 in/10 ms; hitter slope reliable (0.60); artifact check next

TIMING-01.status: after-swing carryover +0.11 in/10 ms; hitter slope reliable (0.60); artifact check next

columns.Attempt: TIMING-01 without its artifact, and which hitter trait it found. (a) Carried timing measured within one pitcher's one pitch type in one season (fixed effects, flight times centered there): the same pitch preceded by different pitches; contact depth (hitter's usual depth removed) on the previous pitch's flight time after a take, after a foul and after a miss, and on the pitch two back. (b) Speed-follow: how far contact moves out front per 10 ms of slower flight across one pitcher's pitches, pooled (6.7 inches would be no re-timing at all, 0 perfect re-timing) and per hitter (shrunk slope, 2025), against the carried trait (each hitter's after-swing slope within pitcher-types); reliability across the halves of 2025. (c) Misses in 2026 through July on top of a flexible whiff model that sees flight time, slowness against the pitcher's average, the speed change and whether he swung at the previous pitch: speed-follow with its products with slowness and with the speed change; carried with its product with the speed change after a swing. Checked on synthetic plate appearances first, in three worlds: a pitcher-level depth effect with no carried timing gives TIMING-01's estimator a false slope (-0.054 [-0.067, -0.040]) and this one none (after a take -0.001, after a swing -0.009, both intervals across zero); planted carried timing after swings (share 0.15) and hitter speed-follow (SD 0.3 inches per 10 ms) are recovered as an after-take slope of -0.002, an after-swing slope of -0.58 (share 0.087: contact is only seen when the timing error was small enough, so the estimate runs low), speed-follow reliability 0.59 against 0.30 for carried, and speed-follow times slowness +0.59 on misses; with neither, everything is near zero (speed-follow reliability 0.05)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) within pitcher-types, after a take the previous pitch's flight time moves contact depth by at most 0.03 inches per 10 ms either way, in both seasons; after a swing it moves it negatively (a slower previous pitch, a later swing) with the interval excluding zero, a carried share between 0.005 and 0.05, in both seasons; (2) two pitches back after a swing, less than half of that; (3) pooled speed-follow between 0.3 and 1.2 inches per 10 ms (4 to 18% of a speed difference not re-timed), interval excluding zero; (4) hitters' speed-follow correlates at least 0.4 between the halves of 2025, more than the carried trait; (5) on 2026 misses, speed-follow times slowness positive with the interval excluding zero, and the speed-follow terms gain with the interval excluding zero; (6) the carried trait adds under 0.05 nats per 1,000 swings beyond speed-follow. Decision rule: (1) makes timing carried from a swung-at pitch, and only from one, a measured mechanism with its share; (4) and (5) make speed-follow the hitter timing measure of the matchup engine in place of TIMING-01's slope, frozen and scored once on the untouched set (TIMING-03) before it is used or shown; if (5) fails, speed-follow describes hitters but does not predict their misses. Results (run 37882811823; within 3,672 pitcher-types in 2025 and 3,375 in 2026; 197,410 and 140,872 contact swings): the pitch's own flight within its type +1.23 inches per 10 ms (2025) and +1.16 (2026). **After a take, a slower previous pitch puts contact farther out front: +0.106 inches per 10 ms of the previous pitch's flight [0.094, 0.120] (2025), +0.098 [0.081, 0.114] (2026)**, the opposite of carried timing. After a swing the previous pitch's slope drops by 0.081 [0.054, 0.110] (2026: 0.051), after a miss by 0.134 more (2026: 0.205), so a missed pitch's timing does carry (net -0.11 and -0.16 inches per 10 ms, shares 0.016 and 0.023) and a fouled one nets about zero. Two pitches back: after a take -0.015 [-0.031, +0.001], after a swing -0.18 more [-0.21, -0.15] (2026 -0.17): a swing two pitches back still carries. Speed-follow within each pitcher, across his pitch types: **+1.53 inches per 10 ms [1.49, 1.57] in 2025 and +1.52 in 2026: 23% of a flight-time difference between one pitcher's pitches is not re-timed.** Hitters' speed-follow: SD 0.34 inches per 10 ms, halves correlate 0.54; the carried trait: SD 0.11, halves 0.18. Misses on 2026 swings: speed-follow -0.21 [-0.27, -0.17] (hitters whose contact moves out front on slower pitches miss less), times slowness +0.007 [-0.005, +0.019], times the speed change +0.021 [0.008, 0.035], gain 0.17 [0.08, 0.27]; the carried trait adds 0.002. Predictions (1) failed (takes move timing, in the opposite direction), (2) failed (two back carries more than one back), (3) failed (1.53, above the range), (4) held, (5) failed for the slowness product (the gain held), (6) held. **Under the rule nothing is promoted: carried timing is not a single mechanism, and speed-follow does not pass (5) as registered.** What the run found instead, to be confirmed with fuller controls before any claim: two opposite sequence effects in where contact is made: after a taken pitch, hitters meet the next pitch as if expecting the other speed (a slow pitch taken, the next one met earlier: pitchers alternate speeds and hitters appear to know it), and the timing of a swing, above all a miss, persists for one or two pitches. The speed-follow trait predicts misses through its main term, which may overlap the contact window (CONTACT-03); TIMING-03 tests both.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: contrast after takes +0.10 in/10 ms; nothing promoted

TIMING-02.status: contrast after takes +0.10 in/10 ms; nothing promoted

columns.Attempt: TIMING-02's two sequence effects with fuller controls (development data: Savant 2025 and 2026 through July). Contact depth (hitter's usual depth removed) on the previous pitch's flight time, with fixed effects for every cell of pitcher, pitch type, season and the previous pitch's outcome kind (taken for a ball, taken for a strike, fouled, missed), so a previous pitch is compared only with previous pitches of the same outcome before the same pitch of the same pitcher; the count as twelve categories, the pitch number, the previous pitch's side, height and zone, the pitch's own flight and location, platoon. Variants: cells also split by the previous pitch's family (fastball, breaking, offspeed), to see whether the speed or the type is what hitters key on; alternations (previous pitch of another family) and repeats separately. Misses on 2026 swings: speed-follow (TIMING-02) and the contact window (CONTACT-03) alone and together. Checked on synthetic plate appearances first: TIMING-02's design leaked a planted after-swing effect into after-take slopes when the sample was split (alternations +0.18, repeats -0.24 with nothing planted after takes), because the after-swing shift differed by pitch type; with cell fixed effects every after-take slope is within 0.06 of zero in the planted world and within 0.03 in the null, and the planted after-swing slope is recovered at -0.66 to -0.71
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) after a taken ball and after a called strike the previous pitch's flight slope is positive, +0.04 to +0.15 inches per 10 ms with the interval excluding zero, in both seasons; (2) after a miss it is negative with the interval excluding zero in both seasons; (3) within the previous pitch's family the after-take slopes fall by at least half (hitters key on the type they just saw, not its exact speed); (4) alternations and repeats reported, no prediction; (5) speed-follow and the window correlate positively, and speed-follow gains at least 0.05 nats per 1,000 swings beyond the window with the interval excluding zero. Decision rule: if (1) and (2) hold, both sequence effects are frozen (this code) and confirmed once on the untouched set (TIMING-03F), and the scouting reading is stated (after a take hitters meet the next pitch as if expecting the other speed; a missed swing's timing persists); if (1) fails, TIMING-02's after-take result was the design's artifact. If (5) holds, speed-follow is a hitter trait candidate for its own frozen test; if not, it is a facet of the contact window. Results (run 37883288815; 195,396 contacts in 2025, 138,932 in 2026 through July): slope of contact depth on the previous pitch's flight, inches per 10 ms, with cell fixed effects and full controls: **after a called strike +0.122 [0.097, 0.144] (2025) and +0.135 [0.098, 0.172] (2026); after a taken ball +0.036 [0.021, 0.055] and +0.033 [0.014, 0.056]; after a foul -0.018 and +0.015 (zero); after a miss -0.186 [-0.230, -0.145] and -0.222 [-0.278, -0.159].** With cells also split by the previous pitch's family, the after-take slopes vanish (called strike +0.034 [-0.026, +0.108] and -0.029; ball 0.000 and -0.029) while after a miss stays (-0.17 and -0.33). Alternations: after a called strike +0.102 and +0.095; repeats -0.006 and -0.026. Own flight within type +1.34 and +1.26. Misses: speed-follow and window correlate 0.45; window alone gains 0.23 [0.14, 0.32], speed-follow alone 0.18 [0.09, 0.27], both 0.28 [0.18, 0.39] (speed-follow -0.106 [-0.142, -0.070] beside the window; the increment over the window, 0.053, had no interval computed). Predictions: (1) held in sign and interval for both kinds of take in both seasons, but the range failed for taken balls (0.036 and 0.033 against at least 0.04); (2) held; (3) held (the after-take slope is about the previous pitch's family, not its speed within the family); (5) the correlation held, the interval on the increment was not computed, so it is not met. **Under the rule nothing is frozen from this registration** ((1) failed its range for balls). Reading: after a hitter takes a strike, he meets the next pitch as if expecting the other kind of pitch (a slower family taken for a strike, the next pitch met earlier; a faster one, later), and after he misses, the missed swing's timing carries into his next contact; a fouled pitch carries nothing. The first effect is about pitch family, so it is an expectation of alternation, not a perceptual speed contrast. These are confirmed only by a new registration on fresh data (TIMING-03F).
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: after called strike +0.12-0.13; after miss -0.19 to -0.22

columns.Attempt: TIMING-03's design scored once on the untouched set: every contact swing from August 1, 2026 with a previous pitch in the plate appearance (Savant), cell fixed effects for pitcher, pitch type, season and the previous pitch's outcome kind, full controls, the same variants. Code: timing_final_study in tools/brl_matchup.py, frozen in the commit that adds this row (the depth code of timing3_study restricted to the untouched rows); it refuses to run without final_eval and a frozen commit. Checked on synthetic plate appearances: planted after-swing carried timing recovered at -0.65 and -0.72 with after-take slopes within 0.03 of zero; nothing planted, every full-control slope within 0.03 of zero
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run; one scoring.** Predictions on the untouched contacts (full controls): (a) after a called strike the slope is positive, +0.05 to +0.20 inches per 10 ms of the previous pitch's flight, interval excluding zero; (b) after a miss it is negative with the interval excluding zero; (c) after a taken ball the point estimate is positive; (d) with cells split by the previous pitch's family, the after-called-strike slope is within 0.06 of zero. If either fails, the development result is recorded as not confirmed. Results (run 37883572585, frozen commit 8795ff00; 65,356 untouched contacts with a previous pitch, August 1 to September 27, 2026): slopes in inches of contact depth per 10 ms of the previous pitch's flight, full controls: **(a) after a called strike +0.151 [0.101, 0.192]; (b) after a miss -0.239 [-0.317, -0.146]**; (c) after a taken ball +0.026 [-0.007, +0.055]; after a foul -0.008. (d) Within the previous pitch's family, after a called strike +0.087 [-0.064, +0.232], outside the predicted 0.06 of zero (its interval is wide). Alternations: after a called strike +0.064, after a ball +0.048; repeats after a miss -0.52 [-0.92, +0.04]. **(a), (b) and (c) held, (d) failed: under the rule both sequence effects are credited as forward-tested; whether hitters key on the previous pitch's family or on its speed stays open.** Stated: after a hitter takes a called strike, he meets the next pitch farther out front the slower that strike was, about 0.15 inches per 10 ms of its flight (a changeup taken for a strike against a fastball taken for a strike, roughly 0.6 inches); after he misses, he meets the next pitch later the slower the pitch he missed, about 0.24 inches per 10 ms; a fouled pitch and a taken ball carry little. These are sizes of where contact happens, small in outcomes (SEQ-01 found no gain in misses from sequence surprise); they go to the scouting view as sequencing notes.

columns.Attempt: CONTACT-02's frozen miss model scored once on the untouched set: the rates model (gradient boosting on the pitch's speed, movement, location, approach angles, spin, extension, release height, count, type, platoon and arm angle, with the hitter's whiff rate and bat speed from earlier swings) plus one term, the hitter's contact-depth spread from earlier contact swings (shrunk with k = 50), its coefficient fitted on the rates model's cross-fitted logits; the recipe refitted on all development swings (2025 and 2026 before August 1, at least 30 earlier contacts) and scored on every swing from August 1, 2026 (Savant). Code: contact_final_study in tools/brl_matchup.py, frozen in the commit that adds this row; it refuses to run without final_eval and a frozen commit. Also reported: the flexible model with attack angle and spread (CONTACT-01's G2). Checked on synthetic swings first: with no spread effect the term is +0.03 per 10 inches [-0.03, +0.10] and gains -0.01; with a spread effect that is purely the hitter's level, the whiff rate absorbs it by August and the term, fitted where earlier-swing histories are thinner, over-corrects (gain -0.57), so the untouched gain is positive only if the spread carries more than a better estimate of the hitter's level
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run; one scoring.** Predictions: the coefficient negative with the interval excluding zero (development -0.90 per 10 inches); the gain over the rates model on the untouched swings positive with the interval excluding zero, about 0.2 nats per 1,000 swings; observed misses fall across spread quintiles beyond the rates model. Decision rule: if both hold, the contact window (spread of contact depth) is credited as a forward-tested predictor of misses beyond a hitter's whiff rate and enters the matchup engine's miss model; if the gain fails, it is recorded as a development-only result (a better early estimate of the hitter's level, not new information). Results (run 37882301605, frozen commit 618cc7f3; 534,943 development swings, 107,290 untouched swings from August 1 to September 27, 2026, whiff rate 22.7%): coefficient **-0.86 per 10 inches of spread [-0.98, -0.73]** (development -0.90); **gain over the rates model +0.16 nats per 1,000 swings [0.05, 0.27]**; the rates model's error by spread quintile runs from -0.8 points (narrowest windows, 8.3 inches: observed 22.2%, rates model 21.4%) to +0.9 (widest, 10.0 inches: 22.7% against 23.5%), and the frozen model removes it at both ends (22.3% and 22.6%). The flexible model with attack angle and spread gains +1.07 [0.66, 1.43] on the same swings. **Both predictions held on untouched data: credited.** A hitter's contact window, the spread of where along the flight he meets the ball, measured from his earlier contact swings, predicts his misses beyond his whiff rate two months ahead: hitters who meet the ball over a wider range of depths miss less than their rate says, those with narrow windows more. It enters the matchup engine's miss model.

columns.Attempt: In-game win chance with the PROD-03 package. Who pitches the late innings and how long starters go change the game's simulated win table most from the sixth inning on, and the in-game test has far more power than the pregame one (every 2026 plate appearance is a scored state). Two 2026 replays with the game's win table recorded at every real state (split halves, as in LIVE-04): CTX-02 settings and PROD-03 settings, same seeds; scored as the page shows it (the game table averaged with the league table on the log-odds scale, anchored to the headline with the square-root fade)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before either replay.** Prediction: the package's in-game Brier over all 2026 states better than the reference by 0.0001 to 0.0006, with at least two thirds of the gain in innings 6 and later. Decision rule: if PROD-03 switches the package on and LIVE-05's paired difference by game has its 95% interval entirely above zero (worse), the package is switched back off pending a look at late-inning management; otherwise it stands. Results (runs 37873185010 reference and 37873219559 package; 2,427 games, 189,700 scored states, paired by game): game table noise-free Brier 0.156225 against 0.156445, -0.00022 [-0.00100, +0.00061]; **as the page shows it (anchored, averaged with the league table, 10,000 games) 0.156727 against 0.156843, -0.00012 [-0.00042, +0.00020]**; by innings (page) 1-3 -0.00036, 4-6 +0.00026, 7-9 -0.00025, extras -0.00062; runner on third with fewer than two out +0.00062. The size prediction held at its lower edge (0.00012 against 0.0001 to 0.0006); the timing prediction failed (the early innings gained as much as the late ones, the middle innings lost). **Under the rule the package stands in game when it is switched on (the interval is not above zero)**: in-game win chances are no worse with the fitted bullpens and leash and probably slightly better.

columns.Attempt: Game-to-game spread of runs. In the CTX-02 replays the simulated team-run distribution (averaged over games) is narrower than the real one: SD 3.12 against 3.21 (2026) and 3.11 against 3.25 (2025); too few 1-2 run games (23.3% against 25.0%; 23.5% against 24.2%) and 10+ run games (7.0% against 7.2%; 6.9% against 7.9%), too many 3-5 (38.2% against 36.1%); game totals SD 4.44 against 4.51 and 4.40 against 4.60. A simulator with fixed rates misses what varies by the day: starters' stuff, lineups' days, conditions. Win probabilities are close to calibrated (slope 1.02 in 2026, 0.86 in 2025, wide intervals). Built: brl_live.provider_adjust.DayForm, one shock per batting team and world on the chances of reaching base (log-normal, centered), applied after the other layers. In the engine with league-average hitting the added variance of team runs is about 52 sigma squared (sigma 0.08, 0.12, 0.16: SD 3.01 to 3.07, 3.14, 3.23), so the gaps imply sigma 0.13 (2025) and 0.11 (2026). Test: CTX-02 settings plus the shock, 2026 with 0.13 (from 2025) and 2025 with 0.11 (from 2026), same seeds
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any replay.** Predictions against the CTX-02 replays: team-run SD up to 3.17-3.25 (2026) and 3.15-3.22 (2025); game-total SD up 0.08 to 0.20; mean total within 0.03; P(over the line) Brier better in both seasons; win Brier within 0.0003 either way. Decision rule: on (ADJUST day_form_sigma, 0.12 from both seasons) if P(over) is better in both seasons with the pooled interval's upper end below zero, the pooled win Brier difference's upper end is below +0.0002, and the team-run SD moves toward actual in both. Results (runs 37864772513, 37864803481): team-run SD 3.12 to 3.27 (actual 3.21, 2026) and 3.11 to 3.22 (3.25, 2025), closer to actual in both (2026 now 0.06 over); game-total SD 4.44 to 4.66 (4.51) and 4.40 to 4.56 (4.60); scores of 1-2 runs 23.3 to 23.7% (25.0) and 23.5 to 23.8% (24.2), 10+ 7.0 to 7.9% (7.2) and 6.9 to 7.5% (7.9); mean total +0.05 and +0.04 (9.04 against 8.96; 8.96 against 8.90); P(over the line) Brier -0.00037 [-0.00095, +0.00023] and -0.00043 [-0.00114, +0.00028], pooled -0.00039 [-0.00085, +0.00005]; win Brier +0.00004 and -0.00061, pooled -0.00029 [-0.00075, +0.00019]; total squared error -0.016 and -0.001. Predictions held for the spread in 2025, P(over) and the win Brier; the 2026 spread overshot (3.27 against 3.17 to 3.25) and the mean total rose more than predicted (+0.05 and +0.04 against 0.03: a shock on reaching base adds runs on average, as run scoring is convex). **Not switched on: the pooled P(over) interval's upper end is +0.00005, not below zero.** Better in both seasons on every totals measure; it fails only the strict bound. A re-test with paired streams (METHOD-01, which cuts simulation noise in such comparisons by 71 to 84 percent) and the shock centered on runs rather than on reaching base is the next registration for it.

columns.Attempt: DISP-01 re-tested as its row said: paired streams (METHOD-01, which cuts simulation noise in such comparisons by 71 to 84 percent) and the shock centered so mean runs stay level. DISP-01's shock raised mean totals by 0.05 (2026) and 0.04 (2025) runs a game because runs are convex in reaching base; with a run elasticity of about 1.5 to reaching base, an extra downward shift of the shock's mean of 0.004 (2026, sd 0.13) and 0.003 (2025, sd 0.11) cancels that. Reference: the CTX-02 configuration with paired streams; the same with the centered shock; same seeds; 1,000 worlds; both seasons (2025 with the inputs fitted on 2026 and the reverse, as DISP-01). Scored as DISP-01 (team-run SD against actual, P(over the line) Brier, win Brier, mean total)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the replays.** Predictions: team-run SD moves toward actual in both seasons; mean total within 0.02 runs a game of the reference; pooled P(over) Brier difference's upper end below zero; pooled win Brier difference's upper end below +0.0002. Decision rule (DISP-01's): if all hold, day form is proposed for production (a production change, so it needs Alec's approval); if not, it stays off. Results (runs 37902607182, 37902636013, 37902663425, 37902690574): team-run SD 3.120 to 3.259 against actual 3.210 (2026) and 3.108 to 3.207 against 3.249 (2025), toward actual in both; game-total SD 4.445 to 4.640 (4.510) and 4.403 to 4.543 (4.596); mean total 8.981 against 8.981 and 8.921 against 8.923 (the centering worked); **P(over the line) Brier -0.000366 [-0.000900, +0.000136] (2026) and -0.000403 [-0.000841, +0.000049] (2025), pooled -0.000381 [-0.000740, -0.000045]**; total squared error -0.017 and +0.008, pooled -0.005 [-0.026, +0.016]; **win Brier +0.000205 [-0.000292, +0.000689] and -0.000007 [-0.000472, +0.000449], pooled +0.000099 [-0.000235, +0.000411]**; win calibration slope 1.02 and 0.94. Predictions held for the spread, the mean total and P(over); **the win Brier bound failed (pooled upper end +0.00041, above +0.0002).** Under the rule day form stays off. Reading: a day-form shock fixes the width of the run distribution and the totals, but it also pulls each game's win chance toward even, and the win chances were not too confident to begin with (slopes near 1). A totals-only use (win chances from the plain worlds, totals from the shocked ones) would need its own registration and a cost check.

columns.Attempt: Where by inning the simulator's runs differ from real ones: the CTX-02 2026 replay re-run with the same seeds, recording simulated runs by inning and the real score before each inning (replay rows now carry both). The bullpen fixes lowered totals by 0.05 to 0.07 and the running plays add 0.14, so the level question is where the rest of the excess sits
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered while the replay was queued, before any result.** Prediction: simulated minus actual runs per team-inning within 0.02 in innings 1-5 (mostly starters), and above +0.01 on average over innings 6-9 (bullpens under the hand-set rules). Results (run 37869327258, 4,854 team-games): per team-game 4.492 simulated against 4.481 actual; simulated minus actual by inning +0.004, +0.001, +0.011, +0.014, -0.021, +0.001, +0.011, -0.029, +0.012, extras +0.006 (sampling SD about 0.013 per inning). Innings 1-5 held except the fifth (-0.021); **innings 6-9 average -0.001, not above +0.01: the late-inning excess predicted is not there.** No inning carries a systematic excess. Together with RUNS-01, RUNS-02 and the totals of PROD-02: the reference simulator's run level is right by inning in 2026 because two level errors cancel (the stack's season level carried from 2025, +0.04 runs per team-game, against the base-running kernel's shortfall without the running plays); the plays fix the second and expose the first, and in 2025 the plays' rate from other seasons overshoots. Both are level calibrations, not a missing mechanism: the running plays come back with in-season re-anchoring of the stack's level and the plays' rate. Who bats is ruled out (substitutes, -0.003 to -0.012 runs a game).

columns.Attempt: Why the swing model over-calls chases (diagnostic). On the 4,991 graded games, hitters chased 152,037 times against 169,053 expected by the league swing model and 167,365 by the hitter maps: about 11% high in both seasons, 18% on fastballs, 4% on breaking balls, 20% when the hitter is behind in the count. The league swing model reads the pitch at the decision moment (a straight-line projection 0.26 s out) while 'outside' is where the pitch crossed. Two explanations: (A) selection at the edge: among pitches that look alike at the decision moment, the ones that end outside are the ones hitters swing at less (hitters read more than the straight line), so any model on the decision-moment location over-calls swings on pitches that end outside and under-calls them on pitches that end inside, in sample as well as after; (B) drift: the model is right on the rows it was fit on and wrong on later rows. Measured in the report lane (tools/brl_report.py, params calibration_diag and calibration_only, no report built): expected against actual swings on the training rows and on the rows after the as-of date, by crossing zone, family, distance outside (0.1, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 ft bands), count group and whether the pitch looked like a strike at the decision moment, with the hitter maps alongside; as of 2025-07-01 (2024 and 2025 loaded) and 2026-08-01 (2025 and 2026). Sums only. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the runs.** Prediction (A): on the training rows the league model's outside-zone expectation runs 5% to 15% above actual swings with fastballs highest, the excess largest within 0.25 ft of the edge and on pitches that looked like strikes, and the inside-zone expectation below actual; the rows after the as-of date look the same within 3 points. (B) is supported instead if the training rows' outside-zone expectation is within 2% of actual while the later rows are 8% or more high. Next step either way: (A) a league term for where the pitch crossed (zone side and distance outside, by family) in the report's swing model and the structural engine's, registered with its own gate on later months (level of expected chases within 3% in each season, swing log loss better, the maps' gain kept); (B) recency weighting of the league fit. **Results (runs 38060917628 and 38060946758):** (A) holds, with one part wrong. On the training rows the league model's expectation for pitches that end outside runs 8.2% (as of 2025-07-01) and 8.7% (2026-08-01) above actual swings, fastballs 15%, breaking balls 2%, offspeed 6%; pitches that end inside run 3.6% below; pitches that looked like strikes and ended outside 12 to 13% above. The rows after the as-of date look the same (8.6% and 10.9%), so it is the model's structure, not drift. The wrong part: the excess is not at the edge. It is about 1% within 0.1 ft of the edge and grows with distance: 4 to 5% at 0.1 to 0.25 ft, 10 to 11% at 0.25 to 0.5 ft and 20% at 0.5 to 1 ft. The hitter maps carry the same excess (they are fitted on the league's offset).
columns.Disposition and evidence: (A) holds; the excess grows with distance outside; SWING-CROSS-01 registered

CAL-01.status: (A) holds; the excess grows with distance outside; SWING-CROSS-01 registered

columns.Attempt: The league swing model reads where the pitch crossed as well as where it looked at the decision moment (CAL-01's finding). A crossing block is added to the league swing model in the report (tools/brl_report.py, params swing_cross) and in the structural engine that prices aims (tools/brl_discovery.py PAModels, the same flag): the signed distance from the true crossing to the nearest zone edge (negative inside), hat basis at -1, -0.5, -0.25, 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 ft, by family, 24 columns at the end of the design. The hitter maps stay on the decision moment and are refitted on the new offset. A scattered aim's crossing moves with it (the pool swaps the crossing part of the logit). Smoke test on a synthetic world (scratch cross/smoke.py): runs both ways, the pitcher-propensity weight read by its index rather than as the last column. Measured with CAL-01's diagnostic, now with log loss sums: as of 2025-07-01 and 2026-08-01, the term off and on (four report-lane runs, calibration only). **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the runs.** Prediction: with the term, on the rows after the as-of date, the expectation for pitches ending outside is 0.98 to 1.02 of actual swings in both runs (fastballs 0.96 to 1.04) and for pitches ending inside 0.98 to 1.02; the log loss over all later pitches improves by 1 to 15 nats per 1,000 for the league model and for the maps; the maps' gain over the league on later outside pitches stays within 70% to 110% of its value without the term. Gate, in both runs: outside 0.97 to 1.03 overall and 0.95 to 1.05 for each family, inside 0.97 to 1.03; the league's and the maps' log loss over all later pitches lower than without the term; the maps' outside gain at least 70% of its value without the term. If the gate holds, the term goes on in the daily report and the engine, and the aims are re-priced (VALUE-18's lane) before any run figure is stated again; the figures now on the site were priced with the decision-moment model alone. **Results (runs 38061589673 and 38061613146 as of 2025-07-01, 38061636214 and 38061660303 as of 2026-08-01; scratch cross/compare.py):** on the later rows the expectation for pitches ending outside went from 1.086 to 1.008 (2025) and 1.110 to 1.024 (2026) of actual swings; fastballs 1.157 to 1.010 and 1.194 to 1.040, breaking balls 1.018 to 1.003 and 1.037 to 1.016, offspeed 1.065 to 1.013 and 1.063 to 1.006; inside 0.973 to 1.009 and 0.975 to 1.011; the excess by distance outside is gone (half a foot to a foot out: 1.201 to 1.007 and 1.266 to 1.045). Log loss over all later pitches: league -7.47 and -6.74 nats per 1,000, maps -5.69 and -5.28; the maps' gain over the league on later outside pitches kept 86% and 89% (20.98 to 18.05, 22.08 to 19.66). The prediction held except the 2026 outside level (1.024 against the predicted 1.02 at most; inside the gate). **Gate passed in both runs: on in the daily report and the engine from October 10, 2026** (tools/brl_report.py SWING_CROSS true). The hitter cards' run figures and the plans are re-priced by the report itself at the next build; the stated aiming figures wait for VALUE-18X (the How page and METHODS.md say so). Reports built before the switch keep their old grades until they are rebuilt.
columns.Disposition and evidence: gate passed; adopted October 10, 2026

columns.Attempt: The aiming value re-priced with the corrected swing model (SWING-CROSS-01). VALUE-18F's run repeated exactly (value2_study, seasons 2023 to 2026, final_eval on the later-period months August 1 to September 27, 2026, maps and the league from 2023-2025, 0.6 ft of scatter, within type, specific, pitch estimand, pool from training, reprice boundary, bands and structural, 200 resamples, five placebo draws) with params swing_cross true: the study's league swing model and the engine (PAModels) both read where the pitch crossed, and a scattered aim's crossing moves with it. These months are reused validation (rule 6), not untouched; this is a re-pricing of a stated figure after a model fix, not a new test. Smoke test on a synthetic world (scratch cross/smoke_value.py): runs both ways. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) the structural outside-only figure between -30 and -48 runs per 6,200 plate appearances (VALUE-18F -43.5); (2) the own part's calibration slope outside between 0.88 and 1.05 (0.960); (3) the pitch-estimand regression figure (points, 0.6 ft) between -20 and -35 (-29.4). Decision rule: the aiming figure stated on the site and in METHODS.md becomes this run's, the structural figure with the regression's beside it, written as a range rounded to 5 runs, and the inside part re-priced the same way; if (1) falls under 30 the structural figure is stated all the same; the Report tool's calibration constants (0.95 outside, 0.82 inside) are replaced by the measured slopes if either differs by more than 0.05. **Results (run 38062560248, 184,318 test pitches, 412 hitters):** structural outside-only -42.3 runs per 6,200 plate appearances [-45.2, -39.4] (VALUE-18F -43.5), inside -22.7 (-23.3); own-part calibration slope 0.967 [0.928, 1.012] outside and 0.822 inside (0.960 and 0.830); the pitch-estimand regression's figure (points, 0.6 ft) -29.4 [-34.0, -25.1] (unchanged), by side -24.2; the structural choices priced by the band regression -25.0. The engine still prices an extra swing about 35% higher than the realized outcomes of these months (-0.00118 against -0.00087 per point). (1), (2) and (3) held. Under the rule the stated figure becomes about 30 to 40 runs over a team's season from outside pitches (42 by the engine's components, 29 by realized outcomes; the earlier 30 to 45 came from rounding 43.5 up), the inside part about 23; the calibration constants stay 0.95 and 0.82 (measured 0.967 and 0.822, within 0.05).
