columns.Attempt: The other pieces the plans are priced with, checked the way CAL-01 checked the swing model (diagnostic, descriptive): the whiff model on swings, the called-strike model on takes and the foul model on contact, expected against actual on the training rows and the rows after the as-of date, by season, family and the signed distance from the true crossing to the nearest zone edge (eight bands from half a foot inside to half a foot outside). Motivation: VALUE-18F and VALUE-18X found the engine pricing an extra swing about 35% higher than the realized outcomes show; a miscalibrated piece would be one source. Report lane, tools/brl_report.py calibration_components (with calibration_diag), as of 2025-07-01 and 2026-08-01, calibration only, sums only. What I expect, written before the runs: whiff and foul within 3% overall on the later rows; the called-strike model off by 5% or more in some edge band on 2026 rows, because 2026 locations are measured at the middle of the plate and the zone is the ABS zone (rule 5) while the model mixes seasons. A piece off by more than 3% overall or 8% in a band with at least 5,000 rows gets its own registered fix. **Results (runs 38064418743 as of 2025-07-01 and 38064444024 as of 2026-08-01):** the whiff and foul models are calibrated (later rows 0.991 and 0.996 whiff, 1.001 and 0.986 foul; every edge band within 4%). The called-strike model is not: it mixes seasons, and the edge calls move from season to season. On the later rows it calls 3.2% and 3.1% too many strikes overall, and in the bands just off the plate far too many: 1.117 (2025) and 1.382 (2026) within 0.1 ft outside, 1.298 and 1.568 at 0.1 to 0.25 ft, 1.06 within 0.1 ft inside; offspeed 1.07 and 1.09. On the training rows the same model is low on the earlier season and high on the later one in every edge band (2026 rows 1.380 against 2025 rows 0.829 just outside), so each newer season calls fewer strikes off the plate than the one before (2026: the ABS zone and the location measured at the middle of the plate, rule 5). This is a priced piece: a take just off the plate is valued as too likely a strike, which overprices takes and strike-stealing aims there and shifts the count chain's strikeouts and walks. Registered fix: CS-SEASON-01.
columns.Disposition and evidence: the called-strike model miscalibrated at the edges by season; CS-SEASON-01 registered

columns.Attempt: Each season's own called-strike profile at the zone edge (CAL-02's finding). The called-strike model (report and engine) gets a block per season: hats on the signed edge distance at the true crossing (the location block's knots), zero outside the row's season (tools/brl_discovery.py cs_season_block, params cs_season). Today's pitches are priced with the target season's profile: the as-of year once it has 20,000 training takes, else the latest earlier season (cs_target_season); the calibration check reads each row with its own season's. Smoke test on a synthetic world (scratch cross/smoke_cs.py): runs, falls back to the earlier season early in a season. columns.Attempt: Where the engine's price of a swing parts from what swings produce (diagnostic, descriptive). VALUE-18F, 18X and 18Y all found the engine pricing an extra swing on an outside pitch about 35% higher than the realized outcomes show (-0.00118 against -0.00087 runs per point); CAL-02 found the whiff and foul models calibrated and the called-strike model off at the edge (now PROD-05). This checks the whole chain the plans are priced with: the engine's value of a swing (whiff, foul, the run value of a ball in play, the count values) and of a take (called strike, the count values), against the value of the state each swing and take actually led to (the next count, or the plate appearance's result when it ended), on the same pitches, and the ball-in-play value alone on balls in play. League level with each row's own hitter and pitcher scalars, no maps. Report lane, tools/brl_report.py calibration_values (params calibration_values), as of 2025-07-01 and 2026-08-01, calibration only, sums only, the season strike profile on. Smoke test on a synthetic world (scratch cross/smoke_cal3.py): runs; there the swing value is 10 to 13% less costly to the hitter than what the swings produced, in sample and later, so part of any gap can come from multiplying calibrated pieces. What I expect, written before the runs: on outside pitches the engine's swing value is more costly to the hitter than what the swings produced, by 10% or more, with the ball-in-play value as the main source (the linear in-play model does not know a chase put in play often finds a hole); the take value within 5%; the in-play value within 3% overall. A piece off by more than 5% overall or 10% outside gets its own registered fix. **Results (runs 38070193906 as of 2025-07-01 and 38070209581 as of 2026-08-01; engine against realized, runs per 100 decisions on the later rows):** (1) outside pitches, where the aiming value lives, are priced right: swings -8.86 against -9.01 (2025) and -9.04 against -9.26 (2026), takes +3.30 against +3.29 and +3.82 against +3.83, so the engine's swing-minus-take value there, about -0.12 runs per extra swing, is what the average outside swing and take produce. The expectation was wrong: the 35% gap to the realized-outcome regression is not a miscalibrated piece; it says the swings a hitter's own tendency adds cost him less than the average chase there (one reading, not tested: a hitter who chases a spot more also handles it better), which is why the stated range carries both figures. (2) Inside the zone the engine prices swings as worse for the hitter than they were: -1.92 against -1.28 (2025) and -2.06 against -1.68 (2026), the same on the training rows (-1.96 against -1.50 and -2.01 against -1.47), all of it in counts with fewer than two strikes (2025 even or ahead -2.52 against -1.47, behind +2.11 against +2.87; two strikes -3.85 against -3.79) and most in the heart of the plate (more than half a foot inside +0.39 against +1.45). Since it shows in sample, it is structure, not drift. (3) Takes inside are close (-3.90 against -4.08 and -3.54 against -3.73). (4) The value of a ball in play moves with the period: 4.69 against 5.01 per 100 balls in play in July to September 2025 (6% low) and 4.60 against 4.26 in August and September 2026 (8% high), while in sample it matches (4.53 against 4.40 and 4.69 against 4.60). Both (2) and (4) are past the row's bar and get their own work: CAL-03b finds which piece makes (2) (whiff, foul or in play, by count), and the in-play level by period is a separate fix.
columns.Disposition and evidence: diagnostic; outside priced right; inside swings and the in-play level off

columns.Attempt: Which piece makes CAL-03's inside-swing gap (diagnostic, descriptive): CAL-03's runs repeated with the swing's pieces summed on the same rows, expected against actual: misses (the whiff model), fouls ((1 - miss) times the foul model), balls in play ((1 - miss) times (1 - foul)) and their value, by zone, family, count group and edge band (tools/brl_report.py calibration_values). Smoke test on a synthetic world: runs; there the whiff sum matches in sample (8,327 against 8,327) but fouls come out 11% short and balls in play 8% long, so multiplying a calibrated miss model by a foul model fit only on contact can miss even in sample. What I expect, written before the runs: the same pattern on real pitches, fouls short and balls in play long in counts with fewer than two strikes, which is CAL-03's gap (a foul there costs the hitter a strike, a ball in play pays him). **Results (runs 38070947538 as of 2025-07-01 and 38070963183 as of 2026-08-01):** misses are right (training rows 22,160 expected against 22,258 and 21,993 against 22,015) but fouls come out long and balls in play short, on the training rows as much as later: fouls 43,506 expected against 37,384 and 44,367 against 37,574 (16 to 18% high), balls in play 30,038 against 35,264 and 29,186 against 35,171 (15 to 17% low); the in-play value given contact is close. That is CAL-03's inside gap: in counts with fewer than two strikes a foul costs the hitter a strike and a ball in play pays him. The direction was the reverse of the expectation, and the size points at a bug, not a fit: the foul model was fit with the hitter's whiff propensity as an input and the engine evaluates it at zero. columns.Attempt: Where the engine's price of an extra chase parts from what chases produce (diagnostic, descriptive). CAL-03 found the average outside swing and take priced right, so the gap behind the stated range (the engine's -0.00118 runs per point of swing chance against -0.00087 from realized outcomes, VALUE-18F to 18Z) is about which swings a hitter's own tendency adds. This splits the later rows' pitches out of the zone, for hitters with maps, by the hitter's own part at the pitch (his map's swing chance minus an average hitter's with his same levels: under -10, -10 to -5, -5 to 0, 0 to 5, 5 to 10, over 10 points) and sums, per bin: swings against the map's and the league's expectation, misses against the whiff maps' and the league's, the engine's swing value with his maps and without them against what the swings produced, the take value against what the takes produced, and the ball-in-play value. Report lane, tools/brl_report.py calibration_maps (params calibration_maps), as of 2025-07-01 and 2026-08-01, calibration only, every correction of October 10 on. Smoke test on a synthetic world (scratch cross/smoke_cal4.py): runs. What I expect, written before the runs: the swings are calibrated by the maps in every bin (the record's bins already show it); the engine's swing value with maps is close to realized in the low bins but more costly to the hitter than realized in the high bins (over 5 points), by 10 to 30%, because a hitter who chases a spot more also makes better contact there than his whiff map and his contact level say. If so, a registered fix follows (the hitter's contact by location in the engine). **Results (runs 38076327570 as of 2025-07-01 and 38076342985 as of 2026-08-01; about 450 hitters, 159,000 and 103,000 later pitches out of the zone):** the swing maps are right in every bin (expected against actual swings within 1 to 5%). The whiff maps are too flat: hitters whose map says they lay off a spot miss more when they do swing there than the map says (under -10 points: 2,088 expected against 2,319 actual and 1,332 against 1,473, 10% short), and hitters whose map says they chase a spot miss less (over 10 points: 3,595 against 3,472 and 2,360 against 2,220, 4 to 6% long). So the realized value of a swing improves from the low bins to the high ones more than the engine's does (2025: realized -0.108 runs per swing under -10 to -0.087 over 10, engine with maps -0.101 to -0.089; 2026: -0.115 to -0.086 against -0.105 to -0.090). The take value is right in every bin (within 0.002). The expectation had the direction right but the size and shape wrong: the miss is a gradient across both ends, 7 to 9% at the low end and 0 to 9% at the high end, not 10 to 30% at the high end. It is in the whiff maps, not the contact value. Follow-up: WHIFF-LAM-01 (less shrinkage for the whiff maps).

The whiff maps' penalty toward the league drops from 30 to 10 in the report and the engine (tools/brl_report.py LAM_W, params lam_w; the same maps feed the plans' pricing, the miss grids and the player cards). Measured with CAL-04's split, now over pitches in and out of the zone, as of 2025-07-01 and 2026-08-01, penalty 10 against 30 with every other piece the same (four calibration-only runs). Smoke test on a synthetic world: runs. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the runs.** Gate, in both runs: (1) whiff log loss of the maps on the later swings lower with 10, on pitches out of the zone and on all pitches; (2) misses expected against actual on pitches out of the zone in the two extreme bins closer to 1 than with 30, the bin under -10 at 0.95 or above and the bin over 10 at 1.03 or below. Prediction: log loss lower by 1 to 5 nats per 1,000 swings out of the zone and by 0 to 3 on all swings; the extreme bins 0.94 to 0.98 and 1.00 to 1.03. If it holds: 10 on in the report and the engine, the aiming value re-priced, the reports rebuilt. **Results (2025-07-01: runs 38077001415 with 30, 38077015748 with 10; 2026-08-01: 38077031101, 38077049003):** gate not met. Out of the zone the looser maps help (log loss -0.83 and -0.85 nats per 1,000 swings; the extreme bins 0.901 to 0.927 and 1.035 to 1.010, 0.905 to 0.937 and 1.062 to 1.035), but over all swings log loss is worse (+0.16 and +0.21), and the bin under -10 stays below 0.95. Inside the zone the same gradient shows (2026: under -10 at 0.950, over 10 at 1.127 with 30). So shrinkage is not the cause: the hitters who swing more at a spot miss less there than any location map says, in and out of the zone. Not adopted; the penalty stays 30. Follow-up: WHIFF-OWN-01 (the hitter's swing tendency at the pitch as an input to the whiff model).
columns.Disposition and evidence: gate not met; not adopted

columns.Attempt: The hitter's own swing tendency at the pitch as an input to the engine's whiff model (CAL-04 and WHIFF-LAM-01: a hitter who swings more at a spot misses less there than any location map says, in and out of the zone). One column, the hitter's swing map's part at the pitch in logit units (zero for a hitter without a map), in the league whiff model and in the foul model that shares its inputs; the whiff maps are fit on top of it, and plans price a hitter's swings with his own part at each spot (tools/brl_discovery.py PAModels whiff_own; tools/brl_report.py WHIFF_OWN, params whiff_own). The report's own count chain and the player cards keep the location-only whiff model. Smoke test on a synthetic world (scratch cross/smoke_wo.py): runs, and the weight comes out near zero there (+0.004), where no such link was built in. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the runs.** Measured with CAL-04's split as of 2025-07-01 and 2026-08-01, against WHIFF-LAM-01's runs with penalty 30 (38077001415, 38077031101; the code without the input is unchanged). Gate, in both runs: (1) whiff log loss of the maps on the later swings lower, out of the zone and over all swings; (2) misses expected against actual in the two extreme bins out of the zone within 0.95 to 1.05 (from 0.901 and 0.905 under -10, 1.035 and 1.062 over 10). Prediction: the input's weight negative; log loss lower by 1 to 5 nats per 1,000 swings out of the zone and 0.5 to 3 over all; the extreme bins 0.95 to 1.00 and 1.00 to 1.04. If it holds: on in the engine, the aiming value re-priced, the reports rebuilt. **Results (runs 38077717228 as of 2025-07-01 and 38077734656 as of 2026-08-01, against 38077001415 and 38077031101):** gate not met, on (1). Out of the zone it does what it should: log loss -0.88 and -1.12 nats per 1,000 swings, the extreme bins 0.979 and 0.985 (2025), 0.990 and 1.001 (2026), and the engine's swing value now follows what the swings produced across the bins (2026 under -10: -0.111 against -0.115 realized, was -0.105; over 10: -0.086 against -0.086, was -0.090). Inside the zone one shared weight overcorrects: the low bins go from 0.905 and 0.950 to 1.046 and 1.107, and over all swings log loss is slightly worse (+0.10 and +0.04). The link between swinging more and missing less is stronger out of the zone than in it. Not adopted. Follow-up: WHIFF-OWN-02, one weight out of the zone and one inside, gated on windows these runs have not seen.
columns.Disposition and evidence: gate not met; not adopted

columns.Attempt: WHIFF-OWN-01 with one weight for pitches that cross out of the zone and one for pitches that cross in it (two columns, the hitter's swing map's part times each zone indicator; params whiff_own 2), in the league whiff model and the foul model that shares its inputs; plans price each spot with the weight for where it crosses. Smoke test on a synthetic world (scratch cross/smoke_wo.py): runs; settings 0 and 1 reproduce the earlier numbers exactly. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the runs.** Gated on windows WHIFF-OWN-01 did not use: as of 2024-07-01 (a season no whiff run has looked at) and 2026-06-01, CAL-04's split, the input on (2) against off (0) with everything else the same (four calibration-only runs). Gate, in both runs: (1) whiff log loss of the maps on the later swings lower, out of the zone and over all swings; (2) misses expected against actual in the two extreme bins out of the zone within 0.95 to 1.05; (3) the two extreme bins inside the zone within 0.92 to 1.08. Prediction: the weight out of the zone negative and larger than inside; log loss lower by 0.5 to 1.5 nats per 1,000 swings out of the zone and 0.1 to 1.0 over all; the extreme bins out of the zone 0.96 to 1.03, inside 0.93 to 1.07. If it holds: on in the engine (WHIFF_OWN 2), the aiming value re-priced, the reports rebuilt. **Results (2024-07-01: runs 38078219957 off, 38078235263 on; 2026-06-01: 38078251696, 38078267690):** gate not met, on (2). (1) held: log loss -0.44 and -1.10 nats per 1,000 swings out of the zone, -0.01 and -0.32 over all. (3) held: inside extremes 1.074 and 1.070 (2024), 0.997 and 1.064 (2026). (2) did not: out of the zone the low bin is now right (1.038, 1.026, from 0.905 and 0.878) but the high bin overshoots (0.945 and 0.922, from 1.040 and 1.029). In run values the engine now follows what the swings produced across the bins much more closely (2026 under -10: -0.114 against -0.112 realized, was -0.103; over 10: -0.084 against -0.086, was -0.090). The weight is fit on the training rows with each hitter's swing map from those same rows, which likely overstates it; not adopted. Follow-up: WHIFF-OWN-03, the weight fit with each half of a hitter's training games read by the map from the other half.
columns.Disposition and evidence: gate not met; not adopted

columns.Attempt: WHIFF-OWN-02 with the weights fit by cross-fitting: each hitter's training games split by game number into two halves, each half's rows read by the swing map fit on the other half, so a map's in-sample fit does not inflate the weights; plans and later rows still use the full maps, and the whiff maps are fit on top of the full-map offset (params whiff_own 3). Smoke test on a synthetic world (scratch cross/smoke_wo.py): runs; settings 0 and 2 reproduce their earlier numbers. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the runs.** Gated on windows no whiff run has used: as of 2024-09-01 and 2025-05-01, CAL-04's split, on (3) against off (0), four calibration-only runs. Gate, in both runs: (1) whiff log loss of the maps on the later swings lower, out of the zone and over all swings; (2) the two extreme bins out of the zone within 0.95 to 1.05; (3) the two extreme bins inside within 0.92 to 1.08. Prediction: weights smaller than WHIFF-OWN-02's in size; log loss lower by 0.3 to 1.2 nats per 1,000 swings out of the zone and 0 to 0.5 over all; the extreme bins out of the zone 0.96 to 1.04. If it holds: on in the engine (WHIFF_OWN 3), the aiming value re-priced, the reports rebuilt. **Results (2024-09-01: runs 38078867274 off, 38078880836 on; 2025-05-01: 38078896258, 38078911772):** gate not met. 2024-09-01 passed every part (log loss -1.72 out of the zone and -0.35 over all; extremes out of the zone 0.982 and 0.955, inside 1.013 and 1.018). 2025-05-01 did not: log loss -0.20 out of the zone but +0.01 over all, the high bin out of the zone 0.942 and the high bin inside 1.081. Cross-fitting did not take out the overshoot at the high end. Across WHIFF-OWN-01 to 03 the pattern holds in every window: a hitter's swing tendency at a spot carries real information about his misses there, most at the low end (hitters who rarely chase a spot miss more when they do), but one straight-line weight on it overcorrects the heavy chasers. Not adopted; the engine keeps the location-only whiff model. The next step would give the input a curved shape, gated on windows not yet used; left open.
columns.Disposition and evidence: gate not met; not adopted; open

WHIFF-OWN-03.status: gate not met; not adopted; open

columns.Attempt: The curved version of WHIFF-OWN-03: the hitter's swing tendency at the pitch enters the whiff and foul models with separate slopes below zero (a hitter who lays off the spot) and above zero (one who chases it), each separately out of the zone and in it (four columns), cross-fitted as in WHIFF-OWN-03 (params whiff_own 4). Smoke test on a synthetic world (scratch cross/smoke_wo.py): runs; settings 0 and 3 reproduce their earlier numbers. The last attempt in this line: if it misses, the whiff input stays out and the question is closed for this season. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the runs.** Gated on windows no whiff run has used: as of 2024-05-01 and 2025-09-01, CAL-04's split, on (4) against off (0), four calibration-only runs. Gate, in both runs: (1) whiff log loss of the maps on the later swings lower, out of the zone and over all swings; (2) the two extreme bins out of the zone within 0.95 to 1.05; (3) the two extreme bins inside within 0.92 to 1.08. Prediction: the slope below zero out of the zone the largest in size; log loss lower by 0.5 to 2 nats per 1,000 swings out of the zone and 0 to 0.6 over all; the extreme bins out of the zone 0.96 to 1.04. If it holds: on in the engine (WHIFF_OWN 4), the aiming value re-priced, the reports rebuilt. **Results (2024-05-01: runs 38079508737 off, 38079523133 on; 2025-09-01: 38079538492, 38079555198):** gate not met, on (2) in both and (1) in 2024 (log loss -0.17 out of the zone but +0.08 over all; 2025: -0.91 and -0.17). The low bin out of the zone is fixed (1.028 and 1.001, from 0.909 and 0.891) but the high bin overshoots again (0.941 and 0.936, from 1.041 and 1.041), a separate slope notwithstanding. One likely reason: maps fit on half a hitter's games are shrunk more, so the cross-fitted weights are learned on smaller values than the full maps the plans use. In run values the engine with the input tracks what the swings produced at both ends (2025 under -10: -0.112 against -0.115 realized; over 10: -0.082 against -0.082), which is the part the aiming value depends on, but the registered gate was on misses. As written in the row, the line is closed for this season: the engine keeps the location-only whiff model, and the stated range keeps both figures.

WHIFF-OWN-04.status: gate not met; closed for the season

columns.Attempt: The lineup before one is posted. The simulator and the game plans use the team's most recent lineup (rule 'last'). A manager sets his lineup by the opposing starter's hand, so the alternative is the team's most recent lineup against a starter of today's opposing starter's hand within 30 days, else the last one (rule 'hand', brl_live/lineups.py). Measured in the report lane (params lineup_study; tools/brl_report.py lineup_study) on every team-game of 2025 and 2026 in the pitch table (regular season and postseason), from the team's games on earlier days only; today's opposing starter's hand is the actual starter's (live, the probable pitcher's). Metrics: starters named (the projection's nine against the actual nine, 0 to 9) and right spots; differences paired by team-game, 95% intervals by bootstrap over team-months (4,000 draws). Settings fixed before the run: 30 days for 'hand'; for LINEUP-02, 10 games, 45 days and 5 games. Smoke test on a synthetic platoon (brl_live_tests/test_lineups.py). **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Gate, in each of 2025 and 2026: starters named, hand minus last, with the 95% interval above zero; right spots not lower by more than 0.25 per team-game. Prediction: 'last' names 7.4 to 7.9 of 9; the opposing hand differs from the last game's in 30 to 40% of team-games, and there 'hand' names 0.6 to 1.2 more; overall +0.2 to +0.4. If it holds: 'hand' is the rule in the simulator and the plans (brl_live/lineups.py RULE), unless LINEUP-02 holds too. **Results (run 38082910875, receipt research/report-38082910875.json):** gate met. Starters named, hand minus last: 2025 +0.42 [0.37, 0.46] (6.87 to 7.29 of 9, 4,954 team-games), 2026 +0.50 [0.46, 0.54] (6.83 to 7.33, 4,906); right spots +0.62 [0.54, 0.70] and +0.70 [0.61, 0.78]. Where today's opposing hand differs from the last game's (40% of team-games in 2025, 44% in 2026): +1.04 and +1.12. Predictions: the level of 'last' wrong (6.83 to 6.87 against 7.4 to 7.9); the changed share a little above its range; the gain where it changed inside; overall above. Postseason (94 and 48 team-games): +0.22 both years, intervals wide. On from the commit that recorded this result: brl_live/lineups.py RULE 'hand', in the simulator (projected lineups) and the game plans.
columns.Disposition and evidence: passed; on

columns.Attempt: The usual lineup against that hand (rule 'freq'): over the team's last 10 games against a starter of that hand within 45 days, the nine with the most starts, among hitters who batted in one of the team's last 5 games or started the latest of those 10, in their average batting spot. It keeps a regular through his day off and keeps the platoon. Same run and metrics as LINEUP-01. **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Gate, in each of 2025 and 2026: starters named, freq minus hand, with the 95% interval above zero; right spots not lower than 'hand' by more than 0.5 per team-game. Prediction: +0.1 to +0.3 starters named over 'hand'; right spots lower by 0 to 0.4. If both gates hold, 'freq' is the rule; if only LINEUP-01, 'hand'; if neither, 'last' stays. **Results (same run):** gate not met. Starters named, freq minus hand: +0.10 [0.07, 0.14] in 2025 and +0.12 [0.09, 0.15] in 2026 (that part held), but right spots lower by 0.99 [0.89, 1.08] and 1.10 [0.99, 1.21] (limit 0.5): ordering the nine by their average spot scrambles the order. Prediction on spots wrong (0 to 0.4). Stays off; 'hand' is the rule.
columns.Disposition and evidence: failed (batting spots); off

columns.Attempt: The last lineup against today's hand, with the regulars back (rule 'swap'): LINEUP-01's lineup, except that a hitter in it who started at most 30% of the team's last 10 games against that hand (within 45 days, at least 5 such games) gives his spot to the hitter not in it who started at least 60% of them and batted in one of the team's last 5 games, the least-started first. It keeps LINEUP-01's batting order and fixes a lineup copied from a regular's day off, which is where LINEUP-02 found its extra starters. Same study (params lineup_study), now also on 2024, which no lineup rule has been chosen on (2023 loaded for history when the table has it). **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Gate: in 2024, starters named, swap minus hand, with the 95% interval above zero, and right spots not lower by more than 0.1 per team-game; in 2025 and 2026 (used to choose 'hand'), starters named above zero. Prediction: +0.05 to +0.15 starters named; right spots within 0.05 either way. If it holds, 'swap' is the rule (brl_live/lineups.py RULE). **Results (run 38087732321, receipt research/report-38087732321.json):** gate not met. 2024 (4,944 team-games): starters named, swap minus hand, +0.070 [0.047, 0.093], but right spots lower by 0.103 [0.087, 0.120] (limit 0.1). 2025 +0.078 and 2026 +0.081 named (spots lower by 0.086 and 0.092). Prediction right on starters named, wrong on spots (the regular goes into the fill-in's spot, usually lower in the order than his own). Stays off; 'hand' stays the rule. The same run replicated LINEUP-01 on 2024, which no lineup rule was chosen on: hand minus last +0.45 [0.41, 0.50] starters named, +0.57 [0.49, 0.65] right spots.
columns.Disposition and evidence: failed (spots, by 0.003); off

Player pages open with percentile rankings the way the public player pages draw them: hitters on batting average, slugging, strikeout %, walk %, chase %, whiff % and hard-hit % (95 mph and up); pitchers on strikeout %, walk %, whiff %, chase %, hard-hit % against, average against and main fastball speed (four-seam or sinker, whichever he throws more). A separate review found six wording defects in these pieces, fixed in d99b9524e.

columns.Attempt: Do the hitter tags the plans print hold up on later pitches? (diagnostic with registered predictions) The page tags a hitter from his training pitches against the league with fixed thresholds (hitterTags): Chases a lot (chase rate 4 points or more over the league), Patient (6 under), Swings and misses (misses per swing 5 over), Puts the bat on the ball (7 under), Takes the first pitch and Swings at the first pitch (first-pitch swing rate 12 points under or over his side's league), Expands with two strikes and Shrinks the zone with two strikes (two-strike chase rate out of MLB's zones 11-14, 8 over or 10 under his side's league). For hitters with 300 or more training pitches, tags from 2024-2025 scored on 2026 regular-season pitches before August 1 (the matchup program's untouched months stay out) and tags from 2023-2024 scored on 2025: for each tag, the tagged hitters' rate minus the league's on the test pitches, weighted by their test pitches, with intervals from resampling hitters. Also the two-strike change against his own chase in the other counts, net of the league's change on his side: its season-to-season correlation, its correlation with his chase level, and tags at one standard deviation. Report lane, tools/brl_report.py tag_study (params tag_study), aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_tags.py): habits that carry over keep their tags, habits redrawn each season do not.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: each of the six chase, whiff and first-pitch tags holds in both test seasons (the tagged hitters' test difference in the tag's direction at least half its threshold, interval excluding zero). The two level two-strike tags hold too, mostly by repeating the chase tags: at least 60% of Expands with two strikes hitters also carry Chases a lot, and at least 50% of Shrinks the zone carry Patient. The relative two-strike change persists weakly: season-to-season correlation between 0.15 and 0.45. Decision rules: a tag that fails in either test season comes off the plans. If the relative change correlates 0.3 or more across seasons and its one-SD tags hold in both (test difference at least a third of the threshold in the tag's direction, interval excluding zero), the two-strike tags switch to the relative definition (what he does differently with two strikes); otherwise the level two-strike tags stay but are not shown next to the same-direction chase tag, where they say nothing new. **Results (run 38109976267; cards for 610 and 604 hitters, 395 and 419 with 200 or more test pitches), test difference against the league in points, training difference in brackets, 2026 (tags from 2024-2025) then 2025 (from 2023-2024):** Chases a lot +7.0 [+7.9] and +7.3 [+8.3]; Patient -8.0 [-8.6] and -7.1 [-8.6]; Swings and misses +7.5 [+7.7] and +6.3 [+7.8]; Puts the bat on the ball -9.2 [-10.0] and -9.3 [-9.7]; Takes the first pitch -12.9 [-15.2] and -12.8 [-14.4]; Swings at the first pitch +10.7 [+15.4] and +13.7 [+15.7]; Expands with two strikes +9.8 [+11.9] and +10.8 [+12.2]; Shrinks the zone -9.7 [-12.0] and -8.3 [-12.6]; every interval excludes zero and every tag passes half its threshold. Overlap: 75% and 78% of Expands hitters also carry Chases a lot, 66% and 73% of Shrinks carry Patient (predicted at least 60% and 50%: held). The relative two-strike change correlates 0.64 (320 hitters) and 0.72 (345) across seasons, far above the 0.15 to 0.45 predicted (that prediction missed: it is a stable habit), and -0.31 and -0.34 with the chase level (big chasers rise less from their own base). columns.Attempt: Expected hot zones. A raw zone rate over two seasons rests on 5 to 150 at-bats a zone, so much of the chart is noise. Candidates for a hitter's rate in each of MLB's 13 zones, from training seasons only: raw (his own count ratio); league (the league's rate in that zone for his side); scaled (the league's zone rate times his own overall rate over the league's, his level on the league's shape); and shrunk (his counts plus m pseudo-events at the scaled rate, m fitted). Metrics: batting average per at-bat ending there, swing rate per pitch, miss rate per swing (binary log loss per event) and slugging per at-bat (squared error weighted by at-bats). Regular-season pitches, hitters with 100 or more plate appearances in training; m chosen on training 2023 and 2024 scored on 2025, then everything scored once on training 2024 and 2025 against 2026 (the two-season window the cards use); paired bootstrap over hitters (2,000 draws). tools/brl_report.py zone_shrink_study, report lane, aggregates only
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026: (1) shrunk beats raw on all four metrics with the interval excluding zero; (2) shrunk beats scaled on swing and miss rates with the interval excluding zero (hitters have zone patterns of their own beyond level and league shape); (3) on batting average and slugging shrunk is no worse than scaled (upper end at most +0.0005 nats per at-bat, +0.002 squared error). Decision rule: if (1) holds, the hot-zone charts get an Expected view (shrunk at the fitted m, or scaled where (2) or (3) favors it) beside the standard view, which stays the default; if (1) fails, no Expected view. Results (run 38106740119, receipt research/report-38106740119.json; 462 hitters scored on 2026, 139,165 at-bats, 600,794 pitches, 284,697 swings; m chosen on 2023-2024 to 2025): batting average m 160, shrunk minus raw **-0.0349 nats per at-bat [-0.0428, -0.0278]**, minus scaled -0.00045 [-0.00070, -0.00021], minus league -0.00023 [-0.00080, +0.00035] (raw zone averages predict worse than the league's: 0.5773 against 0.5427); swing rate m 80, shrunk minus raw **-0.0024 [-0.0029, -0.0020]**, minus scaled **-0.0041 [-0.0051, -0.0033]**; miss rate m 80, shrunk minus raw **-0.0089 [-0.0120, -0.0064]**, minus scaled **-0.0030 [-0.0038, -0.0023]**; slugging m 160, shrunk minus raw **-0.0155 squared error [-0.0174, -0.0136]**, minus scaled -0.00052 [-0.00090, -0.00014]. **(1), (2) and (3) held.** Reading: a two-season zone batting average or slugging is mostly noise (shrinking 160 at-bats toward the hitter's level on the league's zone shape predicts the next season far better), while hitters' swing and miss patterns by zone are real and their own. Decision: the charts get an Expected view (shrunk at m 160 for average and slugging, 80 for swing and miss rates; the prior from the same hand and pitch type as the chart, a use the pooled test did not check separately); the standard view stays the default.

columns.Attempt: The hot zones' Expected view against one hand anchors each hitter's level on his own pitches against that hand (ZONES-02). SPLITS-01 found a hitter's own level against a hand, beyond his side's usual split, mostly does not carry over (AVG and SLG r 0.06). Candidate 'anchored': the prior's level from all his pitches of the same family against both hands, relative to his side's league rate on them, applied to the league's zone rates for this hand; m refitted on the same grid. Subsets: pitches from right-handed pitchers and from left-handed pitchers (these decide), and the six hand-by-family crosses the plan rows show (reported). Same windows and hitters as ZONES-02: m chosen on 2023-2024 to 2025, scored once on 2024-2025 to 2026, 100 or more plate appearances in the subset in training, paired bootstrap over hitters (2,000 draws). 2026 was scored before by ZONES-01 and ZONES-02 with other candidates, so this is later-period validation with adaptive reuse (evidence rule 6) and the decision is a product call on it. tools/brl_report.py zone_shrink_study with anchor, zone_estimates_anchored, report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_zone_study.py): with only the league split by hand, anchored beats shrunk; with a large own split by hand, the anchored prior misses it.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026: (1) against lefties, anchored beats shrunk on AVG and SLG with the interval excluding zero; (2) against righties, anchored is no worse than shrunk on any of the four metrics (upper end at most +0.0002 nats per event, +0.0005 squared error for SLG); (3) on swing and miss rates anchored is no worse than shrunk against either hand (the same bounds). Decision rule: if (1) and (2) hold, the page's Expected charts against a hand anchor AVG and SLG on his level against both hands (with the anchored m), and swing and miss rates too where (3) holds and anchored beats shrunk with the interval excluding zero; otherwise nothing changes. **Results (run 38128261865, receipt research/report-38128261865.json; 2026 scored once with this candidate):** anchored minus shrunk, nats per event (SLG squared error). Against lefties (328 hitters): AVG **-0.00115 [-0.00185, -0.00044]** (anchored m 320), SLG **-0.00129 [-0.00225, -0.00040]** (m 160), swing **-0.00032 [-0.00068, -0.000002]** (m 80), miss **-0.00065 [-0.00117, -0.00019]** (m 80). Against righties (427 hitters): AVG -0.00017 [-0.00036, +0.000012] (m 160), SLG -0.00006 [-0.00043, +0.00032] (m 160), swing **-0.000063 [-0.00014, -0.0000005]** (m 80), miss -0.000055 [-0.00018, +0.00007] (m 80). **(1), (2) and (3) held.** Crosses (reported): righty fastballs AVG -0.00033 [-0.00060, -0.00006], righty breaking balls AVG -0.00057 [-0.00100, -0.00016], lefty fastballs AVG -0.00106 [-0.00229, +0.00017]; no cross is worse with its interval excluding zero (lefty breaking balls had 42 hitters, lefty offspeed none at 100 plate appearances). Decision, as registered: Expected charts against a hand anchor AVG and SLG on his level against both hands (m 320 and 160 against lefties, 160 and 160 against righties), swing rates against both hands (m 80) and misses against lefties (m 80); misses against righties keep the old anchor (their interval includes zero). Every pitch-type chart against a hand uses the same anchoring, with the all-pitches m. Page HZ_ANCHOR and hzAnchor.

columns.Attempt: Expected zones for pitchers. The pitcher charts (Where he pitches: AVG, SLG, swing and miss rates against in MLB's 13 zones, to right- or left-handed batters) are raw counts over two seasons. ZONES-01's study read per pitcher (his throwing hand as his side; league rates for pitchers of his hand): raw, league, scaled (his level on the league's zone pattern) and shrunk (m fitted), on pitches to right-handed batters and to left-handed batters separately; pitchers with 100 or more batters faced on that side in training; m chosen on 2023-2024 to 2025, scored once on 2024-2025 to 2026 (pitcher zones were never scored before; the 2026 months after July are later-period validation, evidence rule 6); paired bootstrap over pitchers (2,000 draws). tools/brl_report.py zone_shrink_study with who 'pitcher' and a stand_r subset, report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_zone_study.py): planted pitcher zone patterns recovered.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026, in both batter-side subsets: (1) shrunk beats raw on all four metrics with the interval excluding zero; (2) on swing and miss rates against, shrunk beats scaled with the interval excluding zero; (3) on AVG and SLG against, shrunk is no worse than scaled (upper end at most +0.0005 nats per at-bat, +0.002 squared error). Decision rule: if (1) holds, the pitcher charts' AVG, SLG, swing and miss views get the Expected view (shrunk at the fitted m, or scaled where shrunk does not beat it), with the standard view the default; the location share stays as it is. To left-handed batters (402 pitchers): shrunk minus raw AVG **-0.108**, SLG **-0.042**, swing **-0.0056**, miss **-0.0304** (all intervals below zero); shrunk minus scaled AVG -0.00008 [-0.00020, +0.00005], SLG -0.00004 [-0.00014, +0.00007], swing **-0.0032 [-0.0039, -0.0025]**, miss **-0.0016 [-0.0023, -0.0010]**. **(1), (2) and (3) held.** Decision, as registered: the pitcher charts' AVG, SLG, swing and miss views get the Expected view; swing and miss shrunk at m 80, AVG and SLG at the scaled rate (shrunk did not beat it), the standard view the default (page PZ_EXP_M, pitcherZoneLegend).

columns.Attempt: Does a pitcher's own location pattern, laid over a hitter's expected zones, predict the hitter's results against that pitcher beyond the hitter's level on that pitch type? For each 2026 at-bat ending on a pitch of family f from pitcher p to hitter h: the composite E = the sum over MLB's 13 zones of p's share of family-f pitches to h's side in each zone (training seasons) times h's expected slugging there (ZONES-01's shrinkage, m 160, against p's hand and on family f); the baseline B = the same sum with the league's location shares for that hand, side and family instead of p's. Training 2024 and 2025, regular season; pitchers with 200 or more family-f pitches to that side in training, hitters with 100 or more plate appearances. Scored once on 2026 regular-season at-bats: squared error of total bases per at-bat for E against B, and the slope of actual minus B on E minus B, with bootstrap intervals by pitcher (2,000 draws). tools/brl_report.py matchup_read_study, report lane, aggregates only
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) the slope on E minus B is positive with the interval excluding zero; (2) E's squared error is below B's with the interval excluding zero. Decision rule: if (1) and (2) hold, a hitter's plan shows a matchup read per pitch type (his expected slugging where this pitcher throws it against where an average pitcher does), scaled by the slope; if only (1) holds, the read is shown as a lean with its slope; if (1) fails, no matchup read. Results (run 38108106040, receipt research/report-38108106040.json; 93,623 at-bats of 2026 against 472 pitchers): slope on E minus B **0.457 [0.107, 0.830]**; squared error E minus B **+0.000029 [-0.000222, +0.000273]** per at-bat; the composite moves from the baseline by 0.0185 total bases per at-bat (standard deviation), so after the slope a read would move expected slugging by about .008. Both sums sit about 0.05 below the actual mean (0.348 and 0.346 against 0.395) because the zone shares are of all pitches while the slugging is per at-bat ending there; the comparison is like for like. **(1) held, (2) failed.** Reading: where a pitcher puts the ball does carry into a hitter's results beyond his level on that pitch type, but the effect is far too small to plan on. Decision (product call, rule 3, superseding the registered lean): no matchup read on the page; a read that moves slugging by under .010 would only look like information.
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: (1) held, (2) failed; too small to show: no matchup read

columns.Attempt: How much of a hitter's split by pitcher hand carries over. The splits table and the hot-zone line against a hand show his raw AVG, SLG, chase and miss rates against right- and left-handed pitchers over two seasons; the plans read a hitter against the starter's hand. Candidates for his rates against each hand a season later, from training seasons only: raw (his rates by hand); league (his side's rates by hand); scaled (his overall level, lightly shrunk, times his side's league rates by hand); shrunk (his counts by hand plus m pseudo-events at the scaled rate, m fitted). Metrics: AVG and SLG per at-bat ended on the pitch, chase per pitch out of MLB's zone (11-14), misses per swing (log loss per event; squared error weighted by at-bats for SLG). Regular-season pitches, hitters with 300 or more plate appearances in training, switch hitters left out (a different side against the two hands, 30 or more pitches each); m chosen on 2023-2024 to 2025 from a grid of 0 to 6,400 and 1,000,000 (the scaled rate), then scored once on 2024-2025 to 2026 before August 1; paired bootstrap over hitters (2,000 draws). Also the carry-over of a hitter's own split beyond his side's (against lefties minus against righties, net of his side's league split): correlation and slope among hitters with 100 or more at-bats (300 pitches out of the zone or swings for chase and misses) against each hand in training and half that in the test. tools/brl_report.py split_shrink_study, report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_split_study.py): own splits of SD 0.12 log-odds planted, m 800, shrunk beats raw and scaled, carry-over 0.24 to 0.34; none planted, m 800 or more and carry-over near zero.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026: (1) shrunk beats raw on all four metrics with the interval excluding zero; (2) on AVG and SLG the fitted m is 400 at-bats or more and the carry-over correlation is under 0.25 (a hitter's own AVG or SLG split beyond his side's is mostly noise); (3) on chase and misses shrunk beats scaled with the interval excluding zero (his own swing-decision split by hand is his). Decision rule: if (1) holds, the splits table and the hot-zone line against a hand show Expected numbers (shrunk at the fitted m) when the page's Expected view is on, and the standard view stays the default; if (2) holds, the splits note says how little of an AVG or SLG split carries over, quoting the correlation; where shrunk does not beat scaled the Expected numbers use scaled. If (1) fails, nothing changes. **Results (run 38127261982, receipt research/report-38127261982.json; 317 hitters scored on 2026 before August 1, 123 of them left-handed, 77,486 at-bats, 176,103 pitches out of the zone, 158,335 swings; m chosen on 2023-2024 to 2025):** AVG m 6,400, shrunk minus raw **-0.00076 nats per at-bat [-0.00109, -0.00046]**, minus scaled -0.000001 [-0.000016, +0.000015], minus league -0.00023 [-0.00074, +0.00026]; own split carry-over r 0.06 [-0.08, 0.20] (190 hitters), slope 0.08; league split (lefties minus righties) -18 points for left-handed batters, +9 for right-handed. SLG m 3,200, shrunk minus raw **-0.00096 squared error [-0.00137, -0.00058]**, minus scaled +0.000028 [-0.000019, +0.000074]; carry-over r 0.06 [-0.09, 0.20], slope 0.09. Chase m 1,600, shrunk minus raw **-0.00033 [-0.00050, -0.00016]**, minus scaled -0.000054 [-0.000122, +0.000012]; carry-over r 0.28 [0.11, 0.42] (135 hitters), slope 0.41. Misses m 1,600, shrunk minus raw **-0.00024 [-0.00042, -0.00008]**, minus scaled **-0.000096 [-0.000167, -0.000030]**; carry-over r 0.39 [0.22, 0.53] (114 hitters), slope 0.58. **(1) held on all four; (2) held (m 6,400 and 3,200; r 0.06 and 0.06); (3) held for misses and failed for chase** (its interval includes zero, though the carry-over correlation is 0.28). Reading: a hitter's batting average and slugging against lefties and righties, beyond the usual edge for his side, is noise from one season to the next; the best guess is his level against everyone with his side's usual split. His miss rate split by hand is partly his own. Decision, as registered: the splits table and the hot-zone line against a hand show Expected numbers when the page's Expected view is on (AVG, SLG and chase scaled; misses shrunk at 1,600 swings toward scaled; switch hitters get none, the check left them out), and the splits note quotes the 0.06 carry-over. The standard view stays the default. Not changed: the hot-zone charts' Expected view still anchors each hand on his own level against that hand (ZONES-02); anchoring it on the split's expected level would need its own check.

columns.Attempt: Expected batting average and slugging, the way the public player pages compute them: each measured ball in play (no bunts) takes the league's hit rate and total bases for its exit speed and launch angle (3 mph by 4 degrees, backed off to 6 by 8 where a bin has under 30 balls; unmeasured balls in play at the league's unmeasured rates; strikeouts and other at-bats none), over his at-bats. Does a hitter's expected AVG (SLG) from two seasons predict his next season's AVG (SLG) better than his AVG (SLG)? Table and lines from the training seasons; hitters with 300 or more plate appearances in training and 150 in the test; squared error weighted by test at-bats; a blend weight on expected fitted on 2023-2024 to 2025; scored once on 2024-2025 to 2026 before August 1; intervals from resampling hitters (2,000 draws). tools/brl_report.py xstats_study, xs_table, xs_lines, report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_xstats_study.py): with results driven by contact quality, expected wins; with results driven by something else (speed), raw wins and the blend leans raw.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026: (1) expected AVG predicts AVG better than AVG does, interval excluding zero; (2) expected SLG predicts SLG better than SLG does, interval excluding zero; (3) the fitted blend puts at least half its weight on expected for both. Decision rule: for each of AVG and SLG where (1) or (2) holds, the hitter percentile rankings and cards add an Expected row (expected AVG, expected SLG, labeled as from how hard and at what angle he hits the ball); otherwise nothing changes. **Results (run 38136145933, receipt research/report-38136145933.json; 265 hitters scored on 2026 before August 1, 99.6% of balls in play measured):** AVG: expected minus raw squared error +0.000004 [-0.000097, +0.000108]; correlations with 2026 AVG 0.35 (expected) and 0.38 (raw); the blend (0.65 on expected, fitted on 2025) against raw -0.000041 [-0.000107, +0.000024]. SLG: expected minus raw -0.0000005 [-0.00052, +0.00053]; correlations 0.445 and 0.422; the blend (0.47) against raw -0.00022 [-0.00048, +0.00002]. **(1), (2) and (3) failed**: over two seasons of 300 or more plate appearances, expected AVG and SLG from exit speed and launch angle predicted the next season about as well as the actual numbers, not better. Decision, as registered: nothing changes; no Expected AVG or SLG rows. The Record page's list says so.

columns.Attempt: XSTATS-01 against pitchers: does a pitcher's expected AVG and SLG against, from the exit speed and launch angle of the balls hit off him, predict his next season's AVG and SLG against better than the actual ones? Same table, windows, pitchers with 300 or more batters faced in training and 150 in the test, blend and intervals (tools/brl_report.py xstats_study with who 'pitcher'). A pitcher's average against swings more with balls in play than a hitter's, so expected numbers may help here even though they did not for hitters.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026: (1) expected AVG against predicts AVG against better than AVG against does, interval excluding zero; (2) the same for SLG against. Decision rule: for each where (1) or (2) holds, the pitcher percentile rankings and cards add an Expected row (expected average or slugging against); otherwise nothing changes. **Results (run 38136607768, receipt research/report-38136607768.json; 227 pitchers scored on 2026 before August 1):** AVG against: expected minus raw **-0.00019 [-0.00031, -0.00007]**, correlations with 2026 0.43 (expected) and 0.36 (raw), blend weight 0.84; SLG against: expected minus raw **-0.00044 [-0.00089, -0.00002]**, correlations 0.37 and 0.35, blend weight 1.0. **(1) and (2) held.** Decision, as registered: pitcher percentile rankings and cards add Expected average against and Expected slugging against (cards' lines carry xh and xtb from tools/brl_report.py xs_lines; PCT_PITCHER xavg and xslg; page PCT_ROWS and lineRate). Unlike for hitters (XSTATS-01), a pitcher's average against is noisy enough that the batted balls predict it better.

columns.Attempt: SPLITS-01 for pitchers: how much of a pitcher's split by the batter's side carries over (the pitcher page's splits table, vs RHB and vs LHB: AVG and SLG against, chases, misses per swing). The same candidates with the pitcher's throwing hand as his side (raw; league for his hand; scaled, his level against all batters times his hand's league split; shrunk, m fitted), the same metrics, windows (m on 2023-2024 to 2025, scored once on 2024-2025 to 2026 before August 1), pitchers with 300 or more batters faced in training, bootstrap over pitchers (2,000 draws) and carry-over of his own split beyond his hand's (against lefties minus against righties). tools/brl_report.py split_shrink_study with who 'pitcher', report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check: planted own splits recovered (shrunk beats raw and scaled, carry-over above 0.15); none planted, m 800 or more and carry-over near zero.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026: (1) shrunk beats raw on all four metrics with the interval excluding zero; (2) on misses and chases shrunk beats scaled with the interval excluding zero (a pitcher's split by side follows his pitch mix, which carries over); (3) on AVG and SLG against, the carry-over correlation is under 0.3. Decision rule: if (1) holds, the pitcher splits table shows Expected numbers in the Expected view (shrunk at the fitted m where it beats scaled, scaled otherwise), with the carry-over quoted in its note; if (1) fails, nothing changes. **Results (run 38128749747, receipt research/report-38128749747.json; 343 pitchers scored on 2026 before August 1, 103 left-handed; 74,144 at-bats, 165,388 pitches out of the zone, 150,638 swings):** AVG m 1,600, shrunk minus raw **-0.00085 [-0.00118, -0.00051]**, minus scaled -0.000023 [-0.000074, +0.000025], carry-over r 0.10 [-0.01, 0.21] (242 pitchers); SLG m 1,600, shrunk minus raw **-0.00114 [-0.00168, -0.00067]**, minus scaled -0.000021 [-0.00011, +0.00006], r 0.06 [-0.07, 0.20]; chase m 800, shrunk minus raw **-0.00037 [-0.00055, -0.00020]**, minus scaled -0.000062 [-0.00017, +0.00004], r 0.26 [0.12, 0.40] (166); misses m 400, shrunk minus raw **-0.00030 [-0.00042, -0.00017]**, minus scaled -0.00011 [-0.00026, +0.00004], r 0.32 [0.18, 0.46] (152). League split (against lefties minus righties, AVG against): left-handed pitchers -17 points, right-handed +5. **(1) held; (2) failed** (on chases and misses shrunk does not beat scaled beyond noise, though the carry-over correlations are 0.26 and 0.32); **(3) held** (0.10 and 0.06). Decision, as registered: the pitcher splits table shows Expected numbers in the Expected view, every rate scaled (his level against all batters times his hand's league split), with the carry-over in its note (page pitcherSplitExpected, PSPLIT_EXP_M empty, PSPLIT_CARRY).

columns.Attempt: Hot and cold stretches. Player pages now show a hitter's last ten games; does a ten-game stretch say anything about his next ten beyond his level? Ten-game windows per hitter-season (regular season, 40 or more games; at games 20, 30, 40 and so on): his level is everything before the game this season plus last season, lightly shrunk toward the league (100 plate appearances); the candidate adds k times his last ten games' difference from that level, k fitted by weighted least squares on 2024 and 2025 windows and scored once on 2026 before August 1 (squared error weighted by the next ten games' plate appearances, or at-bats for SLG). Metrics: OBP (times on base per plate appearance), SLG per at-bat, strikeouts per plate appearance. Also the slope on the 2026 windows alone with an interval from resampling hitters (2,000 draws). tools/brl_report.py form_study and form_windows, report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_form_study.py): with talent that drifts from game to game k is 0.14 to 0.16; with steady talent k is near zero.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026: (1) k on OBP and on SLG is under 0.10 (at most a tenth of a stretch's difference from his level carries into the next ten games); (2) adding the last ten games changes the squared error by less than 1% on OBP and SLG; (3) on strikeouts k is larger than on OBP. Decision rule: the game log's note says how much of a ten-game stretch carried into the next ten in 2026 (the test-season slope and its interval), or that it did not carry over beyond noise if the interval includes zero. Nothing else changes. **Results (run 38129227011, receipt research/report-38129227011.json; 2,039 windows from 369 hitters in 2026 before August 1; 3,450 and 3,418 training windows):** OBP k 0.017, 2026 slope 0.019 [-0.027, 0.062], squared error change -0.03% [-0.16%, +0.10%]; SLG k 0.018, slope 0.004 [-0.045, 0.052], change +0.015% [-0.13%, +0.17%]; strikeouts k 0.099, slope **0.147 [0.100, 0.194]**, change **-1.6% [-2.4%, -0.85%]**. A ten-game stretch's difference from his level has SD 73 points of OBP and 144 of SLG. **(1), (2) and (3) held.** Decision, as registered: the hitter game log's note says a ten-game stretch said almost nothing about the next ten in getting on base or slugging (about 2%, within noise) and that strikeouts carried about 15%.

columns.Attempt: Do the changes the hitter pages call out hold? (Registered as CHANGE-01 in commit 89cacf5de; renamed before its results because that ID was taken.) The page says a hitter's chase, miss, strikeout, walk or hard-hit rate changed since last season when it moved at least 3 points (5 for hard-hit) and at least three standard errors between two seasons of 200 or more plate appearances (hitterChanges). For hitters with 200 or more plate appearances in three straight seasons (150 in 2026 before August 1), the changes flagged from the first season to the second, and how much of each was still there in the third: the third season's rate minus the first's over the flagged change, pooled over hitters, with unflagged changes as a reference and intervals from resampling hitters (2,000 draws). Windows: 2023 to 2024 then 2025, and 2024 to 2025 then 2026 (the test). tools/brl_report.py change_study, report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_change_study.py): lasting strikeout changes held above 0.8, reverting ones under 0.2.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on the 2026 window: (1) flagged strikeout and walk rate changes held at least 60%, interval excluding zero; (2) flagged chase and miss rate changes held at least 50%; (3) flagged hard-hit changes held at least 30%. Decision rule: the changes line says how much of changes like these held a season later, rate by rate; a rate whose flagged changes held under 30% or with an interval including zero is dropped from the line. **Results (run 38132555095, receipt research/report-38132555095.json):** the rule flags few hitters with three straight full seasons. 2026 window (201 hitters): chase 8 flagged, held **0.63 [0.31, 0.97]** (mean change 7.2 points); misses 8, **0.55 [0.30, 0.84]**; strikeouts 3, **0.48 [0.24, 0.83]**; walks 2, 0.23 [-0.04, 0.48]; hard-hit 6, **0.82 [0.54, 1.12]**. 2025 window (223 hitters): chase 6, 0.68; misses 13, 0.70; strikeouts 6, 0.84; walks 3, 0.51; hard-hit 3, 0.29 [-0.22, 0.69]. Unflagged changes (2 to 4 points on average) held 0.43 to 0.69 in both windows. **(1) failed** (strikeouts 0.48 under 0.60 on 3 hitters; walks 0.23 with an interval including zero), **(2) held** (0.63 and 0.55), **(3) held** (0.82). Decision, as registered: the changes line quotes how much of changes like each held (chase about 60%, misses 55%, strikeouts 50%, hard-hit 80%) and no longer calls out walk-rate changes. Reading: the flagged samples are small; the broader finding is that a regular's rate changes from one season to the next mostly hold about half to two thirds.

columns.Attempt: A looser rule for the changes line. HCHANGE-01's rule (3 points, 5 for hard-hit, and three standard errors) flagged only 2 to 8 hitters per rate, while smaller changes held 43% to 69% a season later. The same study with changes of at least 2 points (3 for hard-hit) and two standard errors, same windows and hitters (tools/brl_report.py change_study with se_mult 2 and floors).
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on the 2026 window: (1) more hitters flagged than under HCHANGE-01 for every rate; (2) flagged chase, miss, strikeout and hard-hit changes held at least 50%, intervals excluding zero; (3) flagged walk-rate changes held at least 40%, interval excluding zero. Decision rule: each rate whose flagged changes held at least 50% (40% for walks) with the interval excluding zero uses the looser rule on the page, quoting its held share; the others keep HCHANGE-01's rule and wording (walks stay off unless (3) holds). **Results (run 38135647818, receipt research/report-38135647818.json; 2026 window, 201 hitters):** chase 40 flagged (8 before), held **0.62 [0.41, 0.85]**; misses 41, **0.62 [0.44, 0.82]**; strikeouts 28, **0.56 [0.40, 0.71]**; walks 20, 0.39 [0.20, 0.59]; hard-hit 20, **0.70 [0.51, 0.89]** (mean changes 4.6 to 10.1 points). 2025 window: 0.75, 0.64, 0.60, 0.64, 0.71. **(1) and (2) held; (3) failed** (walks 0.39, just under 0.40). Decision, as registered: chase, miss, strikeout and hard-hit changes use the looser rule with their held shares (62%, 62%, 56%, 70%); walk-rate changes stay off (page HC_RATES).

columns.Attempt: A starter's fastball speed from start to start. For each regular-season start with 15 or more of his main fastballs (four-seam or sinker, whichever he threw more that season), its mean speed's change from his earlier starts that season (three or more of them); then his next start: its speed change from the same mean, and his strikeouts, walks and times on base per batter faced against his level (this season before that start plus last season, shrunk toward the league with 100 batters). Slopes per mph fitted on 2024 and 2025 pairs of starts and measured on 2026 before August 1 with intervals from resampling pitchers (2,000 draws); the squared-error change from adding the training slope; and starts after a drop of 1 mph or more against all others. tools/brl_report.py velo_study, game_velo_table, velo_pairs, report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_velo_study.py): with speed that drifts and strikeouts that follow it, both slopes recovered; with steady speed, neither.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026: (1) a last-start speed change carries into the next start, slope 0.3 or more with the interval excluding zero; (2) a drop predicts fewer strikeouts next start: the strikeout slope is above zero with the interval excluding zero, and starts after a drop of 1 mph or more strike out fewer batters than the others; (3) the times-on-base slope is below zero (point estimate). Decision rule: if (1) holds, the plan's starter fold and his page note a last-start fastball change of 1 mph or more from his earlier starts and how much such changes carried into the next start; if (2) also holds, the note adds the strikeout read. Pitcher pages draw fastball speed by game either way (display). **Results (run 38129631856, receipt research/report-38129631856.json; 1,973 pairs of 2026 starts before August 1 from 190 pitchers; 3,328 and 3,340 training pairs; a last start's change has SD 0.70 mph):** speed slope **0.44 [0.37, 0.50]** (training 0.42), squared error -17% [-21%, -12%]; after 102 drops of 1 mph or more the next start sat 0.40 mph below his earlier mean against +0.12 for the others (difference -0.52 [-0.72, -0.33]). Strikeouts per batter: slope **+0.013 per mph [0.006, 0.020]** (training 0.0035), squared error -0.4% [-0.7%, -0.2%]; after drops -2.3 points against his level, others -0.4 (difference **-2.0 [-3.7, -0.2]**). Walks: slope -0.0036 [-0.0073, +0.0001]. Times on base: slope **-0.0098 [-0.0163, -0.0028]**; after drops +1.8 points, others +0.3 (difference +1.6 [+0.2, +3.0]). **(1), (2) and (3) held.** Decision, as registered: the plan's starter fold and his page note a last-start fastball change of 1 mph or more with the carry-over (about 45%) and the strikeout read (page velLastNote, VELO_READ; cards velo_last, velo_games, velo_type from tools/brl_report.py game_velo_list), and pitcher pages draw fastball speed by game (velChart).

columns.Attempt: Relievers on no rest. The plans' bullpen card shows each arm's pitches on the team's latest game days; what does pitching the day before cost? Each regular-season relief appearance with 8 or more of his main fastballs after an earlier appearance that season, by rest: no rest (he pitched the day before), one day, rested (two or more days), and third game in four days. Measures: his fastball's speed against his other appearances that season (leave one out, by fastballs; 30 or more), and his strikeouts and times on base per batter against his level from his other appearances (shrunk toward the league with 50 batters). Category means and differences from rested, on 2024 and 2025 and on 2026 before August 1, intervals from resampling pitchers (2,000 draws). tools/brl_report.py rest_study, report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_rest_study.py): a planted 0.6 mph and 6-point strikeout cost on no rest recovered; none planted, differences near zero.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions on 2026: (1) on no rest his fastball is at least 0.2 mph slower than rested, with the interval excluding zero; (2) on no rest he strikes out fewer batters per batter faced than rested (point estimate); (3) a third game in four days costs at least as much speed as no rest (point estimate). Decision rule: if (1) holds, the bullpen card marks arms who pitched the day before (and three games in four days) and its note quotes the measured speed cost, adding the strikeout difference if its interval excludes zero; otherwise the card is unchanged. **Results (run 38130277653, receipt research/report-38130277653.json; 2026 before August 1: 370 no-rest, 925 one-day, 2,451 rested and 297 third-in-four-days appearances from 379 pitchers; 2024-2025: 1,264, 2,778, 7,435 and 1,049 from 663):** speed against rested, 2026: no rest **-0.16 mph [-0.24, -0.07]**, one day -0.10 [-0.16, -0.03], third in four days -0.04 [-0.15, +0.06]; 2024-2025: -0.16 [-0.21, -0.11], -0.10 [-0.14, -0.06], -0.09 [-0.15, -0.04]. Strikeouts per batter against rested, 2026: no rest +1.1 points [-0.7, +3.1] (2024-2025 -0.1 [-1.1, +1.0]). Times on base: 2026 no rest +0.9 [-1.2, +3.1]; 2024-2025 +1.9 [+0.7, +3.0]. **(1) failed** (the speed cost is real in both windows but 0.16 mph, under the registered 0.2), **(2) failed** (no strikeout cost; 2026 points the other way), **(3) failed** (a third game in four days cost less speed than no rest). Decision, as registered: the bullpen card is unchanged. Reading: a reliever on no rest loses about a sixth of a mile per hour, too little to show in his strikeouts; the times-on-base cost seen in 2024-2025 did not repeat beyond noise in 2026.

columns.Attempt: The third time through the order. Plate appearances against starters (his first pitch in the first inning), regular seasons 2023 to 2026 (2026 before August 1), each with the batter's time through (1st, 2nd, 3rd or later against that pitcher in the game, by at-bat order). Per season the league's OBP (times on base per plate appearance), SLG per at-bat and strikeouts per plate appearance by time through; per starter-season his own third-time gap (third against first and second together, net of the league's gap that season) and its carry-over to the next season (2023 to 2024, 2024 to 2025, 2025 to 2026) among starters with 150 or more third-time plate appearances in both: correlation with an interval from resampling pitchers (2,000 draws) and slope. tools/brl_report.py tto_study and tto_table, report lane, aggregates only. Synthetic check (brl_live_tests/test_report_tto_study.py): a planted 3-point league penalty measured; a starter's own gap carries over when it is his (r above 0.3) and not when redrawn.
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Predictions: (1) in every season hitters' third-time OBP against starters is at least 1 point above their first and second times together; (2) a starter's own third-time OBP gap carries over with r under 0.2; (3) the same for SLG. Decision rule: if (1) holds, the plan's starter fold notes the league's third-time penalty in 2026; if (2) also holds it adds that a starter's own gap did not carry over, and no per-pitcher third-time numbers are shown; if (2) fails, his own gap is shown shrunk by the carry-over slope. **Results (run 38131192178, receipt research/report-38131192178.json):** OBP against starters by time through, first / second / third or later: 2023 .312 / .318 / .328 (22,601 third-time plate appearances), 2024 .302 / .311 / .323, 2025 .306 / .310 / .322, 2026 before August 1 .304 / .319 / .322; third against first and second together +1.3, +1.7, +1.4 and +1.05 points. SLG third against first and second together about +2 to +3 points each season (2026 .419 against about .397); strikeouts fall each time through (2026 24.5%, 20.7%, 19.5%). Carry-over of a starter's own gap, 46 pitcher-season pairs from 34 starters (150 or more third-time plate appearances in both seasons is rare): OBP r 0.12 [-0.26, 0.38], SLG r 0.23 [-0.03, 0.48], strikeouts r -0.10 [-0.35, 0.15]. **(1) held** (2026 by 1.05 points), **(2) held** on the point estimate with a wide interval, **(3) failed** (SLG 0.23). Decision, as registered: the plan's starter fold notes the league's third-time penalty in 2026 and that a starter's own gap did not reliably carry over; no per-pitcher third-time numbers.

columns.Attempt: The hitter chances on the page, re-scored on the live engine, with a calibration fitted across seasons. Each lineup hitter's chance of at least one hit, two or more hits, a home run, a walk and a strikeout, computed the way the page computes them (each of the slot's events kept with his spot's share of the slot's plate appearances, PLAYER-02), from full replays of 2025 and 2026 with the live settings (the settings of TOTALS-08's paired-streams weather replays: each season with tables fitted on other seasons, 1,000 worlds per game, the same seeds) plus each hitter's histograms of hits, home runs, walks and strikeouts (brl_replay/harness.py), against his actual line in that game (box-score facts). PLAYER-02 scored the October 8 engine on 2026 only; the bullpens, the starter leash and the run environment have changed since (PROD-03, PROD-04). Calibration: for each kind of chance, logit(p') = a + b logit(p), fitted by maximum likelihood on one season's hitter-games and applied to the other season's
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any replay.** Predictions: (1) the chance of at least one hit runs 0.5 to 2.0 points above the actual share in both seasons; (2) a home run 0.2 to 1.0 points above, and the tenth of hitter-games with the highest chance 1 to 4 points above; (3) two or more hits 0.3 to 2.0 points above; (4) a walk and a strikeout within 1.5 points of the actual share either way; (5) the calibration passes the rule below for the hit and home-run chances and not for walks. Decision rule: the page shows the calibrated chance of a kind (the Summary's meters and the Odds tab's table) if, in both seasons with the map fitted on the other season, the Brier score falls with the 95% interval's upper end below zero (bootstrap over dates, 2,000 draws, paired by hitter-game) and the calibrated mean is within 0.5 points of the actual share; the map shown is then fitted on both seasons together. Otherwise the raw chance stays. Also reported, not gates: each kind by lineup spot and for hitters with fewer than 200 plate appearances in the prior 365 days. Results (runs 38138625455 for 2025 and 38138601871 for 2026; 43,614 and 43,686 hitter-games): at least one hit 61.2% against 61.3% actual (2025) and 61.6% against 60.7% (2026); two or more hits 21.7% against 22.0% and 22.1% against 21.5%; a home run 11.6% against 11.7% and 12.1% against 11.5%, the top tenth by chance 1.1 and 2.3 points high; a walk 33.7% against 31.6% and 32.8% against 33.2%; a strikeout 62.9% against 61.9% and 61.8% against 61.1%. Hitters with fewer than 200 plate appearances in the prior year: hits 1.0 and 1.4 points high. The levels differ by season (each replay carries its tables from the other seasons: 2025's walk level from 2026 runs 2 points high, 2026's hit level from 2025 runs 1 point high), so a map fitted on one season moved the other the wrong way: Brier change with the other season's map +0.00012 [+0.00001, +0.00022] and +0.000006 [+0.000002, +0.000009] for hits, +0.00007 and +0.00005 for two hits, +0.00006 [-0.00001, +0.00014] and -0.000014 [-0.000026, -0.000003] for home runs, +0.00016 and +0.00057 for walks, -0.00009 and -0.00007 [-0.00017, +0.00002] for strikeouts. Predictions: (1), (3) and (5) failed (2025's hits, two hits and home runs are not high); (2) held for the top tenth only; (4) held for strikeouts and failed for walks (2025, +2.0 points). **No kind passes the rule; the page keeps the raw chances.** The live engine's context table includes the current season through late September, so its level is nearer the season's than either cross-season replay; a fixed cross-season correction would have moved it the wrong way. The lasting pieces: the top tenth by chance runs 2.6 and 2.3 points high on hits and home runs in 2026 (0.7 and 1.1 in 2025), and new hitters 1 to 1.4 points high on hits in both seasons
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: (1), (3), (5) failed; (2) top tenth only; (4) strikeouts only; raw chances stay

PLAYER-03.status: (1), (3), (5) failed; (2) top tenth only; (4) strikeouts only; raw chances stay

The replays that tested the live run environment (TOTALS-08's paired-streams weather replays, runs 38009502287 and 38009599322, 1,000 worlds per game, each season with tables fitted on other seasons) record each starter's simulated strikeout distribution and his actual line: 4,854 starts in 2026 and 4,846 in 2025

The chance of at least 3 to 9 strikeouts against the actual share: within 1.4 points at every line in 2026 (5 or more 50.3% against 49.7%, 7 or more 21.7% against 22.8%, 9 or more 6.6% against 8.0%) and within 2.1 points in 2025 (3 or more 83.3% against 81.2%, 5 or more 53.0% against 51.8%, 7 or more 23.6% against 23.0%).
