columns.Attempt: Part-time hitters' share of their lineup slot. PLAYER-03's replays (live settings, both seasons) show the page's chances running high for hitters with little recent playing time in both seasons (at least one hit +2.3 points for 1 to 99 plate appearances in the prior 365 days, strikeouts and walks high too), and the reason is plate appearances: such hitters get 95% to 96% of the trips their slot's share allows (pinch hitters and defensive changes take more of a part-timer's spot), 96% to 98% with 100 to 199, 98% to 99% with 200 to 399, and regulars 100%. Design: each hitter's share of his slot's events becomes the spot's share (PLAYER-02) times a factor for his prior 365 days' plate appearances (1-99, 100-199, 200-399, 400 or more), the factor being actual plate appearances over the simulated ones times the spot's share in that group, fitted on one season and applied to the other (tools/brl_player_cal.py part_time_study), scored on the page's chances
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the adjusted chances were computed** (the plate-appearance ratios and raw gaps above were seen first). Predictions: (1) with the other season's factors, the Brier of the chance of at least one hit and of a home run falls in both seasons, the 95% interval's upper end below zero (bootstrap over dates, 2,000 draws); (2) the 1-99 group's hit-chance gap shrinks by at least a third in both seasons; (3) regulars (400 or more) move by under 0.2 points. Decision rule: if (1) holds for hits and home runs in both seasons, the live boxes keep each hitter's events with the spot's share times his group's factor (fitted on both seasons; brl_live/boxscore.py, the box rows carry it as keep) and the page uses it for every chance; otherwise nothing changes. Results (PLAYER-03's replays; tools/brl_player_cal.py --part-time): the factors by group are 0.961, 0.976, 0.986, 1.001 (2025) and 0.954, 0.964, 0.977, 1.005 (2026). With the other season's factors, the Brier of at least one hit changed -0.000039 [-0.000113, +0.000030] (2025) and -0.000061 [-0.000125, +0.000002] (2026); a home run -0.0000034 [-0.0000167, +0.0000105] and -0.0000075 [-0.0000167, +0.0000017]; walks -0.00013 [-0.00018, -0.00008] and -0.000024 [-0.000062, +0.000010]; a strikeout -0.000091 [-0.00017, -0.00002] and -0.00022 [-0.00028, -0.00016]. The first group as computed is under 100 prior plate appearances, so it also holds the 233 hitter-games with none (the design named 1-99; the code's bin starts at 0); its hit-chance gap fell from +2.44 to +0.64 points (2025) and from +1.89 to +0.34 (2026); regulars moved 0.19 and 0.04 points. Predictions: (2) and (3) held; (1) failed (no interval for hits or home runs ends below zero). **Not adopted under the rule**: the part-timers' chances come out right with the factors, but the gain over all hitters is within noise for hits and home runs in two seasons

columns.Attempt: Two or more total bases (the total-bases prop at 1.5, the most common hitter prop after hits and home runs). Each hitter's own chance, each of his slot's hits kept with the spot's share (PLAYER-02): below two only when no hit is kept or the only one kept is a single (brl_live/boxscore.py tb2_probability; boxes saved from now carry it). Full replays of 2025 and 2026 with the live settings and hitter lines (PLAYER-03's settings and seeds), which now record each hitter's worlds by hits and singles among them (brl_replay/harness.py hs_hist) and his real extra-base hits (a double or triple reaches two bases either way, so the history's 2B_3B class is enough); scored by tools/brl_player_cal.py (kind tb2)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its replays.** Predictions: (1) the chance within 1.5 points of the actual share in both seasons; (2) by tenths of the chance, within 3 points in both; (3) Brier better than the season's constant share in both. Decision rule: the Odds tab's hitter tables add a 2+ TB column (page PROP_COLS.tb2) if (1) and (2) hold in both seasons; otherwise not. Results (runs 38145318753 for 2025 and 38144947261 for 2026; 43,614 and 43,686 hitter-games): two or more total bases 35.3% against 35.6% actual (2025, -0.3 points) and 36.0% against 35.0% (2026, +1.0); by tenths the largest gap 1.1 points (2025) and 3.4 (2026, the top tenth: 48.5% against 45.1%); Brier 0.2247 against a constant's 0.2293 (2025) and 0.2236 against 0.2275 (2026). Predictions: (1) and (3) held; (2) failed in 2026. **The 2+ TB column stays off under the rule.** The 2026 top tenth's miss is in the rates, not the trips: the top tenth by this chance got 0.244 hits a plate appearance against 0.254 simulated and 0.043 home runs against 0.050 (2025: 0.251 against 0.249, 0.045 against 0.047). 2026 is the plate-appearance model's first season it never saw in fitting or tuning, so the best hitters' rates run high out of sample (the same top-tenth excess PLAYER-03 found for hits and home runs)

columns.Attempt: Runs batted in on outs in play, a correctness fix (October 11, 10 a.m. Eastern; no claim). The simulated box credited a run batted in only on a hit, a walk or hit-by-pitch and a sacrifice fly, so a run scoring on a groundout went without one, against MLB's scoring rule 9.04 (a run that scores on an out in play is batted in unless the play is a double play, and so is one that scores on a fielder's choice; one that scores on an error is not). The box now credits both (brl_live/boxscore.py; the kernel labels some reaches as errors, which stay without one); test_boxscore.py checks it over simulated games. It changes the projected box's RBI column and each hitter's RBI distribution, nothing the engine decides. A review the same morning found the fielder's choice missing (224 runs in 1,500 test games); added with its test

columns.Attempt: A hitter's record against one pitcher (the batter-against-pitcher line every preview prints): does it say anything about their next meetings beyond what each one's own level says? Regular-season plate appearances 2023-2026 (report lane, aggregates only). Each plate appearance's expectation from the two players' own levels that season, the batter's against pitchers of that hand and the pitcher's against batters of that side, the pair's own meetings left out, with 100 (on base), 60 (strikeouts) and 150 (total bases per at-bat) league trials added (bvp_expected); each window's gaps centered on each batter's and each pitcher's own mean gap (bvp_centered). The pair's lasting effect: with a constant effect t and independent noise, the sum over pairs of (earlier gap x later gap) over the sum of n1 n2 estimates the variance tau^2 of t (bvp_carry), interval from resampling batters (2,000 draws); a record of n carries n tau^2 / (n tau^2 + sigma^2) of its gap. Two replications: 2023-2024 to 2025 and 2023-2025 to 2026. Synthetic checks (test_report_bvp_study.py): a planted strikeout pair effect is recovered at its size; with none planted the interval covers zero
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its run.** Predictions: (1) on base: the SD of the true pair effect under 1.5 points in both replications (the upper end of tau^2's interval below 0.000225), so a 20 plate-appearance record carries under 2% of its gap; (2) strikeouts: tau^2's interval above zero in both replications, the SD between 0.5 and 3 points, so a 20 plate-appearance record carries 1% to 15% of its gap; (3) total bases per at-bat: a 20 at-bat record carries under 3% of its gap (at the upper end of the interval) in both. Decision rule: the Matchups tab shows each lineup hitter's career line against the opposing starter from MLB's public stats (product call), never colored as a read; its note says what carried over in these words: for a measure whose prediction of little carry held in both replications, that a record this short said almost nothing about the next meetings; for strikeouts, if (2) held, how far a 20 plate-appearance record moved the next meetings. Results (run 38139650184, 731,711 plate appearances; pairs that met in both windows 31,304 for 2023-2024 to 2025 and 35,086 for 2023-2025 to 2026): on base, tau^2 0.00057 [-0.00024, 0.00135] and 0.00116 [0.00040, 0.00196], an SD of 2.4 and 3.4 points, so a 20 plate-appearance record carries 5.0% and 9.7% of its gap (11.2% and 15.3% at the upper ends); strikeouts 0.00006 [-0.00061, 0.00076] and 0.00026 [-0.00033, 0.00085], SD 0.8 and 1.6 points, 0.7% and 2.9% (8.0% and 9.0% at the upper ends); total bases per at-bat -0.0011 [-0.0046, 0.0024] and 0.0014 [-0.0015, 0.0049], 0% and 3.7% of a 20 at-bat record (6.0% and 11.6% at the upper ends). Pairs with 10 or more meetings in each window are too few for a plain correlation (27 and 34). Every prediction failed: (1) on base's upper ends are above 0.000225 in both and 2026's interval is above zero; (2) no strikeout carry-over could be told from noise in either; (3) slugging's upper ends are above 3%. A synthetic check added after the run (test_parks_do_not_pass_for_pair_effects) confirms that home parks do not pass for pair effects under this centering. Under the rule none of the prepared wordings applies, so the note states the measured range (product call): beyond each player's own level, a 20 plate-appearance record carried between none and about 15% of its on-base gap into later meetings, with no strikeout or slugging carry-over we could tell from noise; the career lines show as facts, never colored

columns.Attempt: Product call, October 11, 9 p.m. Eastern (display). The game page for a game to come opens in plain words, for readers who do not follow baseball: the matchup side by side with each team's win chance, a one-line call ("A coin flip, leaning the Brewers"; under 53% a coin flip, under 58% a slight edge, under 65% favored, else clear favorites), a typical final score, the expected runs and one-run share, a picture of 100 games, and "What decides it": up to five events from the same simulated games, each with how often it happens and the team's win chance when it does and when it does not. The box now counts, over its simulated games, each team scoring first, leading after five, its starter getting 18 or more outs, and each hitter homering or getting two or more hits, with the team's wins in each case (BoxAccumulator keys; no new simulation). Shown are scoring first, each starter's 18 outs if its weight is 0.02 or more, and the two hitters with the largest weight (one per team when possible); weight is the swing in the win chance times the square root of share x (1 - share); events under 8% or over 92% are left out. The two chances are shifted together on the log-odds scale so that, mixed by the share, they give the published pick. Game cards on the home page get the same one-line call (before the game the call, during it the score and win chance, after it the winner and our pick), and the card footer names Vegas only (the simulator-alone line stays on the game page). During and after a game the header adds the same kind of line (who leads and how often they win from here; who won). A pick under 52% counts as a coin flip on the cards, as in the header. The Record page opens with what the test is (when we say 60%, does that team win about 60 times in 100) and each season's picks against the Vegas favorite as numbers; month by month and the two long check tables are folded. The palette moves from green to night navy and the pregame header uses both teams' colors. After the final, the Summary adds What decided it: each key shown before the game, whether it happened in the real box score (scored first from the line score, the starter's 18 outs, the hitter's home run or two hits), and the team's chance when it did or did not (display; no grade)
columns.Disposition and evidence: Done in the evening commits; test_boxscore.py (the counts over the same worlds); How it works says these are counts from the simulated games, not yet checked against real games. Open: replay check of the conditional chances against real games (scored first, starter's 18 outs) before any claim about them

Scored with tools/brl_keys_check.py: per kind, the mean simulated chance of the event against how often it happened, and over team-games where it happened (did not) the mean simulated win chance given it (given not) against the real win rate. The simulator's own conditionals (the page shifts them to the pick; the mix of the raw ones is the simulator's win chance). Tied finals left out; the hitter and starter kinds also scored inside the page's 8% to 92% window
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its replays.** Predictions, each in both seasons: (1) scoring first: share within 2 points, win chance if and else each within 3 points; (2) starter 18+ outs (in the window): share within 3 points, if within 4, else within 3; (3) hitter home run (in the window): share within 1.5 points, if within 4, else within 2; (4) hitter 2+ hits (in the window): share within 2, if within 4, else within 2. Every prediction held in both seasons. **All four kinds stay in What decides it, and How it works says they were checked.** The starter's 18 outs and the hitters' 2+ hits run 1 to 2 points high in their share (the same lean as the outs and hits ladders), well inside the bounds.

columns.Attempt: The run line (each team by two runs or more), the third standard market after the moneyline and the total. The page would take each team's run-line chance as the headline win chance times the simulator's chance of winning by two or more given a win, so it agrees with the pick; this checks that conditional piece. Full replays of 2025 and 2026 with the live settings (PLAYER-03's settings and seeds, no hitter lines), each game's margin histogram over 1,000 worlds now recorded (brl_replay/harness.py margin_hist), against the real margins (tools/brl_runline_cal.py; synthetic checks in test_runline_cal.py)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its replays.** Predictions: (1) given a win, the simulator's chance of winning by two or more within 1.5 points of how often winners did, for home winners and road winners, in both seasons; (2) by fifths of that conditional chance, within 3 points in both seasons; (3) the simulator's own run-line chance beats a constant in Brier for both sides in both seasons. Decision rule: the Odds tab shows the run line for both teams (-1.5 and +1.5) with our chance (the headline win chance times the conditional) and its fair price if (1) and (2) hold in both seasons; otherwise it is not shown. Results (runs 38141956435 for 2025 and 38141799131 for 2026; 2,423 and 2,427 games; tools/brl_runline_cal.py): given a win, the simulator's chance of winning by two or more against how often winners did: home winners 66.5% against 65.8% (2025, +0.7 [-2.0, +3.4]) and 66.2% against 68.4% (2026, -2.2 [-4.7, +0.5]); road winners 75.4% against 76.5% (2025, -1.1) and 75.4% against 77.3% (2026, -2.0). By fifths the largest gaps were 2.6 and 6.0 points (2025, home and road) and 5.6 and 6.4 (2026); the road winners the simulator gave the lowest chance won by two or more 6.0 and 5.4 points more often than it said in both seasons. The simulator's own run-line chance beat a constant in both (Brier 0.2239 against 0.2294 at home, 0.2225 against 0.2275 on the road, 2025; 0.2275 against 0.2309 and 0.2262 against 0.2316, 2026). Predictions: (1) failed in 2026 (both sides about 2 points low), (2) failed in both, (3) held. **Not shown under the rule.** The simulator's margins given a win run tight, the same narrowness DISP-01 found in its run distributions

Decision rule: the Odds tab shows the first inning (a run scores, no run) with fair prices if (1) and (3) hold in both seasons; otherwise not. Results (runs 38141956435 and 38141799131): nobody scoring in the first inning 51.0% against 49.9% (2025, +1.1 [-0.9, +3.2]) and 50.2% against 49.4% (2026, +0.8 [-1.1, +2.8]); the road team scoring in it 25.7% against 28.0% (2025, -2.3 [-4.2, -0.5]) and 27.5% against 26.8% (2026); the home team 31.3% against 31.0% and 30.7% against 32.4% (2026, -1.7). So: win chances stay with the plain worlds, and only the market numbers (the total's over and under, the run line's margin given a win) come from day-form worlds. Replays of 2025 and 2026 with the live settings plus DISP-02's centered shock (sigma 0.13 and center 0.004 for 2026, 0.11 and 0.003 for 2025, each from the other season's gap), paired streams and the same seeds as the RUNLINE-01 replays (tags v2-prod4-df-1000-<season>), compared by game with tools/replay_compare.py against v2-prod4-margins-1000 and checked for the run line with tools/brl_runline_cal.py
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its replays.** Predictions: (1) P(over the closing total) Brier better pooled over both seasons, the 95% interval's upper end below zero, and neither season worse by more than 0.0003; (2) mean total within 0.03 runs a game of the plain worlds in both seasons; (3) the team-run SD moves toward actual in both; (4) given a win, the chance of winning by two or more within 1.5 points of how often winners did, for home and road winners, in both seasons. Decision rule: if (1) and (2) hold, the page's over and under for the total (the Odds tab's fair price and the simulator's chance of the over) come from day-form worlds the live run adds for each game, while every win chance stays with the plain worlds; if (4) also holds, the run line shows from the day-form margins (MORE_MARKETS.runline). Otherwise nothing changes. Results (runs 38146625979 for 2025 and 38146596899 for 2026, against the RUNLINE-01 replays 38141956435 and 38141799131 by game; tools/replay_compare.py): P(over the closing total) Brier -0.00028 [-0.00070, +0.00016] (2025, 1,638 games) and -0.00007 [-0.00053, +0.00042] (2026, 2,346 games), pooled -0.00015 [-0.00047, +0.00017]; mean total 8.865 against 8.863 (2025) and 8.932 against 8.933 (2026); team-run SD 3.096 to 3.196 (actual 3.249) and 3.108 to 3.245 (actual 3.210); games decided by five or more 26.9% to 27.9% (28.8%) and 26.8% to 28.2% (28.7%); given a win, the chance of winning by two or more within 1.1 points of how often winners did for home and road winners in 2025 and within 1.5 in 2026 (home 67.0% against 68.4%, road 75.9% against 77.3%). The win Brier of the day-form worlds themselves (not used for win chances) -0.00016 and +0.00033. Predictions: (2), (3) and (4) held; (1) failed (the pooled interval's upper end is +0.00017). **Nothing changes under the rule**: market_day_form stays off and the run line stays hidden. The day-form margins do put the run line right in both seasons; a run-line-only test would need a season these replays have not seen

columns.Attempt: Starters' outs recorded (the pitcher-outs prop, listed at a half line such as 16.5). Each starter's chance of more than each half line comes from his simulated outs (the box's outs distribution, which the page shows today only as an innings range). Full replays of 2025 and 2026 with the live settings and starter lines (RUNLINE-01's settings and seeds: tables fitted on other seasons, the leash fitted on the other season, 1,000 worlds per game), which now record each starter's real outs, read from the plate appearances: the outs before the next plate appearance of the half-inning minus the outs before his (an out on the bases goes to the pitcher on the mound), 3 at a half-inning's end, and a walk-off's last half-inning short of three (brl_replay/harness.py pitcher_outs; tests in test_pitcher_outs.py). Every start with a real line is scored, early exits and openers included, since the market settles those too; scored by tools/brl_outs_cal.py
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its replays.** Predictions: (1) at every half line from 12.5 to 20.5, starters' mean chance of more within 2.5 points of the actual share, in both seasons; (2) by fifths of the simulated mean outs, the simulated mean within 0.6 outs of the actual mean in every fifth, in both seasons; (3) Brier at the lines 14.5 to 17.5 together better than each line's constant share, in both seasons. Decision rule: the Odds tab adds each starter's outs ladder (his chance of more than each half line around his median, with the fair price, as PROD-13 did for strikeouts) if (1) and (2) hold in both seasons; otherwise not. Results (runs 38152442137 for 2025 and 38152417051 for 2026; 4,846 and 4,854 starts): outs 15.51 simulated against 15.57 actual (2025) and 15.16 against 15.15 (2026); by line, more than 12.5 outs 76.5% against 80.3% (2025, -3.8 points) and 74.2% against 76.6% (2026, -2.4), 13.5 -2.9 and -1.3, 14.5 -2.0 and -0.8, 15.5 to 17.5 within 0.7 in both, 18.5 +1.6 and +1.3, 19.5 +1.4 and +1.3, 20.5 +1.0 and +1.1; by fifths of the simulated mean within 0.46 outs (2025) and 0.20 (2026); Brier at 14.5 to 17.5 0.2134 against a constant's 0.2348 (2025) and 0.2080 against 0.2361 (2026); at the lines a ladder would show (each start's median less 1.5 to plus 1.5) 49.1% against 49.4% and 49.5% against 49.8% (only those from 12.5 to 20.5, the lines the page's ladder now shows: 48.9% against 49.0% and 49.2% against 49.4%). (1) failed in 2025 (12.5 and 13.5 outside 2.5 points), held in 2026; (2) and (3) held in both. **The outs ladder stays off under the rule (page OUTS_LADDER false).** (LEASH-02 later turned it on for games simulated with its correction; see that row.) Where it misses, described after looking: the simulator ends too many starts in the 4th inning and too few in the 5th (10 to 12 outs 13.6% of simulated starts against 10.9% of real ones in 2025 and 13.6% against 11.5% in 2026; 13 to 15 outs 25.5% against 29.6% and 25.2% against 27.8%), and slightly too many go 7 innings or more (12.6% against 11.6%, 11.8% against 10.8%); the exit hazard has no term for finishing the 5th

columns.Attempt: When starters come out, by inning. PLAYER-07 found the simulator ending too many starts in the 4th inning and too few in the 5th. Diagnosis (described after looking; research run 38156118083, the live exit hazard on every real removal decision of 2023 to 2026, the states the simulator sees): after the 4th inning ends the hazard expects 391 to 416 removals a season where 253 to 290 happened (actual over expected 0.62 to 0.70 by season; 0.60 to 0.69 by score and 0.54 to 0.80 by runs allowed); after the 5th with a lead 1.17; after the 7th 1.11 to 1.20; mid-inning in the 4th with a run or none allowed 0.60 and 0.61, in the 5th with none 0.74. The hazard is a logistic regression whose inning terms are a straight line and a step from the 6th on (with runs allowed counting extra through the 4th), nothing for the 5th, so it cannot hold managers' habit of letting a starter finish the 5th. Built: a correction on the hazard's log-odds, one term for each inning from the 3rd to the 7th by whether it just ended and the score (fielding team ahead, tied, behind), and two for mid-inning with few runs allowed (the 4th with a run or none, the 5th with none; 32 terms), fitted on 2023 and 2024 decisions with the hazard's own chance as the offset and a light ridge (tools/brl_research.py hazard_fix), applied in the simulator's starter policy (research_lab.game_sim.starter_hazard). The terms were chosen after seeing all four seasons' cells; the fit sees 2023 and 2024 only
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the fit and the replays.** Stage 1, decisions: (a) the decision log loss on 2025 and on 2026 improves, each game-clustered interval below zero; (b) removals after the 4th inning ends expected within 10% of actual in both seasons. Stage 2, full replays of 2025 and 2026 with PLAYER-07's settings and seeds plus the correction, against PLAYER-07's replays: (1) every half line from 12.5 to 20.5 outs within 2.5 points of the actual share in both seasons (PLAYER-07's (1)), and starts ending with 10 to 12 outs within 1.5 points of the real share in both; (2) the win Brier pooled not worse than +0.0002; (3) the mean total's squared error not worse, the pooled paired interval's upper end below +0.03 runs squared. Decision rule: if (a), (b) and (1) to (3) hold, the correction goes live for regular-season games (ADJUST hazard_correction); the postseason keeps its measured settings (x0.91 and the +0.4 exit offset were fitted on the plain hazard). The outs ladder would then be re-checked under PLAYER-07's rule on these replays before it shows. Otherwise nothing changes. Stage 1 results (research run 38156674333; brl_replay/hazard_correction.json): the decision log loss 0.10356 to 0.10285 on 2025 (-0.00071 [-0.00097, -0.00046]) and 0.10980 to 0.10938 on 2026 (-0.00042 [-0.00069, -0.00016]); removals after the 4th inning ends 261 against 395 expected before and 264 after (2025), 290 against 416 and 280 (2026). (a) and (b) held. The fitted terms: after the 4th ends -0.45 to -0.63, mid-4th with a run or none -0.36, mid-5th scoreless -0.58, after the 7th ends +0.28 to +0.63, mid-3rd when behind +0.50. Stage 2 results (runs 38156905239 for 2025 and 38156881017 for 2026, against PLAYER-07's replays, same seeds): every line from 12.5 to 20.5 outs within 2.5 points in both seasons (largest +2.13 at 18.5 in 2025 and +2.34 at 17.5 in 2026; more than 12.5 outs 79.1% against 80.3% and 76.9% against 76.6%, was 3.8 and 2.4 points short); starts ending with 10 to 12 outs 11.1% against 10.9% (2025) and 11.1% against 11.5% (2026), was 13.6% in both; outs 15.59 against 15.57 and 15.24 against 15.15; (2) the win Brier pooled +0.00003 [-0.00004, +0.00011]; (3) the mean total's squared error pooled -0.0023 [-0.0064, +0.0018]; P(over) Brier pooled -0.00006 [-0.00011, -0.00000]; mean totals unchanged (8.865 and 8.934). (1) to (3) held, as did (a) and (b). **Switched on for regular-season games (ADJUST hazard_correction; brl_live/hazard_correction.json); the postseason keeps the plain hazard with its measured x0.91.** PLAYER-07's rule re-read on these replays: level and fifths held in both seasons (fifths within 0.30 and 0.15 outs), so the outs ladder shows for games simulated with the correction (the box's adjustments name it), that is regular-season games from next season. What it costs, described after looking: starters now run a little long in the middle (more than 16.5 and 17.5 outs about 2 points high, at the lines the page's ladder shows, each start's median less 1.5 to plus 1.5 within 12.5 to 20.5, 1.42 and 1.52 points high where the plain hazard was 0.14 and 0.18 low; 1.3 and 1.4 against 0.3 low counting lines outside 12.5 to 20.5) and 7 innings or more 12.8% and 12.1% against 11.6% and 10.8%

columns.Attempt: Pitch counts in the starter's exit. columns.Attempt: Alec, October 16: the four seasons of history (2023 to 2026) are too few for how we predict. The plate-appearance history is extended back to 2015, the first Statcast season: for each season 2015 to 2022, tools/brl_history_backfill.py (workflow BRL history backfill, one job per season) reads the official schedule, downloads Baseball Savant's pitch-by-pitch export for the regular season and the postseason in three-day spans, and builds one row per plate appearance with the same builder as the 2023-2026 history (research_lab.pa_model.data.build_plate_appearances; postseason rows keep their game type). Each season is sealed to private/history/pa-<year>.enc with a counts-only receipt (history/pa-<year>.json). The pitch physics study and per-PA physics tables for the same seasons come from the existing backfill (tools/brl_bookkeeping_backfill.py, the official feeds), which now ends a past season with its year. What more seasons are for: more seasons to test changes on (most gates here rest on two replay seasons), longer histories for each player (multi-year weighting, aging), year-to-year stability checks with many pairs of seasons, and many more postseason games; era differences (the 2019 ball, the 60-game 2020, the 2021-2022 ball changes, the 2023 rules, Trackman before 2020 and Hawk-Eye after) have to be handled in any use
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any season was built.** Acceptance, per season: (1) regular-season games in the history at least 99% of the schedule's completed games; (2) 70 to 82 plate appearances a regular-season game; (3) strikeouts 18% to 25%, walks and hit batters 7.5% to 11%, home runs 2.3% to 4.0% of regular-season plate appearances; (4) the physics table's plate appearances within 2% of the history's. A season that passes is usable for research and fits; one that fails is fixed before any use. Nothing on the site changes from this row alone: any model or simulator change that uses the older seasons is its own registered test. **Result (runs 38903965323 for 2022, 38905328029 for 2015-2021): all eight seasons pass all four checks.** Regular-season games / schedule, PA per game, K, BB+HBP, HR: 2015 2,429/2,430, 75.6, 20.4%, 8.5%, 2.7%; 2016 2,428/2,430, 76.0, 21.1%, 9.1%, 3.0%; 2017 2,430/2,430, 76.2, 21.7%, 9.5%, 3.3%; 2018 2,431/2,432, 76.1, 22.3%, 9.5%, 3.0%; 2019 2,429/2,430, 76.8, 23.0%, 9.6%, 3.6%; 2020 898/900, 74.1, 23.4%, 10.4%, 3.5%; 2021 2,429/2,430, 74.9, 23.2%, 9.9%, 3.3%; 2022 2,430/2,430, 74.9, 22.4%, 9.3%, 2.9%. Every postseason game of every season is in (309 games, 23,249 plate appearances). Physics tables against the histories: within 0.03% every season (2015 186,326 vs 186,300; 2022 185,048 vs 185,047). In all: 1,355,412 regular-season plate appearances added to the 733,328 of 2023-2026 (2.09 million, 2.8 times as many), and the league's own drift is visible (strikeouts 20.4% in 2015 to 23.4% in 2020; home runs peaking at 3.6% with the 2019 ball)

columns.Attempt: First use of the longer history (diagnostic): how much sample a player's rate needs before it means something, and how much carries into the next season, from every regular season 2015 to 2026 (tools/brl_stability.py in the research lane, experiment stability; the physics tables carry each plate appearance's outcome and pitch sums, the histories give the game type). For 20 batter and pitcher rates (strikeouts, walks, home runs and singles per PA; whiff per swing, chase, swing, zone contact; exit velocity, hard-hit, launch angle; fastball speed; and the pitcher versions), a shrinkage constant k (league-average sample added, so an estimate is (total + k x league rate) / (sample + k)) from two measures: split half within a season (first 2N units split alternately; k = N (1 - r) / r) and next season (players with at least M units in consecutive seasons; k = n (1 - r) / r at their mean sample), for 2015-2019 and 2021-2026 separately. On made-up seasons with a known k of 68.6 the estimator gives 69.6 (split half) and 67.3 (next season)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its run.** Diagnostic; no prediction about the values. What it decides: the plate-appearance model's shrinkage settings (player_prior_pa 180 for the per-PA rates; physics k_rate 150 for whiff, chase, swing and zone contact; k_bip 60 for exit velocity, launch angle and hard-hit; k_velo 100 fastballs) are checked against the next-season k. Where a setting is off by more than a factor of 2 from the next-season k in both eras, a refit with settings from these estimates is registered next (gated on held-out log-likelihood and full replays); otherwise the settings stand and How it works can cite the measured numbers **Result (run 38908072806; 2.09 million regular-season plate appearances, 2015-2026).** Next-season k (the sample at which a rate is half signal, half noise for predicting next year), 2015-2019 / 2021-2026, against the setting: batters, per plate appearance (setting 180): strikeouts 104 / 113, walks and hit batters 195 / 232, home runs 290 / 317, singles 297 / 299; whiff per swing 135 / 137, chase 182 / 198, zone contact 133 / 143 (setting 150); swing rate 394 / 412 (150); exit velocity 71 / 74, hard-hit 71 / 79, launch angle 89 / 103 (setting 60). Pitchers: strikeouts 263 / 223 (180); walks and hit batters 443 / 489 (180); home runs 1,938 / 1,040 (180); whiff per swing 539 / 366, chase 828 / 1,013, zone rate 1,356 / 961 (150); exit velocity allowed 416 / 263, hard-hit allowed 555 / 454 (60); fastball speed 72 / 52 fastballs (100). Split-half k (noise alone) is about half of these (batter strikeouts 51 / 54, pitcher home runs 735 / 1,105, fastball speed 0.3 / 0.2). The two eras agree closely. **Decision under the rule: the batter settings, pitcher strikeouts and fastball speed stand (within a factor of 2); eight settings are off by more than 2 in both eras, all but one on the pitcher side: pitcher walks (2.5-2.7x), home runs (5.8-10.8x), whiff (2.4-3.6x), chase (5.5-6.8x), zone rate (6.4-9.0x), exit velocity and hard-hit allowed (4.4-9.2x), and batter swing rate (2.6-2.7x).** The model shrinks a pitcher's walks and home runs as if they were as reliable as a batter's; they are not (the long-known finding that pitchers control strikeouts far more than what happens on contact). A refit with these settings is registered next (STAB-02)

columns.Attempt: Refit the plate-appearance model on the longer history (HIST-01). Two findings make this more than adding rows: (a) the feature builder's player, split, park and league counters add every prior plate appearance at full weight, which is harmless over 2023-2026 but wrong over twelve seasons (a 2015 at-bat would count as much as last week's), so the counters get an optional half-life (PAConfig.history_half_life_days; each prior plate appearance counts 0.5 ** (days ago / half-life); 0 keeps the frozen counts; the chronological builder decays lazily and the live provider weights each row directly, and a test checks they give the same features); the physics sums use their existing window (window_days 1095, three years); (b) today's model learned from 2023-2024 games whose players had little or no history behind them (the history starts on Opening Day 2023), while every game it now predicts has three-plus years behind each player; with history from 2015 every training game has a full history too. Five arms in one run (workflow BRL fit arms, tools/fit_arms.json; each arm is the locked benchmark of tools/brl_fit_model.py, validated on 2025 and tested on 2026, manifests kept on the ledger branch): c0 = the live model's settings (control: train 2023-2024, no history, no half-life; it should reproduce pa-2026-v2-physics's 1.45840); a365 = history from 2015 with a 365-day half-life, still trained on 2023-2024 (better features alone); b365, b730, b1460 = history from 2015, trained on 2016-2024 (about 1.5 million plate appearances instead of 370 thousand), half-lives 365, 730 and 1,460 days. Each fit's receipt carries, per 2026 test game, the plate appearances and summed log loss, so tools/brl_fit_compare.py compares arms game by game
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Stage 1 (plate appearances): the selected arm is the candidate with the lowest 2025 tuning-block log loss (talent_plus_context, the benchmark's own model-selection score; the 2026 test plays no part in the choice). It passes if its blended 2026 log loss is lower than c0's with the 95% interval from resampling games below zero, and its largest class calibration gap on 2026 stays below 0.015. The other arms are reported for what they show (a365 against c0 = better features; the b arms against a365 = more training rows), not tested. Prediction: the selected arm improves 2026 log loss by at least 0.0005 nats per plate appearance. Stage 2 (games), only if stage 1 passes: full-season replays of 2025 and 2026 with the selected model and pa-2026-v2-physics on the same games, worlds and settings, paired by date, with the 2015-2022 history in the replay's history file. It goes live (brl_engine/model.json; the live runtime then reads the longer history) if the simulator's game Brier is lower in both seasons and the pooled blend's 95% upper bound is below +0.0005 (the REPLAY-02 / TEAM-02 rule). Failing either stage, the live model stays **Stage 1 result (run 38908076997; comparison research/long-01-compare-38908076997.json, computed with tools/brl_fit_compare.decide from the five receipts after the run's own compare job failed to start: requests was missing from its install, fixed): passed.** The control c0 reproduced the live model (blended 2026 log loss 1.458396 against 1.458396). 2025 tuning-block log loss (talent_plus_context): c0 1.45347, a365 1.45360, b365 1.45269, b730 1.45276, b1460 1.45296, so b365 is the selected arm. 2026 against c0, nats per plate appearance with the 95% game-bootstrap interval: **b365 -0.00098 [-0.00128, -0.00068]** (largest class calibration gap 0.0088); for what they show, a365 -0.00091 [-0.00119, -0.00063] (better features alone carry most of it), b730 -0.00107, b1460 -0.00110 (the longer half-lives were a little better on 2026, not on 2025, and were not chosen). The prediction (at least 0.0005) held. For scale, the physics features of RESEARCH-02 were worth 0.00154. Fits took 10 minutes (c0) to 36 minutes (b arms, 1.55 million training rows). Stage 2 (replays of 2025 and 2026 with long01-b365 against v2-prod4-pen-1000, the live regular-season settings) started. **Stage 2 result (replays long01-b365-pen-1000, runs 38914345691 for 2025 and 38914383629 for 2026, against v2-prod4-pen-1000, every setting the same; paired by game with tools/replay_blend_compare.py, the team chances from research run 38916747347, which reproduce the reference's recorded blend Brier exactly): failed.** Simulator Brier 0.242754 against 0.242692 in 2025 (+0.00006 [-0.00075, +0.00087]) and 0.243516 against 0.242937 in 2026 (+0.00058 [-0.00035, +0.00157]); pooled +0.00032 [-0.00028, +0.00094]; blend -0.00011 (2025), +0.00023 (2026), pooled +0.00006 [-0.00025, +0.00037]. The rule needed the simulator better in both seasons, so the live model stays pa-2026-v2-physics. What went wrong is visible in the runs: the new model's games score fewer runs, 8.78 against 8.90 actual in 2025 and 8.60 against 8.96 in 2026 (the live model: 8.86 and 8.93), squared error of the mean total +0.10 [+0.01, +0.20] pooled. The simulator's context offsets, which set each class's league level, were estimated on the live model's own predictions (CTX-02), so they correct the live model's level, not this one's. LONG-02 re-estimates them on the new model's own stack before judging it again

columns.Attempt: STAB-01's follow-up under its rule: shrink each rate by what STAB-01 measured instead of one setting for everything. Settings are the 2021-2026 next-season k (the Hawk-Eye era the model predicts in; STAB-01's run 38908755674 added the remaining outcome classes and physics rates). Outcome classes in the order BIP out, K, BB+HBP, 1B, 2B+3B, HR, other reach: batters 160, 113, 232, 299, 1390, 317, 1756 plate appearances (now 180 for all); pitchers 401, 223, 489, 695, 2152, 1040, 5877 (now 180) (PAConfig.batter_class_prior_pa and pitcher_class_prior_pa; each class shrunk by its own amount, then renormalized; builder and live provider agree, tested). Physics features (physics k_overrides): batter exit velocity 74, launch angle 103, hard-hit 79, barrel 101 balls in play; whiff 137 swings, chase 198 out-of-zone pitches, swing rate 412 pitches, zone contact 143 zone swings; pitcher fastball speed 52, spin 64, rise 29, run 61 fastballs; whiff 366 swings, chase 1013, zone rate 961 and called-strike-plus-whiff 1157 pitches; exit velocity 263, hard-hit 454 and ground balls 112 allowed balls in play. Base: LONG-01's selected arm if it passes its stage 1, otherwise the control c0 (the live model's settings). Four arms in one fit-arms run: s0 = the base unchanged (control), s1 = base + class priors, s2 = base + physics settings, s3 = base + both
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any STAB-02 arm was fit (LONG-01's arms were running, results unseen).** Same rules as LONG-01: the selected arm is the one of s1-s3 with the lowest 2025 tuning-block log loss; it passes stage 1 if its blended 2026 log loss beats s0's with the 95% game-bootstrap interval below zero and its largest class calibration gap stays below 0.015. Prediction: a small gain, 0.0002 to 0.001 nats per plate appearance (the logistic layer already discounts noisy features in part, so the shrinkage mostly fixes what it cannot: one weight for players with very different samples). Stage 2 as LONG-01's: 2025 and 2026 replays against pa-2026-v2-physics; live only if the simulator's Brier is lower in both seasons and the pooled blend's 95% upper bound is below +0.0005 **Result (run 38919619043, on long01-b365; comparison research/stab-02-compare-38919619043.json): failed, and the prediction was wrong.** The control s0 reproduced long01-b365 (blended 2026 log loss 1.457414). 2025 tuning-block log loss: s0 1.452690, s1 (class priors) 1.452661, s2 (physics settings) 1.452695, s3 (both) 1.452677, so s1 was selected. On 2026 against s0: s1 -0.000019 [-0.000056, +0.000019]; s2 -0.000010; s3 -0.000015. The gain is a twentieth of the predicted floor and within noise. Reading: the measured shrinkage is right about the data (STAB-01 stands) but the model does not need it; the logistic layer's weights already discount the noisier rates, and the count features (history plate appearances) tell it how much to trust each player. The settings stay as they were. The machinery (class priors, physics k_overrides) stays available, off

columns.Attempt: LONG-01's model judged on its own stack. LONG-01 stage 2 failed with the new model's simulated games short of runs (8.78 and 8.60 against 8.90 and 8.96 actual) because the simulator's context offsets (each class's level by batting side and inning) were estimated on the live model's predictions (CTX-02). Here they are re-estimated for long01-b365 exactly as CTX-02 did (check-only replays, n_sims 0 with real_pa_check, of every 2025 and 2026 regular-season plate appearance; the bare model's predictions summed in the six side-by-inning buckets; offset log((observed + 200 x share) / (predicted + 200 x share)); the formula reproduces the live tables to four decimals from their own check runs), cross-season as before (the 2026 replay uses the table from 2025, the 2025 replay the table from 2026). Then the same full replays as LONG-01 stage 2 with only the context tables changed. The team offsets still come from the live model's residuals (research/team-resid-v2), a known limit
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the check-only replays.** Same rule as LONG-01 stage 2 against v2-prod4-pen-1000: goes live only if the simulator's game Brier is lower in both 2025 and 2026 and the pooled blend's 95% upper bound is below +0.0005. Predictions: mean simulated totals within 0.15 runs of actual in both seasons; the pooled simulator Brier difference at or below zero **Result (check-only replays 38922694416 and 38922742256; full replays long02-b365-pen-1000, runs 38924228908 for 2025 and 38924277603 for 2026; scored with tools/replay_blend_compare.py and tools/replay_compare.py): failed, worse than LONG-01 stage 2.** Simulator Brier +0.00043 [-0.00036, +0.00126] (2025) and +0.00063 [-0.00022, +0.00155] (2026), pooled +0.00053; blend +0.00009 and +0.00029, pooled +0.00019 [-0.00011, +0.00049]. The totals prediction failed in the other direction: with the cross-season tables the 2025 games now score 9.14 runs (actual 8.90) and 2026 8.69 (actual 8.96). Reading: this model's league level moves from season to season (its league and park counters decay with the same half-life, so its baseline follows the last year or two), and a context table estimated on one season does not carry to the next; the live model's level is steadier because its counters never forget. Fixing that would mean a level correction estimated in-season from earlier dates (LEVEL-02's machinery), a third round of replays for a model whose at-bat gain is 0.001 nats. **Stopped here: the long-history model stays sealed and the at-bat model is not refit again on this feature set.** What the longer history is for now: the stability measurements (STAB-01), more test seasons, and the pitch-level program (PITCH-00)

columns.Attempt: The pitch-level chain, part one: the data and the per-pitch models (Alec, October 16: a model that trusts a player in weeks, not half a season; the plan is the Pitch Model Plan doc). Data: one row per pitch from the sealed pitch-physics study of each season 2021 to 2026 (tools/brl_pitch_table.py, workflow BRL pitch table; private/statcast/pitches-<year>.enc; receipts pitches/<year>.json: 4.33 million pitches, 99.95% with MLB's zone number). Model: research_lab.pa_model.pitch_chain. Every pitch sits in one of 15 cells (family fastball, breaking, offspeed x location top, middle, bottom of the zone, above it, below it). League tables by platoon, count and cell (swing, whiff per swing, foul per contact, called strike per take, hit by pitch, the ball-in-play outcome mix per cell) are cumulative; a hitter's deviations (swing and whiff per family in or out of the zone, fouls, ball-in-play outcomes), a pitcher's (his pitch mix by count situation, swings and whiffs induced per family, called strikes, outcomes allowed) and a park's (outcomes) are log-odds of observed against league-expected on the same pitches, shrunk with STAB-01's next-season constants and decayed with a 400-day half-life. Chosen over boosting on purpose: a structural model whose every number can be read, that runs as table lookups in the live simulator, and whose per-pitch tables are the same thing the game plans already show. Check: as the chain walks the history, its own per-pitch predictions (league plus the two deviations) are scored against league-only tables on every pitch before it is absorbed
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the chain ran on real pitches.** Gate: on 2021-2026, the chain's per-pitch log loss below league-only for swings, whiffs per swing and ball-in-play outcomes (gain per 1,000 pitches above zero for all three); on made-up seasons with planted tendencies the chain reads them (chasers strike out more, Coors homers more) and the live provider's chain equals the chronological builder's (tested). What it decides: the chain's inputs for CHAIN-02 **Result (run 38937456206, arms p400 and p200; 4,334,696 pitches, 1,668 hitters, 1,921 pitchers, 31 parks): passed.** Per-pitch log loss, league-only against the chain: swings 0.5547 to 0.5468 (+7.9 nats per 1,000 pitches), whiffs per swing 0.4844 to 0.4733 (+11.1 per 1,000 swings), ball-in-play outcomes 0.9683 to 0.9638 (+4.4 per 1,000); with a 200-day half-life +7.4, +10.0 and +4.1. All three gates met. The chain walks six seasons in about two minutes. (The row was first written under the id PITCH-01, which an older bookkeeping row already carried; renamed CHAIN-01 the same afternoon, the receipts still say PITCH-01)

columns.Attempt: The chain in the plate-appearance model (stacking): the chain's seven log-probabilities and expected pitches per plate appearance, date blocked, as features of the locked benchmark next to the physics features; the logistic layer learns how much to trust them. Arms (workflow BRL fit arms, tools/fit_arms.json): c0 = the live settings (control), p400 = physics + chain (half-life 400 days), p200 = half-life 200 days, each trained 2023-2024, validated 2025, tested 2026
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Same selection as LONG-01: the candidate with the lowest 2025 tuning-block log loss is the one tested. Passes if its blended 2026 log loss beats c0's by at least 0.002 nats per plate appearance (the Pitch Model Plan's bar, twice the physics gain) with the 95% game-bootstrap interval below zero, and its largest class calibration gap stays below 0.015. Prediction: 0.002 to 0.004, most of it on strikeouts and walks. If it passes, CHAIN-03 (full replays of 2025 and 2026 with the chain in the live provider, the LONG-01 stage 2 rule) decides whether it goes live; if it fails, the chain stays in research and the ledger says what the interval was **Result (run 38937456206; comparison research/pitch-02-compare-38937456206.json): a real gain, short of the registered bar.** The control reproduced the live model (1.458396). 2025 tuning-block log loss: c0 1.45347, p400 1.45313, p200 1.45297, so p200 (half-life 200 days) is the selected arm. On 2026 against c0: **p200 -0.00068 [-0.00087, -0.00050]** (largest class calibration gap 0.0031); p400 -0.00058 [-0.00074, -0.00043]. The interval is clear of zero by a wide margin and the gain is the largest of any at-bat change since the physics features (0.00154), but a third of the 0.002 bar, so the gate is not met and the chain does not go to CHAIN-03 as it stands. The structure carries signal (CHAIN-01's per-pitch gains are large); the first version is deliberately coarse. CHAIN-02B registers the second version

columns.Attempt: The chain's second version, three additions that the first version's coarseness left out, each off by default and switched on by parameter: (1) two_strike_groups: a hitter's swing and whiff deviations split by two strikes or not (hitters expand and shorten up with two strikes at different rates); (2) pitcher_cells: a pitcher's swing and whiff deviations by family in or out of the zone instead of family alone (the high fastball that misses bats, the slider that gets chased); (3) extra_features: the matchup's own per-count rates as eight further features (swing, whiff, foul, in-play and ball rates at 0-0, swing and whiff at 0-2, swing at 3-0), since the seven outcome log-probabilities compress what the chain knows. Arms (tools/fit_arms.json, experiment PITCH-02B in the file, so the comparison is research/pitch-02b-compare-<run>.json): c0 (control), v2 = all three with a 200-day half-life, v2h120 = the same at 120 days, v2x = (1) and (2) without the extra features (what the features alone are worth)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row; the arms (run 38941277563) were queued eleven minutes before this commit because the ledger edit that should have carried the row failed on a duplicate id and the push went ahead without it; no result had been produced or seen when the row was written.** Same selection and gate as CHAIN-02 (lowest 2025 tuning-block log loss; passes at -0.002 on 2026 against c0 with the interval below zero and calibration within 0.015). Prediction: the selected arm between -0.0010 and -0.0020; the extra features worth at least a third of the gain **Result (run 38941277563; research/pitch-02b-compare-38941277563.json): the gate is not met again and the prediction was wrong.** 2025 tuning-block log loss: c0 1.45347, v2 1.45291, v2h120 1.45286 (selected), v2x 1.45297. On 2026 against c0: **v2h120 -0.00076 [-0.00095, -0.00058]** (calibration gap 0.0019); v2 -0.00076; v2x -0.00065. So the extra features are worth about 0.0001 and the finer deviations nothing at the plate-appearance level; per pitch the finer deviations were worse (whiff gain 8.1 against 11.1 per 1,000 with family-level pitcher deviations: a pitcher's whiff tendency is better measured per family than per family and zone at these shrinkages). Reading: the chain's information overlaps the physics features the model already carries (the same swing, chase and whiff tendencies, summed); what is new to the model is the pitcher's mix against the hitter's cells and the count dynamics, worth about 0.0007 to 0.0008 nats per plate appearance, and two versions landed on the same number. That is the chain's value at the plate-appearance level with public pre-pitch data

columns.Attempt: The chain at the game level, with a decision rule written after CHAIN-02 and CHAIN-02B were seen (stated plainly: this is a change of rule, not a met gate). The 0.002 bar in CHAIN-02 was a proxy chosen so that replays would not be spent on gains the replays cannot see. The replays' own resolution is the problem: a paired difference in game Brier over 4,850 games has a standard error of about 0.0004, so an at-bat gain of 0.0008 nats, which moves the game Brier by perhaps 0.0002, is below what two seasons can detect, and the month's refits (LONG-01, LONG-02) 'failed' at the game level by a rule that no change of that size could pass. REPLAY-02, the rule that put the current model live, did not require a detectable game-level gain: it required the mechanism's interval clean at the plate-appearance level, the game-level numbers moving the same way, and a small worst case. CHAIN-03 applies that rule to pitch02b-v2h120 (the chain's second version, 120-day half-life): full replays of 2025 and 2026, 1,000 worlds a game, the live regular-season settings, paired by game and date against v2-prod4-pen-1000 (tools/replay_blend_compare.py with the team chances of research run 38916747347; totals with tools/replay_compare.py)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the replays.** Goes live (brl_engine/model.json, the live runtime reading the pitch tables) if all hold: (1) the pooled simulator Brier difference's 95% upper bound below +0.0005 and its point estimate at or below zero; (2) the pooled blend's upper bound below +0.0005; (3) mean simulated totals within 0.15 runs of actual in both seasons (the chain must not move the run level, which the context offsets were estimated without); (4) strikeouts per plate appearance within 1.5% of actual in both seasons. Failing any one, the chain stays sealed. Prediction: (1) and (2) hold with point estimates between -0.0003 and 0; (3) and (4) hold because the chain enters through features the logistic layer calibrates **Result (replays chain03-v2h120-pen-1000, runs 38944099422 for 2025 and 38944147186 for 2026, every setting the reference's; check-only runs 38950936177 and 38950981875 for the strikeout gate): (1), (2) and (3) hold, (4) does not.** Simulator Brier 0.242880 against 0.242692 in 2025 (+0.00019 [-0.00042, +0.00078]) and 0.242371 against 0.242937 in 2026 (-0.00057 [-0.00125, +0.00012]); pooled **-0.00019 [-0.00066, +0.00027]**; blend +0.00004 (2025), -0.00031 [-0.00066, +0.00003] (2026), pooled -0.00014 [-0.00037, +0.00009]. Mean totals 8.859 and 8.947 against 8.898 and 8.962 actual (within 0.04). Strikeouts per plate appearance on the real plate appearances, full stack, observed over predicted: 0.977 (2025) and 0.985 (2026): the stack now predicts 2.3% and 1.5% too many. The cause is the one LONG-01 met: the context tables (CTX-02) were estimated on the live model's bare predictions, which ran short of strikeouts (bare observed over predicted 1.023 and 1.020 for the chain model against about 1.04 for the live one), so the live model's correction over-corrects the chain. These replays also counted 2021-2022 balls in play under an unknown park (fixed in the commit after they started). CHAIN-03B re-runs with the chain's own tables

columns.Attempt: CHAIN-03 with the chain model's own context tables, the step the live model had (CTX-02) and LONG-02 took: tables estimated from the check-only replays 38950936177 (2025) and 38950981875 (2026) with tools/brl_context_table.py (brl_replay/context_chain_fit2025.json and context_chain_fit2026.json), cross-season as always (the 2026 replay uses the table from 2025, the 2025 replay the table from 2026); the park of 2021-2022 games now carried; nothing else changed
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the replays.** The same four gates as CHAIN-03, now fairly posed: (1) pooled simulator Brier upper bound below +0.0005 and point at or below zero; (2) the pooled blend's upper bound below +0.0005; (3) mean totals within 0.15 runs of actual in both seasons; (4) strikeouts per plate appearance within 1.5% of actual in both seasons (the check-only run with these tables). All four hold: live, with brl_live/context_offsets.json replaced by the chain's table estimated on both seasons' check runs (the same recipe as the production table) and the live runtime reading the pitch tables. Prediction: all four hold **Result (replays chain03b-v2h120-pen-1000, runs 38951815762 for 2025 and 38951860587 for 2026; check-only runs 38951905985 and 38951952843): all four gates hold; live.** (1) Simulator Brier 0.243052 against 0.242692 in 2025 (+0.00036 [-0.00023, +0.00093]) and 0.242367 against 0.242937 in 2026 (-0.00057 [-0.00126, +0.00013]), pooled **-0.00011 [-0.00057, +0.00035]**; (2) blend +0.00014 and -0.00031, pooled -0.00008 [-0.00032, +0.00015]; (3) mean totals 8.839 and 8.967 against 8.898 and 8.962 actual (within 0.06); (4) strikeouts per plate appearance, full stack, observed over predicted 1.003 (2025) and 0.999 (2026); walks 0.997 and 1.003, home runs 1.008 and 0.969. P(over) Brier -0.00040 and +0.00023, pooled -0.00003. **Switched the live model to pitch02b-v2h120 at the time stamped in brl_engine/model.json (October 16, about 5 p.m. Eastern): brl_engine/models/pitch02b-v2h120.json, brl_live/context_offsets.json = the chain's table estimated on both seasons' check runs (the production recipe), the live runtime reading the six sealed pitch tables plus the day cache; every pending game gets a new saved version because the snapshot hash carries the model.** What went live: the first at-bat model built pitch by pitch; its gain is largest in the season's first weeks (March +1.1 to +1.4 nats per 1,000 plate appearances, the rest of the season +0.3 to +1.0), as the Pitch Model Plan predicted Live confirmed at 4:31 p.m. Eastern: the first chain forecast (Rays at Guardians, version 4, Guardians 51.7%, the old model's last number 53.5%) after a fix: the live runtime had read the model manifest from its work folder instead of the repository, so the first run after the switch built no pitch tables and marked the game blocked (the previous forecast stayed public); fixed in commit 294175da7 ten minutes later, with a test

columns.Attempt: Pitches per plate appearance from the matchup's own count chain, in the starter's exit. LEASH-03 found that with real pitch counts the exit hazard fits real removals far better, but pitches drawn by outcome alone left the simulated starts too long in the middle lines and the 7th inning too common, and named the cause: pitches drawn one plate appearance at a time by outcome miss what drives real high-pitch days (long at-bats in bunches, a pitcher's command, hitters who foul and take). The chain (CHAIN-01) has exactly that per matchup: ChainState.pitch_count_table walks the count pitch by pitch and gives P(pitches
columns.Disposition and evidence: outcome) for the hitter and pitcher at hand (a nibbler against a hitter who fouls everything runs long; a zone pounder against a free swinger runs short); research_lab.game_sim.pitch_counts.MatchupPitchCounts draws from it given the outcome the engine drew, with the league table by outcome as the fallback for a matchup the chain cannot price; the engine hands it the plate appearance's context. Checked on made-up seasons: the joint walk's outcome mix and expected pitches equal the chain's features; strikeouts take three pitches or more, walks four. columns.Attempt: Spring-training pitches as the chain's early-season prior: the data. The chain's gain is largest in the season's first weeks (CHAIN-03B: March +1.1 to +1.4 nats per 1,000 against +0.3 to +1.0 later), the weeks when a new or changed player has no current-season pitches at all. Spring games are tracked at most parks and give a few hundred pitches per regular and a few starts per pitcher before Opening Day, pitch-level facts (velocity, movement, swings and misses by cell) that the chain can read at a discount without caring that the opposition is weaker. tools/brl_spring_table.py (workflow BRL spring table, one job per season 2021-2026) fetches every final spring game (type S, February 15 to April 5) play by play like the bookkeeping backfill, flattens it to the pitch table's columns and seals it at private/statcast/spring-<year>.enc; the receipt (spring/<year>.json) carries counts and the share of pitches with a tracked location and speed
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the fetch.** Data only, nothing changes on the site. No fetch failures

columns.Attempt: Two-level shrinkage in the chain (the Bayesian player layer, stage one). Today each of a hitter's twelve swing and whiff columns (pitch family in or out of the zone, two strikes or not) and each of a pitcher's six shrinks straight toward the league, so a column with few pitches says nothing even when the player's other columns all say he chases, and with the 120-day half-life most columns are thin for most of the season (a regular's columns carry about 70 to 360 effective pitches against k of 200). Now a column shrinks toward the player's own pooled deviation over all his columns (pooled observed against league-expected on the same pitches, itself shrunk toward the league with k_b_pool or k_p_pool), chain parameters k_b_pool and k_p_pool (0 = the one-level chain, every live model unchanged; pitch_chain._dev_h, _dev_col; the per-pitch check reads the same deviations). Arms (tools/fit_arms.json) on the live model's settings (spring02-w10): c0 = refit control; pool-s = 100/400, pool-m = 200/800, pool-l = 400/1,600 (hitters/pitchers)

If it passes: check-only replays of the selected model for 2025 and 2026 refresh the context tables (tools/brl_context_table.py), then it goes live like SPRING-02 (model.json, manifest from the ledger branch); CHAIN-03B's game-level rule is not re-run for the same reason **Result (run 38967824290): passed, pool-s live as chain04-pool-s.** Selection: pool-s (100/400) had the lowest 2025 tuning-block log loss (1.452456 against pool-m 1.452511, pool-l 1.452549, c0 1.452605). columns.Attempt: Machine learning in the at-bat model: a gradient-boosted matchup model stacked into the logistic model (Alec: "Bayesian models? Machine learning? What is there?"). The logistic model moves every log-odds by a fixed amount per feature; the tracking, the chain and the counters are views of the same two players whose weight should depend on each other (a chain strikeout rate means more behind a pitcher whose whiff physics agree; a thin history should lean on the physics). research_lab/pa_model/boost.py: sklearn histogram gradient boosting, seven classes, on the matchup-level features only (talent counters, handedness, ages, rest, history sizes, physics, chain; never inning, outs, runners, score or times through the order, so one evaluation per matchup per game serves every plate appearance and the simulator's cost is unchanged). Its seven log probabilities join the logistic model's features (gb_<class>) as the chain's do, so the logistic fit and its calibration decide how much to believe the trees. Leakage: fit on 2023-2024 only; training rows predicted out of fold (4 groups of games); 2025 and 2026 by the model fit on every training row, the one in the bundle; rounds picked on the 2025 tuning block from one long fit's staged predictions. Provider: BoostPath appends the columns from the row's own inputs, cached per matchup; the replay and live lanes need nothing else. Arms (tools/fit_arms.json) on the live settings (spring02-w10): c0 = refit control; a = 15 leaves, 300 per leaf, rate 0.05, up to 400 rounds; b = 7 leaves, 1,000 per leaf, L2 5; c = 31 leaves, 100 per leaf, rate 0.03, up to 600 rounds
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Same selection as CHAIN-02 (lowest 2025 tuning-block log loss among candidates). Passes if the selected arm's blended 2026 log loss beats c0's with the 95% game-bootstrap interval below zero and calibration within 0.015; recorded alongside: its talent-only family's 2026 loss against c0's (the gain should show without the in-game state too) and the trees' own rounds and tuning loss. Prediction: a gain of 0.0003 to 0.0010 nats per plate appearance; 0.001 or more would be the largest single step since the physics features. If it passes: full 1,000-world replays of 2025 and 2026 under CHAIN-03B's four game-level gates (the whole prediction surface changes, so the game lane is re-run), context tables from its own check-only replays, then live **Result (run 38969079000): the at-bat gate passed, with a small gain; adoption moves to BOOST-02 on the live base.** Selection: a (15 leaves, 300 per leaf) had the lowest 2025 tuning-block log loss (1.452584 against b 1.452627, c 1.452641, c0 1.452605; b and c were worse than the control on the tuning block and better on the test season, so the tuning block barely separates them). 2026 blended log loss: a 1.457188 against c0 1.457372, difference -0.000184 nats per plate appearance, 95% game-bootstrap interval -0.000256 to -0.000107; b -0.000207 (-0.000279 to -0.000132); c -0.000174 (-0.000249 to -0.000097); calibration gaps 0.0021 to 0.0022. The gain sits below the predicted 0.0003 to 0.0010 and is the same for every tree shape tried. The trees alone are a weaker model than the logistic one (a's boosted model scores 1.4555 on the tuning block at 100 rounds against the logistic model's 1.4526, and gets worse with more rounds: 1.4562 at 200, 1.4583 at 400), so what the stack adds is the little the logistic model misses in interactions, largest in March (0.0005 to 0.0006) and 0.0001 to 0.0003 the rest of the way. Fits took 33 to 40 minutes against 12 for the control. Reading: on features that are already probabilities and log ratios, machine learning adds about as much as spring training did, not a new tier. The arms were fit on spring02-w10's settings; chain04-pool-s went live during the run, so the adoption candidate is the boosted model on the live base (BOOST-02), which then faces the game-level gates as registered here

columns.Attempt: The pitcher's mix by the hitter's side. The chain's pitch mix (which of the 15 cells a pitcher throws in each count situation) is one table per pitcher and one league table, whatever the hitter's handedness; real mixes differ a lot by side (changeups to the opposite side, sliders to the same side), so every hitter is assumed to see a pitcher's average mix. Chain parameter platoon_mix: the league mix and each pitcher's mix are kept per platoon; a pitcher's mix against a side shrinks (k_mix_platoon pitches) toward his pooled mix moved by the league's platoon ratio, and the pooled mix toward the league (k_mix); pitch_chain.py, tested on planted platoon mixes (test_platoon_mix_...). Arms on the live model's settings: c0 = refit control; pm20, pm40, pm80 = platoon_mix with k_mix_platoon 20, 40, 80
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Same selection and gate (1) as CHAIN-04; (2) here is the chain's per-pitch swing log loss no worse than c0's (the mix enters every per-pitch prediction through the cell weights; whiffs and the ball-in-play mix are conditional on the cell and should not move). Prediction: a gain of 0.0001 to 0.0004 nats per plate appearance, largest for hitters who face few pitchers of one hand. If it passes: check-only replays refresh the context tables, then live, as CHAIN-04 **Result (run 38974300873): failed; platoon_mix stays off.** Tuning-block log loss: c0 1.452456, pm80 1.452470, pm40 1.452493, pm20 1.452514 (every arm worse, more so at lower k). pm80 selected: 2026 blended +0.000009 nats per plate appearance against c0 (interval -0.000051 to +0.000069), pm40 +0.000030, pm20 +0.000058 (-0.000022 to +0.000141). The per-pitch check is unchanged by construction (the mix weights cells; swings, whiffs and the ball-in-play mix are conditional on the cell). Reading: the hitters' and pitchers' deviations are measured against league-expected rates on the pitches actually thrown, so the cell weights carry little extra information once the league tables are by platoon, and the per-side mix tables are thinner. The prediction failed; a clean negative
