columns.Attempt: The day's unseen availability as a per-game shock on the reliever choice. BULLPEN-03/04 measured the miss and it stands on today's settings (LEASH-04's replays): relievers shown at 60 to 80% to pitch pitched 52.3% (2025) and 52.2% (2026); shown at 80% or more, 52.1% and 52.5%; the mean chance is right (30.2% against 31.1%, 29.5% against 30.3%) and the 25-40% bin runs 1.3 to 1.7 points low. The per-entry conditional logit (BULLPEN-01) is fit on real entries and calibrated per entry, but the simulator re-draws it at every entry of every world as if nothing persisted within a game; in real games what keeps the closer in the dugout (a sore arm, a warm-up the night before, a plan) holds for the whole game, so no arm pitches in more than about half of the games the simulator is 85% sure of. Built: research_lab.game_sim.reliever_choice.RelieverChoice(doc, game_sigma): a standard-normal shock times game_sigma added to each candidate's utility, drawn once per reliever and simulated game from the world's seed and his id (GameState.seed, GameState.reliever_shocks; it moves no other random number, so paired comparisons stay paired); replay option reliever_game_sigma; live ADJUST reliever_game_sigma (0.0, off). Test: LEASH-04's replay settings (pitch02b-v2h120, the chain pitch draws, starter lines, paired streams) with sigma 0.75, 1.25 and 2.0, both seasons, scored by tools/brl_bullpen_cal.py and against LEASH-04's replays (sigma 0) by game
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the replays.** Gates, in both seasons: (1) every chance-to-pitch bin from 10% up with 200 or more rows within 5 points of the share who pitched (the under-10% bin holds the call-ups and returns the simulator cannot name, 13 points short either way, and is not gated); (2) the mean chance within 2 points; (3) Brier against the season's constant share better than LEASH-04's by at least 0.0005; (4) no harm: starters' outs half lines move by no more than 0.5 point, the win Brier pooled not worse than +0.0002, the mean total within 0.10 runs a game. Decision rule: the smallest sigma meeting (1) to (4) goes live (ADJUST reliever_game_sigma) and the bullpen note's hedge comes off. Prediction: 0.75 leaves the 60-80% bin 6 to 9 points high, 1.25 brings it within 5, 2.0 overshoots (the top bins fall below the actual share and the 10-25% bin runs high); the mean total rises by 0.02 to 0.08 runs (lesser arms pitch more) **Result (runs 38979794007 to 38979860071, six replays): failed at every sigma; the shock stays off.** The 60 to 80% bin: sigma 0.75 66.0% shown against 52.8% pitched (2025) and 66.2 against 52.0 (2026); 1.25 65.4 against 51.9 and 65.6 against 51.8; 2.0 65.2 against 50.2 and 65.3 against 50.5 (LEASH-04's 66.5/52.3 and 66.7/52.2): the shock moves arms out of the top bins (2,654 rows to 1,955, 1,292 and 678) without moving the miss of those that stay, and the 10 to 25% bin runs high (2.3, 3.8 and 5.7 points in 2025). Brier 0.20293, 0.20326, 0.20485 against 0.20312 (2025): no sigma clears the 0.0005 bar. No harm: outs half lines unmoved, win Brier pooled +0.00008, +0.00012, -0.00001 (intervals within +0.0003), mean totals +0.01 to +0.03. The prediction failed; what persists within a game is not the cause (BULLPEN-08: the choice is calibrated entry by entry; the top two arms enter 25% too often in every cell). BULLPEN-09 (the temperature) is the next test

columns.Attempt: Opponent-adjusted expectations in the chain. A hitter's swing and whiff counters hold observed against league-expected on the same pitches (platoon, count, cell); the pitcher who threw them is not in the expectation, so a hitter who faced the league's best whiff arms for a month reads as a whiffer, and a pitcher who faced free swingers reads as a whiff pitcher. With chain parameter opp_adjust each side's expectation carries the other side's current deviation (the chain's own prediction without the player: the hitter's counters take league moved by the pitcher's deviation, the pitcher's take league moved by the hitter's), the standard strength-of-schedule adjustment (pitch_chain.py absorb_date; test_opponent_adjusted_...: a planted hitter who saw only the whiff machine is no longer read as a whiffer). The league tables, the per-pitch check and the ball-in-play counters are unchanged. Arms (tools/fit_arms.json) on the live model's settings (chain04b-xs-tight): c0 = refit control; opp = opp_adjust (the run is shared with CHAIN-07: its arms tiers and both ride along; this row's gate is judged on the opp arm against c0, the run's selection rule picks the arm to adopt)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Same selection and gates as CHAIN-04: (1) the candidate beats c0 on blended 2026 log loss with the 95% game-bootstrap interval below zero and calibration within 0.015; (2) per-pitch swing and whiff log loss both no worse than c0's. Prediction: a gain of 0.00005 to 0.0002 nats per plate appearance, concentrated in April and May (by midseason opponents average out); per-pitch whiffs 0.5 to 2 per 1,000 better. If it passes: check-only replays refresh the context tables, then live, as CHAIN-04 **Result (run 38982649812, the two-arm run; the shared four-arm run follows): passed.** Tuning-block log loss 1.452253 against c0 1.452393. (1) 2026 blended 1.456882 against 1.457046, difference -0.000164 nats per plate appearance, 95% game-bootstrap interval -0.000203 to -0.000121; calibration gap 0.0037. (2) per pitch: swings 0.54376 to 0.54370, whiffs 0.47029 to 0.47016, both no worse (the per-pitch check itself is barely moved; the gain is in the deviations the plate-appearance model reads). The size held, the timing did not: the gain is smallest in March (-0.00005) and grows through the season (April 0.00016, July 0.00018, August 0.00021, September 0.00028). Reading: with a 120-day half-life the counters hold the recent schedule, and the schedule's bias (divisional runs, September call-ups, who a team happened to face) accumulates rather than averages out; the adjustment removes it. Adoption as registered: check-only replays, context tables, live; the four-arm run (38983124806) repeated opp's result exactly and selected both (opp with CHAIN-07's tiers, -0.000197), which is the model adopted

columns.Attempt: Fastball speed in the chain's cells. The 15 cells are pitch family by location; a 91-mph fastball and a 99-mph fastball in the same spot share a cell, so the league table cannot know that the hard one gets more whiffs, and a pitcher's velocity reaches the chain only through his own whiff deviation (240 swings to stabilize). With chain parameter fb_tiers the fastball family splits by speed (under 93, 93 to 95.9, 96 and up mph; an unknown speed is the middle tier; FB_TIER_EDGES) into 25 cells for the league tables, the pitcher's mix and the ball-in-play mix; the hitters' and pitchers' deviation columns keep the three families (12 and 6 columns), so no player counter gets thinner. A new arm's mix shows his velocity after about 40 pitches (k_mix), and the league table for those cells gives him the whiffs that go with it (pitch_chain.py cell_index, fb_tier; prepare now carries fam, reg and vt; test_fastball_tiers_...: planted, a one-game arm at 98 is expected to miss 1.5 times the bats of the same arm at 90 and the two are identical with tiers off; builder and state agree; 15-cell parity exact). Arms, sharing CHAIN-06's run: c0 = refit control; tiers = fb_tiers; both = fb_tiers with opp_adjust (additivity)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Gates as CHAIN-04, judged on the tiers arm against c0: (1) blended 2026 log loss better with the 95% game-bootstrap interval below zero and calibration within 0.015; (2) per-pitch swing and whiff log loss both no worse than c0's. The run's selection rule (lowest 2025 tuning-block log loss among opp, tiers, both) picks the arm adopted if its own gate (1) holds. Prediction: tiers gains 0.0001 to 0.0004 nats per plate appearance, largest for pitchers with few pitches in the banks (April, call-ups), and per-pitch whiffs 2 to 5 per 1,000 better; both adds the two gains. If it passes: check-only replays refresh the context tables, then live, as CHAIN-04 **Result (run 38983124806, four arms): tiers passed by a hair; both selected and adopted.** Tuning-block log loss: both 1.452227, opp 1.452253, tiers 1.452369, c0 1.452393. tiers against c0: 2026 blended -0.000027 nats per plate appearance (interval -0.000051 to -0.000002, just below zero), calibration 0.0041; per pitch swings 0.54376 to 0.54362 and whiffs 0.47029 to 0.47000, both better. The predicted 0.0001 to 0.0004 did not come: the pitcher's fastball speed already reaches the plate-appearance model through the physics features, so the cells add only what the mix-by-tier knows that a single speed number does not. both against c0: -0.000197 (-0.000246 to -0.000150), calibration 0.0037, per pitch 0.54354 and 0.46987; the two gains add (opp alone -0.000164 in the same run). By month, both: March -0.00001, April 0.00015, May 0.00017, June 0.00012, July 0.00025, August 0.00021, September 0.00034. Adoption: chain67-both (opp_adjust and fb_tiers on the xs-tight settings); check-only replays chain67-check-2025 (run 38991651341) and chain67-check-2026 (run 38991661459) gave the context tables (brl_live/context_offsets.json pooled, largest change against xs-tight's table 0.0058; brl_replay/context_chain67_fit2025/2026.json); live as chain67-both from 9:48 p.m. Eastern, October 16 (brl_engine/model.json)

columns.Attempt: Is the reliever choice too sure of its favorites entry by entry? (BULLPEN-07's first replays, described after looking: the per-game shock moves which arms sit in the top bins but not their miss: at sigma 1.25 arms shown 60 to 80% pitched 51.9% against 65.4% shown, 2025, and the 10 to 25% bin ran 3.8 points high; the miss also holds in every kind of real game: in close wins arms shown 68% pitched 63%, in close losses 56%, in other wins 50%, in other losses 42%.) So the next question is the per-entry chance itself. Research lane, tools/brl_research.py choice_temperature: on every real regular-season relief entry with a choice set (tools/brl_reliever_choice.py choice_rows, the live table's own features), the live table's chance per candidate; calibration by bins of the candidate's chance and of each entry's favorite (mean chance against the share chosen); and a temperature T on the utilities (softmax of u over T, grid 0.6 to 1.6) fitted by maximum likelihood on the other seasons, with the held-out log-likelihood and the bins at the fitted T. Synthetic check (test_choice_temperature_...): planted sets at T 1.6 read as too sure at T 1 and about right at the fitted T. Aggregates only
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: the favorites' bins show the table too sure (chosen share 5 to 10 points under the mean chance in the 40 to 80% bins), and the fitted T is 1.2 to 1.5 in every season with a better held-out log-likelihood. Decision rule: if T from the other seasons is above 1.1 in every season with a better held-out log-likelihood, the live choice reads a temperature (RelieverChoice temperature, ADJUST reliever_choice_temperature, to be built) and BULLPEN-07's replay rule applies to it in place of the shock; if T is within 0.1 of 1 the choice is calibrated per entry and the game-level miss lies elsewhere (the situations the simulator creates or the candidate set) **Result (run 38985237929; 63,415 regular-season entries 2023-2026, 4,731 of them to arms outside the choice set): the live table is calibrated entry by entry; T is 1.0 in every season.** The favorites: mean chance 34.8% against 33.4% chosen over all entries; by bin, 10-20%: 17.8 against 17.9; 20-30: 25.1 against 24.3; 30-40: 34.4 against 32.6; 40-50: 44.4 against 40.6; 50-60: 54.4 against 51.7; 60-80: 68.5 against 67.2; 80 and up: 89.8 against 89.3. Every candidate by bin within 2 points except 30-50% (1.6 and 3.7 high). The temperature fitted from the other seasons is 1.0 for each season (held-out log-likelihood per entry -1.7515, -1.7392, -1.7315, -1.7625 at T 1; every other T on the grid worse). The prediction failed, and the rule's second branch applies: the choice is not too sure of its favorites; the game-level miss (arms shown 60% or more pitch 52%) lies in the situations the simulator creates at its entries or in the candidate set, not in the choice. Taken with BULLPEN-07's first replays (the per-game shock moves which arms sit in the top bins, not their miss), the next diagnostic is the simulated choice sets and entry situations against the real ones, per cell (a replay that records them)

columns.Attempt: The choice's temperature at the game level. BULLPEN-08 found the live choice calibrated entry by entry on the whole (T 1.0 by likelihood), but its favorites run 2 to 4 points high from 30 to 60% (44.4 said, 40.6 chosen) and its second choices a point low (14.3 said, 15.2 chosen), and on today's replays (LEASH-04's) the top two arms by 14-day share enter 0.641 and 0.624 times a team-game against 0.515 and 0.498 real, 25% too often in every inning and score cell, worst when trailing by three or more (+50%) and in the 5th or earlier (+46%); the entries themselves land in the right cells (3.19 a team-game against 3.29). A few points per entry on the same arm compound over the game into the 13-point miss at 60 to 80%. Built: RelieverChoice(doc, temperature): utilities over T (1.0 = as fitted); replay option reliever_choice_temperature; live ADJUST reliever_choice_temperature (1.0). Test: LEASH-04's replay settings with T 1.15 and 1.3, both seasons, scored as BULLPEN-07 (the bullpen bins, the top two arms' entries, the outs ladder, wins and totals against LEASH-04's replays)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the replays (to be launched when the runner queue is clear; two runs at a time).** Gates as BULLPEN-07's (1) to (4), plus (5) the top two arms' entries per team-game within 10% of real in both seasons. Prediction: at 1.15 the 60 to 80% bin comes within 8 points and the top two within 15%; at 1.3 within 5 points and 10% with the 10 to 25% bin no more than 2 points high; the held-out likelihood cost per entry is under 0.003. Decision rule: the smaller T meeting the gates goes live; if neither does, the per-entry map is the next registration **Result (runs 38994071881 and 38994080812, T 1.15, both seasons): no effect; T 1.3 not run.** The 60 to 80% bin 66.2% shown against 53.0% pitched (2025) and 66.4 against 53.0 (2026), against LEASH-04's 66.5/52.3 and 66.7/52.2; the top two arms' entries per team-game 0.642 and 0.625 against 0.641 and 0.624 at T 1 (real 0.515 and 0.498); Brier 0.20312 and 0.20123 against 0.20312 and 0.20134. Wins and totals unmoved (pooled win Brier +0.00012, mean totals +0.01). The prediction failed outright: a temperature on the utilities does not move the simulated choices, because the entries where the top arms are chosen are ones where the table is nearly certain (BULLPEN-08: the 80%+ favorites are chosen 89% of the time in real entries too), so the miss is not in the choice at those entries either. What is left (the next diagnostic): the situations the simulator brings relievers into must differ from real ones inside the inning-and-lead cells BULLPEN-05 checked, most likely mid-inning against inning-end changes (the choice's mid-inning terms) and the arms already used; a replay recording each entry's mid-inning flag and candidate count against the real ones would settle it

columns.Attempt: World Series games get the regular season's starter and bullpen corrections. POST-01 and POST-02 found World Series usage like the regular season's (starters' scale 1.0, reliever exit offset 0.0), yet LEASH-02's starter-exit correction (now LEASH-04's with pitch terms) and RELIEF-04's entry-inning correction were switched on for regular-season games only, so World Series games ran the plain hazards. brl_live/boxscore.hazard_correction_for and relief_corrected now apply to game type W as to R; Wild Card, Division and League series games keep their measured usage on the plain hazards (x0.91 by tier, exit offset +0.4)
columns.Disposition and evidence: A consistency change under Alec's standing approval of October 16 (the World Series cannot be replay-gated: too few games). What it changes: starters in World Series games exit as regular-season starters do with the pitch-count terms, and relievers' entry innings follow RELIEF-04's correction; nothing changes before the World Series

columns.Attempt: Hitters' columns by count situation. A hitter's swing and whiff columns are pitch family in or out of the zone, split by two strikes or not (CHAIN-02B); the chain parameter hitter_counts 'three' splits them instead by even-or-behind with fewer than two strikes, two strikes, and ahead (COUNT3), 18 columns, so a hitter who chases when ahead but not when even is read as such; the pooled prior (CHAIN-04) keeps thin columns sane. Arms, sharing CHAIN-09's run on the live settings (chain67-both): c0 = refit control; hc3 = hitter_counts 'three'; both = with CHAIN-09's out_by_family
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Gates as CHAIN-04, judged on the hc3 arm against c0: (1) blended 2026 log loss better with the 95% game-bootstrap interval below zero and calibration within 0.015; (2) per-pitch swing and whiff log loss both no worse. The run's selection rule (lowest 2025 tuning-block log loss among hc3, obf, both) picks the arm adopted if its own gate (1) holds. Prediction: hc3 gains 0.00003 to 0.00015; the per-pitch swing check improves 0.5 to 2 per 1,000 (counts are where swing decisions differ most) **Result (run 38999960421): failed.** hc3 against c0: tuning 1.452218 against 1.452227; 2026 blended +0.000004 (interval -0.000023 to +0.000032); per pitch swings 0.54372 against 0.54354 and whiffs 0.47027 against 0.46987, both a little worse (thinner columns). The prediction failed; hitter_counts stays 'two_strike'

columns.Attempt: The ball-in-play mix by pitch family. A hitter's (and a pitcher's) in-play outcome mix is one five-class vector; with out_by_family it is kept per family (fastball, breaking, offspeed), each shrunk toward the player's pooled mix (k_b_out_pool 60, k_p_out_pool 150 balls in play) and then toward the league (pitch_chain._dev_multi_h), so a hitter who homers off fastballs and rolls over breaking balls is read as such against a fastball pitcher (test: a planted fastball-only homer hitter against an all-fastball arm reads 1.3 times the homer chance of a hitter with the same homers spread over families; identical with the option off). The park's mix stays one vector. Arms, sharing CHAIN-08's run: obf = out_by_family; both = with hitter_counts 'three'
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Gates as CHAIN-04, judged on the obf arm against c0; (2) here is the per-pitch outcome log loss no worse than c0's (the chain's own ball-in-play check, unchanged by every option so far at 0.96444). Prediction: obf gains 0.00005 to 0.0002, mostly in home runs and extra bases; the per-pitch outcome check improves 1 to 3 per 1,000 balls in play. If either passes: check-only replays refresh the context tables, then live, as CHAIN-04 **Result (run 38999960421): failed.** obf against c0: tuning 1.452301 against 1.452227; 2026 blended +0.000035 (interval -0.000008 to +0.000080); the per-pitch outcome check worse, 0.96733 against 0.96444 (a family's mix is too thin even with the pooled prior; the physics features already carry batted-ball quality by player). both: +0.000043 (-0.000013 to +0.000099). Both predictions failed; out_by_family stays off. Reading, with CHAIN-04B and 07: the chain's cell and column structure is at its useful limit; the remaining at-bat gains are elsewhere (RETRAIN-04)

columns.Attempt: The live model's coefficients are two years old. Every model today is fit on 2023-2024 with 2025 for tuning, calibration and the blend, and 2026 held out as the test; the features are current (the counters, physics and chain read through yesterday) but the weights on them are from a league two seasons gone. RETRAIN-01 measured that cost on the physics model at -0.0015 to -0.0017 nats per plate appearance on 2026's final block (the largest single at-bat gain in the project's record) and RETRAIN-02 did not switch because the gain could not be seen at the game level on 619 games (the replay lane's noise floor is about 0.001 nats, REPLAY-02), the rule CHAIN-03B replaced with: proven at the plate-appearance level, no harm at the game level. Arms (tools/fit_arms.json): c0 = the live model (chain67-both) refit as is; rt = the same settings trained on 2023-2025 with 2026 as the validation season (tune and calibration blocks through about August 12, the final block from August 13 to September 27 as the test, blend_as_test)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Gates: (1) on the games both arms hold (the final block, about 619 games), rt's blended log loss beats c0's with the 95% game-bootstrap interval below zero (tools/brl_fit_compare.py now pairs on the shared games); (2) rt's largest class calibration gap on that block within 0.015. Prediction: a gain of 0.0010 to 0.0018 nats per plate appearance on the block, with calibration no worse. If it passes: check-only replays of rt (2025 and 2026 are in its training and tuning data, so the context tables are read with that in mind: structural side-and-inning corrections the features cannot carry), then live for the rest of the postseason; and a standing process: the production model is refit each spring on the three latest seasons with the current one as the validation season, which this run establishes **Result (run 39001175133): passed.** On the 613 shared games of the final block (August 13 to September 27, 2026; 46,428 plate appearances): rt 1.453561 against c0 1.454636, difference -0.001075 nats per plate appearance, 95% game-bootstrap interval -0.001390 to -0.000731; rt's largest class calibration gap 0.0030 (c0 0.0037). The prediction held at its low end. rt's tuning block (2026 through about mid-June) scored 1.45971, its calibration block and test as above; c0's whole-2026 test 1.456848 for reference. The coefficient drift is worth four times CHAIN-04 and seven times CHAIN-06 on the same at-bats. Adoption: check-only replays retrain04-check-2025/2026 for the context tables (in-sample for rt, noted), then live as retrain04-rt. **Live from October 17, 2026, 12:41 a.m. Eastern** (brl_engine/model.json; context tables from runs 39002123075 and 39002131831, 4,850 games, brl_live/context_offsets.json pooled and brl_replay/context_retrain04_fit2025/2026.json; the 2026 table is in sample for a model whose validation season is 2026). Against chain67's tables the new offsets move strikeouts down about 0.03, doubles and triples up about 0.08 and the other-reach class down 0.06 to 0.08 in every bucket: the retrained coefficients sit on a different in-play mix and the tables carry the level, as they are meant to. RETRAIN-05 (the 548-day physics window on this base) failed, so the live model keeps the full physics history

columns.Attempt: The physics window on the retrained model. RETRAIN-03 found the pitch-physics features limited to the last 548 days worth -0.00065 nats per plate appearance on 2026 (served level reproduced exactly) and left it unswitched under the old rule (the gain could not be seen at the game level; win chances within noise, totals a shade worse in both seasons). Under CHAIN-03B's rule it qualifies if it still helps now that the chain carries recent form with a 120-day half-life. Arms on RETRAIN-04's configuration (train 2023-2025, 2026 the validation season, the final block the test): c0 = retrain04-rt refit; w548 = physics_params window_days 548
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any arm was fit.** Gates: (1) on the shared final-block games, w548 beats c0 with the 95% game-bootstrap interval below zero; (2) calibration gap within 0.015. Prediction: a gain of 0.0002 to 0.0006 (smaller than RETRAIN-03's: the chain now holds part of what the window gave). If it passes: live with the retrained model's context tables (the window changes only the physics inputs; the live loader serves a fitted window automatically)
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: **Failed** (run 39002185993, research/retrain-05-compare-39002185993.json): on the 613 shared final-block games the window arm scored 1.453639 against the control's 1.453561 (the control reproduces retrain04-rt exactly), difference +0.000078 nats per plate appearance, 95% interval top +0.000259; calibration gap 0.0025. The window's gain is gone once the chain carries recent form: RETRAIN-03's -0.00065 came from the physics features standing in for form the old model lacked. Not adopted; the retrained model keeps the full physics history

columns.Attempt: October bullpens. The live sheet's reliever statements this postseason: arms shown at 60 to 80% pitched 48% of the time (58 statements over 14 games); the simulator used 5.4 pitchers a team-game against 5.0 real. In the regular-season replays the same miss at the top comes from arms the replay never lists (7 to 8% of real relief appearances are by arms outside the 14-day pool; the live lane reads the day's roster, so that part is a replay artifact). In October the roster is known, so the miss must be in how the choice and the exits read the postseason: real managers ride two or three arms for longer outings. Research lane experiment postseason_pen (tools/brl_research.py): on every postseason game in the sealed history (2023 on) against August and September: relievers per team-game, batters per relief outing, the share of entries taken by each pool's top arms, the live choice table's calibration and fitted temperature on postseason entries (leave one postseason out), the live exit hazard's removals against its summed chance and the offset that matches them, by round
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the run.** Prediction: the postseason temperature fitted from the other postseasons lands below 1 (sharper than the regular season) in every held-out season, and the matching exit offset for Wild Card, Division and League games is at or below +0.4 once outings run longer. Adoption rule: a temperature goes live for F, D, L and W games only if every held-out postseason's log-likelihood improves at the fitted value and the pooled T is within 0.1 of each; the exit offsets move to the measured values by round when the measured mid and end offsets agree in sign with the move (a realism change, as POST-02 was; no postseason replay exists). Changes reliever appearance chances on the sheet; win chances only through bullpen quality **Result (run 39004477863, research/postseason_pen-39004477863.json; the package's postseasons sealed first as private/history/post-2023/2024/2025.enc, receipts history/post-<year>.json, run 39004353208): twelve postseasons 2015-2026, 472 games, 3,747 relief entries, 9,914 relief decisions.** (1) The prediction on the choice was wrong: the live choice table is calibrated entry by entry in October too (favorites' mean chance 0.352, chosen 0.352; candidate bins within a point to 0.4; the fitted temperature 1.05 to 1.1 with no held-out season gaining more than 0.0075 nats and six of twelve losing). No temperature change; the ADJUST key reliever_choice_temperature_postseason stays at 1.0. (2) Usage: 4.05 relievers a team-game in Wild Card, Division and League games (F 3.90, D 4.05, L 3.82, W 4.11) against 3.35 in the regular season; batters per relief outing 4.56 (26% of outings six or more) against 4.64 (25%) in August and September, so October outings are not longer on average; 6.7% of postseason relief entries are by arms outside the 14-day pool (9.2% in August and September). (3) The exits: against the plain hazard the postseason runs on, mid-inning removals are 1.74 times the hazard's expectation (851 against 488 over 2015-2026; 2022-2026 1.97, offset +0.83) and removals at an inning's end 0.90 of it (1,442 against 1,610; 2022-2026 0.86, offset -0.42); the pooled offset is +0.19, not POST-02's +0.4, and the two kinds move opposite ways. Every postseason 2022-2026 shows the same pattern (mid +0.64 to +1.03, end -0.17 to -0.55); the World Series alone (1,452 decisions) mid +0.68, end -0.44. **Adopted for F, D and L games under the registered rule: ADJUST postseason_exit_offset by decision kind, mid +0.8 and end -0.4 (the 2022-2026 era), from October 17, 2026, 1:30 a.m. Eastern (brl_live.boxscore.manager_for reads a number or a {mid, end} pair).** The World Series measured against the corrected hazard it runs on (POST-04; run 39005667776): 2022-2025 mid +0.89, end -0.29 (519 decisions), all eleven Series +0.66, -0.42, the same pattern, so the Series gets the same offsets from 1:45 a.m. What it should change: fewer relievers a team-game in October (the end-of-inning pulls were 0.7 log-odds too frequent), so the arms the sheet showed at 60 to 80% (they pitched 48%) come down; scored on the rest of this postseason with tonight/score_sheet.py. A realism change, as POST-02 was

columns.Attempt: A postseason replay lane. Every postseason setting so far (POST-01 to POST-05) was a realism calibration with no replay to check it against, because the replay lane held regular-season games only. With the postseasons sealed apart (POST-05), tools/brl_replay.py gains a postseason parameter: it loads the season's postseason rows, reconstructs those games, marks each with its round, and the harness applies the live lane's October usage per game (brl_replay.harness.postseason_game: the round's factor on expected batters, POST-03's tier factor per starter, the reliever exit offsets by decision kind added to the team hooks; the leash stays regular-season). Wild Card, Division and League games run the plain hazards as live; the World Series is replayed apart on the corrected ones. First use: the 2024 and 2025 Wild Card, Division and League games (about 38 a season), model retrain04-rt with the live tables (none of which saw a postseason game), 1,000 worlds, two arms each: the live offsets (mid +0.8, end -0.4) and POST-02's (+0.4, +0.4)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before any run.** Descriptive gates, scored with tools/brl_bullpen_cal.py, tools/brl_outs_cal.py and the receipts' pitchers per team-game: (1) relievers a team-game within 0.25 of the real count in both seasons under the live offsets, and closer than under POST-02's; (2) the reliever appearance bin 0.60-0.80 within 10 points of its actual share pooled over the two seasons, and closer than POST-02's; (3) the starter outs ladder (18+ outs share) within 5 points of real. Prediction: live offsets give 4.0 to 4.4 relievers a team-game against about 4.05 real (POST-02's 4.5 to 5.0), and the 0.60-0.80 bin lands at 55 to 70% (it was 48% in this October's live boxes under POST-02's offsets). If a gate fails, the measured offsets are re-tuned on these replays, not the live games **Result (runs 39035562121, 39035578647, 39036257097, 39036273471; 78 games, 156 team-games; scratch score_post06.py).** The lane works: starters' expected outs 13.22 against 12.92 real, 18 or more outs 23.5% against 24.4% (gate 3 holds). Relievers a team-game: live offsets 3.96 against 4.08 real (2024 -0.10, 2025 -0.15), POST-02's 4.08 (-0.01); like for like, against the appearances by arms the pool holds (41 of 637 real relief appearances, 6.4%, were by arms outside the 14-day pool, which no offset can reproduce): real 3.82, live +0.14, POST-02 +0.26, so gate 1 holds on the like-for-like count and fails on the raw one. Chance-to-pitch bins pooled: 0.60-0.80 shown 67.1%, pitched 58.7% (+8.4) under the live offsets and 67.3% / 58.9% (+8.4) under POST-02's (gate 2: within 10, not closer: a tie); 0.80 and up 83.9% / 73.5% (+10.4, 34 rows) against 84.7% / 66.7% (+18.0, 39 rows); Brier 0.2238 and 0.2283 against 0.2275 and 0.2305 (better in both seasons). Reading: the exit offsets are kept (the Brier and the top bin favor them; the count is low by the arms the pool lacks), and the exits were not the cause of the top-arm miss. The miss is the pool: the 2025-2026 regular-season receipts show the top two arms shown 1.11 appearances against 0.68 real in team-games where an outside arm pitched and 1.05 against 1.04 in the rest, so the simulator hands the outside arms' work to its top arms. That is ROSTER-01 and BULLPEN-10. Prediction scored: the count landed under the predicted 4.0 to 4.4 (3.96), the 60-80 bin inside 55 to 70 (58.7)

columns.Attempt: Daily active rosters (data). The replay's bullpen pool and the reliever-choice fit's candidate sets guess the roster from the relievers used in the last 14 days, so 7 to 9% of real relief appearances (regular season) and 7% (postseason) are by arms the simulator never lists, and in the 2025-2026 replays the whole miss on the top two arms sits in the games where such an arm pitched (team-games with an outside arm: top two shown 1.11 appearances, real 0.68; without one: 1.05 against 1.04). tools/brl_rosters.py (workflow BRL rosters, one job per season from tools/roster_seasons.txt) reads MLB's public active roster for every team on each of its game dates and keeps the pitchers: research/rosters-<year>.json.gz on the ledger branch (public data: team, date, player ids) with a receipt of counts
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the first run.** Expected: about 5,000 team-dates a season, 12 to 14 pitchers a roster, few misses. columns.Attempt: The leg book: every bet leg the simulator prices, scored on replays where neither the at-bat model nor any fitted table saw the replayed season. Alec's aim (October 18): parlay legs that are confident and verified more accurate than the market. Design: at-bat model chain67-both (fitted on 2023-2024; 2025 tuned its regularization and calibration; 2026 never seen), so 2026 is the clean test season and 2025 a secondary one. Every table fitted on the other season or on 2023-2024, including the starter leash (earlier replays used the replayed season's own leash table, leash_fit_<season>; noted as an in-sample input for starter exits). Live settings otherwise: roster pools, BULLPEN-10 tables, chain pitch counts, dropout 0, 1,000 worlds, hitter and starter lines (tags leg01-<season>). Legs: winner, run line, total over 6.5 to 11.5, team total over 2.5 to 4.5, a run in the 1st, first-five winner and total, hitter 1+ hit, 2+ hits, home run, 2+ total bases, 1+ strikeout, 1+ walk, starter strikeouts over 3.5 to 7.5, outs over 14.5 to 18.5, hits allowed over 4.5 and 5.5. Scoring: tools/brl_leg_book.py (calibration by bin, Brier, a logistic recalibration per leg type fitted on one season and applied to the other, cross-game parlays of verified legs, and win and total against the closing line where we hold it)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the runs.** A (leg type, side, bin) is verified when, in both seasons, its hit rate is within the larger of 2 points and 1.96 standard errors of the stated chance with 300 or more legs. Confident legs are verified bins at 70% and up. Prediction: hitter 1+ hit, team scores 1+, starter outs under and total-over legs at low lines verify at 70% and up; home-run yes legs never reach 70%; reliever-driven legs are not in the book. A recalibration map is adopted for the sheet's stated chances only where it lowers the 2026 Brier with a date-bootstrap interval excluding zero (fitted on 2025). Parlays: random 2-, 3- and 5-leg parlays of verified legs from different games must hit within 2 standard errors of the product of their chances. Market: win and over chances against the closing line on the same games, Brier difference with a date bootstrap; no claim of beating the market without an interval excluding zero **Result (October 18; replays leg01-2026, run 39151195010, and leg01-2025, run 39151220341: chain67-both, every table fitted on the other season or 2023-2024, the starter hazard correction on 2023-2024; 2,427 and 2,423 games, about 859,000 legs a season; scored with tools/brl_leg_book.py, as run and --as-shown, the page's run and strikeout reshaping, which differ on four of the 57 verified cells: two strikeout cells verify only as run, a strikeout cell and the under 11.5 at 80% only as shown).** Of 233 (leg, side, chance band) cells at 70% and up, 57 are verified (both seasons within the larger of 2 points and 1.96 standard errors, 300 or more legs each); 160 more were never wrong but have fewer than 300 legs in a season; 15 fail on calibration. Verified: a team scores 1+ (90% band: said 94.5, hit 94.5 and 94.3 for the home team), a team scores 2+ and 3+, the total over 6.5 at 70%, under 11.5, the run line's +1.5 side at 70% (said 73.4, hit 70.2 and 71.7, inside the band), a hitter's no home run (90% band: said 92.8, hit 92.7 and 92.6), under 2 hits, under 2 total bases, no walk, a hitter's 1+ strikeout, and the starter ladders: strikeouts over 2.5 to 4.5 and under 5.5 to 7.5, outs over 11.5 to 14.5 and under 16.5 and 18.5, hits allowed, walks. Failed on calibration: a hitter's 1+ hit at 70% and up ran high in 2026 (said 72.6, hit 69.5; 4,689 legs, 3.1 points against a 2-point allowance), the first-five total ran far high (over 3.5 at 70%: 18 and 15 points; FIRST5-01 had kept it off the page), the away team's over 2.5 runs at 70% (4.4 and 3.3 points high), starter strikeouts over 2.5 and 3.5 at 80% (2.8 to 3.8 points high in 2025), outs under 17.5 and 18.5 at 70% (low in 2025). Parlays of verified 70%+ legs from different games, 20,000 random slips: 2 legs said 67.1 hit 67.1 (2025) and 67.1 / 67.7 (2026); 3 legs 55.0 / 54.8 and 54.8 / 54.7; 5 legs 36.8 / 36.8 and 36.7 / 36.9: chances multiply as stated. Each day's likeliest legs (one a game, verified cells; mostly a starter under 7.5 or 6.5 strikeouts, a hitter's no home run, a starter under 18.5 outs, a team scoring a run): 3 a day, each said 98.8 hit 99.1 (2026) and 98.4 / 98.0 (2025), all three together said 96.5 hit 97.3 and 95.3 / 94.0 over about 180 days; 5 a day together 92.2 / 90.0 and 90.6 / 87.2; 8 a day 84.5 / 81.4 and 82.8 / 77.1: the selection's own optimism (choosing the highest numbers) shows from 5 legs and grows with 8. Market (registered test): win Brier against the closing line ours 0.24258 market 0.24326, difference -0.00068 [-0.00226, +0.00098] (2026, 2,264 games), -0.00008 [-0.00209, +0.00196] (2025, 1,686); over the closing total +0.00265 [-0.00021, +0.00554] and +0.00101 [-0.00275, +0.00483]: level with the market, no claim. Against Kalshi's last pregame trades (KALSHI-01 run 39156567358 with the team-code matching, 2,419 games of 2026, each game once): ours 0.24227 against Kalshi's 0.24327, difference -0.00100 [-0.00256, +0.00063]. Recalibration maps (fitted on one season, applied to the other) lowered the Brier with an interval below zero for the first-five totals, a hitter's home run, a hitter's strikeout, starter strikeouts over 4.5 and the home team over 5.5 runs; the board does not apply them (none of those cells is verified except the hitter's strikeout, whose map moves chances under half a point). Exploratory, designed after a first look at 63 games of partial 2026 results, so registered for a forward test as EDGE-01 and not claimed: buying the simulator's side where it and the market differ by 3 points or more returned, per dollar, +7.6 [+1.1, +13.9] at the books' fair closing price (2026, 1,017 games), +7.5 [+1.0, +13.9] at the fair opening price, +6.6 [+1.0, +12.5] on Kalshi after its full fee (1,147 games), but +0.5 [-6.0, +6.6] at DraftKings' closing prices with its margin and +5.3 [-0.8, +11.7] at the best of seven books; in 2025 +4.2 [-3.1, +12.5] fair close, +7.9 [+0.6, +14.7] fair open, +1.8 [-5.5, +8.6] at DraftKings, and on Kalshi after its fee 0.0 [-6.7, +6.8] (1,080 of 2,106 games from April 16; Kalshi's 2025 winner prices, run 39157937348; Brier ours 0.24343 against Kalshi's 0.24303, difference +0.00040 [-0.00163, +0.00233]), +6.3 [-2.7, +15.1] at 5 points: the 3-point rule did not repeat on Kalshi in 2025. Those sides won about half the time at an average price near 46%: the signal sits in close games, not in the likely legs. **Prediction check:** team scores 1+, low total overs and starter outs unders verified as predicted; a hitter's 1+ hit did not (2026 ran 3 points high); home-run yes legs never reached 70%, as predicted. **Decision:** the leg board (brl_live/page/template.html legBoard, LEG_TABLE from tools/brl_leg_table.py on the --as-shown run) lists today's legs at 70% and up whose cell is verified, each with its two seasons' record and the market's chance where the page holds one; it makes no claim of an edge

columns.Attempt: The published run distributions with their spread made right (TOTALS-04's decision (1), registered then and not yet run). The page states each team's and the total's middle range ("half of games land between"), the chance of 10 or more total runs, the most likely total and the runs chart, all from the simulated histograms, which carry the right means but run about a tenth too narrow (TOTALS-04: a team's predictive variance 9.2 against a residual variance of 10.0 to 10.1; middle-half coverage 0.48). Candidate: each team's simulated mean kept, the histogram replaced by a negative binomial with that mean and the simulated variance times c (Poisson if that is not above the mean), c the residual over the predictive variance on the other season; the total is the two teams' convolution (their residuals are uncorrelated, TOTALS-04). Scored against the raw histograms on LEASH-02's full replays of 2025 and 2026 (v2-prod4-leash2-1000, the live regular-season settings; not yet read for this) by tools/brl_runs_shape.py: each range's own mass against how often the real score landed in it, the chance of 10 or more total runs against the actual share and its Brier, CRPS per team and for the total, paired by date. Display only: win chances, the expected total and every market number are unchanged
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its run.** Predictions, in both seasons with c from the other season: (1) the total's and each team's middle range hold the real score within 1.5 points of their own mass; (2) the chance of 10 or more total runs within 1.0 point of the actual share, its Brier not worse (the paired interval's upper end at most +0.0002); (3) CRPS per team and for the total not worse by more than 0.002 (paired upper ends). Decision rule: if (1) to (3) hold in both seasons, the box's published team and total run distributions become the negative binomial with c pooled over both seasons (live and archived boxes alike; the simulated games and win chances unchanged) and How it works says so; otherwise the page keeps the raw histograms. Results (LEASH-02's replays, 2,423 games of 2025 and 2,427 of 2026; c 1.086 for 2025 from 2026 and 1.105 for 2026 from 2025): the total's middle range held the real total 56.9% of the time against its own mass of 57.2% (2025, +0.3 points; raw histograms 55.8% against 57.4%, +1.6) and 56.3% against 57.1% (2026, +0.8; raw +2.7); each team's middle range +1.4 (raw +1.9) and +1.0 (raw +2.2); 10 or more total runs 39.3% predicted against 39.3% actual (2025, -0.0; raw +0.6) and 39.8% against 40.1% (2026, -0.3; raw +0.3), Brier -0.00014 [-0.00045, +0.00014] and -0.00024 [-0.00055, +0.00009]; CRPS per team -0.0012 [-0.0025, +0.0002] and -0.0012 [-0.0026, +0.0003], for the total -0.0015 [-0.0037, +0.0007] and -0.0008 [-0.0034, +0.0018]. (1) to (3) held in both seasons. **Adopted: the page's run charts and ranges (Odds tab, the after-game likely range) use the negative binomial with RUN_SPREAD 1.0954, c pooled over both seasons; the expected total, win chances and the projected game are unchanged.**

columns.Attempt: The run line again, with TOTALS-05's widened run distributions. RUNLINE-01 failed because the simulator's margins given a win run tight; DISP-03's day-form margins fixed that but were looked at before any run-line test of them. Candidate: given a win, the chance of winning by two or more from the two teams' negative binomials (the simulated means, the simulated variances times c from the other season, as TOTALS-05) convolved as independent, P(margin >= 2) / P(margin >= 1) for the home side and the same for the road side; the page's run-line chance would be the headline win chance times it, as RUNLINE-01 planned. Scored exactly as RUNLINE-01 (tools/brl_runline_shape.py over tools/brl_runline_cal.py) on RELIEF-04's full replays of 2025 and 2026 (v2-prod4-relief4-1000, the live regular-season settings; their margins not yet looked at). The motivation (margins too tight) was seen on earlier replays of the same seasons
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its scoring.** Predictions (RUNLINE-01's): (1) given a win, the chance of winning by two or more within 1.5 points of how often winners did, for home winners and road winners, in both seasons; (2) by fifths of that conditional chance, within 3 points in both seasons. Decision rule: if (1) and (2) hold in both seasons, the Odds tab shows the run line (MORE_MARKETS.runline) from this conditional; otherwise it stays hidden. Results (2,423 and 2,427 games): given a home win, by two or more 78.6% against 65.8% actual (2025, +12.8; the simulator's own margins +0.7) and 78.6% against 68.4% (2026, +10.2; own -2.2); given a road win 78.7% against 76.5% (+2.2; own -1.1) and 78.9% against 77.3% (+1.5; own -2.0); by fifths up to 15.5 and 13.2 points (home) and 5.5 and 2.4 (road). (1) and (2) failed in both seasons. **The run line stays hidden.** What it shows: treating the two teams' runs as independent ignores how home wins end (the bottom of the ninth is not played or stops at the winning run, so home winners win by one far more often); the simulator's own margins keep that and are the better base.

columns.Attempt: Starters' strikeout distributions with their spread made right (the Odds tab's strikeout ladder and the starters' strikeout ranges). Seen on LEASH-02's replays before this row (described after looking): the means are right (4.87 against 4.79 in 2025, 4.69 against 4.70 in 2026) but the residual variance runs 1.07 times the simulated variance in both seasons, and in 2026 the ladder sits high at the low lines and low at the high ones (+0.9 to +1.2 points at 2.5 to 4.5, -0.6 to -1.4 at 6.5 to 8.5), the pattern of a distribution a little too narrow. Candidate: each start's simulated distribution kept and spread, convolved with the step {-1: w, 0: 1 - 2w, +1: w}, w = (c - 1) x its variance / 2, the mass below zero folded onto zero, c from the other season (tools/brl_k_spread.py). Scored against the raw distributions on the same replays (v2-prod4-leash2-1000; the RELIEF-04 replays, if that goes live, change no starter's distribution beyond noise): the chance of more than each line from 2.5 to 8.5 against the actual share, Brier over those lines paired by date, and the middle range's own mass against how often the real count landed in it. Because the motivation was seen on these replays, the decision is a product call on display calibration
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before the candidate was scored.** Predictions, in both seasons with c from the other season: (1) the largest gap across the lines 2.5 to 8.5 smaller than the raw distributions'; (2) Brier over those lines not worse (paired upper end at most +0.0001); (3) the middle range within 1.0 point of its own mass. Decision rule: if (1) to (3) hold in both seasons, the page's strikeout ladder and ranges use the spread distribution with c pooled over both seasons; otherwise they keep the raw ones. Results (LEASH-02's replays, 4,846 and 4,854 starts; c 1.066 for 2025 from 2026 and 1.072 for 2026 from 2025): the largest line gap 2.35 to 1.92 points (2025; 2.5 to 4.5 +2.3, +2.4, +1.8 became +1.7, +1.9, +1.8, the season's level runs 0.08 strikeouts high) and 1.39 to 1.20 (2026; 2.5 +0.9 to +0.2, 8.5 -1.4 to -0.9); Brier over the lines -0.000057 [-0.000117, +0.000003] and -0.000051 [-0.000104, +0.000004]; the middle range 63.2% mass against 62.8% actual (2025, +0.3; raw +1.8) and 63.7% against 63.7% (2026, +0.0; raw +1.5). (1) to (3) held in both seasons. **Adopted: the strikeout ladder, the starters' strikeout ranges and the after-game range use the spread distribution (page K_SPREAD 1.0693, c pooled).**

columns.Attempt: Starters' hits allowed as a prop ladder (the standard pitcher-hits market, next to the strikeout ladder). Each start's simulated hits allowed (the box keeps the distribution) against his real hits, on two sets of full replays of 2025 and 2026: RELIEF-04's (v2-prod4-relief4-1000, the live regular-season settings) and PLAYER-07's (v2-prod4-outs-1000, the plain starter-exit hazard the postseason keeps). Only the season means were seen before this row (4.89 against 4.90 and 4.83 against 4.74 on LEASH-02's). Two candidates: the raw distributions and the same spread to the residual variance by PLAYER-08's step with c from the other season (tools/brl_prop_ladder.py)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its scoring.** Predictions, per replay set: (1) at every half line from 2.5 to 7.5 the mean chance of more within 2.0 points of the actual share in both seasons; (2) Brier at the lines 3.5 to 6.5 together better than each line's constant share in both seasons. Decision rule: if (1) and (2) hold with the raw distributions on both sets, the Odds tab adds each starter's hits-allowed ladder (his chance of more than each half line around his median, from 2.5 to 7.5, with the fair price) for every box; if they hold only with the spread distributions on both sets, the ladder uses those; if they hold (either way) on RELIEF-04's set but not on PLAYER-07's, it shows only for boxes simulated with the corrected starter exits (as the outs ladder); otherwise it is not shown. Results (4,846 and 4,854 starts in each set): RELIEF-04's replays, raw: hits allowed 4.89 simulated against 4.90 actual (2025) and 4.83 against 4.74 (2026); every line from 2.5 to 7.5 within 1.07 points (2025; largest +1.1 at 5.5) and 1.64 (2026; +1.6 at 3.5 and 4.5); Brier at 3.5 to 6.5 0.20200 against a constant's 0.21440 and 0.19959 against 0.21576. PLAYER-07's replays (plain exits), raw: within 0.80 and 1.32 points; Brier 0.20203 against 0.21440 and 0.19944 against 0.21576. The residual over the simulated variance is 0.99 to 1.03, so the spread version changes little (within 1.15 and 1.64; 1.08 and 1.28). (1) and (2) held with the raw distributions on both sets. **Shown: the Odds tab adds each starter's hits-allowed ladder (raw) for every box.**

columns.Attempt: Re-anchoring each outcome's league level in-season (a screen). Outcome levels drift by season and the simulator carries them from its tables (PLAYER-03: with tables from other seasons, 2025's walk-or-HBP chances ran 2 points high and 2026's hit chances 1 point high); at the start of a season the live tables are of the same kind, fitted on earlier seasons. Each date's offsets come only from the season's real plate appearances on earlier dates: per class (out in play, strikeout, walk or HBP, single, double or triple, home run, other reach), log((observed + m x share) / (predicted + m x share)) with m pseudo plate appearances at the predicted shares (the context table's form, CTX-02), applied to the date's predictions (each chance times exp(offset), renormalized). Check-only replays of 2025 and 2026 on the live stack with tables from other seasons (PLAYER-07's settings with no worlds and the real plate-appearance check, which records each game's observed counts, predicted sums and second moments); the log-likelihood change on each date's real plate appearances is computed from those per-game sums (tools/brl_level_cal.py; within 0.1% of the exact change for offsets up to about 0.1 in its tests). Grid: m of 2,000, 10,000 and 50,000; each season is scored at the m with the larger gain on the other season
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its replays.** Prediction: (1) at the m picked on the other season, the season's held-out log-likelihood gain is positive with its bootstrap interval over dates above zero, in both seasons. Decision rule: if (1) holds in both seasons, an in-season league-level layer is built for next season (off by default) and LEVEL-02 is registered: full replays of both seasons with it, gated on the game totals and the hitter chances; otherwise the item is dropped. Results (check-only runs 38152933999 for 2025 and 38152908828 for 2026; 182,487 and 183,685 real plate appearances over 184 dates each): log-likelihood gain per 1,000 plate appearances at m 2,000, 10,000 and 50,000: 2025 +0.097 [+0.007, +0.182], +0.114 [+0.038, +0.187], +0.108 [+0.053, +0.160]; 2026 +0.124 [-0.002, +0.251], +0.146 [+0.039, +0.249], +0.138 [+0.071, +0.204]. Each season picks m 10,000 from the other, so the scored gains are +0.114 (2025) and +0.146 (2026), both intervals above zero: (1) held in both seasons. The season's own level against the tables from the other season mirrors between the two (observed over predicted, log): walk or HBP -0.045 in 2025 and +0.046 in 2026, doubles and triples +0.031 and -0.038, home runs +0.019 and -0.040, strikeouts -0.009 and +0.012; the in-season offsets find each within weeks. The gain is small per plate appearance (about 0.01 nats a game) and shows in most months of both seasons. **Under the rule: the layer is built (brl_live/provider_adjust.py LevelAdjust, off) and LEVEL-02 is registered.**
columns.Delta corrected Brier, 2026: (1) held in both seasons; layer built, off; LEVEL-02 next

columns.Attempt: The in-season league level (LEVEL-01's layer) in full replays. Each date's offsets come from the season's earlier real plate appearances only, m 10,000 (LEVEL-01's pick), applied last in the stack (brl_live/provider_adjust.py LevelAdjust; per-date files brl_replay/level_offsets_<season>.json written from LEVEL-01's check-only runs by tools/brl_level_cal.py --write-offsets). Replays of 2025 and 2026 with PLAYER-06's settings and seeds (live stack, tables from other seasons, hitter and starter lines, paired streams, 1,000 worlds) plus the layer, compared game by game and hitter by hitter with PLAYER-06's replays (runs 38145318753 and 38144947261) by tools/replay_compare.py and tools/brl_player_cal.py --pair. Each season's first date has no offsets, so its games must come out the same in both runs (the check that the pairing holds)
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its replays.** Gates: (1) the hitter chances' Brier summed over the page's five kinds (at least one hit, two or more hits, a home run, a walk, a strikeout) improves in both seasons, the paired interval over dates below zero; (2) the mean total's squared error against the final is not worse, the pooled paired interval's upper end below +0.03 runs squared, and the mean total within 0.1 runs of actual in both seasons; (3) the win Brier pooled not worse than +0.0002. P(over the closing total) is reported, not gated. Decision rule: if (1), (2) and (3) hold, the layer is switched on for next season's regular season (ADJUST level_offsets, the live run keeping the season's sums of observed and predicted outcomes; the postseason keeps the regular season's last offsets); otherwise it stays off. Results (runs 38154688725 for 2025 and 38154660273 for 2026, against PLAYER-06's replays; the first date's game came out the same in both runs in each season, and every later game differs): (1) the hitter chances' summed Brier -0.00033 [-0.00047, -0.00018] in 2025 (walk or HBP 2.0 points high before, 1.1 after; strikeouts 1.0 to 0.5) but -0.00001 [-0.00022, +0.00020] in 2026 (hits 0.95 points high before, 0.47 after, home runs 0.56 to 0.02, but walks -0.36 to +0.98 and strikeouts +0.74 to +1.07); (2) the mean total 8.863 to 8.847 against 8.898 actual (2025) and 8.933 to 8.856 against 8.962 (2026, 0.106 short), squared error pooled +0.019 [-0.004, +0.045]; (3) the win Brier pooled -0.00001 [-0.00017, +0.00015]; P(over) Brier pooled +0.00039 [+0.00008, +0.00071], worse. (1) failed in 2026 and (2) failed. **The layer stays off.** What it shows: putting each outcome's rate right per plate appearance lowers 2026's totals below the real ones (more walks and fewer extra-base hits and home runs, as 2026 had, turn into fewer runs in the simulator than in real games), so the tables' level errors had been offsetting a shortfall in how the simulator turns that mix into runs; and in 2026 the chance of at least one walk was on level before re-anchoring although walks per hitter-game ran 2.7% short (0.390 simulated against 0.401 real; described after looking): real walks bunch into fewer hitter-games than simulated ones, so lifting the rate overshoots the chance. Next: how the simulator converts walks and singles into runs (RUNS-03 and the running plays point the same way)

columns.Attempt: The in-season level together with the running plays, the pairing RUNS-03 pointed to. RUNS-03 found the simulator's 2026 run level right only because two level errors cancel: the stack's season level carried from the other season (+0.04 runs per team-game) against the base-running shortfall without the running plays (TRANS-02's component check: -0.072 runs per team per nine innings without them, +0.008 with them, in 2026). LEVEL-02 removed the first and its 2026 totals fell 0.077 runs a game below the reference, as that reading predicts; TRANS-02 alone added 0.14. Replays of 2025 and 2026 with PLAYER-06's settings and seeds plus both: LEVEL-02's per-date offsets and the running plays with tables from other seasons (brl_replay/running_events_fit_2023_2025.json for 2026, running_events_fit_2023_2024_2026.json for 2025), against PLAYER-06's replays, scored like LEVEL-02
columns.Disposition and evidence: **Registered in the commit that added this row, before its replays.** Gates: (1) the mean total within 0.10 runs of actual in both seasons; (2) the mean total's squared error not worse, the pooled paired interval's upper end below +0.03 runs squared; (3) P(over the closing total) Brier not worse, the pooled interval's upper end below +0.0003; (4) the win Brier pooled not worse than +0.0002; (5) the hitter chances' summed Brier not worse in either season, each interval's upper end below +0.0002. Decision rule: if all five hold, both go on for next season's regular season as a structural fix (ADJUST running_events, and the level layer once the live run keeps the season's running sums); otherwise neither changes. Results (runs started 17:34 and 17:44 UTC October 11, tags v2-prod4-lvrun-1000-<season>, against PLAYER-06's replays): (1) the mean total 8.990 against 8.898 actual (2025, +0.092) and 9.000 against 8.962 (2026, +0.038), held; (2) the mean total's squared error pooled +0.010 [-0.022, +0.042], failed (upper end above +0.03); (3) P(over) Brier pooled +0.00064 [+0.00024, +0.00105], failed (worse in both seasons: +0.00078 and +0.00054); (4) the win Brier pooled +0.00013 [-0.00008, +0.00033], held; (5) the hitter chances' summed Brier -0.00033 [-0.00048, -0.00018] (2025) and -0.00002 [-0.00023, +0.00020] (2026), held. **Neither changes.** The pairing fixed the level as RUNS-03 predicted (2026: 8.933, 8.856 with the level alone, 9.000 with both, against 8.962) but the over and under got worse in both seasons, as it did with the level alone (LEVEL-02): moving the simulator's level toward the season's own does not help it call games against the line
